name: s42_00000.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and round. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center. On the left is a Sights Set sign, an upward arrow on a stem ending in a small diamond. On the right is a water sigil, an S-curve between two teardrops, drawn slightly roughly. Each is small, about a quarter of the ring's radius. A Projection sign, a flat-topped bracket, sits at the south-southeast with its top toward the center. An Aeriforms Defined sign, three short strokes, sits near the ring at the northeast with its top toward the center. A Holding sign, two curved strokes each with a dot, sits at the west, turned with its top toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its small size gives a modest intensity, and its slightly rough lines make the effect a little weaker and shorter lived. Sights Set at the center lets the caster aim the spell at a chosen point. Projection works with it to send the effect outward from the seal toward that point. Holding is likely non-directional, so its rotation does not change its effect. It keeps the water in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. Aeriforms Defined is a poorly understood air modifier. It is read here as giving the water an airy, vapor-like character, which is a guess. Aiming and projection serve one purpose, so the seal combines three kinds of modifier and stays coherent. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no side is favored beyond where the caster aims.
effect: Sends a small, cohesive cloud of misty water outward toward a point the caster aims at. The cloud keeps its shape as it travels. It is fairly weak and thins out and disperses somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00001.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly round. A water sigil of moderate size sits at the center. Four smaller sub-seals sit inside the main ring. At the north-northwest is a neat, closed ring holding a Glaives sign at its center, with no sigil. At the east-northeast is a closed ring holding a small water sigil. At the south-southeast is a closed ring holding a wind sigil. At the west-southwest is a closed but heavily wobbly, lumpy ring holding a light sigil. Seven signs sit near the main ring. Three Crosshair signs are at the north, east-southeast, and south; the north one crosses the edge of the north-northwest sub-seal and the south one crosses the edge of the south-southeast sub-seal. A Convergence triangle at the east-northeast is drawn with a heavy, jagged outline that overlaps the water sub-seal's ring, and its point faces outward rather than inward. A Partition sign at the west faces inward. A Stillness sign sits at the northwest, and a Windows sign, a small hatched ring, sits at the southwest. Some strokes overlap, but every glyph is legible.
justification: The central water sigil sets the element, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. The water and wind sub-seals add their own water and moving air. The light sub-seal adds a glow, but its ring is far from round, so that part is fleeting and may fail to activate. The Glaives sub-seal has no sigil, so it acts only as a modifier, setting how deeply the magic embeds into flesh. The three Crosshair signs are the most numerous modifier, so targeting dominates: the effect is aimed at whatever their short ends point toward, on several sides. Partition outlines the borders of the area of effect. Convergence normally focuses magic to a single point, but here it points outward. Reading this as reversing the focus into a spreading effect is a guess, and it works against both the Partition boundary and the Crosshair targeting. Stillness holds magic in place, which contradicts the outward targeting and the moving air from the wind sub-seal. Windows links two spaces that are not physically connected. Together this stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier around the main sigil, with several pulling in opposite directions. The water sigil and the Crosshair targeting dominate, and the result is likely unstable. The roughness of the Convergence, Stillness, and Partition strokes, and of several sub-seal rings, weakens those parts further and shortens how long they last.
effect: Produces water that is pushed toward targets on several sides within a bounded area, carried on moving air and lit by a faint glow, and able to sink into the flesh of what it strikes. The effect is erratic: the water spreads unevenly instead of gathering, portions meant to hold still waver and slip loose, and the light sputters out almost at once or never appears. Some of the water may surface in an unconnected location, and the whole effect tends to collapse early.

name: s42_00002.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain white background, ring closed and drawn round and neat. A small light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short strokes reaching outward, sits at the center and is small relative to the ring. Near the ring at the north-northwest is a Partition sign, its peaked top toward the ring. It is small and its strokes are slightly uneven. Near the ring at the south-southwest is a four-lobed Billow sign, drawn cleanly. Both signs sit on the western half of the seal, and the eastern half is empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates light, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Light from this sigil diminishes over time. Billow is not at the center here, so it acts as a modifier rather than the core of the spell. It turns what the spell produces into a soft, fluffy, cloud-like mass, which gives the light a puffy, billowing form instead of a beam or point. Partition outlines the borders of an area of effect that extends outward and upward, so the cloud of light is held within a defined region. Its rough strokes slightly weaken that boundary. Both signs sit on the western side with nothing to balance them, so the effect leans west of the seal instead of centering over it. The two modifiers do not conflict, so the seal should hold together.
effect: Produces a modest, soft cloud of glowing light that puffs up within a bounded area offset to the west of the seal. The edge of that area is a little uneven and wavers on its northwest side. The glow dims gradually over time.

name: s42_00003.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Inside the inner ring, a Concealment sign (an eight-armed star with eye marks) sits at the southeast and an Envelopment sign (a slanted stroke with hooked ends) sits at the southwest. In the band between the two rings are five Crushing signs at the north, east-northeast, southeast, south, and west-northwest. Each is drawn with its top toward the center, so the northern one reads as a W and the southern one as an M; all five are inverted. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell that moves and manipulates air, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Crushing is semi-directional, so inverting it reverses its effect: instead of breaking solids apart, the five inverted signs pull crushed or scattered material back into its original form. Five of them spread evenly around the outer band make that reforming strong and even on all sides. Concealment hides a target, and Envelopment makes an effect surround what it targets. Together they wrap the target in a hiding layer, as in shadow-cloaking seals. Read together, the air current carries loose fragments and dust, the inverted Crushing reassembles them, and Concealment with Envelopment shapes the result into a covering that hides whatever it surrounds. These modifiers work toward one purpose and do not contradict each other.
effect: Stirs a steady current of air that sweeps up nearby dust and broken fragments and temporarily fuses them back into solid pieces. Those pieces are wrapped around the target as a shell that hides it from view. When the spell ends, the reformed material crumbles back into loose debris.

name: s42_00004.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The main ring is open, with a gap at the lower right, and is drawn roughly and somewhat out of round. A small fire sigil sits at the center. Six identical signs are spaced evenly around it at about two thirds of the way to the ring, at the northeast, east, south-southeast, southwest, west and north-northwest. Each sign is a small octagon crossed by two lines. Rotation makes some crosses read as a plus and others as an X. The signs at the west and northeast are drawn heavier than the rest. Three smaller closed rings touch the main ring from outside. The rings at the northwest and east-northeast each hold a small light sigil, and the ring at the south holds an Immobility sign at its center.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. The crossed octagon matches no known sign exactly. It is closest to Selection, a cross drawn through an enclosing shape, so reading it as Selection is a guess. Read that way, the six signs confine the spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on. Because they are evenly spaced and non-directional, they push the effect in no particular direction. The two attached light sub-seals add light, which falls within the fire domain, so the heat also gives off a glow. The attached Immobility sub-seal keeps the target fixed in relation to the seal, so it holds its shape and position. The seal does not activate while the ring is open. The rough linework and the ring's uneven roundness would make any effect weaker and short-lived once the ring is closed.
effect: It does not activate as drawn. Once closed, it would make the object it is drawn on give off modest heat and a soft glow, with the effect held fixed in place and kept from spreading beyond that object. The warmth and light would flicker unevenly and die out sooner than a cleanly drawn version.

name: s42_00005.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and fairly round. Two small glyphs share the center side by side: a Strengthening sign on the left and a water sigil on the right, each roughly a fifth of the ring's radius. Four Crushing signs sit about two-thirds of the way out, one each at the north, east, south and west points, with their peaks facing the center. The north one reads as a W and the south one as an M, matching the inverted arrangement. The east Crushing sign is drawn a little roughly; the others are neat. A single Concealment sign, an eight-armed star with eye marks on four arms, sits near the ring at the southeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on water. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Crushing is semi-directional, and all four are inverted, so instead of breaking matter apart they pull scattered material back into its original form. Here that is broken or scattered water, and the reformed shape lasts only while the spell holds. The Strengthening sign at the center makes the reformed water harder and more durable. The lone Concealment sign hides the target. Because it sits only at the southeast, the seal's signs are unbalanced and the hiding leans to that side. Strengthening, reforming and concealment are three compatible kinds of modifier and do not contradict each other. The slightly rough east Crushing sign weakens the reforming pull on that side a little.
effect: Draws scattered or splashed water back together into the shape it held before and firms it so it holds together more solidly, falling apart again once the spell ends. The effect is modest in strength. The reformed water is partly hidden from sight, but the concealment pools unevenly toward one side, and the pull is slightly weaker on the opposite side, so the water there gathers more slowly and loosely.

name: s42_00006.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The outer ring is closed but drawn as a lumpy, uneven loop that is far from round. A small, roughly drawn water sigil sits at the center. Three Dispersion signs sit at the west, north-northeast and south-southeast, each with its stem toward the center and its curve toward the ring. Two Glaives signs sit inside the ring: one at the west-northwest with its prongs toward the ring, and one at the east-northeast inverted, with its prongs toward the center. A Crushing sign at the south is drawn as a W, its points toward the ring. Three small sub-seals sit inside the main ring. At the southwest is a closed sub-seal holding a water sigil that fills about half of it. At the north is a closed sub-seal holding a Projection sign. At the east-southeast is a sub-seal whose ring is open, holding a small earth sigil. Most of the signs are drawn roughly.
justification: The central water sigil sets the element, but its small size gives low intensity. The large water sigil in the southwest sub-seal adds a stronger secondary source of water. The three Dispersion signs, evenly spaced, make the water pour outward in all directions rather than form a beam. Crushing breaks its target into smaller pieces. Acting on water, it most plausibly shatters the flow into fine droplets. The north sub-seal's Projection sign pushes the effect outward from the seal. The earth sub-seal's ring is open, so it contributes nothing until closed. The two Glaives directly contradict each other, one normal and one inverted, so their control over how deeply the magic embeds in flesh largely cancels and behaves unpredictably. The seal also stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: Dispersion, Glaives, Crushing and Projection. Dispersion and the water sigils dominate, but the result is likely unstable. The rough strokes make it weaker and shorter lived. The badly misshapen outer ring means the effect would be fleeting at best or might fail to activate.
effect: Sprays water outward from the seal in all directions as a fine, broken mist, with one side gushing noticeably harder than the rest. The spray sputters and wavers in strength, and wherever it reaches skin it sometimes soaks in deeply and sometimes barely touches. It collapses after only a moment, if it starts at all.

name: s42_00007.png
description: A fully visible seal in black line on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both closed. The outer ring is slightly rough. A small, neatly drawn water sigil sits at the center, roughly a fifth of the ring's radius. A large Reflection sign, an hourglass of two triangles, sits at the northeast against the inner ring. A small Glaives sign sits inside the inner ring at the north-northwest, its prongs pointing toward the center. Three Repetition signs sit in the band between the rings, at the north-northwest, the west-northwest and the south. The west-northwest one is drawn darker and heavier than the others. A Refuse sign straddles the inner ring at the west-southwest, its diamond end toward the center. A small Purification curl sits at the east-southeast, near the inner ring. The signs are spread evenly around the seal.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its small size gives low intensity, and the slightly rough outer ring weakens it a little more. Purification separates waste from water. Refuse points inward, so it draws that waste toward the center. These two signs work together as a cleansing core. The three Repetition signs are the most numerous modifier, so they dominate, and they keep resetting the water to the state it had when first affected. Together with the cleansing core, this holds the water clean. The second ring adds strength to that combined effect. Reflection is unrelated: it targets a reflected image on the surface the seal is drawn on, and its large size gives it real weight. Glaives is also unrelated: it sets how deeply magic embeds into flesh, though it is small and roughly drawn. This stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: cleansing, time-resetting, reflection and embedding. The water, Repetition and cleansing parts dominate, Reflection competes noticeably, and the result is likely unstable.
effect: Gently cleans a small amount of water, pulling impurities to the center and keeping resetting the water so it stays clear. The cleansing wavers and acts unevenly. At times it seems to work on the water's reflected surface rather than the water itself. Water touching skin may cling and seep in briefly before the effect lapses early.

name: s42_00009.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background, ring closed. A wind sigil sits at the center and is fairly large, reaching about halfway to the ring. Four Convergence triangles surround it: three in the inner band at the north-northwest, northeast and southwest, each turned at a different angle, and a fourth just inside the ring at the northeast with its flat edge toward the ring and its point toward the center. Three Binding signs sit close to the ring at the north, southeast and west-southwest, each with its smaller arc toward the center. A Strengthening sign sits at the west-northwest, tilted with its top toward the center. A small Cooling sign sits at the east-southeast, rotated so its bar runs diagonally. A Partition sign sits at the south with its peak toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a spell that moves and manipulates existing air, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Convergence focuses magic toward a single point and packs loose material tightly. With four of these, it is the dominant modifier, so the moving air is drawn together. The three Binding signs are the next strongest. They halt the gathered air and make it act as one unit. Strengthening adds hardness and durability, Cooling lowers temperature, and Partition outlines the borders of the area of effect. That makes five different kinds of modifier on one seal. The compacting signs (Convergence, Binding, Strengthening) work toward the same end and dominate. Cooling and Partition are single, unrelated additions that pull in other directions, so the result is likely unstable. The Convergence triangles are turned inconsistently, which further muddies how evenly the air is focused. The signs are balanced around the ring, so the effect has no favored direction.
effect: Draws the surrounding air inward and presses it into a dense, chilled mass that holds together as a single body inside a bounded area. The mass hardens unevenly and tends to waver at its edges. Its cooling and its boundary flicker in and out, so it may loosen and scatter back into ordinary air sooner than expected.

name: s42_00010.png
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a plain background. The ring is closed but noticeably lumpy and uneven, bulging at the upper left and flattening along the right. A large Strengthening sign sits at the center in place of a sigil, a triangle crossed by a horizontal bar, drawn with thick, jagged strokes and spanning about half the ring's radius. Five Orb signs, each a small circle crossed by a slanted line, sit near the ring at the north-northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest, and northwest. A single Crosshair sign, four short strokes around an empty center and slightly tilted, sits at the west. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Strengthening sign sets the spell's core behavior, which is making material harder, stronger, and more durable. Its large size relative to the ring gives that reinforcement fairly high intensity. The five Orb signs are non-directional and define a spherical space above the seal where material collects, filling from the bottom up under gravity. The Crosshair is directional and points the seal's effect at whatever its shorter ends face. The signs are spread evenly, so no side is favored. These three modifiers support each other rather than conflict. Because there is no element, the spell works on any material brought to it. However, the rough strokes weaken the seal and shorten its life, and the ring is far from round, which makes the effect fleeting and risks the seal failing to activate.
effect: Forms a spherical space above the seal where any material poured into it gathers from the bottom up and is hardened into a tougher, more durable mass, with the effect aimed at whatever the seal targets. The sphere's outline wavers and may not take hold at all. When it does, the hardening sets unevenly and fades after a short time.

name: s42_00011.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed. The ring is lumpy and noticeably out of round, wider at the upper left and flattened in places. A fire sigil sits at the center, small to moderate in size relative to the ring and a little roughly drawn. Two four-lobed Billow signs sit off-center at the east and west, both somewhat rough. Two neatly drawn Immobility signs sit near the ring, one at the north-northwest and one at the south-southeast, each with its crossbar toward the ring. A single Convergence triangle sits at the south-southwest near the ring, with a point turned inward and heavier, rougher strokes. The signs cluster unevenly, with more weight toward the south-southwest.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the seal creates and shapes flame or heat. Its modest size gives modest intensity. Billow turns material into a soft, fluffy cloud, and with two of them flanking the fire sigil, the flame takes a billowing, cloud-like form. The two Immobility signs make the target hold its shape and position relative to the seal. Convergence focuses magic toward a single point and packs loose particles tightly together, which directly opposes Billow's fluffy loosening. The two Billow signs outweigh the single Convergence, so the cloud form dominates, but the two pull against each other and the result is likely unstable. Because the signs are unbalanced toward the south-southwest, where Convergence sits, the effect leans to that side. The rough strokes and the poorly rounded ring make the spell weak and fleeting, and it may fail to activate at all.
effect: Raises a puffy cloud of flame that hangs fixed in place over the seal, keeping its shape as the seal moves. The cloud swells loosely but keeps clumping into a denser knot on one side, so it burns unevenly and lopsided. It flickers and collapses after only a brief moment, and it may sputter out without forming at all.

name: s42_00012.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings. The outer ring is open, broken along its left side. The inner ring, just inside it, is also open, with a gap at the upper left beside the north sign. A small Purification sign, a hooked curl, sits at the center in place of a sigil, at roughly a quarter of the ring's radius. Three Stretch signs are evenly spaced between the center and the inner ring, at the north, east-southeast and southwest. Each has its rounded side toward the center and its open end with flared feet facing out toward the ring. No element sigil and no other signs are present.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Purification sign is the core of the seal. Purification separates waste from water, so the spell works on water rather than calling up an element of its own. Its small size relative to the ring points to a modest intensity. Because Purification is asymmetric, its behavior is less predictable than symmetric signs. Stretch turns solid matter touched by the spell into long, flexible ribbons. Paired with Purification, it would act on the solid waste pulled out of the water rather than on the water itself. Stretch is not known to change when turned around, so drawing it rounded side inward is treated as its normal reading. The three Stretch signs are evenly spaced, so the effect favors no direction. The empty second ring adds no new modifier, but a doubled ring tends to strengthen the core magic slightly. Both rings are open, so the seal will not activate until they are closed.
effect: It does not activate as drawn. Once closed, it would separate dirt and waste from water passing over the seal and draw the separated solids out into long, flexible ribbons, leaving the water cleaner. The purifying is gentle in strength, and how thoroughly it sorts the waste may vary from one use to the next.

name: s42_00013.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and drawn neatly. A tall, narrow glyph sits at the center: a stretched triangle with a short stroke rising from each upper side and a stem below. It resembles a fire sigil drawn tall and reaches about half the ring's radius. Six small, identical unnamed glyphs sit evenly spaced along the inner ring, at roughly north, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest, each with its top toward the center. Each looks like a Stillness sign with its right part missing. Those at the north, southeast, south-southwest and west-southwest are drawn a little roughly. A single Aeriforms Defined sign, three short strokes, sits inside the inner ring at the east, partway between the center and the ring, with its top toward the center.
justification: The central glyph matches no sigil exactly. Its closest match is the fire sigil, stretched tall, so it is read as a fire variant. This is a guess, and it would make the spell create flame or heat, likely drawn upward into a tall shape. Its large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong intensity, and the second ring adds strength to the core spell. The six edge glyphs are closest to Stillness, also a guess, and would hold the magic static in one place. Because they are evenly spaced, the hold is balanced on all sides rather than pushed in one direction. The roughly drawn ones weaken that hold slightly on their sides. Aeriforms Defined modifies a spell toward air and gases. Paired with fire, it would turn some of the heat into warm air. Its lone placement at the east gives that air a slight lean in that direction. The two kinds of modifier do not conflict.
effect: Raises a tall, fairly strong flame or column of heat that stays fixed in place above the seal, surrounded by a body of warm air that drifts slightly to one side. The hold is weaker toward the south and southwest, so warmth slowly leaks away unevenly there and the effect fades sooner than it otherwise would.

name: s42_00014.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a plain background, ring closed. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center. On the left is a small, slightly rough glyph resembling the wind sigil: the spiral and its flanking dashes are present, but the lower part of the spiral is missing. On the right is a somewhat larger, neatly drawn glyph resembling the light sigil, a diamond set in a square with four arms crossing it. Its halves are mirror images of each other. Six signs are spread evenly around the seal. Two Entwining signs sit at the north-northwest and southwest with their tops toward the center. Three Orb signs sit at the northeast, west-northwest and south. At the east-southeast is a glyph resembling a Solidification sign stretched wide and set at an angle. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: Neither central glyph matches a sigil exactly. The left one is closest to the wind sigil and the right one to the light sigil; both readings are guesses. The light glyph is larger and neater, so light dominates and sets the main element. The wind glyph is small, rough and incomplete, so its air-moving contribution is weak and short-lived. The three evenly spaced Orb signs define a spherical space above the seal where the spell's material collects, filling from the bottom up. The two Entwining signs make the effect wrap itself around other objects. The stretched glyph is read as Solidification, also a guess; stretched wide, it would make the magic firmer over a broader area. These three kinds of modifier do not contradict each other, and the signs are balanced, so the spell has no set direction.
effect: Gathers light into a firm, glowing sphere above the seal that can wrap itself around nearby objects. A faint stirring of air drifts the sphere about, but the movement is weak and patchy and dies out well before the light does. The light itself dims gradually over time.

name: s42_00016.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black line on a white background. The ring is roughly drawn, lopsided rather than round, and open with a gap at the upper right. An earth sigil sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring and drawn roughly. Six signs surround it. Two large, bold Strengthening signs sit at the northwest and southeast, each tilted at a different angle. Two Entwining signs sit at the northeast and southwest, tops toward the ring. A small Piercing sign at the east point lies nearly sideways. A small Coil sign at the west point lies on its side, top toward the ring. The signs are evenly spread around the seal.
justification: The earth sigil makes this a spell that works existing solid matter such as stone or soil, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. The single Piercing sign shapes that matter into a projectile, and one sign means one projectile. Strengthening makes the matter harder and more durable. Entwining makes it wrap around whatever it reaches. Coil softens physical matter, which directly contradicts Strengthening. The two large, bold Strengthening signs dominate the single small Coil sign, so the material should mostly harden. Combined with four different kinds of modifier, the result is likely unstable. The balanced placement adds no direction. The rough drawing makes the spell weaker and shorter lived, and the lopsided ring may make the effect fleeting or keep it from activating. The ring is open, so the seal does not activate as drawn.
effect: Does not activate as drawn. Once the ring is closed, it would pull nearby stone or soil into a single hardened projectile that wraps around whatever it strikes. Patches of the projectile would turn soft or crumble unevenly while the rest stayed hard. It would hold its shape only briefly before collapsing, and might fizzle out before it forms at all.

name: s42_00017.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is hand-drawn and slightly lopsided rather than perfectly round. A wind sigil sits at the center at moderate size, about a third of the ring's radius, drawn with somewhat shaky lines. Four Diamond signs stand about halfway out from the center at the northwest, north-northeast, east-northeast and south-southwest, each tilted at a different angle. Two Purification signs, small hooked curls, sit at the west-southwest and southeast, each with its top turned toward the center. Two small Dancing Puppets signs sit near the ring at the northwest and northeast. Most of the inner signs are drawn roughly, and the northeast Dancing Puppets sign is the neatest glyph on the seal.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a spell that moves and manipulates air, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Paired with wind, Dancing Puppets lets objects be lifted and steered through the air. These two are small and sit near the ring instead of surrounding the sigil, so that control is limited and loosely guided. The four Diamond signs likely confine the spell to objects inside the container the seal is drawn on, leaving the container itself unaffected. Purification separates waste from what it acts on, so with a wind sigil it would draw dirt and impurities out of the moving air. It is asymmetric, though, and its behavior is less predictable. The seal combines only three kinds of modifier and none of them conflict, so it holds together. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, so no direction is favored. The rough strokes and the slightly uneven ring make the spell weaker and shorter lived than a neat version would be.
effect: Stirs the air inside the container the seal is drawn on so that the objects within float and tumble about without disturbing the container itself, while dust and grime are pulled out of the circulating air. The currents are gentle and sputter, so objects bob unevenly and sometimes drop. The cleaning works patchily, and the whole effect fades fairly quickly.

name: s42_00018.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but lumpy and noticeably out of round, bulging at the upper left and flattened along the right. A neat wind sigil, an S-spiral flanked by short dashes, sits at the center and is small to moderate relative to the ring. A Regions sign, an angled two-stroke chevron, sits near the ring at the east-northeast with its point toward the ring, so it points outward. Two Convergence triangles sit partway out, one at the north-northeast and one at the east-southeast, each with a point toward the center. Two very small Mimicry signs sit near the ring, one at the west-northwest, drawn sideways along the ring, and one at the south, drawn slightly rough. Most of the signs cluster on the eastern side, leaving the west and southwest nearly empty.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a spell that moves air, and its modest size gives a moderate intensity. The two inward-pointing Convergence signs focus that air down toward a single point. The single outward-pointing Regions sign makes the magic manifest outside the ring on its side, so the focused air is released toward the east-northeast. The signs are unbalanced, with most weight on that side, which reinforces the lean in that direction. Mimicry guides or imitates the movements of a target. No decorative sigil is present, so here it would make the moving air follow or copy a target's motion. Both Mimicry signs are tiny, and one is rough, so that imitation is weak. Direction, focus and imitation are compatible kinds of modifier and do not conflict. However, the out-of-round ring weakens the whole seal and makes its effect short-lived.
effect: Draws air into a tight, focused gust and sends it out from the seal toward one side, where it loosely follows the movements of its target. The tracking is faint and lags behind the target. The gust itself flickers and gives out after only a brief moment.

name: s42_00019.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, drawn in black line. The ring is open, with a wide gap along the west side, and is slightly lumpy but close to round. A fire sigil sits at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Collection signs sit at the north and south points, each with its barred end toward the ring and its open side facing the center. A sideways Reflection sign sits at the east-northeast near the ring. A Projection sign, a bracket shape with its open side toward the ring, sits at the northeast between the sigil and the Reflection sign. A small Envelopment sign sits at the northwest. A Gathering sign at the west-southwest points inward toward the center. A small Pulling sign at the east-southeast has its arrow pointing inward. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. The two Collection signs face inward in their usual orientation and gather material above and around the seal. The inward-pointing Gathering sign actively draws in surrounding material, and the inward Pulling sign pulls it toward the seal. Because the Pulling sign is drawn small, that pull is weak. Together these three signs feed heat and flame into the spell. The Envelopment sign makes the effect surround its target. Reflection targets an image reflected on the surface the seal is drawn on, and Projection casts that image outward. The signs fall into three related groups: drawing in, enveloping, and reflecting and projecting. They do not contradict one another, and the even spacing gives no single direction. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: The spell does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it would draw nearby heat and flame into the seal and wrap them around its target at moderate strength. It would also cast outward a fiery image of whatever is reflected on the surface the seal is drawn on.

name: s42_00020.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring. On the left is a light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes. On the right is a wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes. Three Purification signs, each a small curl with its top toward the center, sit about halfway between the center and the ring. One is at the north, one at the east-southeast and one at the west-southwest, spaced evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The seal has two sigils. The light sigil creates light that diminishes over time. The wind sigil moves and manipulates existing air but does not create it. Both are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is modest. Purification normally separates waste from water. Paired with a wind sigil, it reads as separating dust and impurities from the air being moved. Purification is asymmetric, so its exact behavior is less predictable than that of symmetric signs. Still, all three copies are drawn the same way and evenly spaced, so the effect is balanced and favors no direction. Only one kind of modifier is present, nothing contradicts, and the neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds.
effect: Stirs a gentle current of air through the area around the seal and strips dust and impurities out of it, leaving the air cleaner. A soft glow accompanies the current and lights up the drifting motes as they are separated out, then slowly dims over time.

name: s42_00021.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed and neatly drawn, though slightly uneven in outline. A small wind sigil sits at the center. Five Entwining signs are spaced evenly just inside the ring at the north, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest and west-northwest positions. Four have their tops toward the ring, while the north one is turned at an angle. Two small sub-seals sit inside the main ring, each holding an earth sigil that is large relative to its own small ring. The north-northeast sub-seal is ring closed and a little rough. The south-southwest sub-seal is ring open, with a gap on its lower left, and its earth sigil is fainter and also a little rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the main spell moves and manipulates air. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Entwining makes an effect wrap itself around other objects. With five of them balanced around the ring, the moving air coils around nearby objects evenly from all sides rather than pushing in one direction. The angled north sign does not break this balance. The closed north-northeast sub-seal is a small earth spell that adds manipulation of solid matter such as soil and sand. Its sigil is strong for its ring, but the sub-seal is tiny and roughly drawn, so its contribution is weak and short-lived. The south-southwest sub-seal is ring open, so it does not activate and adds nothing. Wind, Entwining and earth work together without contradiction, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Raises modest currents of air that wind around nearby objects and wrap them from every side. A thin trace of soil or sand is drawn along with the coiling wind, but it thins out and drops away well before the wind itself fades.

name: s42_00022.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil sits at the center at moderate size relative to the ring, its strokes a little rough. Six Dancing Puppets signs sit evenly in the band between the two rings, at the north-northwest, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and west-northwest. Five face the same way. The one at east-northeast is turned the other way round and drawn in a heavier, darker line. Inside the inner ring at the west-northwest sits a small sub-seal with its ring open, a gap on its lower right side. It holds a fire sigil that fills more than half of that small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Its slightly rough strokes make the spell somewhat weaker and shorter lived. Dancing Puppets lets the movement of a target be consciously manipulated. With water as the element, the controlled material is water rather than air. Six of them evenly spaced add no single direction, so the control is free-ranging and steered rather than pushed one way. One Dancing Puppets is turned around. That sign has never been seen inverted, so its effect is unknown, and with five normal signs balancing it, the normal reading dominates. The fire sub-seal has its ring open, so it does not activate and adds nothing. If it were closed, its large sigil within such a small ring would add a concentrated burst of heat, which would work against the water. Only one kind of modifier is active, so the seal holds together.
effect: Raises water that can be steered and made to dart about through the air from a distance, its movements free and lively rather than fixed in one direction. The control is somewhat short lived and loosens before long. The small fire portion stays inert. If it were activated, it would add a sharp pocket of heat that would partly boil or fight the moving water.

name: s42_00023.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Purification sign, a hooked curl, sits at the center in place of a sigil, moderate in size relative to the ring. Two hourglass-shaped Reflection signs sit near the ring, one at the west and one at the north-northeast; the north-northeast one is slightly rougher. A Sights Set sign sits at the east, its diamond end toward the center and its arrow pointing outward toward the ring. Two small closed sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the north-northeast holds a neatly drawn water sigil that fills about half its ring. The one at the south-southwest holds a roughly drawn earth sigil. More of the seal's content sits toward the north-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: Purification is a sign, but here it takes the central position as the core of the seal. It separates waste from water. Because it is asymmetric, its behavior is less predictable than a symmetric sign's. The water sub-seal supplies the water for that core to act on. Its sigil is large relative to its own ring, so this part is the strongest. The earth sub-seal adds control over solid matter, which suits the grit and sediment that purification pulls out. It is small and roughly drawn, though, so that part is weaker and shorter lived. The Reflection signs target the reflected image on a surface, tying the effect to a reflective water surface. Sights Set lets the caster aim the spell at a chosen target. The modifiers do not contradict each other. The water sub-seal and one Reflection sit on the north-northeast side, so the effect favors that direction.
effect: Cleanses a body of water that the caster aims at. It acts most strongly on the side nearest its strongest part and begins at the still, reflective surface. Silt and grit are pulled out of the water and gathered as sediment. The clearing spreads unevenly, and the sediment drops out patchily before the gathering fades early.

name: s42_00024.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil sits at the center: a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, of moderate size relative to the ring. Six Collection signs are spaced around the seal at roughly two-thirds of the way out from the center. Three of them, at the northwest, east and south-southwest, are drawn in the usual orientation with their open side facing the center. The other three, at the north-northeast, southeast and west, are inverted, with their open side turned toward the ring. Normal and inverted signs roughly alternate around the circle. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a fair, middling intensity. Collection gathers material above and around the seal so the spell can use it, which here means drawing in surrounding light. Its open side normally faces inward. Three of the signs are inverted, and an inverted modifier produces the opposite of its usual effect, so those three would scatter or release material outward instead of gathering it. The gathering and scattering signs are equal in number and alternate around the ring. That is a direct contradiction, and neither side dominates. The light sigil still sets the element, but how the light is handled pulls both ways at once, so the result is likely unstable. The even spacing means the conflict has no favored direction and plays out all around the seal.
effect: Draws in surrounding light toward the seal while pushing it back out at the same time. The glow builds and scatters in uneven pulses, brightening near the seal on some sides while light is flung away on others. It flickers rather than holding a steady brightness, and it fades over time like any light the seal produces.

name: s42_00025.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. It has two concentric rings, both closed, with the outer one slightly rough. The center of the inner ring is empty. Four Cooling signs, each a vertical stroke flanked by dots, sit in the band between the rings. They are at the west-northwest, north-northeast, east-southeast and south-southwest points, evenly spaced, with their tops toward the outer ring. The west-northwest and south-southwest ones are a little rougher than the other two. Inside the inner ring are three small sub-seals, each with its own closed ring. A light sigil sits in the one at the northwest, a wind sigil in the one at the east, and a fire sigil in the one at the south-southwest. The fire sub-seal and its sigil are slightly rough. Each sigil fills about half of its sub-seal's radius. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no central sigil, so its three sub-seals supply the elements. Each sub-seal is closed and has a sigil of moderate size relative to its own ring, so each gives a moderate effect. Light creates a glow that diminishes over time. Wind moves existing air without creating it. Fire produces flame and heat. The four balanced Cooling signs act on the whole seal and chill its output evenly in all directions. Cooling directly contradicts the heat of the fire sub-seal. The four Cooling signs outweigh the single, slightly rough fire sub-seal, so cooling dominates and the moving air comes out chilled. The neatly drawn wind and light parts hold steady. The fire's heat keeps pushing against the chill, so that part of the result is likely unstable. The slightly rough outer ring and two rough Cooling signs make the overall effect a little weaker and shorter lived.
effect: Sends a steady, cool breeze through the surrounding area, accompanied by a soft glow that gradually dims. Small flames and pockets of warmth sputter up unevenly and are quickly smothered by the chill. The whole effect fades somewhat sooner than expected.

name: s42_00026.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, main ring closed and neatly drawn. A Pulling sign sits at the center with no element sigil, its arrow pointing south, small to moderate relative to the ring. Six Link signs sit just inside the ring at the north-northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest positions. Those at the east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest have their tops toward the ring. The east-northeast one has its top toward the center, and the north-northeast one is turned roughly upside down, so both read as inverted. A Reflection sign, an hourglass shape, sits near the ring at the north-northwest with its top toward the ring. Two small closed sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the west-northwest holds a Rain sign at its center. The one at the east-southeast holds an earth sigil at its center. Both sub-seals are small relative to the main ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The only element is the earth sigil in the east-southeast sub-seal, so the spell works on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its small sub-seal limits the intensity. The Rain sub-seal summons its target, making material come down from above. Pulling takes the central core in place of a sigil and draws targets toward the seal. Its arrow points south, which biases that pull along the north-south line toward the southern side. Link identifies pieces broken off from, or made from, the same source and links them. Link is likely semi-directional, so the two inverted Links would work against the four upright ones and loosen or break those connections. This is a direct contradiction. The upright Links outnumber the inverted ones, so linking dominates, but not cleanly. Reflection targets a reflected image, which has no clear role alongside earth and pulling. Together the seal stacks pulling, linking, summoning and reflection, which are four unrelated kinds of modifier. Earth, Pulling and the upright Links dominate, Rain is secondary, and Reflection is the least predictable part. The result is likely unstable.
effect: Calls down fragments of stone or soil that came from a common source and pulls them in toward the seal, mostly toward its southern side, with modest force. The links between pieces hold for some fragments and snap for others, so the material arrives in uneven clumps rather than as one gathered mass. The pull sometimes latches onto mirrored or reflected images of the fragments instead of the fragments themselves, so the gathering falters and often stops before it finishes.

name: s42_00027.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, outer ring closed and neatly drawn. A Pointing sign sits at the center in place of a sigil, at moderate size relative to the ring. Six Projection signs, each a flat bracket with its open side facing the center, are spaced evenly just inside the ring at roughly the east, south-southeast, southwest, west-northwest, north-northwest and northeast positions. Two small sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the east-southeast has its ring open on its right side and holds a Binding sign at its center, both neatly drawn. The one at the west-northwest has a roughly drawn, wobbly ring that is open at its upper right, with a small, roughly drawn water sigil at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no element sigil. Pointing takes the center as its core and makes the target manifest in a conical shape that other signs then direct. The six Projection signs push the effect outward from the seal. Because they are evenly balanced, no direction is favored, so the cones are cast out on all sides. These two modifiers work together without contradiction. The main ring is closed and neat, so the main seal activates. Both sub-seals have open rings, so neither activates as drawn. If closed, the water sub-seal would supply water to the spell, but its rough drawing and small sigil would make that supply weak and short-lived. The Binding sub-seal would hold the material together so it moves as a single unit. Without the sub-seals, the main seal has no element of its own and works on whatever material is directed into it.
effect: Shapes any material directed into the seal into cone-shaped points and casts them outward evenly in every direction. The two smaller inner seals do not activate. If closed, they would supply a thin, faltering trickle of water that runs dry quickly and bind it into solid-moving cones, sending out a sparse, short-lived spray of water spikes.

name: s42_00028.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is hand-drawn and slightly uneven in places but stays essentially round. A Collection sign, an X-shaped hourglass figure with a bar across its top, sits at the center in place of a sigil and is fairly large relative to the ring. Four Convergence triangles sit about three quarters of the way out toward the ring, at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast and west-southwest positions. Each has its flat side toward the ring and a point facing inward toward the center. The east-northeast triangle is drawn a little more roughly than the others. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Collection sign at the center acts as the core of the seal. Collection gathers material located above and around the seal so the spell can use it, and its fairly large size gives that gathering a strong pull. The four Convergence signs point inward in their usual orientation. They focus the magic down to a single point and make loose particles pack tightly together and become somewhat rigid. The triangles are evenly spaced, so the gathering favors no direction. Because no element is named, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and acts on whatever loose material is nearby. The two kinds of modifier reinforce each other. The slightly rougher east-northeast triangle only weakens that one side a little.
effect: Draws loose material from above and around the seal and packs it into a single dense, rigid clump at its center. It works on whatever loose matter is close by. Material drawn in from the east-northeast side packs slightly less firmly than the rest.

name: s42_00029.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both neatly drawn. Both rings are open: the outer ring has a wide gap at the upper right, and the inner ring has a gap across the top, from roughly north-northwest to north-northeast. A Dispersion sign sits at the center in place of a sigil, moderately large relative to the ring, with its stem pointing north and its curve facing south. There is no element sigil. An Orb sign, a circle crossed by a diagonal line, sits at the north-northeast near the outer edge, beside the outer ring's gap. A tilted Diamond sign sits inside the inner ring at the east-southeast. A Link sign sits at the south, just inside the inner ring, with its top toward the ring. A small four-lobed Billow sign sits at the west-southwest, resting on the outer ring line. Most of the signs crowd the eastern and southern half, so the layout leans south-southeast.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Dispersion sign acts as the core. It makes the spell pour its magic outward rather than beam it in one direction, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The spell is tied to no element, so it works on whatever material is present. Orb defines a spherical space where material collects from the bottom up. That directly contradicts Dispersion's outward leak. Billow turns available material into a fluffy cloud. Diamond is thought to limit the effect to objects inside a container without touching the container itself. Link joins pieces that came from the same source. Together these are four unrelated kinds of modifier on top of a contradiction between pouring out and collecting. Dispersion dominates as the core, and Billow and Orb shape what comes out. Diamond and Link are the least predictable parts, so the result is likely unstable. The uneven placement pushes the outflow toward the south-southeast. Both rings are open, so the seal cannot activate until they are closed.
effect: It does not activate while its rings are open. If closed, it would pour nearby material outward at moderate strength, drifting mostly toward the south-southeast. Some of that material would puff into soft cloud while some pools in a sphere above the seal, and the flow would waver between spreading out and collecting. Pieces of the same material would intermittently cling together, and the effect would likely collapse before settling into any steady shape.

name: s42_00030.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background with two concentric rings, both open. Each ring has a gap toward the lower left, and both rings are wobbly and noticeably out of round. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, neatly drawn and of moderate size relative to the inner ring. Five small Windows signs, each a circle lined with slanted hatch marks, sit about halfway between the center and the inner ring. They are at the northwest, northeast, southwest, southeast, and east-southeast positions. The east-southeast one is drawn heavier and darker than the others. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and manipulates flame or heat. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a fair intensity. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined, so magic can pass through the seal from one location to another. Here it is drawn as five separate small rings instead of one lining band. Read that way, each one opens its own small passage. The five signs are spread around the seal, so no single direction is favored. They are all the same kind of modifier, so nothing in the seal contradicts itself. Both rings are open, so the seal will not activate until they are closed. Even once closed, the rough, out-of-round rings and the slightly messy hand on most of the Windows signs would make any effect weak and short-lived, and the seal might fail to catch at all.
effect: It does not activate while its rings are open. If closed, it would carry fire or heat through several small passages, letting flame drawn at the seal appear at other locations as though through tiny portals. The passages would flicker open only briefly and unevenly, with the flame sputtering through some of them and fading before it could hold.

name: s42_00031.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. Two rings, both closed and somewhat lumpy rather than truly round: an outer ring with a second ring just inside it. A roughly drawn earth sigil sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Dispersion signs sit on the inner ring. Those at the north-northwest and southwest have their stems toward the ring and their curves toward the center. Those at the east and west are rotated at odd angles. Two roughly drawn Gathering signs sit on the inner ring at the northeast and south, each with its arrowhead pointing outward toward the ring. Three small sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the north-northeast holds a small fire sigil, and its ring is open with a gap on its lower left. The one at the southeast holds a fire sigil, and its ring is closed. The one at the west-southwest holds a Stability and Level Planes sign at its center, and its ring is closed. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell moves existing solid matter such as soil, sand and stone, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The Gathering signs let the spell draw material in from its surroundings, which supplies the earth it works on. The Dispersion signs pour the magic outward instead of beaming it in one direction. They are spread evenly around the ring, so the gathered earth is pushed out on all sides. The southeast sub-seal has a closed ring, so it activates and adds a small fire effect that warms the earth. Its sigil is small, so the heat is mild. The north-northeast fire sub-seal has an open ring and does not activate, so it adds nothing. The west-southwest sub-seal uses Stability and Level Planes as its core, which keeps the affected material balanced in a level plane. Gathering inward and dispersing outward work in sequence rather than against each other, so the seal is not contradictory. However, the rough strokes and rings that are not round enough make the spell weaker and shorter lived, and it may only flicker into effect.
effect: Draws in loose soil and stone from the surroundings and spreads it outward on all sides as a level, mildly warm layer. The effect is weak and brief: the spreading thins unevenly from side to side, the warmth comes and goes, and the layer settles and loses its level shape soon after forming.

name: s42_00032.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed but roughly drawn and lumpy, noticeably less than round. An Expansion sign sits upright at the center, small relative to the ring, its nested corner brackets pointing outward. Four Binding signs, each a pair of stacked arcs, sit about two thirds of the way out at the northwest, north-northeast, southeast and south-southwest, each with its top turned toward the center. Two small, roughly drawn Coil signs sit near the ring at the east-northeast and west-southwest, each rotated at a slant. The signs are evenly balanced around the ring. Three small sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The one at the southeast is neatly drawn with its ring closed and holds an earth sigil filling about half of it. The one at the west-southwest has a slightly rough closed ring and holds a roughly drawn fire sigil. The one at the north-northeast holds a neat fire sigil, but its ring is open, with a gap on its left side.
justification: With no element sigil in the main ring, the Expansion sign at the center acts as the core. Its corners point outward, so it makes its target grow. The linked sub-seals supply the elements. The closed earth sub-seal ties the spell to solid matter such as stone and soil. The closed fire sub-seal adds heat, and its rough sigil makes that heat weaker. The north-northeast fire sub-seal has an open ring, so it does not activate and adds nothing until it is closed. Coil softens physical matter. Binding halts the target's movement and holds it together as a single unit. The modifiers are swelling, softening and binding, all acting on solid matter, and they do not contradict one another. However, the main ring is rough and lumpy rather than round. That makes the effect fleeting and may keep the spell from activating at all. The rough drawing of most signs also weakens the result and shortens how long it lasts.
effect: Softens and warms a mass of stone or soil, holds it together as one lump and makes it swell outward. The swelling is weak and patchy, and the softened mass sags back and stiffens again after only a moment. Sometimes the spell fails to take hold at all. The second source of heat does not activate; if its ring were closed, the mass would grow hotter and soften further.

name: s42_00033.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed and neatly drawn. A Collection sign sits upright at the center, small relative to the ring, and there is no element sigil in the main ring. Two Link signs sit just inside the ring, one at the west-northwest and one at the east-southeast, facing each other across the seal. Eight Purification signs fill the rest of the space. Two sit near the ring, at the northeast and southwest. The other six form a loose circle about halfway out, at the west, north-northwest, northeast, east, south-southeast and southwest. The inner northeast one is drawn darker and thicker than the others. Two small sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The one at the northeast has a closed ring and holds a fire sigil that fills about half of it. The one at the southwest holds an earth sigil of similar relative size, and its ring is open, with a gap at the lower right. The signs are evenly spread around the main ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil in the main ring, the Collection sign at the center acts as the core. It gathers material above and around the seal so the spell can use it. The eight Purification signs separate waste from water. Their number makes cleansing the dominant behavior, applied evenly on all sides. Purification is asymmetric, so exactly how it acts on material other than water is uncertain. The two opposed Link signs identify pieces that broke off from, or came from, the same source and keep them connected. That way the cleaned material holds together as a whole. The closed fire sub-seal, joined by a line, feeds heat into the main spell. Its fairly large sigil gives that heat solid strength. The earth sub-seal is also joined, but its ring is open, so it contributes nothing until it is closed. Once closed, it would extend the spell to solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Only three kinds of modifier are present, and they work toward the same goal without contradiction, so the seal is stable. The one rougher Purification sign slightly weakens the cleansing on that side.
effect: Draws in water and loose material from around the seal, strips the waste out of it, and keeps the cleaned portions that came from the same source bound together, warming them as it works. The cleansing is a little weaker and less thorough on the northeast side. The attached earth portion does not activate; if closed, the spell would also gather and clean stone, sand and soil.

name: s42_00034.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but lumpy and uneven, noticeably not round. A water sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large, about half the ring's radius. Four Strengthening signs, each a triangle with a crossbar, surround it. Two large, heavily drawn ones sit at the north-northeast and south-southwest, each with its apex pointing in toward the center. Two much smaller ones sit near the ring at the east and west, each with its apex pointing outward toward the ring. The signs are evenly spread around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Strengthening makes its target harder, firmer and more durable. It behaves as a semi-directional sign, so its direction does not steer the spell, but facing outward inverts it and reverses its effect. The two large inward-facing signs harden and reinforce the water. The two small outward-facing signs are inverted and would weaken it instead. These directly contradict each other. The larger, bolder inward pair dominates, so the water still firms up overall, but the opposing pair pulls against it and the result is likely unstable. Because the signs are balanced around the ring, no direction is favored. The ring is closed, so the spell activates, but its lumpy, poorly rounded shape makes the effect short-lived.
effect: Gathers a fairly large mass of water and firms it into a dense, durable body that holds together more like a solid than a liquid. Its firmness wavers as it lasts, with patches going soft and sloshing loose before hardening again. The whole mass slackens back into ordinary water after only a short time.

name: s42_00035.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. It is neatly drawn, and the ring is open, with a gap near the top just west of north. Two small glyphs sit side by side at the center. On the left is an Orb sign, a circle crossed by a vertical stroke, with a small Collection sign attached to its top. On the right is a light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, drawn symmetrically. Four Immobility signs sit near the ring at the north, south, west-northwest and east-southeast, each with its bar toward the ring and its curves facing the center. An Entwining sign sits at the northeast, angled across the band. At the southwest is a slightly rough Entwining sign with a small earth sigil fused to its base. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Reading the right half as mirrored onto the left is a guess, but the result keeps the light sigil's usual function. The Orb sign defines a spherical space above the seal where the spell's material collects. The attached Collection is read as feeding that space, which is also a guess, so the light is gathered into a sphere rather than added by hand. The four Immobility signs are evenly spread and make the effect immovable relative to the seal, holding its shape as if frozen. Entwining makes the effect wrap itself around other objects. The southwest variant with an earth sigil is read as Entwining that clings specifically to solid matter, another guess. Because that glyph is a little rough, its grip is weaker than the neat Entwining opposite it. The modifiers do not contradict one another and the signs are balanced, so the seal is not unstable. Because the ring is open, the spell does not activate.
effect: It does not activate while the ring stays open. If closed, it would gather light into a modest glowing sphere held rigidly in place above the seal, with soft tendrils that wrap around nearby objects. The tendrils cling to solid things such as stone or wood, but their hold on one side is looser and slips more easily. The light slowly dims over time.

name: s42_00036.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Three Gathering signs sit inside the inner ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast and south-southeast positions, roughly evenly spaced. Each is turned to a different angle, and their arrowheads all point roughly the same way around the ring rather than straight toward the center. A single small Partition sign sits in the band between the two rings at the west point, its peaked top facing the outer ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size gives the effect moderate strength. The second ring adds strength and room for further effects. Gathering lets a spell draw material in from its surroundings to build its effect, so here the spell pulls in ambient light. The three signs are evenly spaced, so they draw from all sides. Because their arrows all point the same way around the ring, the light may swirl as it gathers, though this reading is a guess. Partition outlines the border of an area of effect that extends outward and upward. Its place in the outer band frames the space where the gathered light settles. Since there is only one Partition sign, the boundary may be firmer on the west side. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not conflict, so the seal is steady.
effect: Draws in surrounding light from every side and collects it into a glowing, bounded space above the seal. The light may drift in a gentle swirl as it gathers. The glow is moderately bright and holds within its borders, then slowly dims over time.

name: s42_00037.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Rain sign sits upright at the center with no element sigil inside it, and it is small relative to the ring. Six Stretch signs sit in the band between the two rings. Four of them, at the east-northeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and north-northwest, have the top of their arch toward the center. The other two, at the east-southeast and west-northwest, are flipped so the top of their arch faces the outer ring. The west-southwest Stretch is a little rough, and the rest are neat. Inside the inner ring are two small closed sub-seals. One at the west-northwest holds an upright Refuse sign, drawn a little roughly. One at the east-southeast holds an upright Envelopment sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Rain sign at the center is the core of the seal. Rain summons a target material, bringing it down from above, so the spell is tied to whatever material is in reach rather than to one element. Its small size gives it a modest strength. The second ring adds more effect and power to the core. The Stretch signs ring the seal and turn solid matter that touches it into long, flexible ribbons. Stretch is thought to be non-directional, so the two flipped signs should act the same as the other four. That keeps the effect even, and with the signs balanced around the ring, no side is favored. The Refuse sub-seal is a directional sign. Drawn upright, it collects unwanted material and waste toward the top of the seal, away from the useful material. The Envelopment sub-seal makes the effect wrap around whatever it targets. Rain sets the core, with Stretch, Refuse and Envelopment as three modifiers that support each other without contradiction, so the seal is not unstable. The slightly rough Stretch and Refuse signs weaken those parts a little.
effect: Draws down nearby material from above in a modest shower. Any solid matter that reaches the seal is spun into long, flexible ribbons that wrap around the target. Debris and waste in the material are sorted off toward the top of the seal, though a little grit slips through, and the ribbons on the west-southwest side form slightly thinner and give out sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00038.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The second ring sits just inside the first. A Link sign sits upright at the center, drawn fairly large relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Eight Aeriforms Defined signs, each made of three short strokes, are evenly spaced about halfway between the center and the inner ring. They sit at the north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west and northwest points, and all are oriented the same way, with the top of each glyph toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Link sign at the center serves as the core of the spell. Link identifies objects that were broken off from, removed from, or made from the same source and creates a link between them. Its fairly large size gives the core a strong presence. Aeriforms Defined has the same design as the strokes on the wind sigil and shares a name with the aeriforms sigil, which creates air. Here it is read as defining or giving form to air around the linked targets, though its exact function is uncertain. The eight signs are balanced and uniformly oriented, so no direction is favored and the effect acts evenly on all sides. The second ring adds strength and steadiness to the core spell. Only two kinds of glyph are present, and they do not contradict each other.
effect: Finds objects that came from the same source and joins them with shaped air, so the pieces stay connected to one another across the space between them, as if held by an invisible tether of air. The hold is even on all sides and stays steady while the spell lasts.

name: s42_00039.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. It has two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Collection sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, moderate in size relative to the ring. No element sigil is present. Three Refuse signs sit about two-thirds of the way out, at the northwest, east-northeast and west-southwest, each with its diamond end pointing toward the center. Three Envelopment signs sit at a similar distance. The one at the south faces the ring. The one at the east-southeast faces the center, and the one at the west-northwest faces the ring. The east-southeast and west-northwest Envelopment signs are drawn a little rougher and heavier than the rest. At the north-northeast is a hooked glyph that matches no known sign exactly; it resembles an Envelopment sign made symmetric by mirroring one half onto the other, and it faces the ring. The signs are spread evenly around the seal. Outside the outer ring at the south-southeast, a short line joins a small closed sub-seal holding a single Expansion sign at its center, drawn large within it with its corners pointing outward. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Collection takes the central role. It gathers material from above and around the seal for the spell to use, so the spell is not tied to one element. The three Refuse signs point inward, and Refuse draws unwanted material and waste toward where it points, so they steer debris toward the central Collection. These two gathering signs reinforce each other. Envelopment makes the effect surround its target, so the gathered material is wrapped in an enclosing layer. The mixed inward and outward facing of the Envelopment signs suggests the wrapping closes from both sides. The north-northeast glyph is closest to Envelopment; reading it that way is a guess, and its mirrored, symmetric form would add an even share of the same wrapping. The two rougher Envelopment signs weaken the wrapping slightly on their sides. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. The linked sub-seal applies Expansion with its corners pointing outward, which makes the target grow. Because the sub-seal is small relative to the main ring, the growth is moderate. Gathering, wrapping and enlarging work together without contradiction, and the signs are balanced, so the seal is stable.
effect: Draws loose waste and debris from all around the seal into a single mass at its center and wraps that mass in an enclosing shell. It then swells the wrapped bundle to a moderately larger size. The shell holds firmly overall but is slightly thinner on its east-southeast and west-northwest sides, where it can sag or leak small bits of debris.

name: s42_00040.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Coil sign, two crossing curved strokes forming a long lens shape, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil and is moderately large relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Seven signs surround it: a Sights Set sign at the northeast with its arrow pointing out toward the ring; a Stability and Level Planes sign at the east-northeast; a small Crosshair at the east-southeast; a Concealment sign, the eight-armed star with eye marks, just west of south; a Glaives sign at the west-southwest, lying on its side with its prongs toward the ring; a Selection sign at the west-northwest; and an inverted Rain sign at the north-northwest. The Sights Set and Rain signs are slightly rougher than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
