justification: With no element sigil, Coil takes the center and sets the core behavior: softening physical matter. It affects only solids and has no effect on liquids or gases. Its moderate size gives a moderate strength. Sights Set and Crosshair both direct the effect at a chosen target. Selection does the opposite and confines the effect to the object the seal is drawn on, which contradicts that aiming. Inverted Rain creates a zone that pushes its target away. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds into flesh, which pulls against that repulsion. Stability and Level Planes holds the target balanced on a level plane, and Concealment hides it. That is far more than three unrelated kinds of modifier, with two direct contradictions. Coil dominates as the core, the paired aiming signs set the main direction, and the Glaives and Stability signs, drawn neatly, add depth and balance. Selection, Concealment and the slightly rough Rain and Sights Set signs are the weakest and least predictable parts. The result is likely unstable.
effect: Softens solid matter at an aimed target and works partway into living flesh, while trying to hold the softened target level and partly hidden from view. The aim wavers between the chosen target and the surface the seal is drawn on, so the softening lands unevenly. The target is pushed away in fits instead of being held, and the concealment flickers on and off before the effect breaks down early.

name: s42_00041.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four spokes, sits upright at the center and reaches about half the ring's radius. Its lines are slightly rough. Five Pulling signs have their arrowheads pointing inward toward the center. Four sit near the ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest. A fifth, drawn bolder, sits closer in at the west. Three Expansion signs, each made of nested corner brackets with corners pointing outward in their normal orientation, sit near the ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast and south-southeast. The east-northeast one is drawn heavier. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect, though its slightly rough lines weaken it a little. Pulling signs with arrows pointing inward draw the target toward the seal. Here five of them, spread around the ring, pull light in from all sides. The fifth Pulling sign at the west sits closer in, but the signs are balanced overall, so no side clearly dominates. Expansion is semi-directional. With its corners pointing outward in normal orientation, it makes the target grow. Only two kinds of modifier are present, gathering and enlarging, and they complement each other rather than conflict. The ring is closed, so the seal activates.
effect: Draws surrounding light in toward the seal from all sides and swells it into a large, bright, growing mass of light gathered over the seal. The glow is strong but slightly uneven along its edges, and it dims and fades somewhat sooner than its brightness suggests.

name: s42_00042.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Concealment sign sits upright at the center of the inner ring: an eight-armed star with an eye mark at each of its north, east, south, and west ends. There is no element sigil. Three small Reflection signs, each an hourglass shape, sit in the band between the two rings. One is at the north, slightly east of true north. One is at the southeast and one at the west-southwest. All three are drawn with their tops toward the center. The north sign is crisp, while the southeast and west-southwest signs are slightly rougher. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Concealment sign is the core of the seal, so the spell hides its target. Reflection works on the reflected image found on the object the seal is drawn on. Placed with Concealment, it makes the hiding draw on that reflection, so the object takes on the look of what its surface reflects. The second ring holds the Reflection signs and adds strength to the core spell. The three signs are evenly spaced and point the same way, so no side is favored and the effect spreads evenly. Only one kind of modifier supports the core, so nothing conflicts. The slight roughness of two Reflection signs makes the reflected part a little weaker on those sides.
effect: Hides the object it is drawn on by covering it in the reflections caught on its own surface, so it blends into its surroundings like a mirror. The concealment holds steadily over most of the object, but now and then faint patches waver and briefly show the object's true surface where the reflection takes hold less cleanly.

name: s42_00043.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the lower left between the southwest and the south. There is no element sigil. An upright Entwining sign sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Crosshair signs, each drawn as a small X, sit about three quarters of the way out at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest points. A single Coil sign sits close to the ring at the north. The signs lean toward the north because the Coil has no partner on the other side.
justification: With no element sigil, the Entwining sign at the center sets the core of the spell. It makes the object the seal is drawn on wrap itself around other objects. Its moderate size gives a moderate strength. Coil softens solid matter, so the object becomes pliable enough to wrap. Coil is likely non-directional, so its orientation does not matter, but as the only sign at the north it tilts the softening toward that side. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. Four evenly spaced Crosshairs aim the wrapping at separate points on the diagonals around the seal. These three kinds of modifier work together without contradiction. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Does not activate while the ring is open. If it were closed, it would soften the object it is drawn on into a pliable, rope-like state and make it wind itself around targets at four diagonal points around it. The softening would be strongest along the northern edge.

name: s42_00044.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. It has two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn, with a band between them. A Detection sign, three vertical strokes of increasing height, sits at the center of the inner ring at moderate size. Four Cooling signs sit in the outer band at the north, east-northeast, south and west-northwest, each rotated differently. The east-northeast and west-northwest ones are slightly rougher than the others. An Immobility sign sits in the band at the west, turned with its top toward the center. Inside the inner ring are two small closed sub-seals. The northern one holds a wind sigil at about half its ring's size, and the southern one holds a four-lobed Billow sign in place of a sigil. The outer signs cluster more on the northwest side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no element sigil, so the central Detection sign is its core. Its exact function is unclear, but it presumably senses a presence and triggers or guides the rest of the spell. The wind sub-seal supplies movement of air, and its small size gives a modest strength. The Billow sub-seal turns available material into a fluffy cloud, so the air moved by the wind sub-seal becomes cloud. The four Cooling signs chill the result. The two rougher ones cool their sides a little less, so the chill is slightly uneven. Immobility keeps the target fixed in relation to the seal so the cloud holds its shape and place. How its sideways orientation changes this is unknown. The signs are unbalanced toward the northwest, so the effect is weighted to that side. The modifiers are cooling, holding and cloud-forming, which work together without contradiction.
effect: Senses a presence, then stirs nearby air into a soft, chilled cloud that stays fixed in place beside the seal, sitting off toward the northwest. The cloud is cooler on some sides than others, and its overall strength is modest.

name: s42_00045.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. A small Concealment sign sits upright at the center: an eight-armed star with eye marks on its cardinal arms, about a quarter of the ring's radius. Six Crushing signs surround it. Four are in normal orientation, with their tops toward the center. One sits at the north near the ring and is drawn with a heavier, slightly rougher stroke. One sits at the south-southeast near the ring. The other two sit about midway out, at the north-northeast and the south-southwest; the south-southwest one is slightly rough. The remaining two are inverted, with their tops toward the ring, and sit about midway out at the northwest and southeast. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Concealment sign at the center is the core of the spell, so its main purpose is to hide the target. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Crushing is semi-directional. In normal orientation it breaks solid matter into smaller and smaller pieces. When inverted it does the opposite and reforms crushed material into its original shape. Here, four normal Crushing signs directly contradict two inverted ones. The four crushing signs outnumber the two reforming ones, so breaking apart dominates, while the inverted pair keeps pulling material back together. Because the seal works against itself, the result is likely unstable. The even spacing means no direction is favored, so the conflict plays out across the whole target rather than on one side. The two slightly rough signs weaken the crushing a little where they sit.
effect: Hides its target from sight while breaking any solid matter in it down toward fragments and powder. The breaking and reforming fight each other, so pieces crumble, partly snap back together, and crumble again in uneven pulses. The concealment flickers as the matter shifts, letting the target show through in places, and the whole effect tends to fade before the target is fully pulverized or fully hidden.

name: s42_00046.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn. The ring is open, with a wide gap across the upper left between roughly the west-northwest and the north. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center at a modest size relative to the ring. Four Diamond signs sit just inside the ring at the south-southwest, west-northwest, north-northeast and east-southeast, each turned roughly side-on. A single Glaives sign sits near the ring at the east-northeast, its stem slanting from the inside and its three-pronged fork reaching toward the ring. At the north-northwest, inside the main ring, is a small sub-seal with its own closed ring and a small wind sigil at its center. The signs cluster more heavily toward the east-northeast side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light. Its modest size gives a modest intensity, and light from this sigil diminishes over time. Diamond limits a spell to whatever lies inside the container it is drawn on, leaving the container itself untouched. Four of them reinforce that confinement. Glaives sets how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh, so the light sinks into living bodies within that space instead of resting on their surface. The closed wind sub-seal adds a small current of moving air. Its small size and slightly rough drawing make that current weak and short-lived. The uneven placement leans the effect toward the east-northeast, where the Glaives sits, so the embedding is strongest on that side. These three modifiers work together without contradiction. The main ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: The spell does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it fills the contents of whatever it is drawn on with a modest, slowly dimming light that sinks into the flesh of living things inside while leaving the container itself dark. The glow embeds most deeply on one side, and a faint stirring of air drifts the light around at first before that current dies away well ahead of the glow.

name: s42_00047.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed but drawn roughly and noticeably lumpy rather than round. Two small sigils sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring: a light sigil on the left and a wind sigil on the right, both upright and roughly drawn. Three inverted Crushing signs sit near the ring, evenly spaced: one at the north as an M-shaped zigzag, one at the lower right, and one at the lower left, each drawn as a stretched zigzag. All three are drawn somewhat roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil creates and shapes light. The wind sigil moves and manipulates existing air. Their small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Crushing is semi-directional, so its placement does not steer the spell, but inverting it reverses its effect. Instead of breaking things into pieces, inverted Crushing pulls scattered or crushed material back into its original shape, and only for as long as the spell lasts. Crushing is normally used on solids, so its reforming effect on light and moving air is less certain. The three signs are evenly balanced, so the reforming pull acts equally from all sides. There is only one kind of modifier and nothing contradicts, so the seal is not unstable. However, the rough lines make it weaker and shorter lived. The ring is not round enough, so any effect is fleeting, and the seal may fail to activate at all.
effect: Draws scattered light and stirred air back together from all sides into a single faint, drifting glow, briefly holding them in a reformed shape. The glow is dim and uneven and flickers as the gathered air wavers. It falls apart almost at once, scattering back to how it was, and sometimes nothing forms at all.

name: s42_00048.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed. The rings are drawn a little roughly, and the outer one is noticeably lopsided rather than truly round. A small Windows sign sits at the center in place of a sigil: a tiny circle lined with slanted hatch marks inside a second circle. It is small relative to the ring. Four Cooling signs, each a central bar flanked by two pairs of dots, sit about halfway between the center and the inner ring at the north, east, south, and west points. Each is rotated so its bar runs out toward the ring, and the south and west ones are drawn more roughly than the others. No element sigil or other sign is present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Windows sign at the center becomes the core of the seal. It connects two spaces that are not physically joined, so the spell opens a small passage from one location to another. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest effect, so the opening is small. The four Cooling signs cool things down, so whatever passes through the connection is chilled. Because the four are evenly spaced, the cooling works evenly on all sides. These are only two kinds of modifier, and they do not contradict each other. However, the rough strokes and the lopsided outer ring weaken the seal and shorten how long it lasts, and a ring this far from round tends to give only a fleeting effect.
effect: Opens a small passage linking the seal to another place, and anything that passes through it comes out chilled. The connection is weak and does not hold steady. The opening flickers, the cooling comes through unevenly, and the whole effect fades after only a short time.

name: s42_00049.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed and neatly drawn. A large Dispersion sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, with its stem pointing up and its curve below. It spans almost half the ring's radius. Five smaller Dispersion signs sit near the ring at the north, north-northeast, east, south-southeast and west. Each has its stem toward the center and its curve toward the ring. A single Columns sign, drawn in a heavier stroke, sits at the southwest with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing inward. The signs are spread evenly around the ring. Outside the main ring at the northeast, a smaller closed ring is joined to it by a short line. That smaller ring holds a single Entwining sign at its center. There is no element sigil anywhere, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind or light sigil is present, so the spell is not tied to one element and acts on whatever material or magic is fed into it. The large central Dispersion sign takes the core position and sets the main behavior: magic pours out of the seal rather than being beamed in one direction. The five ring-side Dispersion signs share the same orientation and are spaced around the ring, so the outflow spreads on all sides. Columns gives an area of effect shaped like a column and drives magic in a direction. As the only Columns sign, it adds a narrower push of the outflow toward the southwest. The linked sub-seal carries Entwining, which makes affected material wrap itself around other objects, and the line joining it applies that behavior to the main seal's output. Dispersion, Columns and Entwining are three modifiers that do not contradict one another. Both rings are closed and neatly drawn, so the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Material fed into the spell pours out strongly and evenly in every direction, with one denser stream pushed outward toward the southwest. Wherever the outflow reaches nearby objects, it wraps and twines around them instead of simply spilling past.

name: s42_00050.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, made of two concentric rings. The outer ring is open, with a wide gap along the upper left between the west-northwest and north points. The inner ring also appears to break near the upper right. A water sigil sits upright at the center, drawn neatly and fairly large, a little under half the inner radius. Nine Holding signs surround it, each a pair of facing curves with the top of the glyph toward the ring. Three larger ones sit inside the inner ring at the east, south-southwest and northwest. Six smaller ones sit in the band near the outer ring at the north, east-northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest. The signs are spread evenly around the seal. A few on the western and southern side, including the northwest, west-northwest, southwest and east-southeast ones, are drawn a little rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Holding is non-directional. It holds the target in the shape defined by the seal while still letting it move. All nine signs are Holding, so the seal uses a single kind of modifier with no contradiction. Their even spacing favors no direction. With no Columns, Regions or other directional signs, the water stays over the seal rather than being sent outward. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. The rough strokes on a few signs slightly weaken the hold on those sides. The ring is open, so the seal does not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: It does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it gathers a strong body of water over the seal and holds it in a round shape matching the seal. The water still moves and flows inside the form without spilling. Along the western and southern edges the hold is a little looser, so the water there wobbles and bulges slightly.

name: s42_00051.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, with no sigil. Three large Gathering signs sit just inside the ring at the east, south-southwest, and north-northwest positions, roughly evenly spaced. Each has its forked base against the ring and its arrowhead pointing in toward the center. A single, much smaller Pulling sign sits near the ring at the west-southwest. Its arrowhead also points inward toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth, wind, or light, and it acts on whatever loose material is around it. The three Gathering signs let a spell draw material from its surroundings to build its effect. Their arrowheads point inward and they are spaced about evenly, so they draw from all around the seal without favoring a side. Pulling is directional, and with its arrow pointing inward it pulls targets toward the seal. Because only one sits at the west-southwest, it adds a pull from that side and makes the seal lean west. The sign is drawn small, so that extra pull is weak. Gathering and Pulling both bring material inward, so they reinforce each other rather than conflict. No sign gives the collected material a shape or purpose.
effect: Draws loose material from all around the seal inward and collects it on the drawn surface, piling it up without shaping it. Material on the west-southwest side gets an extra, gentler tug, so it arrives from that direction a little sooner and more steadily than from elsewhere.

name: s42_00052.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is small relative to the ring, about a quarter of its radius. Five Crosshair signs surround it, each with its top toward the ring. Four sit close to the ring at the northwest, northeast, southeast, and southwest. A fifth sits at the west, somewhat closer to the center than the others. The northeast Crosshair is drawn a little more roughly than the rest. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, acting on flame and heat. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its shorter ends point at. With five Crosshairs facing outward around the ring, the fire is aimed at several separate points around the seal instead of spreading as a general blaze or rising as a single column. The four intercardinal Crosshairs are evenly spaced. The extra one at the west adds a fifth target on that side, and because it sits closer in, that target is likely nearer the seal. The slightly rough northeast Crosshair is a little weaker than the others, so its target is struck less steadily. Only one kind of modifier is present and nothing contradicts, so the seal is stable.
effect: Sends modest bursts of flame or heat outward to five separate points around the seal: four spread evenly around it and one slightly closer on the west side. The flame aimed to the northeast burns a little weaker and flickers more than the others.

name: s42_00053.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. Two light sigils sit side by side at the center, each a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes. The left one is larger, about a third of the ring's radius. The right one is smaller and drawn a little more roughly. Six Detection signs, each three short parallel strokes of increasing length, sit in the band between the two rings. They are at the south-southwest, west, north-northwest, northeast, east and south-southeast positions, each with its top toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: Both sigils are light, so this is a light spell. The larger sigil gives a moderate intensity, and the smaller, rougher one adds a weaker, less steady second source of light. The second ring adds strength and further effect to the core spell. Detection works by sensing presence around the seal; it is the sensing component of light paths that respond to whoever approaches. Six of them evenly spaced in the outer band give the seal awareness in every direction rather than favoring one side. A single kind of modifier works together with the sigils, so nothing contradicts and the seal holds steady.
effect: Produces light that responds to presences sensed anywhere around the seal, glowing when something comes near from any direction. The light comes from two sources: one moderately bright and steady, the other dimmer and slightly uneven. Both gradually fade over time.

name: s42_00054.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes on either side, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Seven four-lobed Billow signs surround it in two groups. Three larger ones sit near the ring at the west-northwest, east-northeast and south. Four smaller ones sit about halfway out, at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates air but does not create it. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Billow is a non-directional sign that turns available material into a fluffy cloud, and its orientation does not change its effect. Seven Billow signs strengthen that conversion. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, so no side is favored. With no Collection or Gathering signs, the spell does not actively pull material in from far away. It works on whatever the moving air already carries near the seal. The seal uses only one kind of modifier, so nothing contradicts and the spell holds steady.
effect: Stirs the surrounding air with considerable force and gathers whatever it carries, such as dust, mist or vapor, into soft, fluffy clouds. The clouds billow up evenly on all sides of the seal rather than drifting in any one direction.

name: s42_00055.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Crosshair sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, its four separated strokes pointing north, east, south and west, and it is fairly large relative to the ring. Four Link signs sit near the ring at the north-northwest, northeast, east-southeast and west-northwest positions, each with its top toward the ring. A Holding sign, a pair of facing curves with dots, sits near the ring at the south-southwest with its top toward the center. A second, smaller Holding sign sits closer in at the west-southwest, turned on its side. There is no element sigil. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Crosshair acts as the core and makes the seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. Its four arms point evenly in the four cardinal directions, so targets are picked out on all sides rather than one. Its fairly large size gives the effect reasonable strength. The four Link signs identify objects that broke off from, or were made from, the same source and tie them together. The two Holding signs are non-directional, so their orientation does not change their effect. They hold the target in the shape set by the seal while still letting it move. Linking and holding work together without contradiction, and only these two kinds of modifier are present, so the seal is stable. Because there is no element sigil, the spell is not bound to fire, water, earth or wind and works on whatever material it targets.
effect: Picks out objects around the seal that share a common source and links them together. It holds them in a fixed arrangement that can still be moved as a whole. The hold is steady and lasts as long as the magic does.

name: s42_00056.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but noticeably lumpy and uneven, bulging and flattening in places rather than forming a true circle. Two sigils sit side by side near the center, both small relative to the ring: a wind sigil on the left and an earth sigil on the right. Six Expansion signs, each made of nested corner brackets, are spaced around the ring. Four point their corners outward, at the northeast, south-southeast, southwest, and west; the southwest one is drawn larger than the rest. Two are inverted with their corners pointing inward, at the north and east, sitting slightly closer to the center than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets solid matter such as stone, sand, and soil as a target. The wind sigil adds the movement of air, so the spell acts on solids and also stirs the air around them. Both sigils are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is modest. Expansion is semi-directional, so it changes size rather than direction. With corners outward it makes its target grow, and inverted with corners inward it makes it shrink. Here four normal signs directly contradict two inverted ones. Growth outnumbers shrinking four to two, so growth dominates, but the opposing pair pulls against it and the result is likely unstable. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored. The ring is closed, but it is not round enough, which makes any effect fleeting and gives the seal a chance of failing to activate at all.
effect: Makes nearby stone and soil swell in size while stirring the surrounding air in a modest gust. The growth comes in uneven pulses, briefly shrinking back before swelling again, so the material never settles at a steady size. The whole effect is short-lived, and it may sputter out before taking hold.

name: s42_00057.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the bottom between the south-southwest and south-southeast. A wind sigil sits upright at the center: an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes on either side, of moderate size relative to the ring. Four Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke with short hooks at both ends, sit near the ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast, and west-southwest positions. They are spaced roughly evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Envelopment makes a magic effect envelop or surround whatever it targets, so the moving air wraps around the target instead of blowing in one direction. The four Envelopment signs are balanced around the ring, so no side is favored and the wrapping is even. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The ring is open, so the seal cannot activate until the gap is closed.
effect: As drawn, it does not activate. Once closed, it would gather the surrounding air into a moderate current that wraps evenly around the target on all sides, enclosing it in a moving shell of wind.

name: s42_00058.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed but roughly drawn, bulging into a lumpy, rounded-triangle shape rather than a true circle. Its center is empty, with no sigil. Four small, smudgy signs sit about two-thirds of the way out toward the ring at the north, east, south and west, evenly spaced. The north, east and west signs are inverted Rain signs, flipped inside-out. The southern one is a Rain sign with its left part missing, also inverted. Three smaller sub-seals sit outside the ring, each joined to it by a short line. The one at the south-southeast holds a fire sigil, ring closed. The one at the west holds a wind sigil, but its ring is open with a gap at the lower left. The one at the northeast holds a Detection sign at its center, ring closed. Each of these central glyphs is of moderate size relative to its small ring.
justification: The main seal has no sigil, so its element comes from the linked sub-seals. The closed fire sub-seal makes fire and heat the material the seal acts on. The wind sub-seal's ring is open, so it does not activate and adds nothing. Inverted Rain normally creates an area where its target cannot exist or is pushed away, so around fire it forms a zone that repels flame and heat. The four Rain signs are balanced, so the zone covers all sides. The southern glyph is read as a Rain sign missing its left part, which is a guess, and it would act only weakly, leaving that side thin. Detection's role is not well established. It most likely senses a presence and lets the ward respond to it, which is also a guess. The modifiers do not contradict each other. However, the rough, misshapen main ring and the smudged signs make the spell weak and short-lived, and they put activation itself at risk.
effect: Forms a ward around the seal that pushes away fire and heat and keeps flames from entering the area, apparently reacting when something nearby is sensed. The ward is thin and patchy on its southern side. It flickers in and out, and it fades after a short time, if it takes hold at all.

name: s42_00059.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn. The ring is open, with a gap near the top just east of north. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Eight Strengthening signs, each a triangle crossed by a bar, form an even circle about two-thirds of the way out toward the ring. They sit at the north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west and northwest points. The four cardinal signs have their apex pointing toward the center. The four intercardinal signs are tilted at varying angles but still face roughly inward. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Strengthening makes its target stronger, harder and more durable. With eight of them evenly spaced, the reinforcement is applied evenly on all sides and no direction is favored. Light from this sigil normally diminishes over time, so the Strengthening signs work against that fading and make the light more robust. There is only one kind of modifier and nothing contradicts it, so the seal is coherent and neatly drawn. Because the ring is open, the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: It does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it would produce a moderately bright, even glow around the seal. The light would be reinforced, so it holds steady and fades far more slowly than ordinary magical light.

name: s42_00060.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. A Concealment sign, an eight-armed star with eye marks on its cardinal arms, sits at the south about halfway to the ring and is drawn a little roughly. A Binding sign, two stacked arcs, sits near the ring at the north. Two small Purification signs sit on the western side: one near the ring at the west-southwest and one at the northwest. The east side of the seal is empty, so the signs lean toward the west. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Binding halts the movement of the target material and holds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit, gathering the water into one body. The two Purification signs separate waste from water, which suits a water sigil. Because Purification is asymmetric, its exact behavior is less predictable, and with both signs on the western side the cleansing is weighted toward that side. Concealment hides its target, so the bound and cleaned water is shrouded from view. Its slightly rough drawing makes the hiding weaker and shorter lived than the rest of the spell. There are only three kinds of modifier, and they do not contradict each other.
effect: Draws water together into a single still mass, strips waste out of it, and hides it from sight. The cleansing works more thoroughly on the western side than the eastern. The concealment flickers at its edges and fades well before the water is released.

name: s42_00061.png
description: A fully visible seal on a white background, ring closed. A small earth sigil sits upright at the center. Six signs sit near the ring. A Repetition sign is at the north-northeast, tilted. An Aeriforms Defined sign, three short strokes of rising length, is at the east-northeast, angled. A Rain sign is at the east-southeast with its top toward the ring. A Launch sign is at the south-southwest, opening inward with its apex toward the ring. A second Rain sign is at the west and appears inside out compared to the eastern one. A Strengthening sign, a triangle crossed by a bar, is at the north-northwest, rotated well off upright. The Launch and Strengthening signs are drawn with heavier, rougher strokes than the rest. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on existing soil, sand and stone. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Rain summons its target in a falling form. The inside-out Rain at the west is inverted, so it creates an area where the target is pushed away. These two directly contradict each other and largely cancel, leaving the material settling unevenly. Launch sends its target outward toward where it points in a powerful but short-lived burst. Strengthening hardens the material. Aeriforms Defined is a wind modifier with no clear role on an earth sigil. Repetition keeps resetting affected matter to the state it had when the spell first touched it. The earth sigil, the Launch burst and Repetition dominate. With more than three unrelated kinds of modifier stacked together, and with two of them contradicting, the result is likely unstable.
effect: Pulls loose soil and grit toward the seal and hurls hardened clumps outward toward the south-southwest in a brief burst. Grit drifts down on the eastern side while it is pushed away on the western side, so material piles up lopsidedly. The thrown clumps keep snapping back toward their original loose state, so they flicker between hard and crumbling in flight and the burst fizzles out early.

name: s42_00062.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small Solidification sign, two little circles joined by a short vertical line, sits upright at the center where a sigil would normally go. There is no element sigil. Four Stillness signs sit near the ring at the northeast, northwest, southwest and southeast points, each rotated so its top faces the ring. The northeast and southwest Stillness signs are drawn with heavier strokes than the other two. The signs are evenly spaced, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: Solidification is a sign, but here it takes the center in place of a sigil and sets the core behavior: magic and material inside the seal become more solid. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest strength. With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and acts on whatever material is within its reach. Stillness holds a magical effect static in a single location, and four of them evenly spaced keep that hold balanced on all sides, so the effect is not pushed in any direction. Solidification and Stillness are two compatible kinds of modifier that reinforce each other, and the ring is closed and neatly drawn, so the spell activates and stays steady.
effect: Firms up loose material placed on or over the seal and holds it fixed in one spot, so it keeps its shape and does not drift or shift. The hardening is modest, enough to set soft or loose matter rather than turn it rock-hard.

name: s42_00063.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large earth sigil sits upright at the center, reaching nearly half the ring's radius. Five signs are spaced unevenly around it. A Link sign sits at the west, about halfway to the ring, turned with its top toward the ring. An Entwining sign sits near the ring at the south, also with its top toward the ring. A small Piercing sign sits at the southeast, about halfway out. A Glaives sign sits near the ring at the east-southeast, drawn inside the ring with its prongs facing the center. A single Regions sign sits near the ring at the northeast, its point aimed inward toward the center. The north and northwest are empty, so the signs cluster toward the southeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell works existing solid matter such as stone and soil without creating it. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Piercing turns the material into projectiles. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself in flesh, which pairs with Piercing as an offensive core. Entwining makes the material wrap around its target. Link identifies and joins pieces that came from the same source. The lone Regions sign points inward, which confines magic to within the ring, and that works against projectiles meant to fly outward. With the signs bunched to the southeast, the effect leans that way. The seal stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier, with Piercing and Regions pulling in opposite directions. The large earth sigil, Piercing and Glaives dominate. Regions holds the spikes close to the seal, while Entwining and Link are the weakest and least predictable parts, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Tears stone and soil into hard, sharp spikes that drive deep into anything nearby, mostly toward the southeast, with considerable force. The spikes tend to stall close to the seal instead of flying free. Some curl and wrap around whatever they strike, and fragments sometimes snap back together with others from the same stone. These secondary effects happen unevenly from spike to spike, and the volley often breaks apart before reaching full strength.

name: s42_00064.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small upright fire sigil sits at the center. Three Sights Set signs lie inside the ring, each with its diamond end toward the ring and its arrow pointing inward. One is long and sits at the northwest, one is long and sits at the east, and a much shorter, compact one sits closer in at the west. Near the ring at the south-southwest is a glyph that matches no single known sign. It is a Columns-like stroke with a short crossbar on the end facing the center and a small open circle on the end near the ring. The signs are not evenly spaced and cluster more on the western side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame or heat. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Sights Set aims a spell at a point or target the caster chooses. With three of them pointing inward from different sides, the aim is strong and easy to steer. The south-southwest glyph most closely reads as a Columns sign joined to a Solidification circle, which is a guess. Under that reading, it gives the fire a column-shaped area of effect and makes it denser and more cohesive than loose flame. Only two kinds of modifier are present, aiming and a solidified column, and they do not contradict each other. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady. Because the signs are unbalanced toward the west, the effect carries a pull to that side.
effect: Produces a modest, dense column of flame that holds together firmly and can be aimed at a chosen target. Left unsteered, the column tends to lean and drift toward the west.

name: s42_00065.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The main ring is a little rough and open, with a clear gap at the top. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center, both small to moderate relative to the ring: an Immobility sign on the left and a neatly drawn light sigil on the right. Seven Diamond signs are spaced around the ring about halfway to two-thirds of the way out, at the north, north-northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and west-northwest. Each is rotated differently, and several are drawn roughly with heavy, uneven strokes. Three small sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The one at the west-northwest has its ring closed and holds a Binding sign. The one at the northeast holds an earth sigil, and its ring is open. The one at the south also holds an earth sigil, and its ring is open as well.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light. Its moderate size gives moderate intensity, and that light diminishes over time. Immobility shares the center and makes its target hold shape and stay fixed relative to the seal, so the light is pinned in place rather than drifting or beaming outward. The Diamond signs confine the effect to whatever is inside the object the seal is drawn on, leaving the object itself untouched. Their known effect does not depend on rotation, and their placement is balanced, so the effect has no direction. The closed Binding sub-seal joins the held material into a single unit. Both earth sub-seals have their rings open, so they contribute nothing until closed. Once closed, they would add a hold on solid matter inside the container. The modifiers work together without contradiction, so the seal is not unstable. However, the main ring is open and must be closed before anything activates. The rough drawing of the main ring and several Diamonds would make the result weaker and shorter lived.
effect: As drawn, the seal does not activate. If closed, it would fill the inside of the object it is drawn on with a moderate light, held fixed as a single steady mass while the object itself stays unlit. Because the seal is roughly drawn, the glow would sit unevenly, dimmer in some spots than others, and fade sooner than normal.

name: s42_00066.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, neatly drawn, with the ring open at a gap across the top between north and north-northeast. An upright fire sigil sits at the center, about a third of the ring's radius in size. Four Orb signs, each a small circle crossed by a short line, sit near the ring: one at the east, drawn a little heavier and rougher than the rest, one at the southwest, one at the north-northwest, and one at the west-southwest, slightly closer to the center than the others. Three of the four Orbs crowd the western half, so the arrangement leans toward the west-southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on flame and heat, and its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Orb is non-directional and defines a spherical space above the seal where the spell's material collects, but only material added in directly, filling from the bottom up under gravity. All four modifiers are the same sign, so nothing contradicts and the seal is not unstable. Because Orb has no direction, its orientation does not steer the effect, but the uneven placement, with most Orbs clustered to the west-southwest, likely shifts the sphere toward that side. The slightly rough eastern Orb makes the boundary on that side a little weaker. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: As drawn, it does not activate. Once closed, it forms an invisible sphere of moderate strength above the seal that holds any fire fed directly into it, with the flame pooling at the bottom and rising as more is added, like liquid filling a bowl. The sphere sits off-center toward the west-southwest, and its eastern side holds less firmly, so flame there tends to flicker and leak slightly through the boundary.

name: s42_00067.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large, reaching about half of the ring's radius. Six small Windows signs, each a little circle lined with short slanted hatch marks, surround it about halfway between the sigil and the ring. They sit at roughly the north, northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest, and west-northwest positions, evenly spaced. The east-southeast Windows sign is drawn with heavier, darker strokes than the others. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, so it creates and controls flames and heat. Its large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong intensity. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined, creating a portal-like passage between locations. Here it is drawn as six separate small signs rather than as a band lining the ring, so the seal reads as having several small openings instead of one broad passage. The six signs are evenly spaced, so no direction is favored. No Doorways sigil or other glyph fixes where the openings lead, so the destination is set by the caster or the linked counterpart rather than by this seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is not contradictory. The heavier east-southeast sign is slightly rougher than the rest, which makes that one opening a little weaker than the others.
effect: Produces strong flames and heat and passes them through several small portal-like openings, so the fire emerges at a separate, linked location instead of only at the seal. The openings carry the fire evenly, though one of them runs slightly weaker and flickers more than the rest.

name: s42_00068.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Repetition sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Glaives signs, each a stem ending in a three-pronged fork, sit well out toward the ring. Those at the northwest and southeast have their prongs toward the center. Those at the east-northeast and south have their prongs toward the ring. The signs are spaced unevenly, with more weight toward the east-southeast. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: Repetition takes the center as the core of the spell. It continuously resets whatever it affects to the state it had when the spell first took hold, undoing changes, and its moderate size gives a moderate strength. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh, so this resetting effect is driven into a living body rather than an object's surface. Glaives are semi-directional, so their orientation does not steer the spell. Reversing a semi-directional sign reverses its effect, though Glaives have never been shown reversed. Here two face inward and two face outward, so the pairs work against each other: one pair drives the magic deep and the other would hold it shallow or push it back out. Repetition dominates and sets what the spell does, while the opposed Glaives fight over how deep it reaches, so the result is likely unstable. The uneven spacing toward the east-southeast makes the effect stronger on that side.
effect: Sinks into a living body and keeps resetting it to the state it was in when the spell took hold, undoing wounds and other changes as they happen. How deep it reaches keeps shifting, gripping firmly in some places and slipping toward the surface in others. Some parts of the body snap back while others drift, and the hold is noticeably stronger on one side.

name: s42_00069.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap along its west side running from about west-northwest down to south-southwest. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Refuse signs sit about halfway out. The ones at the north, east and west have their diamond ends toward the center and their crossed strokes toward the ring. The one at the south-southwest is reversed, with its diamond toward the ring. Four Crushing signs sit farther out near the ring. The ones at the south-southeast and northwest are drawn normally. The ones at the east-northeast and west-southwest are inverted, and the west-southwest one sits beside the gap in the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and works with flame and heat, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward where it points. Three Refuse signs point inward, drawing waste toward the center. The single reversed one at the south-southwest pulls some of it back out toward that side. Crushing is semi-directional. Drawn normally, it breaks matter into smaller pieces, and inverted, it reforms crushed matter. Here two normal and two inverted Crushing signs directly contradict each other. Neither side outweighs the other, so the breaking and reforming fight over the fire. The inward Refuse pull and the fire sigil dominate, and the Crushing pair makes the result likely unstable. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: It does not activate while the ring is open. Once the ring is closed, it would draw nearby waste and debris toward the seal and burn it in a moderate fire, while a trickle of refuse keeps drifting out toward the south-southwest. The flames repeatedly splinter into scattered sparks and then pull back together, so the fire flickers and burns unevenly and may gutter out before the gathered waste is consumed.

name: s42_00070.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Levitation sign stands upright at the center in place of a sigil, with its arrow pointing north, and it is small relative to the ring. Eight Regions chevrons surround it in two loose bands, with no element sigil anywhere. In the outer band, near the ring, the chevrons at the north, east-southeast and west-southwest point outward toward the ring, while the one at the south points inward toward the center. In the inner band, about halfway out, the chevrons at the north-northwest, east-northeast and west-southwest point outward, while the one at the south points inward. The two inward chevrons sit one above the other on the south side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Levitation takes the center and sets the core behavior: floating a target into the air. Because no element is named, it is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and acts on whatever objects fall within its reach. The short Levitation sign means a modest lift with limited height, speed and carrying weight. Regions signs set where magic manifests relative to the seal. Six of them point outward and are spread evenly, so the effect appears outside the ring rather than within it, with no single direction favored. The two southern Regions point inward, which directly contradicts the outward majority on that side and pushes the effect from the south back across toward the seal. The outward signs dominate, so the lift mostly forms around the outside of the ring. The south side is likely unstable, because the two inward signs pull against the rest there. The clean drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates reliably.
effect: Gently lifts objects in a band around the outside of the seal and lets them hover at a low height, while anything inside the ring stays on the ground. On the south side the lift is uneven: objects there drift back toward the seal and bob or sink unpredictably instead of holding steady.

name: s42_00071.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Six Partition signs, each a triangle resting on a doubled arched line, are spaced around the seal about two thirds of the way out from the center. They sit at the north-northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest, west, and north-northwest positions. Their rotations vary from sign to sign rather than all facing the same way. The eastern sign, for example, has its triangle turned toward the center, while the others are tilted at different angles. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Partition is a directional sign that outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending outward and upward. Whatever effect fills that area is set by the glyphs inside it, which here is only the light sigil. Six Partition signs spread evenly around the ring enclose a region on all sides, so no single direction is favored. Because their angles differ, the outline they draw is likely irregular rather than a perfect circle. Only one kind of modifier is present and nothing contradicts it, so the seal activates and holds steady.
effect: Fills a clearly bounded zone around and above the seal with a moderate, even light, with distinct edges where the glow stops. The edges of the lit area are slightly irregular rather than perfectly round, and the light gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00072.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but slightly lumpy and not perfectly round. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, neatly drawn and moderate in size, reaching a little under half the ring's radius. Three Dispersion signs sit close to the ring at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest positions, spaced roughly evenly. Each has its stem pointing toward the center and its curved end facing outward toward the ring. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell. It acts on existing solid matter such as soil, sand and stone and does not create any. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Dispersion makes a seal's magic pour or leak outward rather than beaming it in one direction. All three signs share the same orientation and are balanced around the ring, so no side is favored and the outflow spreads evenly in all directions. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The ring is closed, so the spell activates, but its uneven, not-quite-round shape weakens the seal and shortens how long the effect lasts.
effect: Loosens nearby soil, sand or loose stone and lets it spill outward from the seal in an even, spreading flow on all sides, at moderate strength. The flow comes in slightly uneven pulses rather than a steady stream and dies out sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would allow.

name: s42_00073.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center at moderate size relative to the ring, its lines slightly rough. Four Binding signs, each a larger arc over a smaller arc, sit near the ring at the northwest, east-northeast, south and southeast, with the larger arc toward the center. The southeast one sits closer to the ring than the others. Two Aeriforms Defined signs, each three short fanned strokes, sit at the north-northeast and west-southwest, with their tops toward the center. The signs are spread evenly around the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity, and its slightly rough lines weaken it a little and shorten how long it lasts. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. With four Binding signs, the water is held firmly as one cohesive mass. Aeriforms Defined is tied to gases. Its exact function is uncertain, so reading it as giving the bound water an airy, vaporous form is a guess. There are no directional signs and the modifiers are balanced, so the effect stays at the seal and is not pushed in any direction. The two kinds of modifier do not contradict each other.
effect: Draws water together into a single cohesive mass of mist or vapor that hangs still over the seal and moves only as one body. The mass is of moderate size. Its edges waver slightly, and it fades somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00074.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large Link sign sits upright at the center, reaching about halfway to the ring, in place of a sigil. Three very small Mimicry signs sit about three quarters of the way out from the center, at the west-northwest, northeast and south-southeast positions. Each is rotated so its top faces the ring, and the three are spaced evenly around the seal. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so Link takes the center and sets the core behavior. It identifies objects that broke off from, were removed from, or were made from the same source, and links them together. Drawn large relative to the ring, it forms a strong, clear link. Mimicry guides or imitates the movements of a target object. With no decorative sigil to copy, the linked pieces have only each other to imitate, so the movement of one is passed on to the rest. The three Mimicry signs are evenly spaced, so no direction is favored. They are drawn very small, however, which makes the imitation faint compared with the strong link. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they support each other, so the seal is stable. With no element sigil, it is not tied to any one material.
effect: Links pieces of any material that came from the same source, so that moving one piece makes the others copy its motion. The link holds firmly, but the copied movements are faint. The other pieces follow only loosely and lag behind, tracing smaller versions of the original motion.

name: s42_00075.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small earth sigil sits upright at the center. A Projection sign, a flat bracket, sits at the north point in the band between the two rings. Its flat side faces the center and its open side faces the outer ring. Inside the inner ring, a Stretch sign sits at the northeast, about halfway out, its arch toward the center and its opening and feet facing outward. A small Link sign sits at the southwest, about halfway out, rotated with its top toward the center. No other signs are present, and more of the signs sit on the northern side of the seal than the southern. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. The second ring adds strength and further effects to the core spell. Stretch turns solid objects that touch the seal into long, flexible ribbons. Link identifies pieces that broke off from, or were made from, the same source and joins them. Projection pushes the effect outward from the seal. Because it is the only Projection sign and sits alone at the north, with the other signs also weighted northward, the outward push favors that side. The seal uses three kinds of modifier that work together without contradiction, and the neat drawing and closed rings mean it activates and holds steady.
effect: Turns stone or soil that touches the seal into long, flexible ribbons, joins together ribbons that came from the same source, and sends them out from the seal toward the north. The effect is modest in strength but steady, slightly reinforced compared to a single-ringed version.

name: s42_00076.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is neatly drawn but open, with a wide gap at the south-southwest. A water sigil sits upright at the center, fairly large, reaching about halfway to the ring. Six Aeriforms Defined signs, each three short strokes, sit just inside the ring at the north-northwest, northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest and west-northwest. Three face inward with their tops toward the center (north-northwest, east-southeast, southwest). The other three are inverted, with their tops toward the ring (northeast, south-southeast, west-northwest), so normal and inverted signs alternate around the ring. Four small Dancing Puppets signs sit about halfway between the center and the ring at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Dancing Puppets allows a target's movement to be manipulated, letting it fly and be moved through the air. Four evenly spaced copies and no directional signs mean the motion has no set direction, so the water darts about erratically. Aeriforms Defined is tied to air and serves as an air modifier. Read as a guess, it gives the water an airy, gaseous quality. It is most likely semi-directional, so its three inverted copies would reverse that effect and strip the air back out. These normal and inverted copies directly contradict each other. They are equal in number and evenly spaced, so they largely offset each other rather than favoring one side. The water sigil and Dancing Puppets therefore dominate, while the air component is likely unstable. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Does not activate while the ring stays open. Once closed, it would lift a large amount of water into the air and send it darting around in erratic, unguided motion. The water would keep puffing into frothy, airy spray and then abruptly condensing back into dense blobs, flickering unevenly between the two states as it moves.

name: s42_00077.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The band between the outer and inner rings is empty. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center and is modest in size relative to the rings. Six Cooling signs, each a vertical stroke with two dots on either side, are spaced evenly just inside the inner ring at roughly the north, northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest and west-northwest positions. Each is oriented with its top toward the ring. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell that manipulates, collects or creates water. Its modest size relative to the rings gives a moderate intensity. Cooling cools its target, and six of them strengthen that chilling. Cooling has no set direction and no directional signs are present. The signs are evenly spaced, so the effect stays at the seal and spreads evenly rather than being pushed toward any side. The second ring holds no signs, so it adds no modifier of its own. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the neat drawing and closed rings mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Chills water at the seal to a steady cold, cooling it evenly from all sides without moving it in any direction. The effect is moderate and holds consistently while the spell lasts.

name: s42_00078.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed. The rings are wobbly and slightly lopsided rather than truly round. The center is empty, with no sigil. A Strengthening sign sits on the inner ring at the north-northwest, tilted so its apex points sideways along the ring. A Glaives sign stands just inside the inner ring at the south, its three prongs pointing toward the center. A small Holding sign, two curved strokes with dots, sits near the inner ring at the southwest. All three signs are neatly drawn. Two of them crowd the lower left, so the arrangement leans toward the southwest.
justification: With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. It acts directly on whatever the seal targets. Strengthening makes the target harder and more durable. Glaives set how deeply the magic embeds into flesh, so the effect reaches into a living body instead of resting on its surface. Holding keeps the target in the shape defined by the seal while still letting it move. These are three distinct modifiers that do not contradict one another, so the seal is not unstable. The rough, poorly rounded rings weaken it, giving a short-lived effect. The lean toward the southwest concentrates the magic on that side.
effect: Sinks into a living body and hardens it, keeping its current form firm and resistant to damage while still letting it move. The hardening is shallow and uneven, strongest on one side and patchy on the other. It wavers and fades quickly instead of holding for long.

name: s42_00079.png
description:
A fully visible seal on a white background. The main ring is closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil sits at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Six signs sit near the ring:
- A Stability and Level Planes sign at the north.
- A small Detection sign at the east.
- A small Pulling sign at the south-southeast, its arrowhead pointing in toward the center.
- A Gathering sign at the south-southwest, its forked head facing the ring.
- An inverted Crushing sign at the west, drawn as a zigzag.
- A bold Levitation sign at the northwest, its arrow pointing out toward the ring.

Two small sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line, and both have closed rings. The northwest sub-seal holds a fire sigil and the southeast sub-seal holds a water sigil. Each sigil is large relative to its small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification:
The wind sigil sets the core element, so the spell moves air at a moderate intensity. Levitation is directional; pointing outward at the northwest, it floats the target and lifts it toward that side. Stability and Level Planes keeps the floating target balanced on a level plane. The inward-pointing Pulling sign draws material toward the seal from the south-southeast, and Gathering pulls in material from the surroundings, so the two reinforce each other.

The inverted Crushing sign would reform broken matter back into its original shape, which has little to act on in an air spell. Detection adds a sensing function whose exact role is unclear. The two linked sub-seals feed fire and water into the spell, each strongly for its size. These two elements work against each other.

The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier: lifting, leveling, drawing in, reforming and sensing, alongside two opposing linked elements. The wind core dominates, with Levitation, Stability, Pulling and Gathering forming a coherent floating-and-drawing-in effect. Crushing, Detection and the clashing fire and water feeds are secondary, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Draws in surrounding air and loose material and floats it upward on a level plane, drifting toward the northwest, while heat and moisture are fed into the moving air. The warmth and wetness arrive unevenly, swinging between dry hot gusts and damp cool ones, sometimes bursting into puffs of steam. The lift wobbles off level, and loose fragments caught in it occasionally clump back together for a moment. The effect tends to sputter out before the gathered air settles.

name: s42_00080.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Five signs surround it, all neatly drawn. A Stability and Level Planes sign, two wavy parallel lines, sits near the ring at the west-northwest. A Partition sign sits at the west-southwest with its top facing the ring. An Expansion sign of nested corner brackets sits at the east-southeast, inverted with its corners pointing inward. A Coil sign, two crossing curves, sits at the south. An Immobility sign sits close to the ring at the east, with its top facing the ring. More signs sit on the lower half than the upper half. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates air without creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Partition, facing outward, outlines the borders of the area the effect fills. Stability and Level Planes holds whatever is affected balanced on a level plane. The inverted Expansion shrinks its target. Coil softens solid matter but cannot act on gases, so it has nothing to work on in the moving air and only affects solid objects caught in the spell. Immobility fixes its target in place and holds its shape, which directly contradicts wind's job of moving air. The seal stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier: boundary, leveling, shrinking, softening and immobility. The wind sigil, Partition and Stability dominate, defining a bounded, level zone of moving air. Immobility fights the motion, while shrinking and Coil are secondary, so the result is likely unstable. The signs are unbalanced and lean toward the south, which pulls the effect that way.
effect: Stirs a moderate current of air inside a marked boundary that tries to keep objects floating level, with the whole zone drifting toward the south. The air keeps stalling and restarting as it locks in place, and the bounded area shrinks unevenly. Solid objects caught in it soften in patches instead of evenly, and the effect tends to collapse before it settles.

name: s42_00081.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed. Both rings are lumpy and lopsided rather than round, bulging into an uneven, almost pentagonal outline. A water sigil sits at the center, roughly drawn and modest in size relative to the inner ring. Six small Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke with hooks at both ends, sit on or just against the inner ring. They are at the north-northeast, east-northeast, south-southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest, spaced roughly evenly, and most are drawn roughly. A small, neatly drawn sub-seal sits inside the inner ring at the southwest. Its ring is closed and holds a light sigil that fills about half of it. The south-southwest Envelopment sign sits just below the sub-seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the main element, so the spell creates and moves water. Its modest size gives a modest intensity. The six Envelopment signs make that water surround and wrap whatever the spell targets. Their even spacing means no side is favored, so the coating forms all the way around. The neat sub-seal adds a separate light effect, and its large sigil within its own small ring gives a small but steady glow. The signs do not contradict each other, and only one kind of modifier is present. However, the main seal's rough strokes make it weaker and shorter lived. Both outer rings are far from round, which makes the main effect fleeting and puts its activation at risk. The neatly drawn sub-seal is not affected by these flaws and holds up better than the main seal.
effect: Wraps the target in a thin shell of water that clings evenly on all sides. One part of the shell glows with a small, soft light. The water coat forms weakly and patchily, may sputter out before it fully closes around the target, and collapses after only a short time. The glow stays steady a little longer before it gradually dims.

name: s42_00082.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed but roughly drawn, slightly lumpy and not perfectly round. A water sigil sits at the center, fairly large at about half the ring's radius, and drawn roughly. Two Pulling signs sit at the northeast and southwest, both with their arrowheads pointing inward toward the center. Five Crushing signs surround the sigil. Three are drawn normally: one at the southeast with its top toward the ring, and one each at the north-northeast and northwest, rotated with their tops toward the center. Two inverted Crushing signs sit at the east and west points. The signs are spread evenly around the ring. Three small sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line and each with a neatly drawn closed ring. The southeast sub-seal holds an earth sigil, the west-southwest one holds a light sigil, and the north-northeast one holds a wind sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the main element, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong base intensity. The rough drawing of the sigil and the ring weakens that strength and shortens how long the spell lasts. A ring this uneven may also make the effect fleeting. The two inward-pointing Pulling signs draw water toward the seal, and because they sit opposite each other, the pull is balanced rather than twisting. Crushing is semi-directional, so its rotation does not steer the spell, but inversion reverses it. The three normal Crushing signs break the drawn-in water into ever smaller pieces, while the two inverted ones push crushed material back toward its original form. These directly contradict each other. Normal Crushing outnumbers inverted Crushing three to two and dominates, but the result is likely unstable. The linked sub-seals add their own elements on a small scale because of their size. Wind moves air around the effect, light adds a glow, and earth extends the effect to solid matter caught in it.
effect: Pulls nearby water toward the seal and shatters it into a fine spray, but the spray repeatedly clumps back into droplets in uneven bursts before breaking apart again. Weak currents of air swirl the mist, which glows faintly, and any grit or pebbles caught in it are partly ground down. The whole effect wavers in strength and tends to fade sooner than expected.

name: s42_00083.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn as a lumpy, irregular loop that is noticeably out of round, bulging and flattening at several points. Two sigils share the center, both small relative to the ring: a fire sigil on the left and a water sigil on the right, both upright and somewhat roughly drawn.
