Three Detection signs, each a set of three slanted parallel strokes of different lengths, sit at the west-northwest, east-southeast and south-southeast. Two Concealment signs, eight-armed stars with eye marks, sit at the southwest and northeast. Two Pulling signs sit near the top of the ring. The one at the north-northwest is inverted, with its arrowhead pointing out toward the ring. The one at the north-northeast is upright, with its arrowhead pointing in toward the center. Several signs are a little rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire and water sigils are opposed elements, and both are small, so each gives only a modest effect. Neither dominates, since fire is slightly larger but drawn about as roughly as water. The Pulling sign pointing inward draws the target toward the seal. The inverted Pulling sign beside it pushes away, so the two largely cancel near the north and leave only a churning back-and-forth there. The Detection signs make the seal sense presences around it, while the Concealment signs hide the target, so these modifiers also work against each other. With contradictory sigils, opposing Pulling signs, and Detection set against Concealment, the elements dominate only weakly and the result is likely unstable. The rough strokes make it weaker and shorter lived. The ring is closed but not round enough, so any effect is fleeting and the seal may fail to activate at all.
effect: When it activates at all, it produces a weak, sputtering mix of small flames and water that fight each other, hissing into bursts of steam that die out almost at once. Nearby objects are tugged toward the seal and shoved away by turns. Its reaction to approaching presences flickers between revealing and hiding them before the whole effect collapses.

name: s42_00084.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is roughly drawn and not quite round, and it is open with a wide gap at the upper right, between roughly the north-northeast and the east. A large, neatly drawn Diamond sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, reaching about halfway to the ring. There is no element sigil. Two Expansion signs, each made of nested corner brackets with their corners pointing outward, sit near the ring at the northeast and southwest. The northeast one is a little rough. Two small Solidification signs, each two circles joined by a short line, sit at the north-northwest and southeast, both slightly rough. The four signs are evenly balanced around the center, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Diamond sign at the center sets the core behavior. Diamond confines a spell to objects held within the container it is drawn on, leaving the container itself unaffected. Its large size makes it the dominant part of the seal. Expansion is semi-directional, and with its corners pointing outward in the normal orientation, it makes the target grow. Solidification makes the affected material more solid. These modifiers complement each other, and the balanced placement favors no direction, so the seal is not unstable. However, the ring is open, so the spell will not activate. The rough, out-of-round ring would also make any effect weaker and short-lived even once the ring is closed.
effect: As drawn, the seal does not activate. If closed, it would make the contents of the vessel it is drawn on grow larger and firmer, while the vessel itself stays unchanged. Because the seal is drawn roughly, the growth would be modest and brief: the contents swell and stiffen unevenly, then soon soften and shrink back. A poorly closed ring might flicker out at once or fail to take hold at all.

name: s42_00085.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fairly large earth sigil, reaching about half the ring's radius, sits upright at the center. Six Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke with short hooks at both ends, are grouped in three pairs spaced roughly evenly around the seal: one pair at the east and east-southeast, one at the south-southwest and southwest, and one at the north-northwest. In each pair, the inner sign sits about halfway out with its top toward the center, and the outer sign sits close to the ring with its top toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, sand, and soil. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Envelopment makes a magical effect surround whatever it targets, so the earth wraps around the target instead of rising, crushing, or moving in one direction. Envelopment's sign type is unknown, so it is not certain whether facing it the other way changes its behavior. Each pair has one sign facing the center and one facing the ring, which most likely defines both an inner and an outer surface for the envelope and gives it real thickness. The three pairs are evenly spread, so the coating forms equally on all sides. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the seal is neat and closed, so it activates and holds steady.
effect: Draws surrounding stone, sand, or soil around the target and wraps it in a thick, even shell of earth on every side. The shell forms quickly and is solid enough to fully encase whatever it covers.

name: s42_00086.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An Entwining sign sits upright at the center, small relative to the ring, and there is no element sigil. Six Strengthening signs, each a triangle crossed by a bar, are evenly spaced just inside the ring at the north, northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest. Each points its apex inward toward the center, and a few sit close enough to touch the ring. The southern Strengthening sign is drawn slightly rougher than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. The Entwining sign takes the center in place of a sigil and sets the core behavior: it makes the object the seal is drawn on wrap itself around other objects. It is small relative to the ring, so the wrapping is of modest strength. Strengthening makes its target harder, stronger and more durable, so the six signs reinforce whatever the spell acts on. They are evenly spaced and all face inward the same way, so the reinforcement is balanced and favors no direction. Entwining and Strengthening are compatible, and only two kinds of modifier are present, so the seal is not unstable. The slightly rough southern sign makes the reinforcement a little weaker on that side.
effect: Makes the object the seal is drawn on wind itself around a nearby object and grip it with modest force. The wrapped object is hardened and made durable so it resists tearing or loosening, though the hold is marginally less firm on one side.

name: s42_00087.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed but noticeably lumpy and uneven rather than round. A small Selection sign, a cross through a small square, sits at the center in place of a sigil. There is no element sigil. A Levitation sign sits near the ring at the north, its crossbar toward the ring and its arrow pointing in toward the center. A Columns sign sits near the ring at the west-northwest, its crossbar toward the ring and its stem toward the center. A small Coil sign lies sideways partway out at the east-northeast. A Cooling sign sits near the ring at the southwest, and a Detection sign, three parallel strokes of increasing length, sits near the ring at the southeast, angled with its top toward the ring. Several glyphs are drawn somewhat roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Selection takes the center and confines the spell to the object the seal is drawn on. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Levitation floats the target, with its arrow pointing inward in its usual orientation. The single Columns sign adds directed force, and because it stands alone at the west-northwest, it tilts the motion toward that side. Coil softens solid matter, and Cooling chills it. Detection has an unclear function and adds no predictable behavior. The seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: lift and direction, softening, cooling, and detection. Levitation and Columns, applied through Selection, dominate. Softening and cooling are secondary, and Detection is the least predictable part, so the result is likely unstable. The lumpy, not-quite-round ring and the rough strokes further weaken the spell and shorten its duration.
effect: Lifts the object the seal is drawn on a short way into the air and drifts it off toward the west-northwest. At the same time, it chills the object and leaves it soft and pliable. The lift wavers and sputters, and the softening and cooling take hold unevenly across the object. The effect is brief and may collapse almost as soon as it begins.

name: s42_00088.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The inner ring sits a short distance inside the outer one, leaving an empty band between them. A four-lobed Billow sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, at a moderate size relative to the ring. Six small Rain signs are spread around it, all inside the inner ring at roughly the same distance from the center: north, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest. Each is a four-pointed concave square with short tick marks, drawn inside-out so it reads as inverted. The six are spaced fairly evenly around the center. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so Billow at the center sets the core behavior: it turns available material into a soft, fluffy cloud, and the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity, and the second ring adds strength to the core spell. Rain is semi-directional with radial symmetry, so drawing it inside-out inverts it. Instead of summoning material, inverted Rain makes an area where the target material cannot stay and is pushed away. With six inverted Rain signs balanced around the seal, that push is even on all sides and has no single direction. The two parts do not contradict each other. Billow sets what the material becomes, and inverted Rain sets where it goes, pushing it outward from the seal. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and all are drawn neatly, so the spell holds steady.
effect: Turns whatever material is within reach into a soft, fluffy cloud and pushes it evenly outward on all sides. This leaves a clear space over the seal ringed by a cushion of cloud. The effect is moderately strong and holds steadily.

name: s42_00089.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in thin black line on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both closed. The outer ring is fairly round, but the inner ring is noticeably rough and slightly lopsided. At the center sits a small upright glyph, about a quarter of the inner ring's radius. It is a fire sigil, a triangle with short strokes off its upper sides, plus an extra short stroke hanging from its bottom edge. At the west-southwest, near the inner ring, is a Repetition sign with a small Columns sign attached to its left side, set with its top toward the center. At the southeast is a Sights Set sign lying diagonally, its diamond end toward the center and its arrow pointing out toward the ring. At the northwest is an Envelopment sign, a slanted zigzag stroke with its top toward the ring. All three signs sit in the upper-left, lower-left, and lower-right parts of the interior, with the west-southwest side carrying the most weight. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central glyph matches no sigil exactly. The closest is the fire sigil, and reading the extra bottom stroke as a minor fire variant is a guess, so the spell is taken to create and shape flame or heat. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Repetition keeps resetting what it affects to the state it had when the spell first touched it, so the flame is restored instead of burning down. The small Columns attached to it gives the effect a column shape. Because it is the only Columns sign and sits off to one side, it pushes the effect toward the west-southwest. Sights Set lets the caster aim the effect at a chosen point. Envelopment makes the magic surround whatever it targets. The Columns lean and the Sights Set aim point different ways, so the caster's aim sets the main line while the Columns drags it sideways. This is a pull between the two, not a full contradiction. The modifiers fall into three kinds: time reset, direction and aim, and envelopment. None of them cancel the others outright. The second ring frames the core spell. However, the rough, not quite round inner ring makes the effect weaker and shorter lived than a neatly drawn seal would.
effect: Produces a modest flame that the caster can aim at a target and wrap around it. The flame keeps renewing itself to its starting state instead of dying down. The flame tends to drift toward the west-southwest, away from the aimed line, so the wrap sits unevenly on the target. It flickers and gives out sooner than expected rather than holding steadily.

name: s42_00090.png
description:
A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is closed but drawn a little roughly and is slightly out of round. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center, neatly drawn and fairly large relative to the ring. Six signs surround it unevenly, with more weight toward the south.

- A small, roughly drawn Crosshair sits near the ring at the west.
- Two Strengthening signs are present. A bold, slightly rough one sits at the northeast. A neat one sits at the west-southwest, about halfway between the center and the ring.
- A neatly drawn Collection sign sits at the east-southeast, about halfway out and rotated at an angle.
- A small, slightly rough Binding sign, drawn as two stacked arcs, sits near the ring at the southeast.
- A neatly drawn Refuse sign sits at the south-southwest, rotated so it points off-axis.

Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification:
The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light. Its fairly large size gives a fairly strong intensity. The two Strengthening signs make the effect harder and more durable. Binding makes the magic hold together and act as a single unit. Collection draws on material above and around the seal. Refuse pulls unwanted material toward where it points, and here it points at an angle toward the south-southwest. Crosshair aims the effect at whatever its short ends point at, but it is small and rough, so the aim is weak.

The seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: hardening and binding, gathering material, sweeping waste, and targeting. The light sigil and the paired Strengthening signs dominate, with Binding supporting them. The gathering, sweeping and targeting parts pull in different directions, so the result is likely unstable. The southern lean of the signs biases the effect toward that side. The slightly rough ring makes the spell somewhat weaker and shorter lived.
effect: Produces a fairly bright light that packs into a firm, dense glow and drifts toward the south side of the seal. It tries to settle on a target to the west, but its aim wavers and slides off. Meanwhile it unevenly drags loose dust and debris into a scattered heap off to one side. The glow flickers as these pulls compete and fades sooner than a light spell normally would.

name: s42_00091.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A large Convergence triangle sits upright at the center with one point facing down. It fills a sizable share of the inner ring. There is no element sigil. Four Rain signs, each a square with its sides curved inward and short strokes radiating from the corners, sit inside the inner ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest positions. Each is set with its top toward the center, in normal orientation. Their centers are empty. The north-northeast Rain sign is a little rougher than the other three. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind or light sigil is present, so Convergence takes the central position and sets the core behavior. It focuses the spell's magic down to a single point and packs loose particles tightly together. Its large size relative to the ring makes that focusing strong. Rain summons a target object, as a sudden fall or as rainfall. These four Rain signs are in normal orientation rather than flipped inside-out, so they summon instead of repelling. They hold no sigil in their centers, so the summoning is not tied to one element and acts on whatever material the spell is given. The four signs are evenly spaced, so the fall comes equally from all sides. The second ring strengthens the effect. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction. The slightly rough Rain sign at the north-northeast is a little weaker than the others, so the fall from that side is thinner and shorter lived.
effect: Calls down a rain of material over the seal and draws it together into a single point above the center, where it packs into a dense, compact mass. The fall comes evenly from all sides with notable strength, though the stream from the north-northeast runs thinner and dies off sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00092.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil, an upright triangle with three short strokes, sits at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Six small Crosshair signs sit about two-thirds of the way from the center to the ring, at the north, east-northeast, southeast, south, west-southwest and northwest positions. Each is rotated so its top faces the ring. They are spaced evenly around the seal, and no other signs are present. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, so it creates and shapes flame or heat. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. With six Crosshairs all facing outward, the fire is aimed at six separate points around the seal rather than spreading as a general blaze or rising as a single column. Because the signs are evenly spaced, no direction is favored. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Sends moderate bursts of fire outward from the seal, each striking a separate target at one of six points spaced evenly around it. The flames stay focused on those points instead of spreading into a general blaze.

name: s42_00093.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but slightly uneven and roughly drawn. At the center is a fairly large glyph of six crossing spokes, two long diagonal strokes crossed by a short horizontal bar. It matches no named sign exactly. Two small Mimicry signs sit far out toward the ring, one at the west-southwest and one at the east-northeast, each with its top toward the ring. The east-northeast one is drawn roughly. Three zigzag Crushing signs sit about halfway out at the northwest, north-northeast and south-southwest, each with its top toward the center. A single neatly drawn wide arc sits at the southeast, opening toward the center. The signs are evenly spread around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind or light sigil is present, so the central glyph acts as the core. It most closely resembles Concealment without its eye marks. This is a guess, and read that way it hides a target. Its large size relative to the ring points to a fairly strong effect. The three Crushing signs face the center, the same orientation as inverted Crushing. Inverted Crushing pulls broken or powdered material back into its original shape, but only temporarily. The southeast arc is closest to a single-curve Binding sign, also a guess. Binding would halt the reformed material and make it move as one unit. The two Mimicry signs make the spell imitate the movements of a target. Concealment, reforming, binding and imitation all point toward one coherent purpose, so nothing contradicts. The signs are balanced, so no direction is favored. The rough ring and the rough strokes on most signs weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts. The roughest Mimicry sign makes the imitation the least reliable part.
effect: Pulls broken or powdered material back into the shape it originally had and holds it together as a single piece. The reformed object is shrouded from sight and copies the movements of its target. The copied motion is jerky and lags behind, and the concealment thins in patches. The whole effect fades fairly quickly, at which point the material falls back into its broken state.

name: s42_00094.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a gap at the north-northeast just above the northeast sign, and its line is a little rough. A Refuse sign, a diamond over crossed legs, sits upright at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Five Pulling signs sit about three quarters of the way out, at the north, northeast, west-northwest, west-southwest and south. All five are inverted, with their tails toward the center and their arrowheads pointing outward toward the ring. The north one is drawn a little roughly. At the east-southeast sits an unnamed glyph: a narrow right-angled triangle with a small circle at one corner. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Refuse takes the center and sets the core behavior: gathering unwanted material such as waste. As a directional sign drawn upright, it sends that material toward the north. Pulling normally draws things toward the seal, but these are all inverted, so they push material away instead. Spaced evenly around the ring, they push outward on every side with no favored direction, and the rough north sign makes the push slightly weaker there. The east-southeast glyph matches no known sign. Its closest match is Convergence, because of its triangle shape, but this is a guess. Read as Convergence, it focuses the magic on that side down to a single point, so the outward push there narrows into a tighter stream. Gathering waste and pushing it outward work together rather than against each other, so the seal is coherent. The slightly rough ring makes the effect weaker and shorter lived, and because the ring is open, the seal will not activate until it is closed.
effect: The spell does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it would gather loose waste and refuse around the seal and shove it outward on all sides, with a mild drift toward the north. The push is slightly feebler to the north, while to the east-southeast it narrows into a tight, concentrated stream, and the clearing force fades fairly quickly before it fully sweeps the area clean.

name: s42_00095.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn as two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil sits upright at the center and is small relative to the ring. Five Columns signs sit in the band between the two rings. Four of them, at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest, are inverted, with their stems pointing out toward the outer ring and their crossbars resting on the inner ring. The southwest one is drawn a little roughly. The fifth, at the south, faces the normal way, with its crossbar toward the outer ring and its stem pointing toward the center. Inside the inner ring are three small round Windows signs, each a circle lined with slanted hatching, at the north, south and southwest, roughly halfway between the center and the inner ring. The signs cluster toward the south-southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. The second ring adds extra strength and room for further effects. Inverted Columns manifests horizontally rather than vertically, letting magic spread outward much like Dispersion. With four of them on the diagonals, the water spreads sideways from the seal instead of rising. The single normal Columns at the south gives a column-shaped push. Because the signs are unbalanced and cluster toward the south-southwest, the effect leans that way. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined. With three of them inside the inner ring, part of the water passes through a linked opening and comes out in another place. The rough southwest Columns weakens that part of the spread slightly. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other, so the seal works steadily.
effect: Water spills outward from the seal in a low, sideways spread that leans toward the south-southwest, with a modest stronger surge pushing south. Part of the water flows through a linked opening and comes out at a separate connected location. The spread on the southwest side is a little thinner and fades sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00096.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small earth sigil sits upright at the center. Five Levitation signs surround it. The largest sits at the northeast, its crossbar almost touching the ring and its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. The other four point outward, which is inverted: a small one at the north-northwest and another at the south-southeast, both near the ring; a medium one at the west-southwest near the ring; and a medium, slightly roughly drawn one at the east, set noticeably closer to the center than the others. The signs are spread fairly evenly around the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell moves existing solid matter such as stone and soil. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Levitation floats its target into the air. Longer signs carry more weight and send it farther or faster. The northeast sign has its arrowhead inward, the usual orientation, and is the longest, so it supplies the main lift. The other four are inverted, and inverted Levitation works to cancel normal Levitation. One upright sign set against four inverted ones is a direct contradiction. The large northeast sign dominates in strength, but the inverted signs keep pulling against it, so the result is likely unstable. The even spacing keeps the lift from favoring any one side, though the slightly rough east sign is a little weaker. Its position closer to the center makes the push on that side uneven.
effect: Lifts a modest amount of stone or soil from beneath the seal, but the lift keeps fighting itself. The material rises in fits, bobs and stalls partway up, and drifts slightly off center, and it tends to sink back down well before the magic would otherwise run out.

name: s42_00097.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, with no sigil. Four Crosshair signs sit roughly two-thirds of the way out from the center. Two larger ones face each other across the seal at the north-northeast and south-southwest, with their tops toward the ring. Two smaller ones sit at the southeast and northwest, with their tops toward the center. The north-northeast Crosshair is drawn slightly rougher than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so the seal names no kind of magic to deliver. Crosshair is directional and makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. The north-northeast and south-southwest pair point outward along one axis, so they aim at points beyond the ring on opposite sides. Being larger, they reach farther and hold more firmly. The smaller southeast and northwest pair point inward along a crossing axis, so they aim at points drawn in toward the center. These are four signs of a single kind, spread evenly around the ring, so they do not contradict each other and the seal is not unstable. The slightly rough north-northeast sign makes the aim on that side a little weaker and less precise.
effect: Fixes four target points: two farther out beyond the edge on opposite sides, and two closer in toward the middle along a crossing line. With no element to carry, nothing visible appears at those points; it only marks them. The far point toward the north-northeast is held a little less steadily than the others.

name: s42_00098.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and roughly round. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, about half the ring's radius. Eight Levitation signs are spaced around the outer part of the seal, at the north-northwest, northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest, west-southwest, and west-northwest. Seven have their arrowheads pointing inward toward the sigil. The northeast sign is inverted, with its arrowhead pointing outward toward the ring. The northeast, east-southeast, and west-northwest signs are drawn larger and bolder than the other five. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame. Its size, about half the ring's radius, gives a fairly strong intensity. Levitation floats its target into the air, and when the signs are balanced around the ring it shapes the target into a sphere. Here the eight signs are spread evenly, so the fire rises as a ball above the seal. Levitation's length sets how far the target travels, how much it can carry, or how fast it moves. The longer east-southeast and west-northwest signs add reach and lift on those sides. The inverted northeast sign works against the regular Levitation signs, and it is also one of the longer ones. This is a direct contradiction. The seven inward-pointing signs dominate, so the fire still floats, but the opposing pull on the northeast side makes the result likely unstable.
effect: Creates a fairly strong ball of fire that floats in the air above the seal. The sphere does not hold steady: its northeast side keeps dipping and dragging against the lift, so the ball wobbles, sags lopsidedly toward that side, and may sink or lose its round shape before the spell would otherwise end.

name: s42_00099.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The inner ring sits well inside the outer one, and all glyphs are inside the inner ring. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center. It is moderate in size relative to the ring, and its strokes are a little rough. A Repetition sign sits near the inner ring at the west-northwest, with its top toward the center. Three small Mimicry signs sit at the west-southwest, east-northeast and south-southeast. The west-southwest and east-northeast signs are rotated at different angles, roughly upside down, and the south-southeast sign has its top toward the ring. Most of the signs crowd the western and southern side, leaving the north and east largely empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity, but its slightly rough strokes make the effect a little weaker and shorter lived than a clean sigil would. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Mimicry guides or imitates the movements of a target. With no decorative sigil present, the air copies the target's motion in a simpler form, and three Mimicry signs strengthen that imitation. Repetition continually resets whatever it affects to the state it had when the spell first touched it. Here it returns the moving air to its starting point, so the imitated motion replays instead of drifting off. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The uneven placement of the signs biases the effect toward the southwest.
effect: Stirs a current of air that copies the movements of its target in simplified form, then snaps back to where it began and replays the motion again and again. The current pulls toward the southwest, so the copying is stronger and more faithful on that side. It grows faint and sluggish toward the northeast, and the whole loop wavers slightly and fades somewhat sooner than a steadier casting would.

name: s42_00100.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. Two signs sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring. On the left is a Stretch sign, an arch open at the bottom with small feet. On the right is a Windows sign, drawn as a small ring of slanted strokes. Eight Detection signs, each three parallel strokes of increasing length, surround them. Six sit in the band between the two rings, at the north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest, each rotated at a different angle. Two more sit just inside the inner ring at the west and the south, with the tops of their strokes toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Stretch and Windows share the center as the spell's core. Stretch turns solid objects into long, flexible ribbons on contact with the seal. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined, like a portal. The second ring adds strength to the core effect. Detection is tied to sensing presence. Eight Detection signs spread evenly around both bands give the seal a wide, balanced sensing range with no favored direction, so the core effect responds to whatever is detected nearby. Only three kinds of modifier are present and none contradict each other, so the spell holds steady. The small center signs keep its intensity modest.
effect: Senses solid objects that come near the seal from any direction. Each one that touches it is drawn out into a long, flexible ribbon and fed through into another, distant space, as if threaded through a portal. The stretching is modest in strength, so it works best on small or soft objects.

name: s42_00101.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is small relative to the ring. Inside the inner ring, three Glaives signs sit about halfway out, at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest. Each has its three-pronged head toward the center and its stem reaching toward the inner ring. In the band between the two rings, four smaller Glaives signs sit at the east-northeast, south, west-southwest and west-northwest. These face the other way, with their heads toward the outer ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell that moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh, so the moving air is driven into a living body rather than stopping at its surface. Glaives can sit outside a ring as long as they stay connected to it, which fits the second set in the outer band. The signs are spread evenly, so no direction is favored. However, the inner Glaives face inward and the outer Glaives face outward, so one set is inverted relative to the other. Glaives behave as semi-directional signs, and inverting a semi-directional sign reverses its effect. The two sets therefore work against each other, with one driving the magic deeper and the other drawing it back out. The inner set is larger and sits closer to the sigil, so it likely dominates, while the more numerous but smaller outer set pulls against it. This makes the result likely unstable.
effect: Drives a modest current of air into a living target's body, so it sinks beneath the skin instead of brushing against it. How deep it reaches keeps wavering, sinking in and then being pushed back toward the surface. The effect lands unevenly from moment to moment and may fade before it settles in.

name: s42_00102.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a gap at the upper left between the north and west-northwest positions. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring: a neatly drawn Link sign on the left and a roughly drawn fire sigil on the right. Two Stability and Level Planes signs, each a pair of wavy strokes, sit about three quarters of the way out at the northeast and southwest; both are somewhat rough. Four Projection signs sit just inside the ring at the north, east-southeast, south and west-northwest. Each has its flat bar toward the center and its open side facing the ring. The signs are evenly spread around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, and its rough drawing makes the fire weaker and shorter lived. Link shares the center as a second core. It identifies things that came from the same source and links them, so flames sharing one origin are tied together. Stability and Level Planes is non-directional and holds its target balanced in a level plane in the air, like something floating on water. The two signs sit opposite each other, so that hold is even. Projection pushes an effect outward from the seal. The four Projection signs are evenly spaced, so no direction is favored and the flames are cast out on all sides. These are three kinds of modifier that work together without contradiction, so the seal is not unstable. The rough Stability signs make the level hold less dependable. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: It does not activate while the ring is open. If closed, it would produce small linked flames that float outward from the seal on every side, held level in the air and reacting together as one set. The flames would be faint, would bob and tilt out of their level plane, and would gutter out sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00103.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small upright fire sigil, roughly a fifth of the ring's radius, sits at the center. Six Stretch signs, each an arch with short feet, are spaced evenly around it about three quarters of the way to the ring. They sit at the north-northeast, east, southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest. Each has its rounded top toward the center and its open, footed side facing the ring. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and manipulates flame and heat. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Stretch draws what the spell acts on out into long, flexible ribbons, and it is meant to surround a central sigil, as it does here. Applied to fire, it pulls the flames into ribbon-like streamers rather than a ball or a beam. Stretch is most likely non-directional, so pointing the signs' tops inward should not change their effect. Six of them evenly spaced give a balanced result with no favored direction. There are no Columns, Regions or other directional signs, so nothing drives the flame outward. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Produces modest flames that draw out into long, flexible ribbons of fire, curling evenly on all sides of the seal rather than shooting in any one direction. The ribbons stay fairly gentle and close to the seal.

name: s42_00104.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in rough black lines on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the upper left, and it is lumpy and uneven rather than round. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, small relative to the ring. Six Convergence triangles are scattered around the middle of the seal at the east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest, west, and north-northwest positions. They are rotated at different angles, so their points do not consistently face the center. Two Levitation signs sit at the north and south points, both inverted with their arrowheads pointing outward toward the ring. All glyphs are shaky but readable, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame, and its small size gives a modest intensity. Convergence focuses a spell's magic down to a single point and packs it tightly. With six of them the focusing is strong, but their mixed angles mean the pull toward that point is uneven rather than cleanly centered. Levitation normally floats its target, and inverted it is known only to oppose regular floating. Reading the two outward arrows as holding the flame down rather than lifting it is a guess. Because they are paired north and south, they balance each other and add no drift. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they do not contradict each other, so the seal is not unstable. However, the rough strokes and the far-from-round ring make the effect weak and short-lived, and they risk it failing to activate. The open ring means it will not activate at all until closed.
effect: It does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it would gather a small flame into a single tight point that stays low at the seal instead of floating upward. The point drifts and wobbles as it fails to hold a clean center, burns weakly, and gutters out after a moment, if it lights at all.

name: s42_00105.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The outer ring is closed but roughly drawn, with a lumpy, uneven outline that is noticeably out of round. There is no element sigil at the center. Instead, a single upright Columns sign sits there, drawn roughly, at about a third of the ring's radius. Four Orb signs sit near the ring at the east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast and north-northwest. Each is a small circle crossed by a diagonal line, drawn somewhat roughly. At the west point sits a fainter, gray glyph that matches no known sign: an arrowhead like the Gathering sign with a small circle on its stem, its point facing the center. A small sub-seal sits inside the ring at the east-northeast. Its ring is closed and neatly drawn, and a neat wind sigil fills about half its radius. The east-northeast Orb sign sits on the edge of this sub-seal's ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no element sigil, so the wind sigil in the sub-seal sets the element: moving and manipulating air without creating it. The sub-seal is small relative to the main ring, so the wind it supplies is modest even though its sigil is neat and fairly large within its own ring. The Columns sign takes the place of a sigil at the center and gives the effect a column shape. Standing upright and alone, it pushes the effect straight up rather than to one side. Orb signs are non-directional and define a spherical space above the seal in which material collects from the bottom up. The four Orbs repeat that space-defining role. The west glyph most closely resembles Gathering, though the added circle makes this a guess. Read that way, it actively draws surrounding material in, which supplies the Orb space without anything needing to be added by hand. Its point faces inward, which fits drawing material toward the seal. These parts work together without contradiction and stay within three kinds of modifier, so the seal is not unstable. However, the rough drawing weakens the spell and shortens how long it lasts, and the ring is lumpy enough to risk a fleeting effect or a failure to activate.
effect: Draws the surrounding air inward and gathers it into a modest spherical pocket raised above the seal, filling from the bottom up like a gentle, contained updraft. The pocket is weak and short-lived; it may flicker into being only briefly, or the seal may fail to take hold at all, with the sphere sagging and spilling its air before it fully fills.

name: s42_00106.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but a little rough and slightly lopsided rather than perfectly round. A small water sigil sits upright at the center, about a quarter of the ring's radius. There are seven Launch signs. Five point their tips inward toward the center: one at the northwest, a close pair at the northeast, one at the southeast, and one at the southwest, all near the ring. The other two point their tips outward toward the ring: one at the west and one, drawn larger and bolder than the rest, at the south. A Diamond sign sits at the east, partway between the center and the ring. Most strokes are drawn roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell works with water. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Launch makes the target generate in the direction it points, as a powerful but short-lived burst. Five Launch signs point inward and two point outward, so they push in opposite directions. The inward majority dominates, driving the bursts toward the center. The outward pair at the west and south pulls against them, so the result is likely unstable. Diamond confines the spell to material held inside the container the seal is drawn on, without affecting the container itself. Only two kinds of modifier are present. The rough strokes and slightly uneven ring make the spell weaker and shorter lived than a clean version.
effect: Water held inside the marked container erupts in sudden, short spurts that rush toward the middle and collide there. Stray jets break the other way, sputtering out toward the west and south. The bursts come unevenly and lose force quickly, and the whole effect fades after only a few spurts without harming the container.

name: s42_00107.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. A large Gathering sign sits upright at the center, its arrowhead pointing north, spanning about half the ring's radius. Eight Repetition signs surround it. Three sit in an inner band, about halfway out, at the south-southwest, north-northwest and east. Five sit close to the ring, at the west-northwest, northeast, south, north-northwest and west-southwest. Their orientations vary: some have their tops toward the ring and others toward the center. The Repetition signs at the south and west-southwest are drawn with heavier, slightly rougher strokes than the rest. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the large central Gathering sign acts as the core of the seal. It lets the spell draw material in from its surroundings, and its size relative to the ring gives that pull considerable strength. Repetition continually resets whatever the spell affects to the state it had when the spell first touched it, like a spring that restores an object if it is changed. Eight of them spread evenly around the ring make the reset strong and even on all sides, with no favored direction. The differing orientations of the Repetition signs have no known effect. The few roughly drawn Repetition signs slightly weaken the reset on the south and west-southwest sides. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other, so the seal works steadily.
effect: Draws loose material from around the seal into it and holds that material fixed in the state it had when it arrived. The material does not rot, cool or change shape, and if it is disturbed it springs back to its original form. On the south and southwest side the hold is slightly weaker, so material there may shift or change briefly before snapping back.

name: s42_00108.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn neatly, with the ring open at a gap in the upper left. A wind sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Detection signs, each three parallel strokes of increasing length, surround it. One sits at the north about halfway out, a second further out at the north-northeast, a third at the east-southeast, and a fourth at the southwest. The southwest one is drawn a little more roughly than the rest. Two Pointing signs sit right against the ring, one at the west just below the gap and one at the east. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The precise function of Detection is not well established beyond helping a spell sense its surroundings, so reading it as sensing nearby presences is a guess. Four of them spread around the seal give that sensing reach on every side. The two Pointing signs make the moved air take a tapered, conical shape. No Columns or other directional sign steers those cones, and the signs are balanced, so no direction is favored. The rougher southwest Detection sign weakens the sensing on that side slightly. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. Because the ring is open, the seal cannot activate until the gap is closed.
effect: The spell does not activate while its ring remains open. Once closed, it would shape the surrounding air into moderate, cone-shaped currents that sense presences around the seal and react to them evenly in every direction. Sensing toward the southwest would be slightly weaker and patchier than on the other sides.

name: s42_00109.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in thin black line on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, with no sigil and no central sign. Four small Crosshair signs sit inside the ring: one at the north, one at the east-southeast and one at the west-southwest, each about two-thirds of the way out, plus one at the south-southwest close to the ring. Four Glaives signs, each a straight stem ending in a three-pronged fork, are spread among them. At the west-northwest the prongs face the ring. At the east-northeast the stem runs out to touch the ring and the prongs face the center. At the south, partway out, the prongs point down toward the ring. At the north-northeast the Glaives sits at a slant, with its prongs angled down and inward. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil and no sign standing in for one at the center, so nothing sets what kind of magic the seal produces. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. With four spread around the ring, the effect is aimed at several separate points rather than one. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh, so the targeted magic is driven into living bodies. Glaives have never been seen inverted, so reading the mixed orientations is a guess. Read that way, prongs facing the ring and prongs facing the center give different depths, so the embedding is not uniform. Only two kinds of modifier are present, targeting and embedding, and they work together without contradiction. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored. Because the core is empty, the spell has little substance to deliver.
effect: Picks out several living targets around the seal and sinks magic into their bodies, lodging deeper in some than in others. With nothing at its core to give the magic a form, what it embeds is faint and shapeless, so each target feels at most a brief pressure or prickle where it settles.

name: s42_00110.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, neatly drawn. The ring is open, with a gap at the lower left between the west-southwest point and the south point. There is no element sigil. A large upright Dispersion sign sits at the center, about half the ring's radius. Six Pointing signs sit just inside the ring at the north, east-northeast, east-southeast, south, west-southwest and west-northwest points, each with its top toward the ring. A seventh Pointing sign sits closer to the center at the southeast, tilted slightly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Dispersion sign is the core of the seal. It makes the magic pour outward from the seal instead of beaming in one direction, and its large size gives that outflow strong force. Pointing is non-directional and makes the target take a conical shape. Seven of them shape the outpouring into many tapered points. The six outer Pointing signs are evenly spaced, so no side is favored. The seventh sign at the southeast adds a little more of the same effect on that side but does not steer the spell. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they do not conflict, so the seal is stable. The open ring keeps it from activating.
effect: As drawn, the seal does not activate. Once closed, it would forcefully pour whatever material is fed into it outward in all directions as a spray of sharp, tapering cones, slightly denser toward the southeast. Because it has no element of its own, it works on any material supplied to it.

name: s42_00111.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the upper right between the north-northeast and the east. The ring is a little rough and slightly egg-shaped rather than perfectly round. Two water sigils sit side by side at the center, each moderate in size relative to the ring. The left one is drawn in thin, neat lines and the right one in heavier, rougher strokes. An Expansion sign of nested corner brackets sits near the ring at the north-northwest, with its corners pointing outward, and is a little roughly drawn. A Stillness sign sits at the north-northeast. A Link sign sits at the east-southeast, turned so its top faces the ring. A Sights Set sign sits at the south, with its arrow pointing up toward the center. A Coil sign lies on its side at the southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The two water sigils make this a water spell, and together they give a fairly strong effect even though each is only moderate in size. Expansion with its corners outward makes the target grow. Stillness holds a magical effect static in one place, while Sights Set lets the caster aim the effect at a target, so these two pull directly against each other. Link identifies material that came from the same source and connects it. Coil softens physical matter but has no effect on liquids, so it does little against the water. The seal stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier, and two of them contradict each other. The water sigils dominate, with Expansion and Link shaping the water and the Stillness and Sights Set conflict deciding whether it holds or moves, so the result is likely unstable. The rough, slightly out-of-round ring and the rougher second sigil weaken the spell and shorten its life. Because the ring is open, the seal does not activate.
effect: The spell does not activate while the ring is open. If closed, it would gather water that came from a single source, swell it into a larger mass and try to send it toward an aimed target. The mass would keep stalling in place and lurching forward, swelling unevenly on one side. It would last only briefly before it slumps apart.

name: s42_00112.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap on the west side, and it is lopsided rather than round, flattened on the left and bulging to the right. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center and is moderately large relative to the ring. Seven Sights Set signs surround it. Those at the north-northeast, east, west and south-southwest have their arrows pointing outward toward the ring. Those at the north-northwest and south-southeast are inverted, with their arrows pointing back toward the center. The sign at the west-northwest is drawn much heavier and bolder than the rest and stands almost upright, its arrow pointing north rather than straight out from the center. The signs vary in size: the north-northeast, south-southwest and west-northwest ones are larger, and the others are small. Some strokes are a little rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light, which fades over time. Its moderate size gives a fair intensity. Sights Set lets the caster aim a spell at a chosen point or target. Here the signs are spread evenly around the seal but aimed in conflicting directions. Most point outward, and two inverted signs point back at the center. Sights Set has never been seen inverted, so reading the inward pair as pulling the aim back toward the seal is a guess. That inward pull directly contradicts the outward signs. The outward signs outnumber the inward ones and dominate, and the bold, nearly upright west-northwest sign is the strongest single influence. It biases the aim northward. Because of the contradiction, the result is likely unstable. The ring is open, so the seal does not activate. Its lopsided shape and rough strokes mean that even once closed, the effect would be fleeting or might fail to start.
effect: The seal does not activate as drawn. If closed, it would produce a fairly bright light that the caster can aim at a target, but the aim would jerk between directions and keep drifting back toward the seal, tending to pull northward. The light would flicker unevenly and fade out after only a short time.

name: s42_00113.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Levitation sign sits upright at the center of the inner ring, arrow pointing north, at moderate size, in place of a sigil. There is no element sigil. Four small zigzag signs sit in the band between the rings, evenly spaced. Two are inverted Crushing signs, one at the northwest drawn neatly and one at the southeast drawn a little roughly. A normal Crushing sign sits at the west-southwest. At the east-northeast is a fragmentary glyph that looks like the upper strokes of a Crushing sign with its lower part missing. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: Levitation takes the center and sets the core behavior: it floats the target into the air. Because it stands upright and is directional, the lift goes straight up, and its moderate length gives a moderate height and carrying strength. With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind, so it acts on whatever material sits on or above the seal. Crushing is semi-directional. Normal Crushing breaks solids into smaller pieces, and inverted Crushing pulls crushed material back into its original form. The fragmentary glyph is closest to an uninverted Crushing sign; reading it that way is a guess, and its missing strokes would make its pull weaker. The seal therefore holds two inverted Crushing signs against one full and one partial normal sign, and these directly contradict each other. The inverted signs dominate slightly, since both are complete while one of the opposing signs is broken. The rough southeast sign weakens that dominance a little, so the result is likely unstable. The second ring adds strength to the whole seal.
effect: Lifts material above the seal into the air and tries to draw its broken pieces back together into their original shape. The reforming keeps fighting a pull to crumble, so fragments snap together, then crack and shed grit again in uneven pulses, never holding one form for long. The floating mass rises to a moderate height but wobbles as the pieces shift.

name: s42_00114.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a clear gap at the southeast, and its outline is lumpy and noticeably out of round. A fire sigil sits upright at the center in heavy strokes, slightly rough, spanning about half the ring's radius. Four Reflection signs, each an hourglass of two touching triangles, sit at the north, east, south and west points, about three quarters of the way out. Each is aligned along the line to the center, so the north and south signs stand vertical and the east and west signs lie horizontal. The north and east signs are neat, while the south and especially the west signs are drawn more roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and manipulates flame or heat. At about half the ring's radius it is fairly large, which points to a strong effect. Reflection works on a reflected image held by the surface the seal is drawn on. Four of them spaced evenly around the ring favor no direction, so the effect spreads evenly over that surface instead of being pushed to one side. Only one kind of modifier is present and nothing contradicts, so the seal is not unstable. The ring is open, so it will not activate until the gap is closed. The out-of-round ring and the rough sigil and lower signs would make any effect fleeting and weaker than its size suggests, and the ring may fail to activate at all.
effect: The seal does not activate while the ring is open. If closed, it would call up strong flame within the reflections on the surface it is drawn on, so fire appears wherever the mirrored image shows it, spread evenly across the surface. Because the drawing is lopsided and rough, the flames would flicker into being only briefly, burn unevenly where the strokes are weakest, and die out quickly, or the seal might not ignite at all.

name: s42_00115.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Five Binding signs, each a pair of stacked arcs with the larger arc toward the ring, sit about halfway out from the center: one at the north-northeast, one at the east-southeast, two side by side at the south-southwest and south-southeast, and one at the west. Three Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke hooked at both ends, sit right at the edge of the ring and overlap its line, at the north, east-northeast, and west-southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates, collects, or creates water. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit, and five of them make that hold firm. Envelopment makes the effect surround whatever it targets, and its three signs at the ring's edge push that wrapping quality to the outside of the bound mass. No directional signs are present and the signs are spread evenly around the ring, so no side is favored and the water moves as one piece rather than in a set direction. Only two kinds of modifier are used, and both work toward the same result, so the seal is stable.
effect: Draws water together into a single cohesive mass that holds its shape and moves as one body instead of splashing or flowing apart. The mass wraps around its target and encloses it evenly on all sides, holding it with moderate strength.

name: s42_00116.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with its main ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil sits at the center, upright and large, reaching about half the ring's radius. Four Stability and Level Planes signs sit evenly near the ring at the north, east, south and west points. Each is rotated so its top faces the ring. Three small sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The north-northeast sub-seal has a closed ring around a small, roughly drawn water sigil. The west sub-seal has a slightly lumpy, roughly drawn ring around a roughly drawn wind sigil. The south-southeast sub-seal has a neat closed ring around a Stillness sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the core element, so the spell creates light. At half the ring's radius it gives a fairly strong intensity. Stability and Level Planes makes the target balance on a level plane in the air. Four of them evenly spaced keep that balance even on all sides, so the light floats level rather than drifting. The linked sub-seals add their own magic to the main spell. Stillness holds a magical effect static in one location, which pins the floating light in place. The water sub-seal adds water. Its sigil is small and rough, so that contribution is weak. The wind sub-seal moves air, but both its ring and sigil are roughly drawn. A ring that is not round enough makes the effect fleeting, so the air movement is faint and short-lived. Stillness and Stability both work toward holding the effect steady, so they reinforce each other. The weak wind is too feeble to fight that hold, so the seal is not unstable overall.
effect: Creates a fairly bright light that floats level in the air and stays fixed in one spot above the seal, slowly dimming over time. A thin mist of water gathers around it, but it forms patchily and unevenly. A faint breeze stirs around the light at first and dies away well before the light fades.

name: s42_00117.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both closed. The outer ring is slightly uneven rather than perfectly round. A neatly drawn wind sigil sits upright at the center: an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes on either side, of moderate size relative to the ring. Three Coil signs, each a pair of crossing curved strokes, sit just inside the inner ring at the west-northwest, east-northeast, and south positions. Each is rotated to a different angle, and the three are evenly spaced. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates air without creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Coil softens a target object but only affects physical matter, so it cannot act on the air itself. It instead applies to solid objects the moving air reaches. Coil is likely non-directional, so the different rotations of the three signs do not change their effect. Their even spacing means no direction is favored, so the air moves around the seal rather than toward one side. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. The slightly uneven outer ring weakens the hold a little, so the effect does not last quite as long as a cleanly drawn seal would. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts.
effect: Stirs a moderate breeze around the seal with no set direction, softening and loosening the solid objects it passes over so they become pliable. It has no softening effect on water or other liquids, or on the air itself. The breeze tapers off somewhat sooner than expected, and the softening fades with it.

name: s42_00118.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, outer ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Six Columns signs sit just inside the outer ring, spread evenly around it. Those at the north-northwest, east and south-southwest have their crossbars toward the ring and stems pointing toward the center. Those at the south-southeast, west-northwest and northeast are inverted, with crossbars toward the center and stems pointing toward the ring. Three small sub-seals, each about a fifth of the main ring's radius, sit inside the main ring. The north-northwest one is a neat closed ring with a fire sigil filling about half of it. The east one is a roughly drawn closed ring holding a slightly rough light sigil. The southwest one is a slightly rough closed ring with a roughly drawn Pointing sign at its center in place of a sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. The three normal Columns signs give the light a column-shaped area of effect rising above the seal. The three inverted Columns signs make it manifest horizontally instead, spilling outward much like Dispersion. Both orientations are equally represented and evenly spaced, so neither direction is favored, and the light both rises and spreads sideways. The fire sub-seal is neat and has a large sigil for its ring, so it adds a small but solid burst of flame and heat at its position. The east light sub-seal is roughly drawn, so its added glow is weaker and shorter lived. The Pointing sub-seal shapes the magic into a cone that Columns can then direct. Because it is drawn roughly, that shaping is weak and uneven. The seal uses only Columns and Pointing as modifiers alongside its fire and light sigils, with no contradiction, so it holds together, though its rough parts perform poorly.
effect: Produces a moderate light that rises from the seal in a column while also spreading outward across the surrounding area, dimming gradually over time. A small, steady flame burns at one side and gives off warmth. A fainter secondary glow flickers on the other side and fades well before the main light, while the light's tapering into a pointed cone wobbles and holds its shape only unevenly.

name: s42_00119.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but slightly uneven and not quite round, bulging a little in places. Two glyphs share the center, both upright and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits just left of center, small relative to the ring. A smaller Entwining sign sits just right of center. Four Stillness signs sit about two thirds of the way out toward the ring, at the north, east, south and west points. Each is rotated so its top faces the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates existing solid matter such as stone, soil, sand and wood rather than creating it. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Entwining shares the center and serves as a second core, making the affected material wrap itself around other objects. Stillness holds a magical effect static in a single location. Four of them, evenly spaced and all facing the center, favor no direction and fix the effect firmly in place. Only two kinds of modifier are present, wrapping and holding, and they work together without contradiction. The neat glyphs give a clean reading, but the slightly rough, not fully round ring makes the effect weaker and shorter lived than a cleanly drawn seal would.
effect: Causes nearby soil, stone or roots to coil around a target and hold it fixed where it stands, with modest strength. The grip stays locked in place while it lasts, but it begins to loosen and crumble sooner than expected, letting the target work free after a short time.

name: s42_00120.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil sits at the center, small relative to the inner ring and a little roughly drawn. Five Solidification signs, each two small circles joined by a line, are spaced evenly inside the inner ring at the west, north-northwest, northeast, east and south-southeast, about halfway out from the center. A larger, boldly drawn Partition sign sits inside the inner ring at the southwest, with its peak pointing toward the center. Four smaller Partition signs sit in the band between the two rings at the west-northwest, north-northeast, east-southeast and south-southwest, each angled along the ring with its peak facing outward. The south-southwest one rests against the inner ring line. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell, so it moves and shapes existing air rather than creating it. Its small size gives a modest intensity, and its rough drawing slightly weakens and shortens the effect. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Solidification makes the magic within the seal more solid, and five balanced Solidification signs firm up the moved air evenly on every side. Partition is directional and outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending outward and upward. The four outward-facing Partitions in the outer band set a boundary all the way around the seal. The single large Partition at the southwest points inward, so that side's border is drawn in toward the center, and its larger size makes this pull fairly pronounced. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they reinforce each other, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Draws the surrounding air into a firm, invisible barrier that rises around and above a bounded area. The barrier is solid enough to push against and stop light objects. Its southwest side bends inward toward the center, leaving the enclosure dented on that side. The barrier is modest in strength and holds steadily, but it thins and fades somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00121.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the top (north). A Convergence sign sits at the center in place of a sigil. It is a downward-pointing triangle with its flat side up, drawn fairly large, about a third of the ring's radius. Six Glaives signs, each a three-pronged fork on a stem, are spread evenly around it about two thirds of the way out. They sit at the north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest, each with its prongs toward the ring and its stem toward the center. There is no element sigil and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Convergence takes the center and sets the core behavior. It draws the seal's magic together and focuses it to a single point, and it can pack loose matter tightly. Its fairly large size makes that focusing strong. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh. Six of them, evenly spaced, push that embedding deep and favor no direction. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they reinforce each other, so the seal reads as coherent rather than unstable. Because the ring is open, the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: As drawn, the seal does not activate. If closed, it would gather magic into a single tight point and drive it deep into the flesh of the target, acting evenly from all sides rather than in one direction. With no element attached, it would act as a focused carrier that embeds whatever magic it is paired with deep in the body.

name: s42_00122.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small fire sigil sits upright at the center, well under a quarter of the ring's radius. In the band between the two rings sit six Strengthening signs, spread evenly at roughly the south-southwest, west, northwest, north-northeast, east and southeast positions. Each has its apex toward the center. Inside the inner ring, four bold Launch signs sit at the north, east, south and west points, about halfway between the sigil and the inner ring. Each has its peak toward the center and its arms opening outward. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest base intensity. Launch drives its effect in the direction it points as a powerful but short-lived burst. All four Launch signs point inward and are evenly balanced, so no side is favored and the bursts converge on the center instead of pushing the flame off to one side. The second ring adds further effects and stronger magic to the core spell. The six Strengthening signs in that ring make the result harder and more durable, which toughens the flame and lets the burst hold together a little longer than a bare launch would. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they reinforce each other rather than conflicting. A couple of strokes are slightly less even than the rest, which only marginally affects the balance.
effect: Throws out a sudden, forceful burst of flame from all four sides that converges over the seal and erupts upward. The flame is dense and resilient for its modest size and holds together through the burst before quickly burning out. One side of the eruption may come through very slightly weaker than the others.

name: s42_00123.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is somewhat uneven, slightly flattened toward the lower right rather than perfectly round. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Nine Gathering signs surround it. Five form an inner circle about halfway to the ring, at the west, north-northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest. Four form an outer circle near the ring, at the north, east, south and west. All of them point their arrowheads inward toward the center except the southwest one, which is turned to point roughly east, across the center rather than at it. The northwest, southeast and north signs are drawn a little roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Gathering lets a spell actively draw material in from its surroundings to build its effect. With nine of them, this pull is strong, so the spell draws in ambient light rather than relying only on light it creates itself. Their inward orientation and balanced spacing focus that pull evenly on the seal. The southwest sign is turned off the center, so the pull on that side is drawn sideways instead of straight in. The three roughly drawn signs pull slightly weaker than the others. The ring is closed, so the spell activates, but it is not perfectly round, which shortens how long the effect holds. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is not contradictory.
effect: Draws surrounding light in from all sides and concentrates it into a moderately bright glow at the seal. The pull is slightly uneven: light from the lower left drifts in at an angle rather than straight in, and the glow dims sooner than a steady lamp would, fading as the gathered light runs out.

name: s42_00124.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn.
