A Convergence sign, an upright downward-pointing triangle, sits at the center in place of a sigil and is moderate in size relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Six Sights Set signs surround it. Two sit in the band between the rings, at the northeast and southwest, each with its arrow pointing outward toward the outer ring. Four sit inside the inner ring with their arrows pointing inward toward the center. Two are thin, at the north-northwest and southeast, and two are drawn with heavier strokes, at the northeast and southwest, lying on the same diagonal as the outer pair. The arrangement is balanced, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Convergence sign is the core of the seal. It focuses the spell's magic down to a single point and packs loose particles tightly together, and its moderate size gives a moderate strength. Sights Set lets the caster aim a spell at a chosen point or target. The four inner Sights Set signs point inward, which ties the aiming to the focal point that Convergence creates. The two outer signs point outward along the northeast–southwest diagonal, which extends that aim beyond the seal. How Sights Set behaves when it points outward is not established, so reading the outer pair as carrying the aim outward is a guess. The second ring strengthens the spell and holds the outer pair as a further layer. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction. The balanced layout favors no single side, so the caster's aim chooses the target rather than the seal.
effect: Draws whatever material or magic is brought to the seal into a single tight, compact point, with moderate strength. The caster can aim that focused point at a chosen target, most readily along a diagonal line out from the seal. The effect is not tied to any element.

name: s42_00125.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed but drawn roughly, bulging into a slightly squarish, uneven circle. A small wind sigil sits upright at the center. Near the ring are four signs: a small Repetition sign at the north, a Detection sign at the east-northeast, a Convergence triangle at the east-southeast with its point turned upward rather than toward the center, and an inverted Expansion sign at the west-northwest with its corners pointing inward. Two small sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the southwest has its ring closed and a Dispersion sign at its center. The one at the northeast has its ring open, with a gap on its right side, and an earth sigil at its center. The signs cluster toward the upper right, so the layout leans north-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves air, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Convergence focuses the magic toward a single point. Here it is turned sideways, so the focusing is only loosely aimed. The inverted Expansion sign shrinks its target. Repetition keeps resetting what the spell affects to its starting state. Detection is a sensing sign whose exact role is unclear, so it most likely makes the effect respond to something nearby. The closed southwest sub-seal adds Dispersion, which pours magic outward and works directly against Convergence. The northeast sub-seal has its ring open, so its earth magic does not activate and adds nothing. The seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier, and two of them contradict each other. The wind sigil, Convergence and Repetition dominate, while Dispersion pulls against them, so the result is likely unstable. The roughly drawn, not quite round outer ring also makes the effect weaker and shorter lived. The cluster of signs on one side biases the effect toward the north-northeast.
effect: Draws air inward into a small, tightened knot that drifts toward the north-northeast and pulses as it keeps snapping back to its starting state. The knot does not hold. It periodically bursts and scatters outward in uneven puffs, and its pulses seem to quicken or falter when something comes near. The whole effect is faint and fleeting, collapsing after a short time.

name: s42_00126.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but slightly uneven and not perfectly round. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits at the center and is small relative to the ring. Six Gathering signs sit near the ring at roughly even intervals: west-northwest, north, northeast, east-southeast, south, and southwest. Each has its arrowhead end toward the ring and its forked stem toward the center. The southern one is drawn slightly more roughly than the others. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell, so it moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Gathering lets a spell draw material in from its surroundings to build its effect. Six of them strengthen that pull. Because they are spread evenly around the ring, no side is favored, and air is drawn in equally from every direction instead of being pushed one way. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is coherent and not unstable. The slightly rough ring and the rougher southern sign make the spell a little weaker and shorter lived than a clean drawing would.
effect: Draws surrounding air in toward the seal evenly from all sides, creating a gentle, steady inward breeze that gathers at its center. The pull is modest, runs slightly weaker on the southern side, and fades somewhat sooner than a cleaner drawing would allow.

name: s42_00127.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Three Partition signs sit about two-thirds of the way out from the center, at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest positions, spaced roughly evenly around the ring. Each has its peaked, triangle-topped end facing the center and its stacked arcs toward the ring. No other signs are present. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates existing solid matter such as stone, sand and soil without creating any. Its large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Partition is a directional sign that outlines the borders of an area of effect. That area extends outward and upward, and whatever the other glyphs call for manifests inside it. Three Partition signs placed at even intervals mark out a balanced, roughly three-sided boundary around the seal. With the earth sigil as the only other element, the earth magic is confined to that outlined region. No sign pushes the effect toward one side. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Marks out a roughly three-sided area around the seal and forcefully works the existing stone and soil inside it. The ground within the boundary shifts and rises while the earth beyond the edges stays untouched, leaving sharply defined borders.

name: s42_00128.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Five Binding signs, each a larger arc paired with a smaller one, sit about two-thirds of the way out at the north-northwest, north-northeast, east, south-southwest and west. Each has its larger arc nearer the center and curving toward it. At the south-southeast is a small, thinly drawn glyph shaped like a Gathering sign with a small circle on its stem, its forked end toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. With five Binding signs spread around the ring, the flame is held in one cohesive mass rather than spreading or flickering outward. The south-southeast glyph matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Gathering, though the circle on the stem is unexplained, so this reading is a guess. Read as Gathering, it lets the spell draw material and heat from its surroundings to feed the effect, and with its fork toward the center that pull runs inward. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they work together, so the seal is stable.
effect: Draws in heat and fuel from the surroundings and holds it as a single compact, steady mass of fire that stays in place over the seal instead of spreading. The flame burns at a moderate intensity and moves as one body if disturbed.

name: s42_00129.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil sits at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Two Dispersion signs sit on the right side, one at the east and one at the east-northeast, each with its stem pointing toward the ring and its curved base toward the center. A Rain sign sits at the north-northeast and a small Mimicry sign at the north-northwest. A small Windows sign, a single ringed circle of short markings, sits right against the ring at the north. A large, boldly drawn Strengthening sign sits at the west-northwest, tilted almost upside down. A Cooling sign sits at the southwest, slightly rotated, and a small Repetition sign sits at the south-southeast. Most signs crowd the upper and right side, so the arrangement leans toward the north-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. Rain summons the water as falling rain, and the two Dispersion signs make it pour outward rather than beam in one line. Because these and most other signs cluster to the north-northeast, the effect is pushed toward that side. Cooling chills the water, and Strengthening, drawn large, makes it harder and more durable, so the chilled water stiffens. Repetition keeps resetting what it affects to its starting state, including temperature, which directly contradicts Cooling and Strengthening. Mimicry has no decorative sigil to imitate, so it adds only aimless guided motion. Windows appears as a single small mark rather than lining the ring, so any link to another place is faint. The seal stacks far more than three unrelated kinds of modifier, with a direct contradiction between Repetition and Cooling. The water sigil, Rain and the Dispersion signs dominate, Strengthening is the strongest secondary part, and the result is likely unstable.
effect: Brings down a moderate, chilled rain that spreads outward, falling mostly toward the north-northeast side. The drops stiffen and harden unevenly, then keep snapping back to their original warmth and softness, while the shower twitches in odd, aimless patterns and sometimes spatters from nowhere. The rain sputters in uneven bursts and tends to collapse well before it should.

name: s42_00130.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. A Pulling sign sits at the north-northwest with its arrowhead and triangle pointing out toward the ring, so it is inverted. Two Glaives signs are present. One at the east has its prongs facing the ring. The other, at the southeast, has its prongs facing the center. A Windows sign, a small circle lined with slanted strokes, sits just south of center. A four-lobed Billow sign sits near the ring at the south-southwest. A Binding sign, two stacked arcs, sits at the west-southwest and is rotated off-axis. Most of the signs cluster on the southern half of the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its large size gives it a fairly strong intensity. The Pulling sign is inverted with its arrow outward, so instead of drawing things in it likely pushes the light away from the seal. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself into flesh. Here the two face opposite ways, which is a direct contradiction, so the depth of embedding is uncertain. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined, Billow turns material into a soft cloud, and Binding halts movement and makes material act as a single unit. That stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier: pushing, embedding, portal linking, cloud forming and binding. The light sigil and the outward push dominate, and the Glaives come next. Windows, Billow and Binding are weaker, scattered influences. The southward cluster tilts the whole effect toward that side. The result is likely unstable.
effect: Throws a fairly bright light outward from the seal, mostly toward the south, where it tries to sink into the flesh of whatever it strikes. How deep it sinks wavers from moment to moment, with some bursts biting in and others barely grazing the surface. The light sputters into puffy, cloud-like clumps that briefly clump together or flicker out somewhere else entirely, and the whole effect fades and collapses early.

name: s42_00131.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Eight Projection signs surround it, each a flat bracket with its top toward the ring and its open side facing the center. Four sit about two thirds of the way out, at the west-northwest, northeast, east-southeast and south-southwest. The other four sit close to the ring, at the east-northeast, southeast, south and west-southwest. More of them cluster on the lower right, so the arrangement leans toward the south-southeast. Outside the ring at the north-northwest, a short line joins a much smaller sub-seal. Its ring is closed but slightly lumpy and uneven, and a small upright light sigil sits at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the main seal creates and shapes flame and heat. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a fairly solid intensity. Projection pushes a given effect outward from the seal, and having eight of them strengthens that outward casting. The signs are unbalanced, with more on the south-southeast side, so the projection is biased in that direction rather than spreading evenly. The joined sub-seal carries its own light sigil, so it adds light to the spell. Light belongs to the domain of fire and pairs naturally with it. Its ring is a little rough, so that added light is weaker and shorter lived than the main effect. Only one kind of modifier is present in the main seal, and nothing contradicts it.
effect: Casts flame and heat outward from the seal with fair strength, most heavily toward the south-southeast. A fainter glow of light accompanies the flame, wavering slightly and dying out well before the fire does.

name: s42_00132.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and a little rough. A Dancing Puppets sign sits upright at the center, small relative to the ring, and no element sigil is present. Four Envelopment signs sit near the ring at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest. The northeast one is drawn smaller and thinner, and the southwest one is heavier. Two upright Reflection signs sit about halfway out at the north and south. A third Reflection sign sits close to the ring at the west, turned on its side with its top toward the ring, and drawn larger and bolder than the others. There is no matching sign at the east. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Dancing Puppets sign is the core of the seal. It lets the movement of a target be consciously manipulated, even at a distance. Reflection targets the reflected image found on the object the seal is drawn on, so the thing being moved is that reflection rather than the object itself. The four Envelopment signs make the effect surround whatever it targets, so the reflection wraps around the object. Only three kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction. Reflection's type is unknown. The turned, outward-facing Reflection at the west may favor that side, but this is a guess. The small center and the slightly rough drawing make the spell weaker and shorter lived.
effect: Takes the reflected image on the object it is drawn on, wraps it around the object like a moving shroud, and lets that image be steered and animated from afar. The motion is faint and short lived. It may lean toward one side, and it flickers and loses its hold sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00133.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large, upright Gathering sign sits at the center in place of a sigil, spanning almost half the ring's radius. There is no element sigil. Six Collection signs surround it, spread evenly around the ring at the north, north-northwest, west, south-southwest, south-southeast and east. Four of them, at the east, south-southwest, south-southeast and north-northwest, have their barred top toward the center and their open side facing the ring. The other two, at the west and north, sit farther out and face the opposite way, with their barred top toward the ring and their open side facing the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Gathering sign at the center sets the core behavior: it actively draws material in from the surroundings so the spell can use it. Its large size gives that pull considerable strength, and without an element the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. Collection gathers material above and around a seal, and its open side normally faces inward. The west and north Collection signs follow that orientation and reinforce Gathering. The other four are reversed, with their open sides facing outward. Collection is directional or semi-directional, so reversing it likely turns its effect around, releasing or pushing material away instead of collecting it. This directly contradicts both Gathering and the two normally oriented Collection signs. Gathering dominates as the central and largest element, but the four reversed signs outnumber the two normal ones and strongly oppose it, so the result is likely unstable. The even spacing means no single direction is favored, so the conflict plays out all around the seal.
effect: Pulls loose material of any kind from the surroundings toward the seal with considerable force. The draw is uneven: material that gathers on some sides is shoved back out on others, so the collected mass churns, shifts and scatters instead of settling into a steady pile.

name: s42_00134.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and drawn a little roughly. A water sigil sits upright at the center, drawn a little roughly and large relative to the ring. Six signs sit about midway between the sigil and the inner ring, each with its top toward the ring. Three Immobility signs sit at the north, southeast and west-southwest. Two Stillness signs sit at the south and west-northwest. At the northeast is a heavier glyph that matches no known sign exactly; it looks like a Stillness sign with a small Columns sign attached at its left. The signs are evenly spaced around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect, and the second ring adds further strength. Immobility makes the target immovable relative to the seal, so it holds its shape as if frozen. Stillness keeps a magical effect static in a single location. These two signs reinforce each other rather than conflict. The northeast glyph is read as Stillness with an attached Columns sign, which is a guess. Under that reading it adds more stillness and gives the held effect a column-shaped area. Because only one small Columns stub is present and the signs are balanced around the ring, it does not push the effect in any clear direction. Only three related kinds of modifier are present, so the seal is not unstable. The slightly rough rings, sigil and signs make it somewhat weaker and shorter lived than a neatly drawn version.
effect: Locks a large body of water in place above the seal, holding it rigidly in a column-like shape as if frozen while it stays liquid. The hold is strong at first, but it loosens sooner than it should. The water's edges slowly sag and drip before the whole mass is released.

name: s42_00135.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but slightly lumpy, bulging a little at the upper right, though still close to round. A Stability and Level Planes sign, three wavy vertical lines, sits at the center in place of a sigil and is moderate in size relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Six signs are spread fairly evenly around it. A Diamond sign sits at the northeast. A Link sign sits at the south-southeast, turned on its side. A Coil sign sits at the south-southwest, tilted. A Stillness sign sits at the southwest, lying sideways. A Solidification sign, two small circles joined by a short line, sits near the ring at the west-northwest. A very small, thin Piercing sign sits near the ring at the north-northwest, set at an angle. The Link, Coil and Piercing signs are drawn somewhat roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Stability and Level Planes takes the center and sets the core behavior: material balances on a level plane, free to shift but always kept flat and upright. The spell is not tied to any element and acts on whatever material it reaches. Diamond confines the effect to the contents of whatever the seal is drawn on, not the container itself. Stillness holds the effect static in one place, and Solidification firms the material. Both are drawn neatly, so they reinforce the center. Link joins pieces that came from the same source. Coil softens physical matter, which directly contradicts Solidification. Piercing turns material into projectiles, which works against Stillness. The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier. The neatly drawn center, Stillness, Solidification and Diamond dominate. The rough, small Coil, Link and Piercing signs are weaker, so the result is likely unstable. The slightly uneven ring also shortens how long the effect lasts.
effect: Holds the contents of a vessel level and still, firming them into a steady, linked mass. The firmness wavers as the material keeps going soft in patches and hardening again. Small shards occasionally spit from the surface, and the hold fades sooner than expected.

name: s42_00136.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed but drawn roughly, with a lumpy, uneven outline that is noticeably not round. A large Pointing sign sits at the center. Six smaller Pointing signs are spaced evenly about two thirds of the way out, at the north, northeast, east-southeast, south, west-southwest and west-northwest, each with its top turned toward the center. These are roughly drawn, and the west-southwest one is smudged into a blot, though it still reads as Pointing. Three small sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The north sub-seal holds a Coil sign, and its ring is open with a gap at the upper left. The east-southeast sub-seal holds a water sigil, and its ring is closed. The west-southwest sub-seal holds a Levitation sign, and its ring is closed. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no sigil in the main ring. The joined water sub-seal supplies the element, so the spell works on water. Its sigil is moderate in size within a small sub-ring, which gives a fairly modest amount of water. Pointing fills the center and surrounds it, so it sets the core behavior. It is non-directional, so turning the outer signs toward the center does not change it, and it shapes the material into a cone. The six outer Pointing signs are balanced and only reinforce that shaping. The closed Levitation sub-seal floats the shaped water into the air. There are no Columns or other directional signs, so the cone is not driven anywhere. The Coil sub-seal has an open ring, so it adds nothing. Even if it were closed, Coil affects only solid matter and would not act on water. Only shaping and lifting are active, so the seal is not unstable. However, the lumpy, poorly rounded main ring and the rough strokes weaken the spell and make its effect fleeting, and it may fail to activate.
effect: Gathers a modest amount of water into a sharp, cone-shaped mass and floats it in the air above the seal, where it hangs without being sent in any direction. The cone holds its point only briefly before its edges soften and waver, and it soon slumps and falls apart. The spell may also sputter and fail to take shape at all.

name: s42_00137.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two rings, both closed. The outer ring is slightly lopsided and not perfectly round, and a second ring sits just inside it. A fire sigil, small relative to the ring and drawn somewhat roughly, sits upright at the center. Six Dancing Puppets signs surround it, each a small ring with four little circles and crossing strokes, set at the north, east, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest. They vary in size and neatness. The north, southeast and west-southwest signs are larger and heavier, and the north and west-southwest ones overlap the inner ring line. The east, northwest and south-southwest signs are smaller and finer. There are no other signs, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and moves flame. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Dancing Puppets lets a target's movement be manipulated, even from a distance. Paired with fire instead of wind, it would set the flames themselves darting and weaving through the air. No directional sign is present and the six signs are spread evenly around the ring, so no direction is favored and the motion stays erratic. Only one kind of modifier is used, so nothing conflicts. The second ring adds strength to the spell. However, the rough sigil, the uneven sign drawing and the not-quite-round outer ring weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Produces small flames that dart and dance erratically through the air around the seal, and they can be steered loosely from a distance. The flames flicker unevenly as they move, and some sputter out sooner than others. The whole display fades after a short time.

name: s42_00138.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Diamond sign sits upright at the center, neatly drawn and fairly large relative to the inner ring, with no element sigil present. An inverted Expansion sign sits at the east-southeast against the inner ring, with its nested corner brackets pointing inward, drawn a little roughly. A Refuse sign sits at the west-southwest just inside the inner ring, turned on its side with its diamond head facing roughly toward the center and its crossed legs toward the ring, also a little rough. In the band between the two rings, at the south-southwest, sits a small glyph of a vertical stroke flanked by dots. It resembles Cooling but with its halves mirrored. The signs are unevenly spread and gather toward the south.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Diamond serves as the core. It limits the spell to whatever is held inside the container the seal is drawn on, not the container itself, and the spell works on any material. The second ring strengthens the whole seal. Expansion is semi-directional, and inverted with its corners inward it shrinks its target. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward where it points; its head faces inward, so waste is drawn toward the middle. The outer-band glyph matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Cooling, which is a guess, and under that reading it lowers the temperature of the contents. Shrinking, waste collection and cooling do not contradict each other. The slightly rough Expansion and Refuse signs make those two effects a little weaker and shorter lived. Because the signs lean south, the effect is heavier on that side.
effect: Shrinks and chills the contents of the container it is drawn on while leaving the container itself untouched. Any waste or unwanted matter among the contents is drawn together toward the middle. The shrinking and sorting are somewhat weak, fade sooner than the chill, and act more strongly on the contents toward the south side than elsewhere.

name: s42_00139.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center. It is small relative to the ring and its lines are slightly rough. Four Launch signs sit just inside the ring at the north-northeast, east, south-southwest and west positions. Each has its peak pointing outward toward the ring. The signs are evenly spaced, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell that moves existing air rather than creating it. Its small size relative to the ring gives it a modest intensity, and its slightly rough drawing makes the effect a little weaker and shorter-lived than a clean sigil would. Launch sends the spell's magic out in the direction it points, as a powerful but short-lived burst. All four Launch signs point outward and are evenly spaced, so no single direction is favored and the air is driven out on four sides at once. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing in the seal works against itself.
effect: Blasts sudden bursts of air outward from the seal in four directions at once, like a quick shove of wind on every side. The gusts are modest and die away almost as soon as they start, with some bursts fading slightly sooner or weaker than the others.

name: s42_00140.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A large earth sigil sits upright at the center, reaching about halfway to the outer ring. Eight Binding signs, each a pair of stacked arcs, surround it. Five sit inside the inner ring: at the north-northwest and west-northwest with their tops toward the ring, and at the east, southwest and south-southeast in varied orientations. The southwest sign is drawn with a heavier stroke than the rest. Three more sit in the band between the two rings, at the northwest, east-northeast and south, each tilted at a different angle. The signs are spread evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell acting on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Every modifier is Binding, which halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. Eight of them reinforce that one effect. Binding's directional behavior is unknown, so their varied rotations are not read as changing the result. Because the signs are balanced, no side is favored. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. With only one kind of modifier and neat, closed rings, nothing in the seal conflicts.
effect: Halts loose earth, stone and sand within its range and locks the material together into a single solid mass. The mass holds firmly and moves only as one piece. The hold is strong and spreads evenly on all sides of the seal.

name: s42_00141.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring's outline is slightly lumpy rather than perfectly round. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes on either side, sits upright at the center and is large, reaching about half the ring's radius. Seven Cooling signs, each a short stroke flanked by dots, are spread evenly around the outer part of the seal at the north-northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, south-southwest, west-northwest and northwest positions. They face different directions. The one at the northwest is drawn noticeably larger than the others. There are no directional signs, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air without creating it. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Cooling lowers the temperature of what the spell acts on. The sign is semi-directional or non-directional and has never been seen reversed, so its different rotations are read as making no difference. The larger Cooling sign at the northwest strengthens the chill slightly on that side. All seven signs share one modifier, so nothing contradicts and the seal is not unstable. With the signs evenly spread and no Columns, Regions or other directional signs, the moving air is not sent in one set direction. The slightly uneven ring is still round enough to activate, but it may shorten how long the effect lasts.
effect: Stirs the surrounding air into a strong, chilling wind that swirls around the seal without blowing in any single direction. The cold is slightly sharper on the northwest side. The wind may die down somewhat sooner than a perfectly drawn version would.

name: s42_00142.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Four bracket-shaped signs sit close to the ring at the north, east-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest, each with its open side facing the center. Three of them match the Projection sign; the east-southeast one is a little rough. The south-southwest one is a Projection-like bracket with an extra dot inside it. Three more Projection signs sit about two-thirds of the way out, at the north, east-northeast and west-southwest. These are inverted, with their open sides facing the ring; the north one is a little rough. Two Entwining signs sit at the same middle distance, one at the northwest and one at the southeast, opposite each other. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a spell that moves air. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Projection pushes an effect outward from the seal, so the three outer Projection signs cast the moving air away from it. The dotted bracket matches no known sign; its closest match is Projection, and treating it as one is a guess. Read that way, it adds a fourth outward projector. The three inner Projection signs are inverted. Inverting a sign reverses its effect, so these would draw the air back toward the seal, directly opposing the outer ones. The four outer projectors outnumber the three inverted ones, so the outward push dominates, but the conflict makes the result likely unstable. The two Entwining signs make the effect wrap around other objects, so the projected air coils around whatever it reaches. The slightly rough signs at the east-southeast and north weaken those parts a little. Because the signs are balanced, no single direction is favored.
effect: Sends fairly strong currents of air outward in every direction. The currents coil around nearby objects and wrap them in swirling wind. The outward push falters at intervals and tugs back toward the center, so the wrapping air loosens and tightens irregularly, and it is slightly weaker on the east-southeast and north sides.

name: s42_00143.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, large relative to the ring at about half its radius, with slightly rough lines. Four Levitation signs sit roughly two-thirds of the way out, at the north-northeast, east, south-southwest and west, each with its arrowhead pointing outward toward the ring. Two Convergence triangles sit at the west-northwest and southeast, each with its flat side toward the ring. The west Levitation sign and the southeast Convergence sign are drawn more roughly than the rest. The six signs are spread evenly around the sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame. Its large size relative to the ring gives it high intensity. Levitation floats the spell's magic above the seal, and when its signs are balanced it tends to shape the result into a sphere. The four Levitation signs are evenly spaced, so no direction is favored and the flame rises straight up. Convergence focuses magic toward a single point and packs it tightly, which pulls the flame into a compact core instead of letting it spread. These two kinds of modifier work together without contradiction. The closed ring means the seal activates. The rough strokes on the sigil and several signs weaken it slightly and shorten its life, most noticeably on the west and southeast sides.
effect: Creates a strong, tightly packed ball of fire that floats steadily above the seal. The flame burns hot but flickers slightly and dies out sooner than a cleanly drawn version would. Its west and southeast edges sag and sputter a little unevenly as it fades.

name: s42_00144.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. At the center is an earth sigil of moderate size relative to the ring. A small Rain sign is attached to its left side, overlapping the sigil's left dot. Two Columns signs sit at the south-southeast and south-southwest, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the center. A Pulling sign sits near the ring at the east, its arrowheads pointing inward toward the center; it is drawn roughly. A Collection sign sits at the north-northeast with its open side facing inward. A Gathering sign sits at the north-northwest with its arrow pointing outward toward the ring. There are two Billow signs, both a little rough: a large one at the west near the ring and a smaller one at the north-northwest just inside the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell acting on solid matter such as soil and sand, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The attached Rain sign modifies the sigil so the material is summoned and comes down as falling rain. Collection, Gathering and the inward-pointing Pulling sign all draw material in, so the seal pulls loose earth toward itself from its surroundings. Pulling is roughly drawn, so that pull is weak and patchy. The two Billow signs convert the gathered material into a fluffy cloud, and their slight roughness makes that conversion uneven. Both Columns signs sit on the southern side, so the column they create is pushed toward the south instead of rising straight up. The rising column also works against the falling motion set by Rain. The seal stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: drawing material in, cloud conversion, column direction and rainfall. The earth sigil, the gathering signs and Billow dominate and form the core of the spell, while Columns and Rain shape how the result moves. The result is likely unstable.
effect: Draws loose soil and sand toward the seal and puffs it into soft, cloud-like clumps that lift in a moderate column leaning to the south, then sift back down like a light rain. The pull falters and grabs material in uneven spurts. Some clumps stay gritty instead of turning fluffy, and the column wavers as the falling earth breaks it apart before it reaches full height.

name: s42_00145.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil sits upright at the center, an S-curve between two teardrops. It is fairly large, reaching about half the ring's radius. Three Convergence triangles sit near the ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast and west-northwest, each with one point facing inward toward the sigil. Two Detection signs, each three parallel strokes of increasing length, sit at the south-southeast and north-northwest, set at different angles. At the south-southwest is a small glyph of crossing spokes with no eye marks, closest in form to Concealment. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. The three inward-pointing Convergence signs focus the magic down to a single point and pack loose material tightly together. Because they are evenly spaced, the water gathers at the center instead of being pushed to one side. Detection lets the spell sense presences around it. The spoked glyph matches no known sign exactly. Reading it as Concealment without its eyes is a guess, and under that reading it hides the gathered water from view. That makes three kinds of modifier: focusing, sensing and hiding. They do not contradict one another, and the balanced layout and closed ring let the spell activate and hold steady.
effect: Draws water together into a single tight, dense mass above the seal with considerable strength. The mass responds to presences that come near it. It is also kept hidden from sight, so the water stays concealed until something approaches.

name: s42_00146.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring: a water sigil on the left and a fire sigil on the right. A small Concealment sign, an eight-armed star with eye marks, sits about halfway out toward the south-southwest. Five Aeriforms Defined signs, each three short fanning strokes with the longest in the middle, sit just inside the ring at the north-northeast, east, southeast, west-southwest and northwest, all with their tops toward the ring. The northeast, west-southwest and northwest ones are drawn a little rough, the northwest one with heavier strokes. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water and fire sigils share the center as two cores, so the spell works with water and heat together. Heat applied to water drives it toward vapor. Both sigils are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is modest. Aeriforms Defined ties a spell to gases and making air apparent. With five of them spread evenly around the ring, the heated water is given form as a gas that fills the seal's surroundings evenly rather than pushing in one direction. Concealment hides a target, so the vapor serves to obscure rather than to scald or move things. There are only two kinds of modifier and they work together. The three rougher signs slightly weaken the effect on those sides.
effect: Produces a modest cloud of warm steam that spreads evenly around the seal and hides whatever lies within it from view. The mist is somewhat thinner and patchier toward the northeast, west and northwest, where it drifts apart a little sooner.

name: s42_00147.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but roughly drawn and noticeably lumpy rather than round. At the center sits an unfamiliar sigil: a circle with an S-curve inside it, ringed by eight evenly spaced dots. It spans roughly half the ring's radius and is drawn roughly. Four Collection-like signs sit about two-thirds of the way out, at the north, east, south and west points, each tilted at a different angle. The east and south ones match Collection. The north one has an extra dot on its left side. The west one has an extra stroke from its left edge. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central glyph matches no listed sigil exactly. Its S-curve inside a circle is closest to the wind sigil, so reading it as a wind variant is a guess. Under that reading the spell moves and manipulates air, and the sigil's large size relative to the ring points to a fairly strong intensity. Collection draws in material from above and around the seal so the spell can use it. The north and west glyphs are read as Collection variants, also a guess, because the extra dot and extra stroke match no known sign and do not clearly change the gathering behavior. All four sit at evenly spaced points around the seal, so the gathering pulls equally from every side, though their uneven tilts make it less even than a neatly drawn version. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. The rough linework weakens the spell and shortens its life. Because the ring is not round enough, the effect is fleeting and the seal may fail to activate.
effect: Draws the surrounding air in toward the seal from all sides, gathering it into a fairly strong but short-lived churn of wind above the seal. The pull comes in uneven gusts that waver from side to side. It fades almost as soon as it forms, and on some castings it sputters out without starting at all.

name: s42_00148.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background with two concentric rings, both closed. The outer ring is slightly uneven in shape. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring, its lines a little rough. Seven Piercing signs, each a short stroke through a small diamond, are spread around the inner ring about two-thirds of the way out from the center. They sit at the north-northwest, northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest, and west-northwest. They point alternately toward the ring and toward the center. The northeast sign is drawn with heavier, rougher strokes than the rest, and the southwest sign is noticeably smaller. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Piercing is non-directional, so the way each sign is turned does not matter. It shapes the magic into projectiles, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many form, so seven signs give seven air projectiles. The second ring inside the first strengthens the core magic. There is no Columns, Regions, or other directional sign, and the Piercing signs are balanced around the ring, so the projectiles are not aimed toward one side and instead fly outward around the seal. The slightly rough ring and sigil weaken the spell a little. The heavy, rough northeast sign and the small southwest sign should produce the least reliable and the weakest projectiles. All the signs are of one kind and do not contradict each other.
effect: Gathers the surrounding air into seven bolts and fires them outward in all directions from the seal, with moderate force. The bolt to the northeast forms unevenly and can veer or break apart early. The bolt to the southwest is smaller and weaker than the rest, and the whole volley fades slightly sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00149.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn, though slightly uneven in roundness. The center is empty, with no sigil. A Binding sign, two stacked arcs, sits at the north point about two thirds of the way out, turned so its top faces the center and the arcs open toward the ring. A Solidification sign, two small circles joined by a short line, sits at the northwest, slightly tilted. A Mimicry sign sits near the ring at the northeast, rotated with its top toward the center and drawn a little heavier and rougher than the rest. A small Piercing sign, a diamond on a line, sits near the ring at the southeast. All signs are small relative to the ring, and three of the four crowd the upper half, so the layout leans toward the north-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil, the spell is not tied to an element and acts on whatever material falls within its reach. Solidification makes that material more solid, and Binding halts its movement and holds it together as a single unit. These two are closely related and reinforce each other. Piercing is non-directional and makes the target manifest as a projectile. Binding's orientation toward the center is read as its usual effect, though how it behaves when turned this way is a guess. Mimicry makes the target imitate the movements of something else. Without a decorative sigil to copy, it would follow the motion of whatever the material is directed at. Because the Mimicry sign is roughly drawn, that part of the effect is weaker and shorter-lived than the rest. The modifiers fall into three compatible kinds, hardening and binding, projectile shaping, and imitation, so the seal is not unstable. The signs cluster to the north-northeast, which biases the effect toward that side. Their small size keeps the overall strength modest.
effect: Draws loose material together, hardens it into a single solid piece shaped like a projectile, and sends it out toward the north-northeast. The projectile then copies the movements of what it is aimed at. This copying is loose and lags behind its target, and it fades well before the hardened piece itself loses its shape.

name: s42_00150.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn roughly in black on a white background. The ring is closed but noticeably lumpy and uneven rather than round. A large fire sigil sits upright at the center, reaching about half the ring's radius. Five Stretch signs surround it, each an open arc with its curved top toward the center and its gap facing the ring. Three sit about halfway out, at the east-southeast, southwest and north-northwest. Two sit farther out near the ring, at the west-northwest and north-northeast. A small Billow sign, a four-lobed clover, sits near the ring at the south. Line weights vary from sign to sign, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and manipulates flame and heat. Its large size relative to the ring points to a strong effect. Stretch turns what the spell acts on into long, flexible ribbons, and five of them make that the main shaping force. Billow turns material into a fluffy cloud, which competes directly with the ribbon shape Stretch imposes. Stretch dominates by number, while the single Billow pulls part of the fire toward a cloud form, so the result is likely unstable. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored. The rough drawing weakens the spell and shortens its life, and the poorly rounded ring makes the effect fleeting and may keep it from activating at all.
effect: Produces strong flames that stretch out into long, flexible ribbons of fire in every direction around the seal. The ribbons waver and sometimes break apart into soft, puffy clouds of flame instead of holding their shape. The fire flickers briefly and dies out quickly, and at times it fails to ignite at all.

name: s42_00151.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed but roughly drawn and slightly lumpy rather than perfectly round. A roughly drawn earth sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Seven signs, all drawn somewhat roughly, are spread fairly evenly around it near the ring. A Stillness sign sits at the north-northeast and a second Stillness sign at the west-southwest. A Solidification sign, two small circles joined by a line, sits at the east-northeast. An inverted Crushing zigzag sits at the east-southeast, and a Collection sign sits at the south-southeast. A small Billow sign sits near the ring at the northwest, and a larger Billow sign sits closer to the center at the south-southwest. Two small sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each closed, neatly drawn, and joined to the main ring by a short line. The one at the west-northwest holds a wind sigil, and the one at the east-southeast holds an earth sigil. Both sigils are large relative to their small rings. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as soil, sand, and stone, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Collection gathers material from above and around the seal for the spell to use. The two Billow signs turn that material into a fluffy cloud. The two Stillness signs hold the effect static in one place. Solidification makes the material more solid. Inverted Crushing reforms crushed material back toward its original shape. The neat earth sub-seal reinforces the earth working with strong magic, and the neat wind sub-seal adds strong movement of air around the effect. Billow, which loosens matter into soft cloud, directly contradicts Solidification and inverted Crushing, which pack and reform it. Beyond that, the seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier. The earth core, the paired Billow signs, and the paired Stillness signs dominate, while Solidification and inverted Crushing pull against them, so the result is likely unstable. The rough linework weakens the spell and shortens its duration, and the lumpy ring makes its hold fleeting.
effect: Gathers loose soil and sand around the seal and puffs it into a billowing earthen cloud that hangs in place over the seal while currents of air stir around it. The cloud never settles into one form: patches suddenly harden into clumps or snap back into chunks of their original shape while the rest stays soft. The mass flickers between these states before collapsing back into loose dirt well before a steady spell would end.

name: s42_00152.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but a little rough and not perfectly round, with a slightly flattened, lumpy outline on the right side. A Dancing Puppets sign sits upright at the center, a small ring with four little circles at the north, east, south, and west points, each crossed by short strokes. It takes up a moderate portion of the ring, and there is no element sigil. Six Solidification signs, each two small circles joined by a short line, sit near the ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest, and west-northwest positions. The east-southeast one is drawn with a heavier line than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Dancing Puppets sign at the center serves as the core of the seal. It lets the caster consciously control a target object's movement. Without a wind sigil, nothing ties that motion to flight through the air. Its moderate size gives a moderate strength. Solidification makes magic drawn within or connected to it more solid. Six of them spread evenly around the ring firm up the controlled target on all sides without favoring a direction. Solidification is symmetric end to end, so pointing some toward the ring and some toward the center does not appear to change its effect. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they do not conflict. The slightly rough, imperfectly round ring weakens the spell and shortens how long it lasts.
effect: Stiffens the target object into a firm, solid state and lets the caster steer its movements at will while it holds its rigid shape. The hold is somewhat weak and short-lived. The object's firmness and responsiveness waver now and then, and the effect fades sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00153.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed but drawn roughly and noticeably out of round, bulging into a squarish shape. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, about a third of the ring's radius, also drawn roughly. All signs sit near the ring. One Coil sign is at the south-southwest, standing nearly upright, and another lies on its side at the west. A Binding sign, two stacked arcs, sits at the west-northwest with its top toward the center. At the southeast is a small, faintly drawn glyph shaped like a Gathering sign with a small circle on its stem, rotated at an angle. Most signs crowd the west and southwest, leaving the north and east empty.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its modest size gives a moderate-to-low intensity. Coil softens physical matter and does not work on liquids or gases. With fire, it works through heat on nearby solids, not on the flame itself. The southeast glyph matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Gathering, so reading it that way is a guess. As Gathering, it draws material in from the surroundings for the spell to use. Binding halts the target's movement and makes it act as a single unit, so the softened, gathered material would clump into one mass. The three modifiers work in sequence: gather, soften, bind. They do not contradict each other, so the seal is not unstable. The signs are unbalanced toward the southwest, but none are directional. The effect is stronger on that side without being aimed. The rough drawing and poorly rounded ring make the spell weak and short-lived, and it may only take hold briefly.
effect: Gently heats solid material drawn in from around it until it softens, then holds the softened material together as a single lump. The warmth is mild and uneven, working far more on the southwest side than elsewhere. It fades quickly, often letting go before the material has fully softened or fused.

name: s42_00154.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, main ring closed and neatly drawn. A small light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center. Six cross-shaped signs sit about two thirds to four fifths of the way out from the center. Five match Crosshair: north-northwest, west-northwest, east-southeast, south-southwest, and a darker, heavily stroked one at south-southeast. Some point their tops toward the ring and others toward the center. The sixth, at north, is a Crosshair with an extra stroke from its bottom edge, matching no named sign exactly. The east-southeast and south-southeast Crosshairs and the north glyph are drawn somewhat roughly; the rest are neat. Three small closed sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line: a fire sigil at west-northwest, a wind sigil at east-northeast, and a Piercing sign at south. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the core element, and its small size gives modest intensity. The fire sub-seal adds flame and heat, which shares light's domain and reinforces it. The wind sub-seal adds moving air, which can carry the effect. The Piercing sub-seal makes the magic manifest as projectiles. Crosshair makes an effect target whatever its short ends point at. Here the Crosshairs face both inward and outward and are balanced around the ring, so the shots go to several separate targets rather than one direction. The north glyph is read as a Crosshair variant, which is a guess, and its extra stroke would stretch that aim farther along its line. Targeting and projectile shaping do not conflict, and the extra elements support each other, so the seal is coherent. The rougher Crosshairs weaken the aim on those lines.
effect: Fires several small, hot bolts of light, driven along on rushing air, each striking a separate target around the seal. Bolts on a few lines fly less true and hit more weakly, scattering slightly off their mark, and the glow of every bolt dims as it travels.

name: s42_00155.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed but slightly rough. A fire sigil sits upright at the center. It is fairly large, reaching a little under half the ring's radius, and its lines are slightly uneven. A Rain sign sits at the north, about halfway between the center and the ring, in its normal orientation and slightly rough. A Launch sign sits at the east at a similar distance, its peak pointing outward toward the ring and its open side facing the sigil. A second, noticeably smaller Rain sign sits at the west-southwest. It is drawn roughly and appears inverted, facing toward the center. The signs cluster on the north and east sides, leaving the south and southwest empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong intensity, though the rough strokes weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts. The normal Rain sign at the north summons the element, bringing fire down from above. Launch sends the target out in a powerful but brief burst toward where it points, so flame shoots out to the east and quickly runs out. The inverted Rain at the west-southwest does the opposite of normal Rain and creates an area where the element cannot exist or is pushed away. Normal and inverted Rain contradict each other directly. The larger, cleaner northern Rain dominates, while the small, roughly drawn inverted one acts as a weaker counterforce. Launch adds a separate eastward burst. Because of the direct contradiction, the result is likely unstable. The uneven layout biases the whole effect toward the north.
effect: Calls down flames from above, concentrated toward the north of the seal, while a sudden jet of fire bursts out to the east and dies away almost at once. A small patch to the west-southwest pushes the fire back, so the falling flames gutter and sputter unevenly where the two forces meet. The firefall flickers in strength and tends to fizzle out sooner than its size would suggest.

name: s42_00156.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, and there is no element sigil. Eight Binding signs, each a pair of nested arcs, are spread around the seal. Five sit close to the ring at the north, east, south, southwest and west, with the curved top of each facing outward toward the ring. Three sit about halfway out at the northeast, south-southeast and west-northwest, with their tops facing inward toward the center. The southern sign is drawn slightly rougher than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil and an empty center, the seal is not tied to any element and acts on whatever material is within its reach. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. It is the only kind of modifier present, so nothing contradicts it, and eight of them strongly reinforce the hold. Binding's directional type is unknown, so the outward-facing outer signs and inward-facing inner signs are read as working toward the same effect. That reading is a guess. The signs are balanced around the ring, so the hold favors no direction. The single slightly rough sign at the south weakens that side a little.
effect: Stops material over the seal from moving and holds it together as one solid mass, so it can only be moved as a single unit. The hold is firm and even, though it grips a little more loosely along the southern edge, where loose bits occasionally slip free.

name: s42_00157.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed but slightly uneven in shape. A large fire sigil sits upright at the center, neatly drawn and spanning about half the ring's radius. Six Detection signs, each a set of three parallel strokes of increasing length, surround it. Three sit about halfway out, at the southwest, north-northwest and east-southeast, with their tops toward the ring. The southwest one is drawn heavier and rougher than the rest. The other three sit close to the ring, at the east-northeast, southeast and west-southwest, with their tops toward the center. A single Columns sign sits near the ring at the south, with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the center. More signs sit on the southern and eastern side than elsewhere. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Detection is tied to sensing presence, so the six Detection signs make the fire respond to things around the seal rather than burning blindly. Some face outward and some inward, so the sensing covers both the space near the center and the area out by the edge. The lone Columns sign gives the fire a column-shaped area of effect. Because it is unbalanced and sits alone at the south, together with the overall lean of the signs, the column is pushed toward the south-southeast instead of rising straight up. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The slightly rough ring weakens the spell a little and shortens how long it lasts. The rougher southwest Detection sign makes the sensing on that side less reliable.
effect: Produces a strong flame that senses nearby presences and flares toward them as a column of fire, angled toward the south-southeast rather than straight up. The fire burns out somewhat sooner than a neater seal would allow, and it reacts sluggishly or sometimes not at all to things approaching from the southwest.

name: s42_00158.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. A large Regions sign, an upright chevron pointing north, sits at the center in place of a sigil and spans almost half the ring's radius; its strokes are a little rough. A roughly drawn Strengthening sign sits near the ring at the north-northeast, its top toward the ring. A neatly drawn Dispersion sign sits near the ring at the south-southeast, tilted at an angle rather than squared to the ring. Two Convergence triangles are present. One sits near the ring at the west-southwest, flat side toward the ring and point toward the center. The other sits about halfway out at the east-northeast, rotated and drawn a little roughly. More signs cluster on the eastern side than the western side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and acts on whatever material or magic is brought to it. Regions is a directional sign that sets where magic manifests relative to the seal. A single large Regions pointing north sends the effect firmly toward that side. Its size gives that push considerable strength, though its rough lines weaken it somewhat. The two Convergence signs focus the magic toward a single point and pack loose particles tightly together. The Strengthening sign makes the result harder and more durable, but it is drawn roughly, so its contribution is weaker. Dispersion makes magic pour outward, which directly contradicts Convergence's focusing. With two Convergence signs against one Dispersion, focusing dominates, and Regions sets the direction. The opposing pull from Dispersion makes the result likely unstable. The signs lean toward the east, so the effect is biased that way rather than travelling due north.
effect: Draws in whatever material is fed into the seal, packs it into a hard, compact mass and drives it out toward the north, veering somewhat to the east. The mass never holds together cleanly. It keeps shedding material outward in uneven leaks, its hardness varies from spot to spot, and it may loosen or crumble before reaching its full reach.

name: s42_00159.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in thin black line on a white background. The ring is neat but open, with a clear gap at the upper right between the north-northeast and east-northeast. A single wide arc sits at the center, curving downward like a shallow bowl and spanning about half the ring's width. No element sigil is at the center. Four small signs are spaced evenly around it, each roughly two thirds of the way out toward the ring. At the north-northeast is a Gathering-like sign with a small circle on its stem. At the east-southeast is a small right-angled triangle with a circle at one corner. Sights Set signs sit at the south-southwest and west-northwest, each with its diamond end toward the ring and its arrow pointing toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central arc matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Binding drawn with a single curve, so reading it as Binding is a guess. As the core, it would halt the target material's movement and hold it together as one unit. Its large size gives that holding effect a strong hold. The triangle with a circle is closest to the fire sigil, also a guess. Read that way, it supplies the element, and its small size relative to the ring gives only modest heat. The Gathering-like sign with a circle on its stem is closest to Gathering, again a guess. It would draw in material from the surroundings for the spell to use. The two Sights Set signs point inward and let the caster aim the effect at a chosen point or target. The signs are evenly spaced, so no direction is favored. The modifiers support one another rather than conflicting. Because the ring is open, the seal does not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: The seal does not activate while its ring stays open. Once closed, it would draw loose material from its surroundings and bind it into a single solid mass at a point the caster aims at. The bound mass would carry a faint, modest warmth rather than strong heat.

name: s42_00160.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. A Partition sign sits upright at the center, a small triangle atop a flat bar with two outer strokes splaying downward. It is small relative to the ring. Six Stillness signs sit about halfway between the center and the ring, at the southwest, west, north-northwest, north-northeast, east, and south-southeast positions. Each is turned so its top faces the center. They are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Partition takes the center and sets the spell's core behavior. It outlines the borders of an area of effect, and that area extends outward and upward in all directions from the seal. Whatever manifests inside the area is set by the other signs present. Here those are the six Stillness signs, which hold magic in place so the effect stays static in a single location. Because they are evenly balanced around the ring, no side is favored, and the boundary is not pushed in any direction. The small central glyph gives the area a modest strength. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they reinforce each other rather than conflict. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady. Without an element, the spell does not act on fire, water, earth, or wind. It shapes and fixes a space rather than producing a substance.
effect: Marks out a modest bounded zone that rises outward and upward from the seal and stays fixed in place without drifting or shifting. Any magic within that zone is held static, so effects inside it stay put instead of spreading or moving away.

name: s42_00161.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small fire sigil sits upright at the center, about a quarter of the ring's radius in size. Six Crosshair signs surround it. Four sit roughly halfway out at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest, each facing outward toward the ring. A fifth, larger and slightly rougher, sits farther out at the south-southeast. A sixth sits at the east, turned the other way so it faces the center. More signs gather on the southeast side than anywhere else. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Crosshair is a directional sign that makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. The four intercardinal Crosshairs aim the fire at separate points around the seal, and the extra one at the south-southeast adds another target on that side. Because it is a little rough, its share of the effect is weaker and shorter lived. The east Crosshair is reversed to face the center, so it turns its targeting back toward the seal itself. With most signs clustered toward the southeast, the effect favors that side. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the reversed sign changes aim rather than contradicting the others, so the seal holds together.
effect: Sends small, modest flames or bursts of heat to several separate points around the seal, with more of them landing toward the southeast. One flame is drawn back onto the seal's own center. The farthest flame to the south-southeast burns weaker than the rest and gutters out sooner.

name: s42_00162.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed but a little rough. There is no element sigil in the main ring. A small Coil sign, two crossing curved strokes, sits upright at the center. Five Repetition signs sit near the ring at the north-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest, each with its top toward the center. The south-southwest one is drawn heavier and rougher than the others. A single Entwining sign sits near the ring at the east-northeast, rotated almost upside down and drawn roughly. Two small closed sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the south-southeast holds a neatly drawn wind sigil. The one at the north-northwest holds a Collection sign at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Coil sign is the core of the seal, so the spell softens solid matter. Coil works only on physical matter, not liquids or gases. The five Repetition signs keep resetting the affected object to its starting state, and repetition applied to softened matter makes it elastic and springy. These two kinds work together and dominate the seal. The Collection sub-seal gathers material above and around the seal for the spell to use. The wind sub-seal is small but neatly drawn, and it adds a gentle movement of air. The lone Entwining sign makes the affected object wrap around other objects. Its near-inverted rotation has no known effect, but because it sits alone on one side, the wrapping favors the east-northeast. Together the seal stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: softening with springback, collection, air movement and entwining. Coil and Repetition dominate, and Entwining is the weakest part. The result is likely unstable. The rough ring and rough signs also make the spell weaker and shorter-lived.
effect: Gathers loose solid material from around the seal and softens it into a springy, elastic mass that keeps bouncing back to its original shape, nudged along by a light stir of air. The mass tries to wrap around nearby objects, but it only grips unevenly toward one side and often slips loose. The springiness wavers from moment to moment, and the whole effect fades sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00163.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, with no sigil. Five Aeriforms Defined signs, each a fan of three short strokes with a longer middle stroke, sit just inside the inner ring at the north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast, south and west, each with its tip toward the center. The east-northeast sign is a little rougher than the others. Four smaller Aeriforms Defined signs sit in the band between the two rings at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest, each turned at a different angle. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil, the seal has no element, so the spell's character comes entirely from its signs. Aeriforms Defined shares its design with the modifier strokes of the wind sigil and its name with the Aeriforms sigil, so it is tied to air and to making gases apparent or defined. It likely acts as a semi-directional sign, so the varied rotations of the outer signs change only their strength, not the direction of the effect. The five inner signs all point inward and are spread evenly, so the effect gathers within the inner ring instead of pushing to one side. The second ring adds a further layer and strengthens the magic, and the four outer signs set a matching air effect in the band between the rings. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. However, there is no sigil to supply power, so the effect stays mild. The slightly rough sign at the east-northeast gives that side a little less hold than the rest.
effect: Gives shape to the air over the seal, holding a calm, defined body of air inside the inner circle with a thinner layer of air around it. The effect is gentle and spread evenly, though it is held slightly more loosely toward the east-northeast, where the air thins and drifts a little sooner than on the other sides.

name: s42_00164.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is neatly drawn but open, with a gap on the right side at the east-southeast. The center is empty, with no sigil. A Launch sign sits at the northwest with its top toward the ring. At the west is a bracket shape that resembles a Projection sign with its bottom part missing; its top faces the center. A Crushing sign at the east, drawn as a vertical zigzag, has its top toward the center, so it is inverted. At the southeast sits a small ring of hatched strokes resembling a Windows sign, with an extra dot on one side, rotated. At the southwest, near the ring, is a circle crossed by a diagonal line, resembling an Orb sign with an extra stroke. The signs are unevenly spread and lean toward the southwest.
justification: With no sigil, the spell is not tied to any element and acts on whatever material is brought to it. Its strength is not set by a sigil, so the signs alone shape it. Launch sends the target out in a powerful but short-lived burst toward where it points, here toward the northwest. Inverted Crushing does the opposite of crushing, temporarily pulling broken material back into its original shape. The partial bracket is read as Projection, which is a guess, and would push the effect outward from the seal. The hatched ring is read as Windows, also a guess; the extra dot is unexplained. Windows would connect the seal to a space that is not physically joined to it. The slashed circle is read as Orb, another guess, and would hold added material in a spherical space above the seal. That makes five unrelated kinds of modifier: bursting, reforming, projecting, linking spaces and containing. Launch and inverted Crushing are the clearest and dominate. Orb and Windows pull against Launch by holding and relocating the material instead of firing it. Combined with the southwest lean, the result is likely unstable.
