The ring is open, so the seal does not activate.
effect: As drawn, the seal does not activate. If closed, it would gather broken material poured into a sphere above the seal and briefly pull it back toward its original shape. It would then fire that material outward in a short, forceful burst toward the northwest. The burst drifts off line toward the southwest, the reformed shape crumbles unevenly before it settles, and parts of the material flicker away as if passing elsewhere before the spell collapses early.

name: s42_00165.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An Expansion sign of four nested corner brackets sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, with its corners pointing outward. It is fairly large, taking up a bit over a third of the ring's radius. Three Pulling signs sit just inside the ring at the north, east-southeast and southwest points, evenly spaced. Each has its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so the Expansion sign at the center acts as the core of the spell and is not tied to any one element. Expansion is semi-directional. With its corners pointing outward, it makes its target grow, and its fairly large size gives that growth notable strength. Pulling draws the target toward the seal when its arrow points inward, as all three do here. None of them is angled, so they add no twisting. The three Pulling signs are evenly spaced, so the pull is balanced from every side and favors no direction. With no Selection or Diamond sign present, the spell is not limited to the object the seal is drawn on, and the Pulling signs point the effect at things drawn in from around it. The two kinds of modifier work together without contradiction.
effect: Draws nearby objects steadily toward the seal from all sides and makes them grow noticeably larger as they are pulled in. The pull runs straight inward, without twisting.

name: s42_00166.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small upright light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center. Six Partition signs, each a peaked roof shape over a long bar, are spaced evenly about two-thirds of the way out from the center. They sit at the west, north-northwest, northeast, east, south-southeast and southwest, each with its peaked top toward the center. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Partition is a directional sign that outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending both outward and upward. The effect inside that area is set by the glyphs within it, here the light sigil. Six evenly spaced Partition signs all face the center the same way, so together they mark out a closed, roughly six-sided boundary around the sigil with no side favored. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Fills a bounded, roughly six-sided region over the seal with soft light, walled off so it rises upward within that space rather than spreading beyond its edges. The glow is even throughout but modest, and it slowly dims over time.

name: s42_00167.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap across the top running from north toward the northeast. A water sigil sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. A Strengthening sign sits near the ring at the east, its triangle pointing inward toward the center. Three Refuse signs sit at the north, west and south, each with its diamond end toward the center and its crossed legs toward the ring. The north one is drawn more roughly than the rest. Two smaller Refuse signs sit farther out at the southeast and northwest, both reversed, with their diamond ends toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward wherever it points. The three inward-facing Refuse signs pull waste in toward the center from the north, west and south. The two reversed Refuse signs on the southeast-northwest diagonal point outward, so they send collected waste back out toward the ring along that axis. Because the two groups act along different axes, they read as an intake and an outlet working in sequence rather than a direct contradiction. The rougher north sign makes the pull from that side weaker and less reliable than from the west and south. Strengthening makes its target harder and more durable, reinforcing the spell's hold. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and the signs are balanced around the ring, so the seal is not unstable. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: As drawn, it does not activate. Once closed, it would draw dirt and waste out of water from three sides toward the center and then expel the collected refuse outward along a diagonal on two opposite sides, leaving the water cleaner and held firmly in place. The draw from the north side is weaker and patchier than from the others, so some waste on that side lingers.

name: s42_00168.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the bottom between the south-southwest and south-southeast. There is no element sigil. A large Entwining sign stands upright at the center, filling about half the ring's radius. Five Cooling signs, each a short line flanked by pairs of dots, are rotated with their tops toward the ring. Three sit about halfway out, at the west-northwest, southwest and northeast. Two sit close to the ring, at the northwest and southeast. More of the Cooling signs cluster on the upper-left side, so the layout leans toward the west-northwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Entwining sign takes the center and sets the core behavior: it makes the object the seal is drawn on wrap itself around other objects. Its large size at the center gives that wrapping a strong grip. The Cooling signs add a chilling effect to whatever the spell acts on. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. Because the Cooling signs gather more heavily on the upper-left, the cold is stronger toward the west-northwest than on the other sides. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: The spell does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it would make the object it is drawn on wrap firmly around a nearby object and chill it as it holds. The cold would be uneven, biting hardest on the west-northwest side of the wrap and staying milder elsewhere.

name: s42_00169.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small earth sigil, upright and about a quarter of the ring's radius, sits at the center. Three Expansion signs, each made of nested corner brackets with the corners pointing outward, sit near the ring at the west-northwest, northeast and south-southeast. The west-northwest one is drawn in heavier, darker strokes than the other two. Two Pointing signs sit near the ring at the east and south-southwest. The eastern one is drawn a little more roughly. The signs are spaced unevenly and cluster more on the southeast side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this a spell that works on existing solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its small size relative to the ring gives it a modest intensity. Expansion is semi-directional, so its position does not steer the spell. With its corners pointing outward, it makes the target grow. Pointing is non-directional and makes the target take a conical shape. No Columns or other directional sign is present to send the cones anywhere, so they form in place. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction. Because more signs sit toward the southeast, the effect is weighted toward that side. The slightly rough eastern Pointing sign is weaker and shorter lived than the rest of the seal.
effect: Shapes nearby stone or soil into cones and enlarges them, producing modest spikes of earth that rise in place around the seal. The spikes grow larger and fuller toward the southeast. On the eastern side, the points come out less sharp and lose their shape sooner than the others.

name: s42_00170.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Six small Mimicry signs are spread around the seal about three quarters of the way to the ring, at the north-northwest, northeast, east, south-southeast, southwest and west positions. Those at the north-northwest, northeast and southwest have their tops toward the ring, while those at the east, south-southeast and west have their tops toward the center. A single Gathering sign sits at the east-southeast, drawn noticeably larger and with heavier strokes than the other signs. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Mimicry guides or imitates the movements of a target object. With no decorative sigil present, there is no creature design to copy, so the water follows a target's motions in a simpler way. Six Mimicry signs strengthen this imitation. Their mixed orientations are spread evenly around the ring, and no inverted effect is known for this sign, so the mix adds no steering or reversal. Gathering lets a spell draw material in from its surroundings. Drawn large and bold, it pulls water in strongly, so the spell does not need to create its own. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The signs are balanced around the closed, neat ring, so the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Draws in water from the surroundings and gathers it into a mass that follows and copies the movements of a nearby target. The copied motions are simple rather than detailed, and the effect is of moderate strength.

name: s42_00171.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly, with a lumpy outline that bulges into flattened, almost polygonal sides rather than a true circle. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits at the center. It is modest in size relative to the ring and slightly rough. Five Launch signs are spread around it about halfway to the ring. Those at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest have their peaks pointing in toward the center; the north-northwest one is neatly drawn and the others are rough. The Launch signs at the northeast and southeast are rotated off that line, so their peaks point sideways around the ring rather than straight in. The northeast one is drawn with a heavy, uneven stroke. A small, neatly drawn four-lobed Billow sign sits near the ring at the northwest. A slightly rough Binding sign, two stacked arcs bulging toward the ring, sits at the south. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its modest size gives a moderate intensity. Launch generates its effect in a strong but brief burst in the direction it points. Three Launch signs point inward, so their bursts drive toward the center from different sides. The two rotated ones push sideways, adding a skewed, swirling push. Billow normally turns material into a soft, fluffy cloud. Placed off to the side rather than at the center, it shapes the light into a puffy, cloudlike mass instead of setting the spell's core. Binding halts movement and holds material together as one unit, which works directly against the outward-moving bursts of Launch. With five signs, Launch dominates. Binding only briefly holds the gathered light together, and Billow gives it texture, so the result is likely unstable. The rough drawing weakens the spell and shortens how long it lasts. Because the ring is not round enough, the effect is fleeting and the seal may fail to activate at all.
effect: Fires short bursts of light inward from several sides, which collide over the center and puff up into a soft, cloudlike clump of glow that briefly holds together. The bursts arrive unevenly and slightly askew, so the clump wobbles and swirls instead of settling. It flickers, loses its shape within moments and fades quickly, and some attempts fizzle before any light appears.

name: s42_00172.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed and neatly drawn. A small fire sigil sits upright at the center. Six Refuse signs, each a diamond above crossed legs, are spaced evenly just inside the ring at the east, south-southeast, south-southwest, west, north-northwest and northeast. They are turned at differing angles, most lying sideways along the ring rather than pointing straight in or out, and the south-southwest one is drawn a little roughly. Three small sub-seals sit inside the main ring. At the west-northwest is a slightly rough closed ring holding an earth sigil. At the east-northeast is a slightly rough closed ring holding an Entwining sign. At the south is a neat sub-seal whose ring is open, with a gap at its upper left, holding a Solidification sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its small size relative to the ring gives modest flames and heat. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward where it points. These six are balanced around the ring but turned at varied angles, so the waste is gathered toward several points along the edge rather than pushed one way. The earth sub-seal adds control over solid matter such as soil, grit and stone, letting the spell move solid debris as well as burn it. The Entwining sub-seal makes the affected material wrap around other objects. Both sub-seal rings are a little rough, so their contributions are weaker and shorter-lived than the core. The Solidification sub-seal has an open ring, so it does not activate. If closed, it would make the gathered material more solid. The active modifiers work together without contradiction, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Draws waste and loose debris, including dirt and grit, toward several points around the seal's edge and burns it with modest flames. The gathered refuse is wound around nearby objects as it burns, but this wrapping is weak and loosens well before the burning stops. The part meant to compact the remains into a solid mass does not take hold, so the leftover ash and grit stay loose.

name: s42_00173.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. An Entwining sign sits upright at the center at moderate size. Four Strengthening signs are spaced evenly around it, about halfway to the inner ring, at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest positions. Each is rotated to match its position, so all four point their apex outward toward the ring. Above the main seal, at the north and outside the outer ring, a small sub-seal is joined to it by a short line. Its ring is closed but roughly drawn and lumpy rather than round. It holds an earth sigil at its center, drawn a little roughly and filling a fair share of that small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no element sigil, so the Entwining sign at its center sets the core behavior: making a target wrap or twine itself around other objects. The four Strengthening signs make the result harder, stronger and more durable. They are evenly spaced and turned the same way, so the reinforcement applies equally on all sides. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. The linked sub-seal supplies the element. Its earth sigil works on solid substances such as stone, sand and soil, so the entwining acts on earth. Because the sub-seal is small, its ring is rough and not round enough, and its sigil is a little rough, the earth part is weaker and shorter lived than the neatly drawn main seal. The seal uses only two kinds of modifier, and they support each other.
effect: Makes stone, sand or soil wind itself around a target and harden into a tough, durable coil that holds it fast. The earth that feeds the spell comes in weakly and unevenly, so the coil can form thin in places. It tends to loosen and crumble well before the hardening itself would give out, and it may fail to take shape at all.

name: s42_00174.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. An Envelopment sign sits upright at the center: a slanted stroke with short hooks at each end, moderate in size relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Six Concealment signs, each an eight-armed star with small eye marks on its arms, surround it in mirrored pairs across the center. One sits at the north about halfway out and one at the south about halfway out. One sits at the west-northwest and one at the east-southeast, a little farther out. Two larger, heavier ones sit close to the ring at the north-northwest and south-southeast. Several of the Concealment signs, including the two near the ring, are drawn somewhat roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Envelopment sign takes the center and sets the spell's core behavior, which is making an effect surround whatever it targets. The six Concealment signs supply that effect: hiding the target. Each one sits opposite a matching partner, so the signs are balanced and the concealment is spread evenly instead of leaning to one side. The larger pair near the ring and the repeated signs strengthen and widen the hiding effect. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they reinforce each other without contradiction. Some of the signs are slightly rough, which weakens their share of the effect and shortens how long it holds in those parts.
effect: Wraps the target in a concealing shroud that hides it from sight on all sides. The cover is thorough but slightly uneven: in a few places it thins, letting faint glimpses show through, and it fades sooner there than elsewhere.

name: s42_00175.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is a little rough and noticeably lumpy rather than perfectly round. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Three Link signs sit near the ring at the east, south-southeast and north-northwest, each rotated so its top faces the center. The east one is drawn more roughly than the other two. At the west point sits a small, neatly drawn octagon with an X inside, in lighter line, which matches no known sign exactly. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates air without creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Link identifies objects that broke off from, were removed from, or were made from the same source and creates a connection between them, and three of them spread that linking evenly around the seal. The octagon with an X is closest to Selection, a cross inside an enclosing shape. This is a guess, and under that reading it confines the spell to the object the seal is drawn on. Together the seal would use air to act on the marked object and the pieces linked to it. The signs are balanced, so no direction is favored. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they do not contradict each other. The rough lines and the uneven, not fully round ring make the spell weaker and shorter lived than a clean seal.
effect: Stirs currents of air around the object the seal is drawn on and links that object to pieces that came from the same source, so the air carries them toward one another. The currents are uneven and gusty rather than steady, the linked pieces drift together haltingly, and the effect fades sooner than it should.

name: s42_00176.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An upright earth sigil sits at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Six Strengthening signs, each a triangle crossed by a bar, are spaced evenly about three quarters of the way out, at the south-southwest, west, northwest, north-northeast, east, and southeast. Each has its apex pointing toward the center. The west, north-northeast, and southeast signs are drawn a little more roughly than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on existing solid matter such as stone, soil, sand, and wood rather than creating it. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Strengthening makes objects stronger, harder, and more durable. All six signs share one orientation and are evenly spread, so no direction is favored and the reinforcement applies equally on all sides. There is only one kind of modifier, so nothing conflicts. The three slightly rough signs weaken their share of the effect a little, making the hardening less even on those sides and shorter lived there.
effect: Hardens and reinforces solid earth, stone, or wood around the seal, making it tougher and more resistant to breaking with a moderate degree of strength. The reinforcement is slightly patchier toward the west, north-northeast, and southeast, where it holds a little less firmly and fades somewhat sooner than elsewhere.

name: s42_00177.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring: a water sigil on the left and a light sigil on the right. At the north-northwest is a third element glyph: an S inside a circle ringed by dots, a variant of the wind sigil. Just beyond it, near the ring at the north, is a Refuse sign with its diamond end toward the center. A Billow sign sits at the west-northwest. A Partition sign sits near the ring at the northeast. A Pointing sign sits at the east, turned on its side. An inverted Rain sign sits near the ring at the southeast. An Aeriforms Defined sign sits at the southwest. More signs are grouped toward the north and northeast than elsewhere. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water and light sigils share the center and act as two cores, so the spell works with water and light. Light fades over time. Both sigils are small, so the intensity is modest. The wind-variant glyph is read as closest to Whorling Wind, which is a guess; it would add a rotating movement of air. Billow turns material into a fluffy cloud. Aeriforms Defined relates to air and supports the airy, cloud-like form. Refuse gathers unwanted material toward where it points, and here that is the center. Partition marks the edge of the area of effect. Pointing gives the result a conical shape. Inverted Rain makes an area where the target cannot exist or is pushed away, which works against Billow and Refuse gathering material inward. The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier and contains this direct contradiction, so the result is likely unstable. The two central sigils dominate. Billow and the airy signs set the form, and the crowding of signs toward the north-northeast tilts the effect that way.
effect: Forms a faintly glowing, misty cloud of water that swirls and tapers into a cone leaning toward the north-northeast, while drawing grit and debris toward its middle. At the same time, water is pushed out of part of the area, so the cloud thins and bulges unevenly and keeps tearing apart as it forms. The glow dims steadily, and the cloud tends to collapse well before it settles into a stable shape.

name: s42_00178.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn a little roughly. A small water sigil, about a quarter of the ring's radius, sits upright at the center and is neatly drawn. Six Crushing zigzags are spaced around the seal, near the ring: at the north-northwest, northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest, and west-northwest. Five are drawn in the normal orientation at varying rotations. The one at the west-northwest is inverted. At the west-southwest, slightly closer to the center, sits a small glyph that matches no known sign exactly. It looks like a Gathering sign with a small circle on its stem, with its forked top toward the center. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Crushing breaks its target into smaller and smaller pieces. Paired with water, which has no solid form to pulverize, it would break the water into fine droplets. Crushing is semi-directional, so the rotations do not steer the spell. Inverting it reverses its effect, so the inverted sign at the west-northwest tries to pull broken material back together. This directly contradicts the other five. The five normal Crushing signs dominate, and the single inverted one pulls against them, so the result is likely unstable. The glyph at the west-southwest is read as Gathering, which is a guess, with the circle as an unidentified addition. Gathering actively draws in material from the surroundings for the spell to use. Its fork points inward, so it would pull nearby water into the seal. The even spacing means the shattering has no favored direction. The slightly rough ring makes the spell a little weaker and shorter lived.
effect: Draws in nearby water and shatters it into a fine, misty spray of tiny droplets around the seal at modest strength. The spray does not settle. Patches of mist keep briefly merging back into larger drops before breaking apart again, so the cloud pulses and thickens unevenly. The effect fades somewhat sooner than a cleaner drawing would allow.

name: s42_00179.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. It has two irregular, slightly rough rings. The outer ring is open, with a clear gap at the upper left. The inner ring sits just inside it and looks uneven and not fully round. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center. It is neatly drawn and small relative to the ring. Six Binding signs, each a large arc over a smaller arc, are spaced evenly around the inside of the inner ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest, west and north-northwest. Each has the curved top of its arcs facing the center. Five are drawn neatly, and the one at the south-southeast is a little rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. Six Binding signs gather the light into one cohesive, unmoving mass. Their even spacing favors no side, and no directional sign is present, so the light is not projected anywhere. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. However, the rough, not quite round rings work against it and make the effect weaker and shorter lived. The single rough Binding sign slightly loosens the hold on that side. The outer ring is open, so the seal does not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it gathers light into a single, still glow that holds together in place over the seal instead of spreading or drifting. The glow is modest and fades over time, and it flickers and loosens unevenly at the edges before dying out sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00180.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils sit side by side near the center, both modest in size relative to the ring. On the left is a light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, drawn slightly rough. On the right is an earth sigil, drawn neatly. Six Levitation signs surround them, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. Four sit close to the ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast and west-southwest; the southern two touch it. Two slightly smaller ones sit closer in, at the east and west-northwest. They are spread fairly evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes the spell act on solid matter such as stone, soil and sand, and the light sigil adds the creation of light, which fades over time. Both are about a quarter of the ring's radius, so the intensity is moderate. The light sigil's slightly rough drawing makes the glow a little weaker and shorter lived than the earth effect. Levitation floats its target into the air, and its inward-pointing arrows are its usual orientation. Balanced Levitation shapes the floating material into a sphere. Here the six signs are evenly spread, so no direction is favored. The two shorter inner signs carry slightly less lift than the outer four but do not unbalance the whole. Only one kind of modifier is present alongside two compatible sigils, so the seal is not contradictory.
effect: Lifts nearby stone or soil into the air and holds it hovering above the seal as a rounded, sphere-like mass that gives off light. The earth holds steady, but the glow is somewhat weaker and dims over time, fading before the floating mass comes down.

name: s42_00181.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large, reaching about two fifths of the way to the ring. Four Piercing signs, each a straight stroke through a small diamond, are scattered around it at different distances: one near the ring at the northeast, drawn small and neat; one at the west-northwest, larger and closer in; one at the south, about midway out; and one near the ring at the southwest, drawn with a thicker, slightly rough line. The signs are not evenly spaced, and more of them sit on the western and southern side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Piercing is non-directional and makes the magic manifest as projectiles, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many are made, so four signs give four projectiles. Because Piercing has no direction, the uneven placement does not aim the spell. There is no Columns, Regions, Crosshair or Sights Set sign to steer the projectiles, so they are not sent toward any chosen target. The roughly drawn southwest sign is weaker than the others, so the projectile it governs is less reliable. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Forms four strong bolts of fire that shoot out from the seal. With nothing to aim them, the bolts fly off in loose, scattered directions rather than at a chosen target. One bolt comes out thinner than the rest and burns out sooner.

name: s42_00182.png
description: A fully visible, neatly drawn seal on a clean background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the lower right between the east-southeast and south-southeast signs. A small upright fire sigil sits at the center, about a quarter of the ring's radius. Five Diamond signs surround it. Three sit near the ring at the north, east-southeast, and west-southwest, and two sit closer in at the northeast and south-southeast. Each is tilted at its own angle. Nothing is hidden or cut off.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives it a modest intensity. Diamond likely makes a spell act only on what lies inside the container the seal is drawn on, leaving the container itself untouched. Diamond has the same shape whichever way it points, so the differing tilts and distances should not change its effect. The five signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored and the effect spreads evenly through the contents. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing in the seal conflicts. The open ring means the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: As drawn, the spell does not activate. Once closed, it would gently heat whatever is held inside the vessel it is drawn on, warming the contents evenly while leaving the vessel itself unheated and unburned.

name: s42_00183.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both open. The outer ring has a wide gap at the upper right, between north and east. The inner ring has a smaller gap on its east side. A water sigil sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring and drawn a little roughly. Three Refuse signs, each a small diamond on a crossed stem, are placed unevenly. One sits inside the inner ring at the northwest, drawn bold, with its top toward the ring. A second sits on the outer ring at the west-southwest and a third on the outer ring at the east-northeast near the gap, both with their tops toward the center. The signs cluster toward the northwest side, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Its slightly rough drawing makes the effect a little weaker and shorter lived. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Refuse is a directional sign that collects unwanted material toward where it points. The two outer Refuse signs point inward and pull waste toward the center. The northwest sign points outward and pushes waste toward the ring on that side. Because these directly contradict each other, the inward pair dominates by number and the outward northwest sign pulls against it, so the result is likely unstable. The uneven placement also biases the effect toward the northwest. Both rings are open, so the seal will not activate until they are closed.
effect: It does not activate while its rings are open. Once closed, it would draw out dirt and debris from nearby water and gather it toward the center of the seal. Part of the waste would keep drifting off toward the northwest instead, so the gathered pile shifts and spreads unevenly, and the sorting wavers and fades sooner than it should.

name: s42_00184.png
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a white background. The ring is closed but lumpy and somewhat uneven rather than truly round. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Three Cooling signs, each a short vertical stroke between two pairs of dots, sit near the ring at the north, the south, and the southwest. The southwest one is tilted diagonally with its top toward the ring. Two Orb signs, each a circle crossed by a line, sit at the west and east. The western one is upright and more roughly drawn, and the eastern one is rotated about 45 degrees. Most of the strokes are slightly shaky, and the signs cluster more heavily toward the southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong glow, and light from this sigil naturally diminishes over time. The two Orb signs are non-directional, so the rotation of the eastern one changes nothing. Together they define a spherical space above the seal where the spell's material gathers from the bottom up. The three Cooling signs make the spell cool things down, so the gathered light carries a chill rather than heat. Cooling has never been shown to depend on direction, but the signs are unbalanced. Two sit on the southern side, one of them at the southwest, so the cooling is weighted toward that side. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without conflict. The shaky strokes and the slightly out-of-round ring weaken the seal and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Forms a sphere of fairly bright, cold light above the seal that chills whatever is placed inside it. The chill is uneven, noticeably colder toward the southwest side of the sphere. The glow fades sooner than usual, flickering and thinning as it weakens before it gives out.

name: s42_00185.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring. A light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes, sits on the left. An earth sigil sits on the right. A single Windows sign, drawn as a small circle lined with hatch marks, sits at the southwest about halfway to the ring and is slightly rough. A Binding sign of two stacked arcs sits at the northeast near the inner ring, with its larger arc bulging toward the center; it is also slightly rough. A second, neatly drawn Binding sign sits at the south, rotated so its arcs bulge toward the east. More of the signs sit in the lower half of the seal than the upper. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the material as solid matter such as stone, soil and sand. The light sigil adds light, so the spell both acts on matter and produces a glow. Both sigils are small relative to the ring, which gives a modest intensity, and the second ring adds strength to the core spell. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. Two Binding signs reinforce this. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined. Here it appears as a single small sign rather than a full lining ring, so the connection is narrow. The signs lean toward the south, so the effect is weighted toward that side of the seal. The Windows sign and one Binding sign are slightly rough, which weakens and shortens their part of the effect a little. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other.
effect: Binds loose stone or soil into a single glowing mass that holds together and moves as one piece. A small window links that mass to another location, so it can be seen or reached from elsewhere. The effect gathers more heavily on the southern side of the seal. The glow and the window are modest, and the window tends to narrow and fade a little sooner than the binding.

name: s42_00186.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is slightly irregular and open, with a wide gap at the lower right between the south and southeast. A neatly drawn fire sigil sits at the center, modest in size relative to the ring. A neat Rain sign sits near the ring at the north-northeast. A thick, heavily stroked Regions sign sits at the east-northeast, pointing outward toward the ring. A roughly drawn Binding sign, two nested arcs turned on their side, sits at the east-southeast, closer to the center than the other signs. A slightly rough Envelopment sign sits at the south-southeast, right beside the gap in the ring. A small, slightly rough Pointing sign sits near the ring at the southwest. Most signs crowd the eastern half, so the layout leans toward the east-southeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame. Its modest size gives a moderate intensity. Rain, drawn upright and neatly, summons that fire as a fall from above. The outward-pointing Regions sign pushes the magic outside the ring rather than onto its surface. These two are the most cleanly drawn signs and dominate the seal. Binding would hold the material together as a single unit, which works against Rain's scattered fall. It is also the roughest sign, so its pull is weak. Envelopment would make the fire wrap around a target, and Pointing would shape it into cones, two further unrelated shaping demands. Five unrelated kinds of modifier are stacked here, and Binding contradicts Rain, so the result is likely unstable. Because the signs are unbalanced toward the east-southeast, the effect drifts that way. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate. Its rough, irregular line also means that even once closed, the effect would be fleeting.
effect: As drawn, it does not activate. If closed, it would bring a moderate fall of fire down outside the seal, drifting toward the east-southeast. The flames would sporadically clump into pointed cones or try to wrap around whatever they strike, but never hold one form, and the downpour would sputter out quickly.

name: s42_00187.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits at the center, modest in size relative to the ring, with a Selection sign just to its east, touching the edge of a sub-seal. Four Purification signs sit near the ring at the north, northeast, southeast and southwest, each turned at a different angle. At the west-northwest, near the ring, is a glyph of crossing spokes that matches no known sign exactly. Three small sub-seals sit inside the main ring. The one at the northwest holds a small light sigil, and its ring is open on the left side. The one at the south-southwest holds a wind sigil, ring closed. The one at the east holds a single Regions sign pointing north, ring closed, drawn a little roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter, and its modest size gives a moderate intensity. Selection confines the effect to the object the seal is drawn on. Purification separates waste from water. It is asymmetric and largely unpredictable, and it sits awkwardly with an earth spell, so here it would at best pull grit and impurities out of the solid surface. Four of these signs at scattered angles make it the strongest modifier, but they also add uneven, unpredictable behavior. The spoked glyph most closely resembles Concealment without its eyes, which is a guess, and would partly hide the affected matter. The wind sub-seal adds moving air. The Regions sub-seal pushes its part of the effect toward the north, and its rough drawing makes that push weaker and shorter lived. The light sub-seal has an open ring, so it adds nothing. The seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: confinement, purification, concealment, wind and direction. The earth sigil and Selection dominate, Purification shapes most of the behavior, and the wind and direction parts come second, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Works on the stone or earthen object the seal is drawn on, shaking loose grit and impurities from its surface and blowing them off in gusts of air, mostly toward the north. The cleansing hits some patches and skips others, the gusts sputter and die out early, and parts of the surface sometimes dim or blur briefly as if partly hidden before settling back.

name: s42_00188.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. An upright Immobility sign sits at the center and is large, reaching about half the inner ring's radius. Four Aeriforms Defined signs, each three short strokes, sit about two thirds of the way out at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast and west-southwest positions, each with its top toward the ring. They are evenly spaced around the seal. The north-northwest sign is drawn a little more roughly than the others. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Immobility sign at the center acts as the core and sets the spell's behavior: the target becomes immovable relative to the seal and holds its shape as if frozen. Its large size points to a strong hold. Aeriforms Defined shares its design with the strokes on the wind sigil and its name with the aeriforms sigil, which creates air, so it ties the effect to gases rather than solids. Four of them evenly spaced add no direction, so the effect is centered on the seal. The second ring adds strength and further effect to the core spell. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The slightly rough north-northwest sign weakens the effect a little on that side.
effect: Fixes a pocket of air around the seal in place, holding it still and firm as if frozen so it keeps its shape and moves with the seal. The hold is strong overall but slightly softer toward the north-northwest, where the still air can drift a little.

name: s42_00189.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The center of the main seal is empty, with no sigil. Nine Columns signs are spread evenly around the seal. Three larger, bolder Columns signs sit at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest, each with its crossbar against the inner ring and its stem reaching toward the center. Three thinner Columns signs sit inside the inner ring at the north-northeast, west and south-southeast, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem toward the center. Three more small Columns signs sit in the band between the two rings: the one at east-southeast faces the center like the others, while the ones at northwest and south-southwest are inverted, with their crossbars toward the center. Outside the main ring at the north-northwest, a small closed sub-seal is joined to the outer ring by a short line. It holds a single upright light sigil of moderate size relative to its own ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no sigil, so its element comes from the linked sub-seal, whose light sigil makes this a light spell. That sigil is moderate relative to its small ring, so the effect has moderate intensity. The second ring inside the main ring adds strength to the core spell. Columns gives the magic a column-shaped area of effect, and more Columns signs widen its range and the amount of magic produced. Because the signs are balanced around the ring, no side is favored, so the column rises straight up rather than leaning. The two inverted Columns in the outer band make part of the magic spread out horizontally, much like Dispersion, around the base of the column. This is a variation on the same modifier rather than a contradiction, so the seal holds steady. Both rings are closed and neatly drawn, so the spell activates and lasts.
effect: Raises a broad, upright column of light straight up from the seal, with some of the light spilling outward horizontally around its base. The light is moderately bright and gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00190.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, about a third of the ring's radius in size, with slightly rough strokes. Six Dispersion signs surround it. Four sit at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest, each with its stem toward the center and its curve facing outward toward the ring; the northeast and southwest pair sit close to the ring, while the southeast and northwest pair sit somewhat closer to the center. The other two sit at the north-northeast and south-southwest, about halfway out, and are drawn with heavier strokes and turned roughly crosswise to the line from the center, on opposite sides of the seal. A few of the signs are slightly rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and manipulates flame and heat. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Dispersion makes a seal's magic pour or leak outward rather than beam in one direction. The four intercardinal Dispersion signs face inward in the same way and are evenly spaced, so the outflow is balanced on all sides. The two crosswise Dispersion signs sit opposite each other. If Dispersion responds to angle the way directional signs do, they would bend part of the outflow sideways, giving it a faint turning motion; this is a guess, since Dispersion's type is not known. Because they are opposed and balanced, they do not pull the effect toward any one side. Only one kind of modifier is used, so the seal is not contradictory. The slightly rough sigil and a few rough signs make it a little weaker and shorter lived than a perfectly drawn version.
effect: Pours moderate flame and heat outward from the seal evenly in every direction, spreading as a loose wash of warmth and fire rather than a focused jet. The outflow may curl slightly as it spreads. The flames flicker a little unevenly and die down somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00191.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small earth sigil sits upright at the center. Six Refuse signs, each a diamond above a crossed X, surround it. Two sit about two-thirds of the way out, at the northeast and southwest, with their diamond tops facing the center. Three more sit close to the ring at the north, west-northwest and south, with their tops facing the ring. A sixth, smaller glyph sits near the ring at the east-southeast, also facing the ring. It is a Refuse sign with a tiny light-like mark attached to it. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell works on solid matter such as soil, sand and stone. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward where it points. The two inner signs point inward, drawing debris toward the center. The three outer signs and the variant point toward the ring, pushing debris outward. These directly oppose each other. The four outward-facing signs outnumber the two inward ones, so the outward sweep dominates, and the result is likely unstable. The east-southeast glyph matches no known sign exactly. The closest reading is Refuse with a small light sigil attached, and this is a guess. Read that way, it sweeps debris outward like the others and adds a faint glow where that material collects. The balanced spacing means no single side is favored.
effect: Separates unwanted grit, pebbles and debris from soil or stone and sweeps most of it outward toward the edge of the seal. Some of the debris is tugged back toward the center instead, so it shuffles back and forth unevenly before settling, mostly along the rim with a small pile in the middle. A faint glow marks one spot on the rim where debris gathers, and the overall sorting stays gentle rather than forceful.

name: s42_00192.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn as two concentric rings, both closed. A small fire sigil sits upright at the center. Eight Launch signs surround it. Four sit in the band between the two rings: at the north, northeast and south they point their tips toward the center, and at the west the tip points outward toward the ring. The other four sit inside the inner ring and are drawn with bolder strokes. At the northeast and southwest their tips point toward the center, and at the west-northwest and east-southeast they point outward toward the ring. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell makes flame and heat, and its small size relative to the ring keeps the intensity modest. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Launch generates the magic in the direction it points as a powerful but short-lived burst. Five of the eight Launch signs point inward and three point outward, so they directly oppose each other. Because the signs are spread evenly, no single side is favored. The inward-pointing majority dominates and concentrates the burst at the center, while the three outward signs pull part of the flame away toward the edge. That conflict makes the result likely unstable.
effect: Throws a sudden, brief burst of modest flame up from the center of the seal, reaching high before it quickly runs out. Smaller jets of fire flare sideways toward the edge at uneven moments, splitting off from the main burst so that it wavers and dies sooner than it otherwise would.

name: s42_00193.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An upright earth sigil sits at the center, fairly large relative to the ring. Four Rain signs, each a small square with spiky strokes at its corners, sit about halfway out at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest points. A fifth Rain sign sits closer to the ring at the east, rotated relative to the others and drawn with heavier, rougher strokes. Three Stretch signs, each an open arch with small feet, sit just inside the ring at the north, west and south-southeast. The north and south-southeast arches have their tops toward the ring, while the west arch has its top toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell moves existing solid matter such as soil, sand and stone rather than creating it. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Rain summons the spell's material so it falls from above in the area around the seal. Rain is semi-directional but radially symmetric, so only an inside-out flip would invert it. The rotated east Rain is not flipped and still acts as normal Rain, but its rough drawing makes its share of the effect weaker and less even. Stretch turns solid matter that contacts the seal into long, flexible ribbons. It is most likely non-directional, so the differing orientations of the three arches do not change it. The signs are balanced around the ring, and their two kinds of modifier work together without contradiction.
effect: Draws up nearby soil and stone and lets it fall back over the surrounding area like a heavy rain, while solid matter that touches the seal is drawn out into long, flexible ribbons. The downpour is fairly strong and even overall, but it thins out and falls patchily on the east side.

name: s42_00194.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Pulling signs are spaced around it, all inverted with their arrowheads pointing outward toward the ring. Those at the north-northwest, northeast and south-southeast sit close to the ring, and a smaller one at the south-southwest sits partway in. Four Aeriforms Defined signs, each a cluster of short parallel strokes, sit at middle distance. Those at the north-northwest, northeast and east all face the same way. The one at the west-southwest is turned the opposite way relative to the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell makes flame and heat, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Aeriforms Defined shares its design with the wind sigil's modifiers and ties the spell to air, so the heat is carried as air rather than open flame. Pulling draws its target toward the seal when its arrow points inward. All four Pulling signs here point outward, so the effect reverses and pushes things away from the seal. The signs are balanced around the ring, so the push favors no direction. The west-southwest Aeriforms Defined sign faces opposite the other three. Since it is likely semi-directional, it partly opposes them. The three matching signs dominate, but the effect is likely unstable on that side.
effect: Produces a moderate wave of hot air that pushes outward from the seal evenly in all directions, shoving loose objects and smoke away from it. On the west-southwest side the outflow wavers, thinning and sputtering in uneven pulses instead of holding steady like the rest.

name: s42_00195.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. At the center is an unfamiliar sigil: an S-curve inside a small circle, ringed by eight evenly spaced dots. It is moderate in size relative to the ring and its lines are slightly uneven. Four Immobility signs sit about two-thirds of the way out, at the northeast, northwest, southeast and southwest points. Each has its curved top toward the ring and its base line toward the center, and the southeast one is a little rough. Four Crosshair signs sit just inside the ring at the north, east, south and west points. The east Crosshair is drawn heavier and rougher than the others. The signs are evenly balanced around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central glyph matches no named sigil exactly. Its S-curve most closely resembles the wind sigil, so reading it as a wind variant is a guess. Under that reading the spell acts on air, and the circle and dots around the S suggest air held within a bounded space rather than blown freely. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Immobility makes its target immovable relative to the seal, holding its shape as if frozen. With four of them evenly spaced, that hold is applied evenly on all sides. Crosshair makes the effect target whatever its short ends point at. With four of them at the cardinal points facing outward, the effect is aimed at separate points in four directions instead of spreading as a general field. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The ring is closed and round, so the spell activates. The slightly rough sigil and a few rough signs weaken it a little and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Locks the air at four points around the seal, one in each cardinal direction, into fixed, motionless pockets that hold their position relative to the seal like invisible stoppers. The hold is moderately strong but lets go somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would. The eastern pocket is the first to loosen and drift.

name: s42_00196.png
description:
A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn as two concentric rings. Both rings are open: the outer ring has a wide gap on the west side, and the inner ring has a gap at the lower left. Two small sigils sit side by side at the center, each about a quarter of the ring radius: a wind sigil on the left and a water sigil on the right. Seven signs are spread evenly around the seal.
- **Between the two rings:**
  - A small Repetition sign at the northwest.
  - A Gathering sign at the north-northeast, its arrow pointing in toward the center.
  - A Convergence triangle at the east, its flat side toward the center and its point toward the ring.
  - A Glaives sign at the east-southeast, its prongs facing inward.
- **Inside the inner ring:**
  - A Crosshair sign at the southeast.
  - A Mimicry sign at the south, its top toward the center.
  - A Sights Set sign at the west-southwest, its arrow pointing outward toward the ring.

Three smaller sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each about a third of its radius and each joined to it by a short line. Each sub-seal ring is closed.
- At the northwest, a roughly drawn ring holds a somewhat rough earth sigil.
- At the east, a slightly rough ring holds a large, neat light sigil.
- At the south-southwest, a neat ring holds a Repetition sign in place of a sigil.
justification:
The wind and water sigils share the center, so the spell moves air and works with water. Both sigils are small, which gives a modest intensity.

The modifiers fall into several groups:
- **Material:** Gathering points inward and draws material from the surroundings. Convergence then focuses it toward a single point. Its point faces outward rather than in its usual inward position, so that focusing is less reliable.
- **Targeting:** Sights Set and Crosshair work together. Sights Set lets the caster aim the effect, and Crosshair locks it onto whatever its short ends point at.
- **Unrelated modifiers:**
  - Glaives set how deeply the magic embeds into flesh.
  - Repetition keeps resetting what the spell affects to its earlier state.
  - Mimicry imitates movement, but there is no decorative sigil for it to copy, so it has nothing defined to mimic.

The linked sub-seals each add an effect:
- The earth sub-seal adds a hold on solid matter. Its rough ring and rough sigil make that part weak and short lived.
- The light sub-seal adds a fairly strong light, since its sigil is large for its ring. The slightly rough ring makes that light less steady.
- The neat Repetition sub-seal reinforces the time-resetting effect.

The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier: gathering, targeting, embedding, time-resetting, mimicry, and the added earth and light. The wind and water core dominates, together with the Gathering and Convergence pair and the aiming pair. Glaives, Repetition and Mimicry pull in other directions, so the result is likely unstable.

Both main rings are open, so the seal will not activate until they are closed.
effect: The spell does not activate while its rings are open. Once closed, it would draw moisture and air from its surroundings into a modest, wind-driven stream of water aimed at a chosen target, which it tries to drive into the target's flesh with a faint glow. The stream's focus keeps loosening and the aim drifts. It repeatedly snaps back to its starting state and twitches in aimless imitating motions, while the glow flickers and any hold on stone or soil fades almost at once.

name: s42_00197.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but lumpy and noticeably out of round, bulging at the corners. A roughly drawn water sigil sits at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Five Dispersion signs surround it at the west-southwest, north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast and south-southwest, each with its stem toward the ring and its curve facing the center. The south-southwest one is drawn noticeably larger than the others, and all five are rough. A neatly drawn octagon with an X inside, matching no known sign exactly, sits at the north-northeast. An Entwining sign sits at the west. At the east is a glyph shaped like a Columns sign with a small circle at the foot of its stem. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity, though its rough drawing weakens it. Five Dispersion signs make the water pour or leak outward rather than beam in one direction. Because they are spaced around the ring, the outflow has no favored side. The octagon with an X is closest to Selection, a guess, which would confine the effect to the object the seal is drawn on. That directly contradicts the outward pouring of Dispersion. Entwining makes the magic wrap around other objects. The eastern glyph sits between Columns and Solidification; reading it as a column that firms its material is also a guess. This stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier, plus a direct contradiction. The water sigil and the five Dispersion signs dominate by number, while the confining, wrapping and firming parts pull against them, so the result is likely unstable. The rough signs make it weaker and shorter lived, and the out-of-round ring makes the effect fleeting or may stop it from activating at all.
effect: Water leaks outward from the seal in a modest, uneven spill on all sides, sometimes pooling back against the drawn surface instead of flowing away. Strands of the water intermittently try to wrap around nearby objects and briefly stiffen before slackening. The flow sputters and collapses after a few moments, and some attempts to cast it produce nothing at all.

name: s42_00198.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the upper right between the north and northeast signs. A small light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center and is small relative to the ring. Six Concealment signs, each an eight-armed star with small eye marks on its arms, are evenly spaced near the ring at the north, northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest positions, each with its top toward the ring. The west-northwest sign is drawn a little rougher than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and manipulates light, and its small size gives a modest intensity. Concealment hides a target. Paired with light, the seal turns its light toward hiding things rather than illuminating them, bending or withholding light so that what lies within its reach is masked. Six Concealment signs spread evenly around the ring favor no direction, so the hiding effect covers the area around the seal uniformly. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The slightly rough west-northwest sign makes that side a little weaker than the rest. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: It does not activate while the ring is open. If closed, it would wrap the area around the seal in a modest veil of light that hides whatever lies within it, with the masking slightly thinner and less reliable on the west-northwest side. Like other light magic, the effect would gradually fade over time.

name: s42_00199.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil, an S-curve between two teardrops, sits upright at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring, its strokes slightly rough. Five small four-lobed glyphs are spaced around it. Four of them are Billow signs, at the south, northeast, southeast, and southwest. The south one sits close to the ring, and the other three sit a little farther in. The fifth sits near the ring at the north. It looks like a Billow sign, but its halves are drawn as mirror copies of each other rather than as one continuous shape. The northwest, west, and east stretches hold no signs. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates, collects, or creates water, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. Billow is a non-directional sign that turns available material into a fluffy cloud. Placed around a water sigil, several Billow signs turn the spell's water into soft, cloud-like masses. The mirrored northern glyph matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Billow, so reading it as a variant Billow is a guess, and under that reading it adds to the same cloud-forming effect. Billow is non-directional, so the uneven spacing does not push the effect toward any side. All the modifiers are of one kind and do not conflict. The slightly rough sigil makes the spell a little weaker and shorter-lived than a cleanly drawn one would be.
effect: Gathers water at the seal and puffs it into soft, fluffy clouds that billow up around it. The clouds are moderately sized and thin out somewhat sooner than they otherwise would, with some patches loosening back into damp mist before the rest.

name: s42_00200.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed. Both rings are noticeably lumpy and out of round, the outer one especially. An Expansion sign, four nested corner brackets with their corners pointing outward, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil and is a little over a quarter of the ring's radius in size. Four smaller Expansion signs, also with their corners pointing outward, sit about halfway to the ring at the northwest, north-northeast, east-southeast and south-southwest, each tilted at a different angle. The north-northeast sign is drawn in bold strokes, while the other three are thinner and slightly sketchy. There is no element sigil and no other sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Expansion sign takes the core position and sets the spell's purpose: changing the size of a target. Expansion is semi-directional, so its tilt does not steer the spell. Only its inversion matters, and every Expansion here has its corners pointing outward, which makes the target grow. The four outer Expansion signs repeat and reinforce that same effect, and they are balanced around the ring, so the growth is even on all sides. The second ring strengthens the magic. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. However, both rings are too far out of round, so the effect is fleeting and may fail to start. There is no Selection or Diamond sign to say whether the spell acts on the object it is drawn on or on something nearby.
effect: Makes its target swell rapidly and evenly in every direction to a much larger size. The growth flickers as it takes hold and lasts only briefly before the target shrinks back to its normal size. Sometimes the spell fails to start at all.

name: s42_00201.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but roughly drawn and somewhat lumpy rather than truly round. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, large relative to the ring, at about half its radius. Seven Pulling signs surround it. Four sit near the ring at the north, east, south-southwest and west, and two sit closer in at the north-northwest and southwest. All six are inverted, with their stems toward the center and their arrowheads pointing outward toward the ring. A seventh Pulling sign near the ring at the southwest is drawn in its normal orientation, heavier than the rest, with its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. A small, faint Piercing sign lies at the south-southeast, turned on its side. Most strokes are shaky, and the signs cluster toward the southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its large size relative to the ring points to a strong effect. Pulling is directional. Pointing inward, it draws the target toward the seal, so the six inverted signs should push the flame away instead. Three of these sit on the southwest side, so the push is strongest in that direction. The single normal Pulling sign at the southwest pulls inward against that same push, which directly contradicts the inverted signs. The outward push dominates because it outnumbers the inward pull. Piercing makes the magic manifest as projectiles, and a single Piercing sign gives a single projectile. The contradiction on the southwest side makes the result likely unstable. The rough strokes and the uneven ring weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts, so it may only flare briefly.
effect: Forms flame into a single bolt and shoves it away from the seal, with the strongest thrust toward the southwest. The bolt wobbles and flickers as it travels, jerking back toward the seal before lurching outward again. It often burns out early or falls short, so it hits much weaker than its size suggests.

name: s42_00202.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils share the center: a light sigil (a diamond inside a square with four spokes) on the left and a slightly smaller wind sigil (an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes) on the right. Both are of moderate size relative to the ring. Four Stretch signs, each an arch with small outturned feet, sit about three-quarters of the way out at the east-northeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and north-northwest positions. Each has its curved top toward the ring and its open side toward the center. Two Cooling signs, each a slanted stroke with a pair of dots on either side, sit at the north-northeast and south-southwest, set diagonally across from each other. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes the seal create and shape light, and the wind sigil adds the movement of air, so the light is carried and moved rather than held still. Both are of moderate size, which gives a moderate intensity. Stretch, placed around the central sigils as it is meant to be, draws whatever the spell acts on into long, flexible ribbons. It normally acts on solids, but alongside a light sigil it is read as drawing the light itself out into ribbon-like strands. The four Stretch signs are evenly spaced, so the stretching favors no direction. The two Cooling signs sit opposite each other and cool the effect, keeping the light cold instead of warm, despite light belonging to the fire domain. This is only two kinds of modifier on two compatible sigils, with no contradiction, and the neat drawing and closed ring let the spell activate and hold steady.
effect: Draws light out into long, flexible ribbons that drift and curl through the air around the seal, carried evenly in every direction by gentle currents. The ribbons give off no warmth, staying cool to the touch, and glow at a moderate strength that gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00203.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Six Stability and Level Planes signs, each a pair of wavy parallel strokes, surround it at about half the distance to the ring. They sit at roughly the north-northwest, northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest positions. The signs at the south, southwest, northeast and east-southeast are drawn a little rougher than the other two. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, creating and shaping flame or heat. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Stability and Level Planes is non-directional, so its orientation does not matter. It makes its target balance on a level plane in the air, like something floating on water that can turn and drift but stays on the surface. Six of these signs are spread evenly around the ring, so no side is favored and the balancing hold is strong. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The slight roughness of four signs weakens their hold a little and makes it less even than the neat signs.
effect: Creates a moderate flame that floats in the air above the seal and stays balanced on a level plane. It can drift and turn, but it keeps its height like something floating on water. The flame holds level most of the time, though it dips or tilts slightly from time to time toward one side.

name: s42_00204.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed but drawn roughly and noticeably lumpy rather than round. A Concealment sign sits at the center, an eight-armed star with an eye mark at each of its north, east, south and west ends. It is moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Pulling signs sit about halfway out at the north, east, south and west points, each with its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center. Two more Pulling signs sit farther out at the northwest and southeast, both inverted, with their arrowheads pointing outward toward the ring. The north and northwest signs are drawn with heavier, rougher strokes than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Concealment sign at the center is the core of the seal, so the spell hides its target, and its moderate size gives a moderate strength. Pulling is directional. Pointed inward, it draws the target toward the seal, and the four evenly spaced inward signs pull equally from every side. The two inverted Pulling signs on the northwest-southeast axis most likely push things away instead, which directly contradicts the inward pull. The four inward signs outnumber the two outward ones, so pulling dominates and concealment stays the core effect, but the clash along that diagonal makes the result likely unstable. The lumpy, not-quite-round ring further weakens the seal, so the effect is fleeting and may fail to take hold at all.
effect: Draws nearby objects in toward the seal and shrouds them from sight as they arrive. Along one diagonal, objects are shoved away instead and jerk back and forth between being pulled and pushed, so the concealment over them flickers on and off. The whole effect is short-lived and can sputter out before it fully hides anything.

name: s42_00205.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small Stretch sign, an arch with short outturned feet, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil. There is no element sigil. Three Sights Set signs sit inside the inner ring. The one at the north-northwest and the one at the south-southeast each have their diamond end near the ring and their arrow pointing in toward the center. The one at the east-northeast is reversed, with its diamond toward the center and its arrow pointing out toward the ring. Two bold Regions chevrons sit at the north-northeast and the west, both with their points facing outward toward the ring. The signs cluster more heavily on the north-northeast side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Stretch takes the center and sets the spell's core behavior: turning solid matter it touches into long, flexible ribbons. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, while the second ring adds strength to the core effect. Both Regions signs point outward, so the magic manifests outside the ring and not within it. Because they sit only at the north-northeast and west, the effect is pushed toward that side. Sights Set lets the caster aim the spell at a chosen point. The outward east-northeast Sights Set agrees with the outward Regions. The two inward-pointing Sights Set signs directly contradict them by aiming back toward the center, where the Regions signs forbid the effect. Those two sit on opposite sides and largely cancel each other's lean. The outward-facing signs dominate, so the spell reaches out toward the northeast, but the opposing aim makes the result likely unstable.
effect: Turns solid objects outside the seal into long, flexible ribbons, aimed at a target the caster picks and favoring the northeast side. The aim wavers and sometimes snaps back toward the seal itself, so ribbons form unevenly, with some pieces only partly stretched before the effect slips off its mark.

name: s42_00206.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background with two concentric rings, both closed. Both rings are slightly lumpy and not quite round, and the outer one is the more uneven. There is no element sigil. A Detection sign, three upright vertical strokes of increasing length, sits at the center at roughly a quarter of the inner ring's radius. Six signs are spread fairly evenly around it, each a little rough.
