A Purification curl sits at the north-northeast and a roughly drawn Stability and Level Planes sign, two wavy lines, sits at the east-northeast. A Solidification sign, two small circles joined by a line, sits at the southeast, with its outer circle resting on the inner ring. A Reflection hourglass sits at the southwest. A Projection bracket sits at the west-northwest, turned nearly upside down relative to the other signs, with its edge crossing the inner ring. A Pointing sign sits at the north-northwest.
justification: With no element sigil, Detection takes the center and acts as the core, so the spell senses the presence of things around the seal rather than working with fire, water, earth or wind. Reflection targets a reflected image, and Projection casts an effect outward. Together with Detection they form a related group that dominates the seal: whatever is sensed is turned into an image and sent outward. Pointing gives that output a conical shape, and Solidification makes the magic firmer. Stability and Level Planes keeps it balanced on a level plane. Purification, an asymmetric sign that separates waste from water, has no clear link to the rest. The seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: imaging, shaping, firming, levelling and purifying. The detection-reflection-projection group dominates, shaping and firming come second, and Purification is the least predictable part, so the result is likely unstable. The rough drawing and the not-quite-round rings also make the effect weaker and shorter lived, even though both rings are closed.
effect: Senses things near the seal and casts a reflected image of them outward as a pointed, partly solid cone held on a level plane. The image flickers and drifts out of alignment, and the cone hardens unevenly, firm in some places and hazy in others. Patches of the image sporadically wash clear, and the whole projection fades or collapses after only a short time.

name: s42_00207.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. A Stretch sign sits near the ring at the south, its curved top toward the ring and its open side facing the center. A Gathering sign sits at the east-northeast with its arrowhead pointing outward toward the ring. A Launch sign sits at the west-southwest with its point toward the ring and its open side facing the center. A Cooling sign, a vertical line flanked by dots, sits close to the ring at the north. A Regions sign sits at the northwest with its corner pointing inward toward the center. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone and soil, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Stretch works directly on solids and turns them into long, flexible ribbons, so it pairs naturally with earth and dominates the seal. Gathering supplies material drawn from the surroundings for the spell to reshape. Two signs pull against each other. Regions points inward, which confines the magic to inside the ring, while Launch points outward and drives a short, powerful burst away from the seal toward the west-southwest. Cooling adds a chill that has little to do with the rest of the seal. With five unrelated kinds of modifier stacked together and a direct contradiction between Regions and Launch, earth and Stretch, fed by Gathering, set the core behavior, and the result is likely unstable.
effect: Draws in nearby stone and soil and stretches it into long, flexible ribbons of moderate strength that are cold to the touch. The ribbons repeatedly lurch outward toward the west-southwest in sudden bursts, then snap back above the seal. They twist unevenly, cool in patches, and the spell tends to give out before the ribbons settle.

name: s42_00208.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Stability and Level Planes sign, drawn as three wavy vertical lines, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil. It is moderate in size relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Inside the inner ring, six Reflection signs (hourglass shapes) are spaced around the center at roughly north, east-northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest and west-northwest. Each has its top toward the ring, and the west-northwest one is drawn with noticeably heavier strokes. In the band between the rings sit four smaller Reflection signs at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast and west-southwest. The east-northeast and west-southwest ones touch the inner ring line, and the east-northeast one is slightly rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Stability and Level Planes takes the central role. It is a non-directional sign that makes its target balance on a level plane in the air, able to turn and drift but always staying level, like something floating on water. Reflection targets the reflected image on the object the seal is drawn on, so the reflection becomes the material the spell works on. Ten Reflection signs spread evenly across both rings give the effect a wide reach without favoring any direction. The second ring carries the smaller outer set and adds strength to the core effect. Those outer signs are small and slightly rough, so they contribute less than the inner six. Only two kinds of glyph are present, and they work together without conflict.
effect: Lifts the reflection held in the surface the seal is drawn on and holds it as a flat image floating level above the seal. The image can turn and drift but always stays level. Its center holds clear and steady, while its outer edges are fainter and fade sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00209.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the bottom between the south-southwest and south-southeast. A light sigil sits at the center, large relative to the ring at about half its radius, with slightly rough lines. Six Gathering signs are spread around it in three pairs, one closer to the center and one nearer the ring. One pair sits at the east and east-northeast, one at the northwest, and one at the south-southwest. In each pair the inner sign has its arrowhead pointing toward the center. The outer east-northeast and south-southwest signs also point inward. The outer northwest sign is drawn heavier and a little rougher, and it is turned to point roughly east along the ring rather than straight at the center. Three small Mimicry signs sit close to the ring at the north, west-southwest, and southeast, each with its top toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Its slightly rough lines make the light a little less steady and shorter lived. Gathering lets a spell draw material in from its surroundings. With most of the arrowheads pointing inward, the seal pulls light toward its center. The pairs are spread evenly, so no side dominates. The rotated outer northwest sign pulls slightly askew, adding a small unevenness on that side. Mimicry guides or imitates the movements of a target. With no decorative sigil to copy, it would give the gathered light simpler movements that follow a target. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: It does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it would draw in surrounding light and concentrate it into a strong, bright glow that follows and imitates the simple movements of its target. The glow flickers slightly, pulls a little unevenly toward the northwest, and dims somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00210.png
description: A fully visible seal on a white background, ring closed but drawn roughly and lumpy rather than round. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. A small Mimicry sign sits at the northwest. A Regions sign sits near the ring at the south, its point aimed toward the center. A rotated Immobility sign sits at the east-southeast. Two Stretch signs sit in the upper right: a larger one at the northeast with its arch toward the ring, and a smaller one at the north turned the other way, with its arch toward the center. All glyphs are drawn roughly, and most signs crowd the northeast half of the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its large size gives the flame real intensity. Stretch normally draws matter out into long, flexible ribbons, so here the fire is pulled into ribbons. The two Stretch signs face opposite ways; Stretch is likely non-directional, so this may not matter, but if it inverts, the two partly cancel. Immobility holds the ribbons in a fixed shape relative to the seal. The single Regions sign pointing inward keeps the magic inside the ring. Mimicry imitates the movements of what a decorative sigil depicts, but no such sigil is present, so as a guess the flame copies stray motion around it. That makes four unrelated kinds of modifier. The fire sigil and Stretch dominate, Immobility and Regions are secondary, and Mimicry is least predictable, so the result is likely unstable. The rough lines weaken and shorten the spell. The badly misshapen ring means it may not activate at all, or only briefly, and the crowding toward the northeast skews it to that side.
effect: If it ignites at all, the spell draws flame into long ribbons that try to hold a set shape inside the seal. They sag and bulge toward the northeast and sputter in places. The ribbons jerk erratically, now and then copying nearby movement, and the whole effect flickers out after only a moment.

name: s42_00211.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small water sigil sits upright at the center, about a quarter of the ring's radius. Three Collection signs sit roughly two-thirds of the way to the ring at the north, east-southeast, and west-southwest positions. Each has its barred end toward the ring and its open side facing the center. Three Aeriforms Defined signs alternate with them at the east-northeast, south, and west-northwest positions. Each is a fan of three short strokes whose converging end points toward the center. The Aeriforms Defined signs at east-northeast and south are drawn a little roughly. All other glyphs are neat, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its small size relative to the ring gives it a modest intensity. Collection gathers material from above and around the seal so the spell can use it. With their open sides facing inward in their usual orientation, the three Collection signs draw surrounding moisture toward the center. Aeriforms Defined is tied to air and gases, and its strokes match the marks beside a wind sigil. Here they converge toward the center the same way, so they are read in their normal orientation rather than inverted. Applied to water, they most likely give the gathered water a gaseous, airborne form. The two kinds of sign alternate evenly, so no direction is favored. They do not contradict each other. The two slightly rough Aeriforms Defined signs weaken their part of the effect a little on those sides.
effect: Draws moisture from the surrounding air and holds it above the seal as a modest, gently drifting cloud of mist. The mist is slightly thinner toward the east-northeast and south and fades a little sooner there than on the other sides.

name: s42_00212.png
description: A fully visible seal on a white background, drawn neatly. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the northwest. Two glyphs share the center, each moderate in size relative to the ring: an earth sigil on the left and a Reflection sign, an hourglass of two triangles, on the right. Six Dispersion signs form an inner circle about halfway to the ring, at the south-southeast, southwest, west-northwest, north-northwest, northeast and east-southeast. Each has its stem toward the center and its curve toward the ring. Three more Dispersion signs sit farther out near the ring. The ones at the north-northwest and east-southeast face the same way as the inner six. The one at the southwest is inverted, with its stem toward the ring and its curve toward the center, and it is drawn larger and heavier than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Reflection shares the center as a second core. It targets the reflected image found on the surface the seal is drawn on, so the earth magic works on the solid matter reflected there. Dispersion makes magic pour outward rather than beam in one direction. With eight upright Dispersion signs spread evenly around the ring, the outflow is even on all sides, and the extra outer signs widen its reach. The single inverted Dispersion at the southwest is larger and heavier than the rest. The exact difference an inverted Dispersion makes is unclear. It is outnumbered, so the outward pour dominates, but that side is likely to behave differently from the others. Only two kinds of modifier are present, so the seal is not unstable. The ring is open, so the spell will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: As drawn, it does not activate. Once closed, it takes the stone or soil reflected in the surface bearing the seal and pours earth outward from the seal evenly in all directions with moderate force. On the southwest side, the flow is partly held back and spreads less evenly than elsewhere.

name: s42_00213.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two rings. The outer ring is roughly drawn and open, with a wide gap at the upper left and another gap on the east side. A second, slightly rough ring sits just inside it. A small water sigil sits at the center, roughly drawn. Three Stretch signs sit against the inner ring: one at the north and one at the northeast, each with its arch toward the ring and its opening toward the center, and one at the south, also arched toward the ring and opening upward toward the center. A single Columns sign sits at the east-southeast, with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the center. No other signs are present, and more signs sit on the eastern side than the western.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives it a modest intensity. Stretch turns matter that touches the seal into long, flexible ribbons. Paired with water, the three Stretch signs draw the water out into ribbon-like strands. The single Columns sign gives the effect a column shape. Because it stands alone at the east-southeast with nothing to balance it, the column is pushed toward that side instead of rising straight up. The Stretch signs also cluster to the north and east, which adds to that lean. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The rough lines throughout make the spell weaker and shorter lived. The outer ring is open, so the seal will not activate until it is closed.
effect: As drawn, the seal does not activate. If it were closed, it would draw a modest amount of water out into long, flexible ribbons and send them leaning off toward the east-southeast. The ribbons would come out thin and uneven, waver along their path, and break apart into ordinary water after a short time.

name: s42_00214.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. There is no element sigil. A Partition sign sits upright at the center, about a third of the ring's radius in size. Four Envelopment signs, slanted strokes hooked at both ends, sit near the ring at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest. Detection signs, three parallel strokes of decreasing length, sit at the north and south, each with its top toward the center. At the east is a matching glyph of three stacked horizontal strokes shortening downward, which reads as a Detection sign stretched wide. At the west is a glyph that matches no known sign: a narrow right-angled triangle tapering downward, with a small circle crossed by a bar at its upper corner. The signs are evenly spaced, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil, the central Partition sign is the core of the seal. It outlines the borders of an area of effect that extends outward and upward, and the other signs decide what happens inside that area. The four Envelopment signs at the diagonals make the effect surround whatever it targets, so the bounded zone wraps around its contents evenly. The three Detection signs at north, east and south, the eastern one stretched, add a sensing quality, so the zone responds to presences within its borders. The stretched eastern sign likely widens that sensing on its side. The western glyph is closest to Pointing because of its tapering cone shape, though this is a guess. Read as Pointing, it gives the effect a tapered, conical form, and its circled bar loosely echoes Orb. Only three kinds of modifier surround the core and none contradict each other. The neat drawing, closed ring and balanced layout mean the seal activates and holds steady.
effect: Marks out a bounded zone around the seal that wraps evenly around everything inside it and senses any presence within its borders. The zone tapers slightly to a point on one side, and its sensing reaches a little wider on the opposite side. It holds steady for as long as the seal stays intact.

name: s42_00215.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a gap at the top just east of north. At the center is a modest-sized unnamed glyph: an S-curve inside a small circle, ringed by eight dots, resembling a variant of the wind sigil. Two Entwining signs sit near the ring, one at the north-northeast with its top toward the center and one at the west-southwest with its top toward the ring. Two Convergence triangles sit at the east and south points, close to the ring, each with a point facing inward. Three Purification signs sit at the north-northwest, southeast and west-southwest, each a small hooked curl about two-thirds of the way out from the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central glyph matches no named sigil, but its S-curve and surrounding marks are closest to the wind sigil, so reading it as a wind-family sigil is a guess. Under that reading the spell acts on air, and its modest size gives a modest intensity. Convergence draws the magic together to a single point and packs loose particles tightly, and both signs here face inward in their usual orientation. Purification normally separates waste from water. Paired with an air sigil, it would separate impurities from the air instead. Because Purification is asymmetric, how it behaves is less certain. Entwining makes the effect wrap around other objects. The two Entwining signs face opposite ways, but this is not a direct contradiction, so they mainly spread the wrapping effect around the seal. With three kinds of modifier and signs balanced around the ring, the seal holds together. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: It does not activate while its ring is open. Once closed, it would draw nearby air together toward a single point, strip dust and impurities out of it, and wrap the cleansed air around a target like a close-fitting current. The cleansing would be uneven, clearing some pockets of air thoroughly while leaving others only partly filtered.

name: s42_00216.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The outer ring is closed but a little rough and slightly lopsided, and a second closed ring sits just inside it. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center at moderate size relative to the ring. Six signs are spaced around it about halfway to the ring, all roughly drawn. Dispersion signs sit at the north-northwest and south-southeast with their tops toward the ring, and at the west-southwest and east-southeast with their tops toward the center. At the east-northeast is a Dispersion-like glyph with an extra stroke from its bottom edge, its top toward the center. At the west-northwest is a Dispersion-like glyph with a small Binding curve attached at its bottom, its top toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Dispersion makes the magic pour outward rather than beam in one direction. Both its normal and inverted forms are known, and here they alternate, with the signs balanced around the ring so no side is favored. The east-northeast glyph is read as Dispersion with a stray stroke, which is a guess, and it adds to the same outward flow. The west-northwest glyph is read as Dispersion joined to Binding, also a guess. Binding halts movement and makes material act as a single unit, so on that side it would hold part of the outflowing air together. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they do not contradict each other. The rough strokes and the slightly uneven outer ring weaken the seal and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Pushes air outward from the seal in a moderate breeze that spreads evenly in every direction, with part of the flow on one side holding together as a denser gust. The breeze comes in uneven puffs rather than a smooth stream, and it fades sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00217.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed. A small fire sigil sits upright at the center. Inside the inner ring are two Purification signs, curled hooks at the northwest and southeast, and two Pointing signs, each a triangle crossed by a bar with curls at both ends, at the east-northeast and south-southwest. The band between the inner and outer rings holds four more Purification signs at the north-northwest, east-southeast, south-southeast and southwest, one of them turned nearly upside down. More signs crowd the southeast side than the northwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, and the second ring adds strength to the core spell. The two Pointing signs make the flame take a tapered, conical shape. No Columns or other directional sign is present to send those cones outward, so they stay close to the seal. Purification separates waste from what it cleans. Paired with fire instead of water, it most plausibly turns the heat into a cleansing heat that burns off impurities. Purification is asymmetric, so how its six copies, one turned over, combine is hard to predict. Because they cluster on the southeast side, the cleansing effect leans that way. Only two kinds of modifier are present and neither cancels the other.
effect: Produces a modest, tapered flame that forms cone-shaped tongues close to the seal and burns impurities and waste out of whatever it heats. The cleansing heat is strongest toward the south-southeast and acts somewhat unevenly elsewhere, scorching away grime more thoroughly on that side than on the opposite one.

name: s42_00218.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but a little rough. Two sigils sit side by side near the center, both small relative to the ring: a light sigil on the left and a water sigil on the right, both roughly drawn. Nine Detection signs, each made of three parallel strokes of increasing length, surround them. Six sit near the ring at the west, northwest, north-northeast, east, south-southeast and south-southwest, each with its top toward the ring. Three more sit closer in at the northeast, southeast and northwest, each turned at its own angle. Most of the signs are drawn roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil creates and shapes light, and the water sigil gathers and moves water, so the seal has two cores working side by side. Both are small relative to the ring, which keeps the intensity modest. Detection works by sensing the presence of things around the seal and triggering the spell in response, much like a path that lights up as someone approaches. Nine of them spread evenly around the ring give the seal awareness on every side with no favored direction. The three tilted inner signs add sensing closer to the center without steering the effect anywhere. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. However, the rough ring, rough sigils and roughly drawn signs make the spell weaker and shorter lived.
effect: Senses anything that comes near the seal from any side and responds with a faint glow and a small gathering of water around it. The response is uneven: the glow flickers and some approaches go unnoticed, while others trigger it late. Both the light and the water fade sooner than a cleanly drawn version would last.

name: s42_00219.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a gap at the bottom just right of south. There is no element sigil. A Refuse sign, a diamond set on top of an X, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring, its lines slightly uneven. Eight Gathering signs surround it, each with its arrowhead toward the center. Four sit near the ring at the north, northeast, southeast and southwest. Four sit somewhat closer in at the east, south-southeast, west-southwest and northwest. Most are neatly drawn, but the northwest and northeast signs are a little rough, the southwest one is shaky, and the west-southwest one is drawn in heavier strokes. The signs are evenly spread, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Refuse sign at the center acts as the core of the spell. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material such as waste toward where it points. Here it stands upright, so collected material is drawn toward its upper side. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Gathering lets a spell actively draw material in from its surroundings. All eight face inward and are balanced around the ring, so they pull evenly from every side toward the center. Both kinds of sign gather material and work together without contradiction. The roughness of several signs, especially the shaky one at the southwest, makes the effect slightly weaker and shorter lived on those sides. The ring is open, so the seal does not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: As drawn, the seal does not activate. Once closed, it would strongly draw waste, debris and other unwanted material in from all around and heap it at the center, piling it toward the upper side. The pull would be a little weaker from the southwest, so refuse on that side gathers more slowly, and the whole effect fades somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00220.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A large Rain sign sits at the center: a square with inward-curving sides and short lines radiating from each side. Its middle is empty, with no element sigil inside it or anywhere else in the seal. Four smaller Rain signs sit in the band between the two rings, at the north, east, south-southeast, and west-northwest positions. They are spread fairly evenly around the band. All five Rain signs look alike, and none appears flipped inside-out. The north sign looks marginally less even than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no fire, water, earth, wind, or light sigil, so the large central Rain sign takes the core position and sets the spell's behavior. Rain summons its target material, which then falls from above, and drawing it large relative to the ring makes that effect strong. Rain is semi-directional with radial symmetry, so rotating it changes nothing, and it would only reverse its effect if drawn inside-out. None of the five signs is drawn that way, so all of them work normally and reinforce one another. Repeating the same sign around the band increases the range and quantity of the effect, and the even spacing means no side is favored. The second ring strengthens the magic further. Because only one kind of modifier is present, the signs do not conflict. With no element to define the material, the spell is not tied to water and acts on whatever loose material is available to it. The slightly uneven north sign weakens that side only a little.
effect: Calls down whatever loose material is available above the seal in a strong, steady, rain-like shower spread evenly over a wide area around it. The spell is not limited to water, so dust, sand, or droplets alike fall like rainfall. The shower is marginally thinner toward the north.

name: s42_00221.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is lumpy and uneven, bulging in places rather than forming a true circle. A water sigil sits at the center, drawn roughly and of moderate size, a little under half the ring's radius. Six Regions signs, each a chevron with its point toward the ring and its open side toward the center, sit near the ring at the north, east, east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and west-northwest positions. Some chevrons are drawn neatly and others slightly roughly. They are spread fairly evenly around the ring, with no side clearly favored. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size relative to the ring gives a fair intensity. Regions sets where magic manifests relative to the seal. With every Regions sign pointing outward, the magic manifests outside the ring and does not take effect within its bounds. Because the six signs are balanced around the ring, no single direction is favored, so the water appears on all sides at once rather than shooting one way. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. The ring is closed, so the spell activates, but its uneven shape and the rough sigil weaken it and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Produces water all around the outside of the seal while the area within it stays dry, forming a loose ring of water on every side. The water comes out thinner and patchier than its strength would suggest, wavering where it forms, and the effect fades sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00222.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the inner ring. Six Gathering signs are spread around it inside the inner ring, at the west, northwest, north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast and south-southwest, each with its arrowed top pointing out toward the ring. Three smaller, lighter Gathering signs sit in the band between the two rings, at the north-northwest, east-southeast and southwest, also with their tops toward the outer ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell that collects, creates and manipulates water. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Gathering lets a spell draw material in from its surroundings to build its effect, and nine of them focus the whole seal on pulling in water. The signs are spaced evenly in both rings, so no side is favored and water comes in from all directions alike. The second ring strengthens the core spell, and the three Gathering signs in it extend the draw further out, though their smaller size makes their added pull lighter. With no directional signs, the gathered water is not sent anywhere and stays at the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is consistent and steady.
effect: Draws water from the surroundings, such as moisture in the air and nearby sources, in toward the seal evenly from every side. The water collects in a strong, steady supply at the seal instead of being sent away from it.

name: s42_00223.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but noticeably lumpy and not round, and the glyphs are roughly drawn. There is no element sigil. A Launch sign sits upright at the center, small relative to the ring. Six signs sit near the ring. A Coil sign is at the northeast, a Pointing sign at the east, and a Piercing sign at the southeast, all with their tops toward the ring. An Orb sign is at the south, also with its top toward the ring. A Concealment sign is at the southwest and an Entwining sign at the west-northwest, both with their tops toward the center. The signs cluster more heavily on the southeast side, and the north and northwest are empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: Launch is a sign, but here it takes the central place of a sigil and sets the core behavior. It generates its target in the direction it points as a powerful but short burst, and since it stands upright that direction is upward. With no element sigil, the spell is tied to no element and acts on whatever material is available to it. Pointing gives the material a conical shape, and Piercing turns it into projectiles. Both sit on the heavier southeast side and dominate the modifiers, so the burst leans that way. Orb conflicts with them because it tries to collect material in a sphere, while Pointing and Piercing shape it into cones and projectiles. Coil softens physical matter, which works against Piercing's offensive projectiles. Concealment would hide the material, and Entwining would make it wrap around things. That stacks far more than three unrelated kinds of modifier, with direct contradictions, so the result is likely unstable. Launch and the Pointing and Piercing pair dominate, while the other signs pull the effect in conflicting ways. The rough drawing and the small central sign make the spell weak and short lived. The poorly rounded ring makes any effect fleeting and may stop the spell from activating at all.
effect: If it activates at all, it fires a brief, weak burst of cone-tipped projectiles upward from whatever material is at hand, veering off toward the southeast. The projectiles waver between hardening into points and sagging soft. Some flicker in and out of sight or briefly curl around nearby objects, and others clump back into a lopsided ball. The whole burst fizzles out almost as soon as it starts.

name: s42_00224.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Nine small Rain-like signs, each a square with concave sides and short strokes at its corners, are scattered around it. Six form an inner circle about halfway to the ring, at the west-northwest, north, northeast, east-southeast, south and southwest positions. Three more sit close to the ring: one at the west-northwest, one at the south, and one at the north-northwest. The north-northwest glyph has a small circle crossed by a line, matching an Orb sign, attached to the side facing the center. None of the signs are inverted, and they are spread evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Rain summons its seal's material down from above in a rainfall-like way. Here the Rain signs are drawn small and scattered rather than surrounding the sigil, and none are flipped inside-out, so they act in their normal form. Paired with wind, they bring air down in many separate falling streams. Eight plain Rain signs spread evenly around the ring mean the effect falls across the whole area with no favored side. The glyph combining Rain with an attached Orb matches no known sign. As a guess, it reads as Rain feeding an Orb, which defines a spherical space where the material collects, so the air falling at that point would pool into a small sphere. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other, so the seal is stable.
effect: Brings air sweeping down from above in many small, steady downdrafts that fall evenly across the area around the seal, like a rainfall of wind. At one point near the edge, the falling air gathers into a small, contained sphere of swirling air instead of spreading out.

name: s42_00225.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. Two rings, one just inside the other, are both closed but drawn roughly. Each is lumpy and almost polygonal rather than round. A large earth sigil sits at the center and reaches about half the ring's radius. Its strokes are slightly uneven. Six small Crushing signs, roughly drawn zigzags, are spaced evenly around it at the southwest, west-northwest, north-northwest, northeast, east-southeast and south-southeast, about midway between the sigil and the inner ring. Each is turned so the peaks of the M shape point toward the center, which makes all six inverted. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this a spell acting on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its large size relative to the ring would give a strong effect. Crushing is semi-directional, so its position does not steer the spell, but inverting it reverses its effect. Instead of breaking solids into smaller pieces, inverted Crushing pulls already crushed material back into its original shape, and only for as long as the spell holds. All six signs are inverted and evenly spaced, so they agree with each other and work evenly on all sides. The second ring would normally reinforce the magic, but it holds no signs of its own. Both rings are far from round, which makes the effect fleeting and may keep it from activating at all. The rough sigil and signs further weaken the spell and shorten its life, cancelling much of the strength the large sigil would give.
effect: Pulls powdered or smashed solid material back together into the shape of the object it came from. The reformed shape flickers into being and holds only briefly. Sometimes it fails to take hold at all, and it often crumbles back into fragments well before a properly drawn version would let go.

name: s42_00226.png
description: A fully visible seal on a white background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. A Coil sign sits near the ring at the northwest. An inverted Expansion sign, its nested corner brackets pointing inward, sits at the west-northwest about halfway out. A small four-lobed Billow sign sits at the east-northeast. At the east-southeast is a circle crossed by a slanted line; it resembles an Orb sign but matches no known sign exactly. An Aeriforms Defined sign, three fanned strokes, sits against the ring at the west-southwest. An Envelopment sign sits near the ring at the south. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Coil softens physical matter. Billow turns material into a fluffy cloud, and the two fit together, so softened earth is puffed into a cloud-like mass. The inverted Expansion has its corners pointing inward, which shrinks its target. The circled glyph most closely resembles Orb, though this is a guess. Read as Orb, it gathers the material into a spherical space above the seal. Envelopment makes the effect surround its target. Aeriforms Defined ties the spell to air, which sits poorly with an earth sigil. The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier: softening, cloud-forming, shrinking, spherical collection, enveloping and air. The earth sigil, Coil and Billow dominate. Orb and Envelopment shape the result, while inverted Expansion and Aeriforms Defined pull against the rest. The result is likely unstable. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell still activates.
effect: Softens nearby soil or stone and puffs it into a fluffy, cloud-like mass. The mass gathers into a rough sphere and wraps around its target. The mass shrinks and swells unevenly as it forms, and pockets of it loosen into dusty air. It tends to lose its rounded shape and slump back into loose earth before the spell runs its full course.

name: s42_00227.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The inner ring sits just inside the outer one, leaving a narrow empty band between them. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Six Dancing Puppets signs are spaced around the sigil, about two thirds of the way out toward the inner ring, at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest positions. Each is drawn as a small ring with little circles on it and curved strokes crossing outward, and each is rotated differently. The east-southeast sign is drawn slightly larger and bolder than the others. There are no other signs, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell that creates and controls flames or heat. Its moderate size gives a fair intensity, and the second ring adds strength to the core spell. Dancing Puppets allows the movement of the spell's target to be consciously steered, even at long distance. Paired with wind it makes objects fly, so paired with fire it makes the flames themselves move and dart through the air. Six of these signs repeat a single modifier and are evenly balanced, so no direction is favored. With no directional signs, the motion follows the caster's control rather than a fixed path. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts and the seal is stable.
effect: Creates fairly strong flames that rise from the seal and can be steered freely through the air, darting, weaving and circling as the caster directs. With no fixed direction of their own, they go wherever they are guided, even at a distance.

name: s42_00228.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is small relative to the rings. Six Cooling signs, each a vertical stroke flanked by two pairs of dots, sit in the band between the inner and outer rings. They are at the north, northeast, east-southeast, south, southwest, and west-northwest positions. They are spaced evenly around the seal. The north and west-northwest signs are drawn slightly less cleanly than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell. It moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it, and its small size gives a modest intensity. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Cooling cools things down. The Cooling glyph is symmetric, so pointing some signs toward the center and others toward the ring should not change their effect. Six of them together give a strong chilling effect on the air the spell moves. The signs are evenly balanced, and there is no Columns, Regions, or other directional sign, so the air is not pushed in any one direction. It stays and circulates around the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is not unstable. The two slightly rough signs only weaken the chill a little on their sides.
effect: Draws the surrounding air into a gentle, steady circulation around the seal and chills it, producing a cool breeze. The breeze spreads evenly on all sides and does not blow in one direction. It is noticeably cold but not forceful, and is slightly less chilly toward the north and west-northwest.

name: s42_00229.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background with two concentric rings, both closed. Both rings are a little rough and noticeably angular, closer to a rounded pentagon than a true circle. An upright Entwining sign sits at the center and reaches a little under half the inner ring's radius. There is no element sigil. Six Stretch signs surround it, spread evenly around the seal. The four smaller ones sit at the north, east-southeast, southwest and west-northwest, each with its arch toward the ring and its opening toward the center. Two larger ones sit at the northeast and the south, both overlapping the inner ring line, drawn the other way round with the arch toward the center and the opening facing outward. Most strokes are slightly shaky, and only the north and west-northwest signs are neatly drawn. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Entwining sign at the center acts as the core of the seal. It makes the object the seal is drawn on wrap itself around other objects. Stretch turns solid objects that touch the seal into long, flexible ribbons. Together they reshape solid material into ribbons that coil around nearby things. Stretch is most likely non-directional, so the two larger signs drawn the other way round probably act the same as the rest. Their larger size strengthens the stretching on the northeast and south sides. The six signs are balanced, so the effect has no set direction. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they work together, so the seal is not unstable. Without a sigil the spell is not tied to one element, but Stretch acts only on solid matter, so liquids and gases are unaffected. The rings are not round enough, which makes any effect fleeting and risks the seal failing to activate. The slightly rough strokes also weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Turns solid objects that touch the seal into long, flexible ribbons that wind themselves around nearby things. The ribbons form and grip only briefly before going slack, and the spell can sputter out without taking hold at all. Liquids and gases are not affected.

name: s42_00230.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil sits at the center: a diamond set inside a square, with four short spokes reaching north, east, south and west. It is of moderate size relative to the inner ring. Four small Sights Set signs sit in the band between the two rings, at the north-northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest positions. Each has its diamond end toward the outer ring and its arrow pointing inward toward the center. The northeast sign is drawn slightly less cleanly than the others. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, which creates and shapes light that diminishes over time. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Sights Set lets the caster aim a spell at a chosen point or target. All four signs point inward and are spaced roughly evenly, so they favor no single direction and give the caster full freedom of aim rather than a fixed heading. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. The slightly rough northeast sign weakens that part of the aiming a little.
effect: Produces a moderately bright light that the caster can aim and hold on any chosen point or target, much like a guided spotlight. The aim holds steady in most directions but wavers slightly when turned toward the northeast. The light gradually dims over time.

name: s42_00231.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn, with the ring open at a gap near the top between the northwest and north. A water sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large, reaching about half the ring's radius. Six Stillness signs are spaced evenly around it at the north-northeast, east-northeast, south-southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest points. Each is rotated so its top faces the ring, and they sit at slightly varying distances from the center. The signs at the east-northeast, south-southeast and south-southwest are drawn a little more roughly than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell that manipulates, collects or creates water. Its large size relative to the ring gives it a fairly strong intensity. Stillness holds magic in place so the effect stays static in a single location. Six Stillness signs spread evenly around the ring favor no direction, so the water is held fixed over the seal rather than pushed anywhere. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. The slightly rough strokes on three signs weaken the hold a little on those sides. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: The seal does not activate as drawn. Once closed, it would hold a sizable body of water fixed and motionless in place over the seal, keeping it from flowing, spilling or drifting away. The hold is firm overall but slackens slightly sooner along the east and south sides, where the water may begin to stir and seep before the rest.

name: s42_00232.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large earth sigil sits upright at the center, reaching about half the ring's radius. Six Pointing signs, each an A-shaped peak flanked by small curls, surround it about two thirds of the way out toward the ring. They sit at the west-southwest, northwest, north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast and south-southwest positions, each rotated so its top faces the ring. The signs are evenly spaced, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates existing solid matter such as stone, sand and soil rather than creating it. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Pointing is non-directional and makes the target material manifest in a conical shape. It normally needs a sign such as Columns to direct those cones, and none is present here. Six identical Pointing signs spaced evenly around the ring favor no side, so the shaping acts evenly all around the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the neat drawing and closed ring let the spell activate and hold steady.
effect: Forcefully reshapes nearby stone and soil into sharp, cone-shaped spikes that form evenly all around the seal. Nothing drives the spikes outward or launches them, so they stay fixed where they form.

name: s42_00233.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but hand-drawn with a wobbly, uneven outline that bulges in places and is noticeably not round. An upright earth sigil sits at the center, fairly large relative to the ring. Five Dispersion signs sit about two-thirds of the way out. The four at the north, east, south and west points each have the stem toward the ring and the curve toward the center. The one at the southwest is flipped, with its curve toward the ring and its stem toward the center. Two Refuse signs, each a diamond over crossed legs, sit at the north-northwest and southeast with their diamond ends toward the center. The west, east and both Refuse signs are drawn a little shakily. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as soil, sand and stone. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a reasonably strong effect. Dispersion makes the seal's magic pour outward instead of beaming in one direction. Four Dispersion signs evenly placed at the cardinal points spread that outflow equally on all sides. The single flipped Dispersion at the southwest is an inverted form whose difference in effect is unclear. It is not expected to change the overall outward spread much. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward where it points. Both Refuse signs point inward, so waste and debris are drawn toward the center of the seal. The outward spread of earth magic and the inward collection of refuse act on different things, so they work together rather than against each other. The ring is closed, so the spell activates. However, its outline is not round enough, and several signs are drawn roughly. This weakens the spell and shortens how long it lasts.
effect: Works the soil and stone around the seal outward in all directions, loosening and spreading it, while sifting out debris and waste and drawing that refuse inward to pile up at the center. The effect is brief. The sweep sputters and runs unevenly, pulling less refuse on some sides than others, and it fades before the ground is fully cleared.

name: s42_00234.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed and neatly drawn, and it holds no element sigil. A Stillness sign sits at the center in place of a sigil, moderate in size relative to the ring. Five Link signs surround it. Four sit near the ring at the northeast, east-southeast, southwest and northwest, each with its top toward the ring. A fifth sits closer in at the south-southwest, about halfway out, facing the opposite way with its top toward the center. Two smaller sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line and each with its ring closed. The one at the southwest holds a Launch sign at its center. The one at the northeast holds a light sigil that fills a large share of its small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil in the northeast sub-seal sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light. Its large size within its own ring gives that light good strength, although the sub-seal is small. Launch in the southwest sub-seal sends magic out in a powerful but short-lived burst. The joining lines feed both into the main seal, where Stillness at the center holds a magical effect static in one location. The four Link signs facing the ring identify material from the same source and tie it together. The single Link facing inward is reversed, so as a semi-directional sign it works against the other four, but the four outnumber it and dominate. Launch, which drives magic outward in a burst, directly contradicts Stillness, which holds magic in place. Stillness dominates because it sits at the center of the larger main ring, and Launch only acts at the start. Light, Stillness and Link set the overall shape. Because of the clash between Launch and Stillness and the reversed Link, the result is likely unstable.
effect: Throws out a sudden burst of light that is caught and held in place as a cluster of linked glowing points, which fade slowly over time. The held light strains against the burst, so it flickers and jitters, and individual points sometimes jerk loose before settling back. One point tends to drift apart from the rest, and the whole cluster may break up before the light has fully faded.

name: s42_00235.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a clear gap at the upper left between the north and west points. At the center is a glyph matching the light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, plus an extra filled dot just off its lower left side. It spans a moderate share of the ring. Four Purification signs sit near the ring at the north, east, south and west points, each with its top toward the ring. The western one is drawn a little heavier and rougher than the other three. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central glyph is closest to the light sigil, so this is read as a light spell. The extra dot matches no known sign. As a guess, it resembles the lone central dot of the time-freezing structure and would slightly hold the light in place, making it linger longer than normal light, which otherwise fades over time. The sigil's moderate size gives moderate intensity. Purification is asymmetric and normally separates waste from water. Paired with light, it would make the glow cleanse whatever it falls on, drawing impurities out of water. The four Purification signs are evenly spaced, so no direction is favored. Because they are asymmetric, their exact behavior is less predictable. The rougher western sign makes the effect slightly weaker on that side. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: As drawn, it does not activate. Once the ring is closed, it would give off a moderate glow that purifies water it shines on, separating out dirt and waste and lingering somewhat longer than ordinary light before dimming. The cleansing would be a little weaker and patchier on the western side.

name: s42_00236.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but slightly rough and not perfectly round. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four spokes, sits upright at the center and reaches about half the ring's radius. Eight signs surround it at uneven distances. A Cooling sign sits at the north. A small Glaives sign sits at the north-northeast near the ring. A Coil sign sits at the east-northeast, tilted. A small Expansion sign sits at the east-southeast near the ring, its corner brackets pointing outward. A Collection sign sits at the southeast with its open side facing inward. A Dispersion sign sits at the south, turned so its curve faces the center and its stem points toward the ring. A Reflection sign sits at the southwest, tilted. A Purification spiral sits at the west. The signs are spread evenly around the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Dispersion makes the light pour outward rather than beam in one direction. Its curve faces inward here, which is inverted, and the difference that makes is unclear. Expansion with its corners outward makes the effect grow. Cooling pulls against the heat that light carries as part of fire magic, so the light should be cold. Collection draws in nearby material. Reflection would tie the effect to reflected images. Coil softens only physical matter, and Glaives set how deep magic embeds in flesh, so neither has much to act on in a light spell. Purification is asymmetric and separates waste from water, which fits poorly here. Eight unrelated kinds of modifier are stacked together. The large light sigil dominates, with Dispersion and Expansion shaping it, so the result is likely unstable. The even spacing keeps any one side from being favored. The slightly rough ring shortens how long the spell lasts.
effect: Releases a strong, cold light that spills outward from the seal and swells as it spreads, glinting off nearby reflective surfaces. The glow flickers and spreads unevenly. Patches brighten and dim at random, and stray dust is sometimes tugged toward the light. The light fades sooner than its strength would suggest.

name: s42_00237.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but a little rough and slightly lopsided. Two glyphs sit side by side near the center. On the left is a Dancing Puppets sign, an inner ring with four small circles and crossing curved strokes. On the right is a light sigil, a diamond inside a square with four short spokes. The light sigil is slightly smaller than the Dancing Puppets sign, and both are small relative to the ring. Six Collection signs are spaced evenly just inside the ring, at the north-northeast, east, southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest. Five have their barred top toward the ring and their open side facing inward. The one at north-northeast is reversed, with its top toward the center and its open side facing the ring. Several Collection signs are drawn a little shakily. At the southeast, inside the main ring, sits a small sub-seal with its own closed but roughly drawn ring. It holds a roughly drawn Stretch sign at its center, and the southeast Collection sign sits just beyond it. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light, which naturally dims over time. Its modest size gives a modest intensity. The Dancing Puppets sign shares the center and lets the target's movement be manipulated, so the light can be made to move and dart through the air rather than sit still. The Collection signs gather material above and around the seal for the spell to use. Five face inward in their usual orientation and dominate. The single reversed Collection at north-northeast directly contradicts them; read as a guess, it would push material away instead of gathering it. That leaves the gathering uneven and likely unstable on that side. The sub-seal adds Stretch, which draws its target out into long, flexible ribbons, so the gathered light is pulled into strands. Its rough drawing makes that part weaker and shorter lived. The slightly rough main ring also shortens the spell's duration. There are three kinds of modifier here: motion, gathering and stretching.
effect: Gathers light around the seal and draws it out into thin, flexible ribbons that can be steered and made to dart and weave through the air. The ribbons are soft rather than bright and fade fairly quickly. The gathering falters on one side, so the light pools unevenly and some strands thin out or snap back into a plain glow before the spell ends.

name: s42_00238.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two closed concentric rings neatly drawn and a wide band between them. At the center, small relative to the rings, sits a fire sigil with a small diamond, matching the head of a Refuse sign, attached to its top point. A Refuse sign sits in the band at the west, lying on its side with its diamond end toward the center and its crossed legs toward the outer ring. A Regions-like chevron with an extra dot on its left side sits in the band at the east-southeast, pointing outward toward the outer ring. A Crushing sign sits in the band at the south-southwest, its peaks pointing inward toward the center. A Detection sign of three parallel strokes sits at the southwest, with its longest stroke crossing the inner ring. No signs appear in the north or northeast, so the signs cluster toward the south and southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. The diamond fused to its top matches no known sigil. The closest reading is a fire sigil merged with Refuse, which is a guess, and it would aim the fire at unwanted material. The second ring adds strength and further effects to the core. The west Refuse sign points inward, so it draws waste toward the seal. Crushing pointing inward is in its normal orientation, so it breaks solid matter into smaller and smaller pieces. The dotted chevron is closest to Regions, also a guess. Pointing outward, it would make part of the magic manifest outside the ring toward the east-southeast. Detection's function is unclear. It is tied to sensing, so as a guess it would help the spell locate its target material. Because the signs are unbalanced and lean south-southwest, the effect is weighted toward that side. The seal stacks four kinds of modifier: collecting waste, crushing, outward placement, and detection. The fire and Refuse core, together with Crushing, dominates. Detection and the altered Regions sign are the least predictable parts, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Draws waste and debris in toward the seal, grinds it down and burns it away with a modest flame. The burning is heaviest on the south-southwest side, while some of the fire licks out beyond the seal toward the east-southeast. The flame flares and gutters unevenly, some debris is only half crushed before it burns, and the spell sometimes passes over refuse it should have caught.

name: s42_00239.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils share the center: a fire sigil on the left and a wind sigil on the right. The fire sigil is moderate in size relative to the ring, and the wind sigil is slightly smaller. Six small Crosshair signs sit near the ring at the north-northwest, northeast, east, southeast, southwest and west positions, each rotated so it faces outward. The Crosshairs at the north-northwest and southeast are drawn a little roughly, and the rest are neat. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets flames and heat as one element, and the wind sigil adds the movement of air. Together they make heat or flame that is carried on moving air. Their moderate sizes give a moderate intensity, with fire slightly dominant over wind. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. Six outward-facing Crosshairs spread evenly around the ring send the effect toward six separate points around the seal, with no side favored. Crosshair is the only kind of modifier present, so nothing contradicts. The ring is closed and neatly drawn, so the spell activates. The two roughly drawn Crosshairs make their targets slightly weaker than the others.
effect: Sends gusts of hot, flame-tinged air outward from the seal in six directions, each striking a separate target around it with moderate force. The gusts aimed toward the north-northwest and southeast are somewhat weaker and die down sooner than the other four.

name: s42_00240.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of a main ring and two smaller linked rings. All three rings are closed. A small wind sigil sits at the center of the main ring. Six Repetition signs are spread evenly around it, about two-thirds of the way to the ring: at the north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest. Each is turned with its top toward the center. The one at the west-southwest is drawn in noticeably darker, heavier strokes than the others. A smaller ring is joined by a short line to the north side of the main ring, holding a fire sigil that fills about half of it. A matching smaller ring is joined to the south side, holding a wind sigil of similar relative size. Its ring line is slightly less even than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central wind sigil sets the main element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air. Its small size relative to the main ring gives a modest intensity. Repetition continually resets whatever the spell affects to the state it had when the spell first took hold, and that reset includes temperature. Six of them, evenly spaced, apply the reset evenly on every side, so the moved air keeps returning to its starting condition instead of drifting or dissipating. The linked northern ring adds fire magic, and its large sigil relative to that small ring supplies a fair amount of heat. The linked southern ring adds a second wind source that strengthens the air movement. Its slightly rough ring makes that added push a little weaker and shorter lived than the rest of the seal. All parts point the same way: moving air, warmed, held steady. Nothing contradicts anything else, so the seal is not unstable.
effect: Produces a gentle, warm current of air around the seal that keeps resetting to its original flow and temperature, so it neither cools nor dies away. The extra strength behind the draft fades somewhat sooner than the warmth, leaving a softer but still steady warm breeze.

name: s42_00241.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large, boldly drawn Launch sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, reaching about half the ring's radius and opening downward. A Collection sign sits at the north-northwest, with its barred end toward the ring and its open side facing inward, drawn a little roughly. A Gathering sign sits at the northeast, with its arrowhead pointing toward the center. A single small Piercing sign sits at the southeast, drawn a little roughly. Three Rain signs, starbursts with short strokes on their sides, sit at the southwest, south-southwest, and west-northwest. None of the Rain signs is turned inside out. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Launch takes the center and sets the core behavior. It sends the spell's material out in the direction it points, here straight up, in a powerful but short-lived burst. Its large size relative to the ring makes that burst strong. Collection, in its usual inward-facing orientation, takes material above and around the seal. Gathering, with its arrowhead pointing inward, actively draws more material in. Together they supply what Launch fires. Without a sigil the spell is not tied to one element and works on whatever material it gathers. Rain summons material and brings it down like rainfall. It is radially symmetric, so rotating it does not invert it, and all three act normally. They make the launched material come back down as a shower around the seal. Piercing makes material manifest as projectiles, and its count sets how many, so one sign yields a single projectile. The modifiers are gathering, rainfall, and projectiles, which is three kinds that do not contradict one another, so the seal is not unstable. Collection and Piercing are drawn a little roughly, which makes their parts slightly weaker and shorter lived than the rest.
effect: Draws loose material in from around the seal and hurls it straight upward in a strong, brief burst. The material then falls back down as a rain-like shower around the seal. Part of it forms a single sharp projectile, which holds its shape less reliably than the rest. The gathering also pulls in a little less than the burst can carry, so the launch thins out quickly.

name: s42_00242.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two glyphs sit side by side near the center, both modest in size relative to the ring. On the left is a four-lobed Billow sign. On the right is an Expansion sign of nested corner brackets with its corners pointing outward. Four Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke with short hooks at both ends, sit about halfway between the center and the ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast, and west-southwest positions, each angled to follow its position around the seal. A single Cooling sign, a short line between pairs of dots, sits close to the ring at the north-northeast. There is no element sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Billow takes the center as the core of the spell. It turns available material into a fluffy cloud, and because no element is set, it works on whatever material is directed into the seal. Expansion shares the center. It is semi-directional, and with its corners pointing outward it makes its target grow, so the cloud swells. The four evenly spaced Envelopment signs make the effect surround its target, so the cloud wraps around whatever it acts on instead of sitting in one spot, and no side is favored. Cooling is not directional, so its position near the ring adds no direction. It cools the result, and as a single small sign its effect is mild. Billow and Expansion are both drawn modestly in size, which keeps the cloud moderate rather than overwhelming. The three modifiers of growth, envelopment, and cooling work together without contradiction. The neat drawing and closed ring let the spell activate and hold steady.
effect: Turns material directed into the seal into a soft, fluffy cloud that swells in size and wraps around its target, enveloping it on all sides. The cloud is noticeably cool to the touch, though only mildly so.

name: s42_00243.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background, ring closed. A water sigil sits upright at the center and is moderate in size, about a third of the ring's radius. Seven Repetition signs are spread evenly around it in two layers. Three sit about halfway between the center and the ring, at the north, east-southeast and southwest, each turned at a different angle. Four sit just inside the ring at the northeast, south-southeast, west-southwest and northwest, each with its top toward the ring. Outside the main ring, two small sub-seals are joined to it by short straight lines, one at the north-northeast and one at the south-southwest. Each has a closed ring with a wind sigil at its center. The sigil fills roughly half of each small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Repetition continuously resets whatever the spell affects to the state it had when the spell first took hold. That reset covers both form and temperature. Seven Repetition signs, balanced around the ring, make this hold strong and even on every side. The varied rotations of the inner signs favor no direction. The two linked sub-seals each carry a wind sigil, which moves air but does not create it. Their sigils are large relative to their own rings, so each gives a fairly strong current, but the sub-seals are small, so their reach is limited. Sitting on opposite sides of the main seal, they move air across the water from two directions. The seal combines only two kinds of effect, which do not contradict each other, and it is neatly drawn with every ring closed, so it activates and holds steady.
effect: Keeps a body of water locked in the state it was in when the spell began. Any change to its shape, amount or temperature is steadily undone. At the same time, two opposing currents of air sweep across it, stirring and rippling the surface, but the water keeps returning to its original form.

name: s42_00244.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is drawn roughly and is noticeably out of round, bulging into a lumpy, almost hexagonal outline. An earth sigil sits at the center, small relative to the ring and slightly rough. Four Windows signs, each a small circle lined with hatched strokes, are spread around it: two farther out near the ring at the west-northwest and east-southeast, and two closer in at the northeast and southwest. A single Diamond sign sits near the ring at the north, tilted slightly. The signs are not evenly balanced and lean toward the north. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined, creating a passage from one location to another. Here it appears as four small separate rings rather than one lining band, which spreads that connection across several points instead of the whole seal. Diamond confines a spell to the objects inside the container it is drawn on, without affecting the container itself. Together they suggest a spell that sends earthen material held inside a container through to another place while leaving the vessel untouched. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they do not conflict, so the seal is not unstable. However, the strokes are rough, which weakens it and shortens its duration, and the ring is far from round, which makes the effect fleeting and risks it failing to activate. The northward lean of the signs biases the effect toward that side.
effect: Sends soil, sand or stone held inside the vessel it is drawn on through a passage to another location, leaving the vessel itself in place. The passage opens only briefly and weakly, carrying small amounts at a time, favoring material on its northern side and flickering shut before much has moved; at times it fails to open at all.

name: s42_00245.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, with no sigil. Four small Billow signs, each a four-lobed clover shape, sit about halfway between the center and the ring at the north, east, south and west points. The western one looks slightly rougher than the others. Four Partition signs sit close to the ring at the northeast, west-northwest, east-southeast and south-southwest. Three of them have their peaked tops toward the ring. The northeast one is flipped, with its top facing the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. Billow is a sign that turns available material into a fluffy cloud. Four of them spaced evenly around the center make that the core behavior of the seal, applied on all sides. Their small size gives a modest effect, and the slightly rough western Billow makes that side a little weaker and shorter lived. With no Collection or Gathering signs, the seal does not draw in material on its own; it only works on material directed into it. Partition is directional and outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending outward and upward. The three Partitions facing the ring set an outward boundary. The flipped northeast Partition faces inward, so the boundary on that side is drawn in toward the center rather than pushed out. This is a single reversed sign within one kind of modifier, not a contradiction. With only two kinds of modifier, the seal is balanced and stable.
effect: Turns material brought into the seal into soft, fluffy cloud that fills a bounded space rising up and out around the seal. The space is pinched inward on the northeast side, so the cloud is shallower there. The western part of the cloud is slightly thinner and fades a little sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00246.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. The center is empty, with no sigil. Seven Stillness signs sit around the seal, each with its top toward the ring. Four sit near the ring at the north, east, south, and west points; the north one is drawn boldly and neatly, the others somewhat lighter. A second, smaller Stillness sign sits about halfway in from the ring at the north, east, and south points, but not at the west. Several signs are a little rough, and the inner east sign is the roughest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil, the seal is tied to no element and has nothing in the center to set its kind of magic. The only modifier is Stillness, which holds magic in place so its effect stays static in one location.
