Doubling the sign at north, east, and south adds to how firmly and widely the hold applies, and the outer ring of four keeps it balanced around the seal, so no direction is favored. One kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. The rough strokes, especially on the inner east sign, make the hold somewhat weaker and shorter lived than a clean drawing would.
effect: Holds whatever magic or material is brought over the seal in place, keeping it fixed and unchanging above the seal rather than letting it drift or fade. The hold loosens sooner than a well-drawn version would, slipping slightly earlier on the east side.

name: s42_00247.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap on the left side running from about the west point down toward the southwest. Two small sigils share the center: a light sigil just left of center and a wind sigil with its flanking dashes just right of center, each small relative to the ring. Seven hourglass-shaped Reflection signs surround them. Four sit near the ring at the north-northwest, east-northeast, south-southeast and west-southwest. Three sit roughly halfway out, at the east, south-southwest and northwest. Each is rotated to align with its position, and the signs are spread evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil creates and shapes light, and the wind sigil moves air. Both are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is modest. Reflection works on a reflected image found on the object the seal is drawn on. Paired with light, this means the spell takes up that reflection and renders it as light. The wind sigil keeps the surrounding air moving, so the rendered image drifts and stirs rather than holding perfectly still. The seven Reflection signs are evenly spread, and because the hourglass shape reads the same from either end, their facing adds no direction. The image is therefore cast evenly around the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, and it does not conflict with either sigil. Because the ring is open, the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: It does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it would capture the reflection showing on the surface it is drawn on and cast it as a soft image of light around the seal, gently drifting and rippling on moving air. The light is modest in strength and slowly fades over time.

name: s42_00248.png
description:
A fully visible seal on a plain white background. The outer ring is neatly drawn but open, with a wide gap at the east-northeast. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Four signs sit near the outer ring:
- An Entwining sign at the north-northwest.
- A Link sign at the west, rotated on its side.
- A Repetition sign at the south-southwest.
- A single Regions sign at the south-southeast, its point toward the center.

Three small closed sub-seals sit inside the main ring:
- At the north, a neat sub-seal holds a large Refuse sign in place of a sigil.
- At the southeast, a sub-seal holds a small earth sigil. Both its ring and its sigil are slightly rough.
- At the west-southwest, a neat sub-seal holds a fairly large water sigil.

The signs are not evenly spread and cluster toward the west and south-southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification:
The earth sigil sets the main element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, soil and sand. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity.

The modifiers:
- Repetition here is a sign rather than the core. It keeps resetting what it affects to the state it had when the spell first took hold.
- Entwining makes affected material wrap itself around other objects.
- Link identifies and connects pieces that broke off from, or were made from, the same source.
- The single inward-pointing Regions sign keeps the magic inside the ring. Because it stands alone, the effect is biased toward its side.

The sub-seals:
- The Refuse sub-seal draws waste toward where it points, which is north.
- The water sub-seal adds a separate, fairly strong water working, sitting on the same side the signs lean toward.
- The small, slightly rough earth sub-seal adds a weak, short-lived earth effect.

The imbalance pushes the whole effect toward the west-southwest. The seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: time reset, wrapping, linking, region control and waste collection. The earth sigil, Link and Repetition dominate. Entwining shapes the motion, and the Refuse and water sub-seals are secondary, so the result is likely unstable. The main ring is open, so nothing activates until it is closed.
effect: As drawn, the seal does not activate. Once closed, it would find fragments of stone or soil from a common source, link them together and wrap them around a nearby object. It would keep snapping them back to their original state whenever they shift. The binding pulls lopsidedly toward the west-southwest, water seeps unevenly into the stone on that side, and grit and debris are dragged off to the north in fits. The weaker earth working at the southeast fades early, so the wrap loosens and re-forms erratically rather than holding a steady shape.

name: s42_00249.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but hand-drawn and slightly lumpy rather than perfectly round. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, small relative to the ring. Two Coil signs sit near the ring, one at the northwest and one at the south-southeast. Four Entwining signs are present. The ones at the north and south sit about halfway out with their tops toward the center. The ones at the east-northeast and west-southwest sit near the ring with their tops toward the ring; the east-northeast one is drawn heavily and roughly. At the east, about halfway out, is an unnamed glyph: an S-curve inside a small circle ringed by dots, resembling a wind-family sigil variant. Several glyphs are drawn somewhat roughly, but the signs are spread evenly around the seal and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as soil, stone and wood. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. The circled S with dots matches no known sigil exactly. Its closest match is Whorling Wind, which manipulates air through rotation, so reading it that way is a guess. On that reading it acts as a second sigil that adds a turning, twisting motion. Coil softens solid matter, which suits the earth sigil because Coil only affects physical material. Entwining makes the affected material wrap around other objects. Two of the Entwining signs face the center and two face the ring, which spreads the wrapping both inward and outward. Entwining has never been seen inverted, so the difference between the two facings is uncertain. Only two kinds of modifier are present, softening and wrapping, and they support each other rather than contradicting. The signs are balanced, so the effect has no favored direction. However, the rough strokes and the slightly out-of-round ring make the spell weaker and shorter lived.
effect: Softens nearby soil or stone into pliable strands and twists them around a target, wrapping it in a coiling grip. The softening is patchy and the wrapping turns unevenly, so the strands slacken and lose their hold after a short time.

name: s42_00250.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Rain sign, a square with concave sides and three short strokes on each side, sits upright at the center. It is modest in size relative to the ring, its middle is empty with no sigil inside, and its lines are a little rough. Six four-lobed Billow signs are spaced evenly just inside the ring, at the north-northwest, northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, southwest and west-northwest positions. The north-northwest and west-northwest Billows are slightly rougher than the other four. No element sigil is present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. Rain sits at the center as the core of the seal. It is drawn upright rather than inverted, so it keeps its normal effect: summoning a target material down over the area, like rainfall. Its empty middle leaves the material unspecified. The six Billow signs are non-directional, so their orientation does not matter. They turn available material into a soft, fluffy cloud, and because they are evenly balanced around the ring, no direction is favored. The two kinds of modifier work together: Billow supplies the cloud form and Rain makes it fall as a shower. The rough strokes on the center and on two of the Billows slightly weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Turns available material into small fluffy cloud puffs and showers them down gently over the area around the seal, like a soft rainfall. The shower is modest. It falls a little unevenly, thinning on the northwest side, and tapers off sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00251.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly, bulging into a lopsided, squarish shape rather than a true circle. A small Coil sign, two crossing curved strokes, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, slightly rough. Five Dispersion signs sit about two-thirds of the way out, at the northwest, northeast, southeast, southwest and south. The four diagonal ones point their stems toward the ring with their curves facing the center. The southern one is flipped, with its stem toward the center and its curve facing the ring. Several are drawn roughly. At the north-northwest, near the ring, sits a neatly drawn glyph lying on its side: a central vertical stroke with mirrored E-shaped branches on either side. It matches no known sign exactly. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Coil sign at the center acts as the core. Coil softens physical matter and cannot affect liquids or gases. Its small size relative to the ring gives the spell low intensity. Dispersion makes magic pour outward instead of beaming in one direction. Five of them spread evenly around the ring send the softening out on all sides. The flipped southern Dispersion follows the same outward-pouring behavior, and the difference between its two orientations is not known. The sideways glyph most closely resembles Stillness, which holds a magical effect static in one place, so this reading is a guess. Read that way, it would tend to anchor the effect against the outward spread. With only one such sign against five Dispersion signs, the outward pour dominates, and the anchoring only slows how far the effect drifts. The bigger weakness is the drawing itself. The ring is not round enough, so the effect is fleeting and the seal may fail to activate. The rough, small glyphs further weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Softens solid objects in a loose spread outward from the seal on all sides, while leaving liquids and air unaffected. The softening is faint and flickers in and out unevenly from spot to spot, lingering slightly near the seal before fading within moments. At times it fails to take hold at all.

name: s42_00252.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed, but it is noticeably lumpy and uneven rather than round, bulging at the upper left and flattening along the right side. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center, both moderate in size relative to the ring. On the left is a water sigil. On the right is a glyph that looks like an earth sigil missing its top crossbar: a V-shaped base with angled side strokes and a dot on each side. Six three-stroke Aeriforms Defined signs sit about two-thirds of the way out from the center, at the west-northwest, north, northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast and southwest. Each fans outward with its top toward the ring. The west-northwest sign is a variant whose two halves mirror each other. The northeast, southwest and west-northwest signs are drawn a little roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the main element, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The second central glyph matches no known sigil exactly. Its closest match is the earth sigil with its top part missing, so reading it as earth is a guess. Under that reading it adds a second core acting on solid matter such as soil and sand, likely at reduced strength because part of it is absent. Aeriforms Defined shares its design with the strokes of the wind sigil and its name with the aeriforms sigil, which creates air. Here it is read as working air into the spell's material. All six face outward, which is their usual orientation, and they are evenly spaced, so no direction is favored. The mirrored variant at the west-northwest is closest to Aeriforms Defined, also a guess, and is read the same way. Only one kind of modifier is present, and it does not contradict the two cores. The ring is closed but not round enough, which makes the effect fleeting and may keep it from activating at all. The roughly drawn signs weaken the effect on their sides.
effect: Works air into water mixed with loose soil, churning it into a frothy, bubbling mud that wells up evenly around the seal. The froth is thinner and weaker toward the northeast, southwest and west-northwest. The whole effect sputters on only briefly and flickers out quickly, and on some attempts it may fail to start at all.

name: s42_00253.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small water sigil sits at the center, slightly roughly drawn. The band between the rings holds five Columns signs, at the north-northeast, east, south, west-southwest and northwest. The south, west-southwest and northwest signs have their crossbars toward the outer ring and their stems pointing inward. The north-northeast and east signs are inverted, with their stems toward the ring and their crossbars toward the center. Inside the inner ring are three more Columns signs, at the north-northeast, southeast and west-southwest, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem toward the center. Outside the main seal at the east-northeast is a small closed ring joined to the outer ring by a short line. A fire sigil sits at its center, filling about half of that small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element. Its small size gives a modest intensity, and its slightly rough lines make the water a little weaker and shorter lived. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Eight Columns signs spread evenly around the seal give the water a column shape. Because the signs are balanced, no side is favored and the column rises straight up, and their number raises the amount of water. The two inverted Columns in the outer band manifest horizontally, much like Dispersion, so part of the water spreads outward around the column's base instead of rising. The linked sub-seal carries its own fire sigil, which is large relative to its small ring. This feeds a fairly concentrated but small-scale heat into the main spell. The modifiers are all one kind, so nothing in the seal contradicts itself.
effect: Raises a modest column of water straight up from the seal, with a little water spilling outward around its base. The water is heated as it rises, so the column comes up warm and lightly steaming. The flow is slightly uneven and dies down sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00254.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is neatly drawn but open, with a gap on the east side just below the east point. A large Immobility sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, reaching about two-fifths of the way to the ring. No element sigil is present. Nine Mimicry signs surround it, each with its top toward the ring. Three larger ones sit near the ring at the west, north-northeast and south-southeast. Six smaller ones form an inner circle about halfway out, at the north, northwest, east-northeast, southeast, south and west-southwest. The east-northeast Mimicry sign is a little rough and blotchy, and all the others are neat. The signs are balanced around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. The Immobility sign at the center acts as the core. It makes the target immovable relative to the seal, holding its shape as if frozen while still letting it be moved as a whole. Its large size gives that hold considerable strength. Mimicry guides or imitates the movements of a target. With no decorative sigil to supply a creature's movements, it has nothing outside the seal to copy. Read together, the many Mimicry signs make the held target follow and copy the motion of the object the seal is drawn on. Immobility still allows movement in its frozen state, so the two modifiers work together without contradiction. The signs are balanced, so no direction is favored. The one rough sign slightly weakens its part of the seal. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: As drawn, it does not activate. Once closed, it locks the target rigidly in its current shape and pose, then makes it move in lockstep with the object bearing the seal, copying each shift and turn while never changing form. The following is slightly looser on one side, where the target can lag a moment behind the motion before snapping back into place.

name: s42_00255.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn as two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center of the inner ring, moderate in size relative to the seal. The inner ring holds nothing else, and all modifiers sit in the band between the two rings. Two Coil signs sit at the east-northeast and the southeast, both drawn small. A taller, stretched glyph resembling Coil sits at the northwest, angled along the ring. At the west-southwest is a small octagon with an X inside that matches no known sign exactly. The signs are spread evenly around the band. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell produces and works with heat. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Coil softens physical matter and does nothing to liquids or gases, so paired with fire it turns the heat toward making solids soft and pliable. Reading the stretched glyph as an elongated Coil is a guess; it would extend or deepen the softening along one axis. The octagon with an X is closest to Selection, also a guess. Read that way, it limits the effect to the object the seal is drawn on. The Coil signs are drawn small, which keeps the softening gentle rather than extreme. The modifiers are evenly spaced, so the effect favors no direction. Only softening and object selection are combined, and they do not conflict.
effect: Warms the object the seal is drawn on just enough to soften it, leaving it pliable and easy to bend or shape, much like wax or metal held near a flame. The heat spreads evenly through the object and is not thrown outward as fire. It has no effect on liquids or gases.

name: s42_00256.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but slightly rough and a little uneven in its roundness. There is no element sigil. A large Stillness sign stands upright at the center, reaching about half the ring's radius. A Coil sign sits at the north. A Collection sign sits near the ring at the east-northeast. A Binding sign, two stacked arcs bowing outward toward the ring, sits at the southwest. A small Mimicry sign, drawn sideways, sits at the west-northwest. A small Windows sign, a ringed circle lined with short markings, sits near the ring at the west. An Aeriforms Defined sign, three short fanning strokes, sits at the south. The signs cluster more heavily on the western side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the large central Stillness sign acts as the core and holds a magical effect static in one place. Its size points to a fairly strong hold. Collection draws in material from above and around the seal. Binding makes that material act as a single unit, and Coil softens physical matter. Aeriforms Defined ties the spell to air or gases. That clashes with Coil, which cannot affect gases. Mimicry imitates movement, but there is no decorative sigil to copy, and imitating movement works against Stillness. Windows connects two separate spaces, which also pulls against holding the effect in one spot. The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier. Stillness dominates, with Collection and Binding supporting it, while Windows, Mimicry and Coil are the least predictable parts, so the result is likely unstable. Windows and Mimicry both sit on the western side and pull the effect that way. The slightly uneven ring makes the spell weaker and shorter lived.
effect: Gathers nearby air and loose material into a single bound mass and holds it fixed in place above the seal, softening any solid bits caught in it. The western edge of the mass will not stay still: it twitches as if copying some motion and flickers as though partly slipping into another space. The hold wavers and gives out sooner than its strength suggests, releasing the gathered material unevenly.

name: s42_00257.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but noticeably out of round, with a lumpy, uneven outline. A water sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Stability and Level Planes signs sit about three-quarters of the way out, at the northeast, east-southeast, west-southwest and west-northwest; the east-southeast one is a little rough. At the south is a Stability and Level Planes sign with a tiny light sigil attached to its inner end, toward the center. At the north is a single thin, wide arc opening downward, like a Binding sign with only one curve. The signs are evenly spread, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives moderate intensity. Stability and Level Planes makes its target balance on a level plane in the air, the way something floats on water, so the water is held as a flat, hovering layer. Four of them, plus the fifth at the south, spread evenly around the ring, keep it level on all sides with no direction favored. The northern arc most closely resembles Binding, though this is a guess. Binding halts the material's movement and makes it act as one unit, so the water would hold together as a single sheet instead of breaking into drops. The tiny light sigil on the southern sign is read as adding a faint glow at that part of the plane, also a guess; its small size keeps it weak. These three kinds of modifier work together without contradiction. However, the ring is not round enough, which makes the spell fleeting and may stop it from activating at all.
effect: Draws water into a single flat sheet that hovers and stays level in the air, holding together as one body, with a faint glow along its southern edge. The sheet forms only briefly and may fail to form at all. When it does appear, it soon sags, wavers off level and breaks apart into falling water.

name: s42_00258.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The band between the outer and inner rings is empty. A Rain sign sits upright at the center, a square with inward-curving sides and short triple strokes at each corner. It takes the place of a sigil and is moderate in size relative to the ring, with nothing drawn in its open middle. Six Holding signs are evenly spaced about halfway out from the center, at the east, southeast, south-southwest, west, northwest and north-northeast. Each is a pair of facing curves with small dots, its top toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil. Rain is a sign that can sit in the center, and here it acts as the core of the seal. Rain summons a target, bringing it down from above like rainfall. Because it is upright and not turned inside out, it summons rather than repels. Its moderate size gives a moderate strength. The six Holding signs are non-directional and keep the target in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. They are evenly balanced, so no side is favored and the held form stays round and centered. The extra inner ring adds strength to the spell even with its band left empty. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction. With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and acts on whatever material it is directed at.
effect: Draws down a steady, rain-like fall of material over the seal and gathers it into a round mass matching the seal's outline. The mass can sway and shift without losing its shape, and it holds together firmly for as long as the spell lasts.

name: s42_00259.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A Selection sign, a small grid of four boxes crossed by a plus whose arms reach past the frame, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil. It is fairly large relative to the inner ring, and its strokes are a little rough. Three small Diamond signs sit in the band between the two rings, at the north-northeast, southeast and west-southwest. They are evenly spaced about a third of the way around from one another, each with its top toward the outer ring. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Selection sign takes the center and serves as the core of the seal. Selection is non-directional and confines a spell's effect to the object it is drawn on. Its large size gives it a strong hold, but the slightly rough strokes make that hold a little weaker and shorter lived. Diamond does the reverse: it makes a spell act only on what is held inside the container it is drawn on, leaving the container itself untouched. These two directly contradict each other. The large central Selection dominates, and the three Diamonds in the outer band pull against it. Because the Diamonds are evenly spaced, they add no direction, only competing targeting. Neither sign supplies an action or an element, so the seal decides only what is affected, not how. The conflict makes the result likely unstable.
effect: Marks the object it is drawn on as the only thing magic may act on, but causes no change of its own. The marking wavers, slipping at moments from the object onto whatever it contains and then back. The hold fades sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00260.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center at a moderate size relative to the ring. Six Refuse signs, each a small diamond above a crossed pair of legs, are spread evenly around it about halfway to the ring. The two at the north and south-southeast have their diamond ends facing the center. The four at the west-northwest, northeast, east-southeast and southwest have their diamond ends facing the ring. The southwest Refuse sign is drawn with heavier, slightly rougher strokes than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell. Its moderate size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong but not overwhelming intensity, and light from this sigil diminishes over time. Refuse is a directional sign that collects unwanted material toward where it points. Four Refuse signs face outward and two face inward. The outward pull and the inward pull work against each other, so the signs directly contradict. The four outward signs outnumber the inward pair and dominate, so the net effect sweeps waste away from the seal toward its edges, while the inward pair draws some back toward the center. Because of this opposition the result is likely unstable. The rough southwest sign is weaker and shorter lived, so that side is cleared less firmly. The signs are evenly spaced, so the outward sweep favors no single direction.
effect: Gives off a fairly bright glow that sweeps dust, grime and debris outward from the seal, clearing the space around it. Some of the debris is tugged back toward the middle, so the mess shifts back and forth and never fully settles, and the southwest side clears more weakly and gives out first. The light gradually dims, and the sweeping fades with it.

name: s42_00261.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An Immobility sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil, drawn as a vertical stroke on a base bar flanked by two curved brackets. It is fairly large, reaching a little under half the ring's radius. Six Coil signs, each two crossing curved strokes, surround it. Four sit close to the ring at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest. Two sit closer to the center, one at the north-northwest and one at the east. There is no element sigil, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Immobility takes the center and sets the core of the spell. It makes the target immovable relative to the seal, holding its shape as if frozen while still allowing the seal and target to be carried together. Its fairly large size gives the effect solid strength. Coil softens a target and works only on physical matter, not liquids or gases. It is non-directional, so the different orientations of the six signs and their two spacings do not change their effect. Their number strengthens the softening, and their spread around the ring keeps it even. Softening and holding work on different aspects of the target, so they combine rather than conflict. With only two kinds of modifier, a closed ring and neat drawing, the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Softens solid matter touched by the seal while locking it firmly in place relative to the seal, so it becomes pliant yet cannot shift or lose its shape. The softening is thorough and even across the whole target. It has no effect on liquids or gases.

name: s42_00262.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center, and its lines are slightly rough. Three Stretch signs sit just inside the ring at the north-northeast, west, and south-southeast positions, roughly evenly spaced. Each has its rounded top toward the center and its open, footed side toward the ring. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, and its slightly rough lines make the effect a little weaker and shorter lived. Stretch turns solid objects that contact the seal into long, flexible ribbons. It works by surrounding the central sigil, and these three signs do that. They are evenly spaced, so no direction is favored. Stretch acts on solids while wind acts on air, so the two divide the work rather than contradict each other: matter touching the seal is drawn out into ribbons, and the moving air carries them. There are no directional signs, so the motion has no set heading.
effect: Draws solid objects that touch the seal out into long, flexible ribbons and sets them rippling and drifting on a gentle current of air around the seal, with no particular heading. The breeze is light and slackens after a fairly short time, leaving the ribbons to settle.

name: s42_00263.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn, with the ring open at a wide gap in the upper right between the north-northeast and east-northeast signs. No element sigil is present. The center holds three vertical strokes, a tall middle line between two shorter ones of equal height, slightly rough and moderately large relative to the ring. It resembles a Detection sign with one half mirrored onto the other. Five eight-armed star signs with eye marks sit near the ring. Four of them are Concealment signs: one at north-northeast (drawn roughly) and one at west-southwest (slightly rough), both with their tops toward the center, and one each at east-northeast and south-southeast, both neat with their tops toward the ring. The fifth, at the southeast, is bolder and resembles Concealment with its top part missing, top toward the center. Four of the five signs crowd the east and south side, so the layout leans toward the east-southeast.
justification: With no element sigil, the central glyph acts as the core. Its closest match is Detection, so reading it as Detection is a guess. Detection is tied to sensing presence, and the mirrored form makes it symmetric, so the sensing would not favor one side. Its fairly large size gives a moderate intensity, though its slight roughness weakens it and shortens how long it lasts. Concealment hides a target, and together with the sensing core the seal would conceal whatever it detects. The southeast glyph is read as a partial Concealment, also a guess, adding a weaker share of the same hiding effect. It is not known whether Concealment changes behavior when turned, so the outward-facing pair is read as hiding in the same way as the others. Because most of the Concealment signs gather on the east-southeast side, the hiding is strongest there and thin to the northwest. The rough north-northeast sign makes that part of the effect weaker. Only two related kinds of modifier are present, so the seal is not unstable. The ring is open, so it will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it senses presences around it at moderate strength and hides them from view, cloaking them well toward the east-southeast but only faintly toward the northwest. The sensing fades sooner than usual, and the hiding toward the north-northeast is patchy and lets through some glimpses.

name: s42_00264.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Five Regions signs, each an angled chevron, point inward toward the center. Four sit close to the ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest. A fifth sits further in at the east-southeast, just inside the outer one there. Three small Windows signs appear, each a hatched ring. One sits near the ring at the north, one partway in at the west, and one toward the south-southeast; that last one is drawn a little roughly. The signs are spread evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Every Regions sign points inward, so the magic manifests only within the ring and not outside it. The doubled Regions sign at the east-southeast adds weight there but points the same way as the rest, so it reinforces that containment rather than redirecting it. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically joined, letting magic pass from one location to another. Here it is drawn as three separate marks rather than as a band lining the ring. Reading them as individual connection points is a guess. Only two kinds of modifier are present: containment and connection. They do not contradict each other, and the balanced layout favors no direction. The slightly rough Windows sign at the south-southeast makes that one link a little weaker than the others.
effect: Kindles a moderate fire confined entirely within the seal's bounds and links that space to another location, so the flames and their heat can be seen and felt through it from elsewhere. One of the links is a little less steady than the others, so the connection there flickers slightly while the fire itself stays contained.

name: s42_00265.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size at a little under half the ring's radius. Three Selection signs sit just inside the ring at the north, east-southeast, and west-southwest points. Each is drawn as a small square crossed by a grid of lines that extend past its edges. Two Columns signs sit about halfway out, one at the north-northeast and one at the west. Each has its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the center. Three Crushing signs sit near the ring at the northeast, south, and west-northwest points, all inverted so they face outward. The three sets of signs alternate evenly around the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Selection is non-directional and confines the spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on. Its three evenly spaced copies keep the flame bound to that surface. Columns gives the magic a column-shaped area of effect. Only two Columns signs are present, at the north-northeast and west, so they are not balanced on opposite sides. The column therefore leans toward the side between them, roughly northwest, instead of rising straight up. Crushing is semi-directional, and inverted it reverses its usual breaking effect, pulling scattered material back into one form for as long as the spell lasts. Crushing is only known from work on solid matter, so its effect on fire is uncertain. Read here, the inverted signs would draw stray sparks and embers back into the main flame, keeping it compact. This reformed state lasts only while the spell holds. The seal uses three kinds of modifier that work together without contradiction, so it should be stable.
effect: Raises a moderate column of fire from the object the seal is drawn on, leaning toward the northwest rather than straight up. Loose sparks and embers are pulled back into the flame, so the fire stays dense and tightly formed instead of scattering. When the spell ends, the flame loses this cohesion and breaks apart.

name: s42_00266.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The main ring is neatly drawn but open, with a gap at the north-northwest just beside the top. A large upright Columns sign sits at the center in place of a sigil, and there is no element sigil. Six signs sit just inside the ring. An inverted Rain sign is at the north-northwest, a Pointing sign at the north-northeast, and a Stillness sign at the east-northeast with its top toward the center. An Envelopment sign sits at the south-southeast, a Levitation sign at the south-southwest with its arrow toward the center, and an Aeriforms Defined sign at the west. The Pointing and Levitation signs are a little rough. At the north-northeast, inside the main ring, is a small sub-seal with a roughly drawn ring that is open at its lower left. It holds a single Reflection sign at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Columns sign acts as the core. It gives the magic a column-shaped area of effect pushed straight out from the seal, and its moderate size gives moderate force. Pointing would taper that column into a cone. Aeriforms Defined ties the effect to air, and Envelopment makes it wrap around its target. Levitation, pointing inward, would float the target. Stillness, by contrast, holds an effect fixed in one place, which directly contradicts Levitation. Inverted Rain creates a zone that the target cannot enter or is pushed out of, which works against Envelopment's wrapping. Together the seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier. The Columns core dominates, with Pointing and Aeriforms Defined shaping it, while the clashing pairs pull against each other, so the result is likely unstable. The rough Levitation and Pointing signs weaken those parts further. The sub-seal's Reflection sign would target a reflected image, but its ring is rough and open, so it adds nothing as drawn. The main ring is also open, so the seal does not activate.
effect: Does not activate as drawn. If closed, it would raise a moderate, cone-tapered column of air that tries to wrap around and lift its target while also pinning it in place and shoving it away. The column flickers between holding still and floating, its edges push outward unevenly, and it tends to collapse early.

name: s42_00267.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly: it is lumpy and noticeably out of round, bulging at several points. A water sigil sits at the center, neatly drawn and of moderate size relative to the ring. A large, heavily lined Strengthening sign sits at the northeast, its apex toward the ring. A Diamond sign sits at the southeast, rotated at a slant, about halfway out from the center. A small Selection sign sits near the ring at the south. A Collection sign sits at the west-southwest near the ring, with its barred end toward the center and its open side facing outward. A small Gathering sign sits near the ring at the northwest, its fork outward and its point angled toward the center. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Gathering and Collection both let a spell draw material from its surroundings, so together they pull in water for the spell to use. Collection here has its open side turned outward instead of its usual inward orientation, so as a reading it reaches for water beyond the ring. Strengthening makes the result harder and more durable, which here would pack the gathered water firm. Selection confines a spell to the object it is drawn on, while Diamond restricts it to the contents of a container and spares the container itself. These two directly contradict each other. Diamond is drawn larger and closer to the sigil, so it likely dominates over the small Selection sign, but the clash makes the targeting likely unstable. The signs are balanced, so no direction is favored. The out-of-round ring weakens the whole seal, so the effect is fleeting and may fail to activate at all.
effect: Draws in water from around the seal and packs it firmly into whatever container the seal is drawn on. The magic wavers between acting on the water inside and acting on the container itself, so the water sometimes slackens or seeps into the vessel's walls. When it does take hold, the effect is brief and the gathered water loosens again almost at once.

name: s42_00268.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn, with two concentric rings. Both are ring open: the outer ring has a wide gap at the lower left, between the west-southwest and the south, and the inner ring has a gap at the lower right, between the east and the south-southeast. A light sigil sits upright at the center, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, drawn at moderate size relative to the inner ring. Four small Repetition signs sit about halfway out inside the inner ring at the north, east, south-southwest and west, each with its top toward the center. Three small Selection signs sit in the band between the two rings at the north, west-southwest and south, each rotated at a different angle. The signs are evenly spread, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes light. Its moderate size gives a moderate brightness. Light from this sigil normally diminishes over time, but Repetition continually resets whatever it affects to the state it had when the spell first took hold. Four balanced Repetition signs therefore keep the light restored to its starting brightness instead of letting it fade. Selection is non-directional and confines a spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on, so the glow stays on that object rather than spreading or projecting outward. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction. The neat drawing and even spacing favor a steady result, but both rings are open, so the seal will not activate until both gaps are closed.
effect: It does not activate while its rings are open. Once closed, it makes the object it is drawn on glow with a moderate, steady light that keeps restoring itself to full brightness, so it does not dim over time.

name: s42_00269.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with three smaller seals attached outside it. The main ring is closed and neatly drawn. A large light sigil, about half the ring's radius, sits upright at the center. Five Reflection signs, each an hourglass of two touching triangles, are spread around it at the northeast, south-southeast, south-southwest, west and northwest, each rotated at a different angle. The northeast one sits close to the ring and the others sit about two-thirds of the way out. The northwest Reflection is drawn a little rougher than the rest. Three small sub-seals are joined to the main ring by short lines. The north-northeast one has its ring closed and holds an earth sigil. The south-southeast one has its ring closed and holds a Partition sign at its center. The west one holds a small light sigil, but its ring is open with a gap at the upper right. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The large light sigil makes this a fairly strong light spell. Reflection targets a reflected image found on the surface the seal is drawn on. Five of them, balanced around the ring and pointing no single way, spread that effect evenly. The slightly rough northwest Reflection makes that part a little weaker. The linked sub-seals add further effects. The closed earth sub-seal brings in manipulation of solid matter such as stone, so the reflected light works through stone surfaces. The closed Partition sub-seal outlines the borders of the area of effect, extending outward and upward, so the light is confined to a defined region. The west light sub-seal has an open ring and does not activate, so it adds nothing for now. Reflection, earth and Partition do not contradict one another, so the seal holds together.
effect: Makes stone surfaces within a clearly bounded area light up with bright, glowing images of whatever they reflect. The images on one side come through slightly fainter, and all of the light slowly dims over time. A small attached light remains inactive; if it were closed, it would add a modest extra glow to the display.

name: s42_00270.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Purification sign, a hooked curl, sits upright at the center in place of a sigil and is moderately large relative to the ring. Ten Binding signs, each a pair of nested arcs, surround it in two loose bands. Four sit about halfway out at the west-southwest, north-northwest, east-northeast and south-southeast, with the tops of their arcs toward the center. Six sit close to the ring at the north-northeast, east-northeast, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest, with the tops of their arcs toward the ring. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so the Purification sign at the center serves as the core of the spell. It separates waste from water, which ties the seal to water without a water sigil. Its moderate size gives a moderate strength. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. That is the only modifier present, so the seal is not unstable. The inner Binding signs face the center and the outer ones face the ring. Reading this as a hold applied from both inside and outside is a guess, since Binding's directional behavior is unknown. Under that reading, the separated waste is gathered and held firmly in place rather than allowed to drift. The even spacing means no side is favored. Purification is asymmetric, so the fine details of how the separation proceeds are less predictable than the binding.
effect: Separates waste from water and binds the separated waste into firm, cohesive clumps that stop drifting and move as single units. This leaves clean water behind and makes the waste easy to lift out whole. The cleansing works at a moderate strength and holds steady while the spell lasts.

name: s42_00271.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed, but it is slightly lumpy and not perfectly round. A water sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring and a little roughly drawn. Four Aeriforms Defined signs, each three short strokes fanning outward with the middle stroke longest, sit at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest points, with their tops toward the ring. The northeast one is slightly rougher than the others. A single Regions sign sits close to the ring at the east point, its apex pointing inward toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Aeriforms Defined shares its name with the sigil that creates air and shares its shape with the wind sigil's modifiers, so it ties the spell to gases. Paired with water, it reads as giving the water a gaseous, vapor-like form. The four Aeriforms Defined signs are evenly placed, so no side is favored. The only Regions sign points inward, and when all Regions signs point inward the magic manifests only within the ring. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not conflict. The slightly rough sigil and the not-quite-round ring weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts, without stopping it from activating.
effect: Fills the space within the seal's bounds with a moderate cloud of water vapor, like a contained mist that stays over the seal instead of drifting away. The mist is somewhat thin and uneven, its edges waver, and it dissipates sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00272.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils sit side by side at the center, both small relative to the ring: a water sigil on the left and a wind sigil on the right. A small Rain sign, drawn a little roughly, sits at the northwest about halfway to the ring. A Reflection sign sits at the northeast. A large, heavy Regions sign sits near the ring at the east, its point aimed inward toward the center. A Partition sign sits near the ring at the west-southwest, rotated at an angle. A Pointing sign sits at the west-northwest near the ring. A roughly drawn Purification sign, rotated so its curl lies on its side, sits at the south about halfway to the ring. The signs are spread evenly around the seal. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil and wind sigil share the center as a double core, so the spell makes water and moves it through the air. Both sigils are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is modest. Rain summons the water as falling drops, and the Regions sign pointing inward keeps the magic inside the bounds of the ring. Partition outlines the borders of that area, which reinforces the inward confinement. Pointing tapers the material into conical shapes, so each drop comes down sharpened. Purification is asymmetric and separates waste from water. Reflection targets reflected images. The seal stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: summoning, tapering, purifying, and reflecting, in addition to the area limits. The two sigils, Rain, and the inward Regions and Partition dominate, so a contained rainfall forms reliably. Pointing shapes it secondarily. Purification is drawn roughly and is asymmetric, and Reflection has no clear partner in the seal, so they are the least predictable parts. The result is likely unstable.
effect: Brings down a light, wind-driven shower of water only within the area of the seal, with drops that fall tapered into small points. The rain gusts unevenly from one side to another. Some patches come down clear while others carry grit, and faint reflected glimmers flicker across the falling drops at random. The shower tends to thin out and sputter before it settles into a steady fall.

name: s42_00273.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An upright fire sigil sits at the center, modest in size relative to the ring. Four Binding signs, each made of two nested arcs with the larger arc toward the ring, sit about halfway out from the center at the northwest, northeast, southeast and southwest. They are evenly spaced. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell that creates and shapes flame or heat. Its modest size relative to the ring gives a moderate intensity. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. Four Binding signs make that hold firm, so the flame cannot scatter, leap outward or spread. They are evenly balanced at the intercardinal points, so no side is favored. With no Columns, Regions or other directional signs, nothing sends the fire away from the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, and the neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Creates a moderate mass of fire that is held together as a single, compact unit, staying in place over the seal instead of flickering outward or spreading. If moved, the flame shifts as one whole body rather than breaking apart.

name: s42_00274.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed and drawn fairly neatly, though slightly uneven in roundness. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Five small glyphs sit near the ring. Two plain Rain signs, small, spiky and roughly drawn, sit at the north-northwest and the west-southwest. At the east-southeast is a larger, neater Rain sign, rotated so its top faces the center, with an extra filled dot on that inner side. At the south-southeast is a rough Rain sign with a small Collection-like crossed stroke attached at its edge. At the east-northeast is a single thin, faint arc that matches no known sign. The signs are spread evenly around the ring.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Rain summons the spell's material and brings it down from above, and four Rain signs spread evenly around the ring spread that fall over the whole area rather than favoring one side. Rain is radially symmetric, so it is only inverted when flipped inside-out. The rotated east-southeast Rain therefore still acts as normal Rain. Its extra dot matches no known mark and adds nothing that can be read. The small Collection attached to the south-southeast Rain gathers air from above and around the seal for the spell to use, which suits a wind sigil that cannot create air. The lone arc most closely resembles Binding drawn with a single line. This is a guess, and it would hold the moved air together so it acts as a single mass. Rain, Collection and Binding work together without contradiction, so the seal is not unstable. However, the rough, small Rain signs make the downpour weaker and shorter lived on their sides of the seal.
effect: Gathers the surrounding air and brings it down over the area around the seal as a fairly strong fall of gusts, like rainfall made of wind, with the air pressing down together as one mass. The fall is uneven: it lands firmly on the east-southeast side but comes in thinner, patchier gusts elsewhere, and it fades sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00275.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but roughly drawn and lumpy, with flattened sides that make it look almost hexagonal rather than round. The center is empty, with no sigil. Four small Sights Set signs sit about three quarters of the way out from the center, at the north, east, south and west points. Each has its diamond end toward the ring and its arrow pointing inward at the center. The eastern sign is drawn heavier and rougher than the others, with its diamond nearly filled in. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil, the seal has no element and no material to work on. Sights Set lets the caster aim a spell at a chosen point or target. All four signs point inward and are evenly spaced, so they balance each other and fix that aim on the center of the seal rather than on any outward direction. The signs are small and roughly drawn, so their effect is weak. A ring this far from round gives a fleeting effect or may fail to activate entirely. Only one kind of modifier is present, so there is no contradiction between signs.
effect: Fixes a faint, caster-directed point of focus at the seal's center but carries no element, so nothing visible manifests there. The focus is weak and fleeting, flickering in and out and often failing to take hold at all.

name: s42_00276.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large, nearly half the ring's radius. A Stretch sign sits at the west, its rounded top toward the center and its open side facing the ring. An Expansion sign of nested corner brackets sits at the west-northwest, with its corners pointing outward. A Projection sign sits at the south, its flat bar toward the ring and its open side facing the center. An Envelopment sign sits near the ring at the north-northeast. A small Repetition sign sits near the ring at the southwest. Most signs cluster on the western and southern side, so the layout leans toward the west-southwest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Projection pushes the effect outward from the seal. Envelopment makes the effect wrap around its target. Expansion with its corners pointing outward makes the result grow. Stretch normally turns solid matter into long, flexible ribbons. Applied to flame it would draw the fire out into ribbon-like streamers, though this is less certain because Stretch is known to act on solids. Repetition keeps resetting what it affects to its original state, which works directly against the growth from Expansion and the reshaping from Stretch. The seal stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier: stretching, expanding, projecting, enveloping and repeating. The large fire sigil dominates, and Projection and Envelopment set the main behavior. Stretch and Expansion pull against Repetition, so the result is likely unstable. Because the signs are unbalanced toward the west-southwest, the effect is biased toward that side.
effect: Throws strong ribbons of flame out from the seal, mostly toward the west-southwest, and coils them around whatever they reach. The ribbons swell as they wrap, then snap back to their starting size, over and over. They pulse unevenly, so some streamers tear apart or gutter out while others flare far larger than intended. The wrap loosens and slips each time the flames reset.

name: s42_00277.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two glyphs share the center, both small relative to the ring: an earth sigil just left of center and a Link sign just right of it. Five Columns signs surround them at the northeast, northwest, west, southwest and southeast, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the center. The southeast Columns sign is smaller and more roughly drawn than the other four. Three of the five sit on the western half, so the arrangement is uneven. There is no sign at the north, east or south. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, sand and soil. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Link shares the center as a second core. It identifies pieces that broke off from, or were made from, the same source and creates a link between them. Columns gives the effect a column-shaped area and drives it with force, and having five of them adds to the amount of material moved. Columns sends the spell toward the side with the most signs. With three on the west side, the northeast and southeast signs only partly offset them, and the empty east side lets the column tilt toward the west-northwest instead of rising straight up. The rough southeast sign adds only a faint push from that side, which strengthens the westward tilt. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction.
effect: Finds pieces of stone or soil that came from the same source, links them together, and drives them in a modest column that slants up and away toward the west-northwest. The push from the southeast side is faint and uneven, so the column drifts a little further west than intended.

name: s42_00278.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, about half the ring's radius across, so it is fairly large. Seven Levitation signs surround it. Six point their arrowheads inward toward the sigil: one each at the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest near the ring, and smaller ones at the north and south, set closer to the center. The seventh, at the west near the ring, is inverted, with its arrowhead pointing outward toward the ring. The southeast sign is drawn with noticeably heavier strokes than the others. The east point has no sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its large size relative to the ring gives it a fairly strong intensity. Levitation floats its target into the air, and when the signs are balanced it tends to shape the result into a sphere. Six inward Levitation signs spread around the ring do exactly that. Sign length sets distance, carrying weight and speed, so the shorter north and south signs add only a little lift. The inverted Levitation at the west directly contradicts the others, because inverted Levitation is known to cancel the effect of regular Levitation. The six inward signs dominate and the fire still rises as a floating sphere. The lone inverted sign removes lift on the western side, though, so the result is likely unstable on that side. Because only one kind of modifier is used, there is no further conflict.
effect: Creates a fairly strong ball of fire that floats in the air above the seal. Its western side keeps losing lift, so the fireball sags and wobbles toward the west instead of holding a clean sphere. That side flickers and dips unevenly while the rest of the flame stays aloft.

name: s42_00279.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is slightly lumpy and not perfectly round. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by an upward and a downward teardrop, sits upright at the center at moderate size relative to the ring, with slightly shaky lines. Six Solidification signs, each two small circles joined by a short line, are spaced around the ring at the northwest, north-northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest, and west, each with its top toward the ring. Most are drawn with thin, even strokes, but the west sign and one lower sign are drawn heavier and less evenly. No other signs are present, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Solidification makes the magic it is tied to more solid, so the water is firmed rather than left to flow. All six modifiers are the same sign, so nothing contradicts them. They are evenly spread around the ring, so no direction is favored, and the effect stays centered on the seal instead of being projected outward. The slightly irregular ring and the shaky sigil and signs weaken the seal and shorten its duration, and the uneven roundness makes the hold less consistent.
effect: Firms water at the seal into a moderate, semi-solid, jelly-like mass that holds together instead of flowing. The mass is not uniformly firm, and some edges stay softer and sag. It loosens back into ordinary water sooner than expected.

name: s42_00280.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn a little roughly. A wind sigil sits upright at the center, neatly drawn and fairly large, reaching a little under half the ring's radius. Six signs are spaced around the outer part of the seal. A Dispersion sign sits at the north-northeast with its stem toward the center and its curve toward the ring. A Reflection sign, an hourglass turned on its side, sits at the east-northeast. A Detection sign of three parallel strokes sits at the southeast. A Stretch sign sits at the south with its arch toward the center and its open ends toward the ring. A Crushing sign sits at the west-southwest with its peaks toward the center, so it is inverted. A Holding sign, a pair of facing curves with dots, sits at the north-northwest, turned roughly upside down. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates air. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Dispersion makes that air pour outward from the seal. Holding pulls the other way: it keeps the target in a shape defined by the seal while still letting it move. Reflection targets a reflected image on the surface the seal is drawn on. Detection's function is unclear. Stretch turns solid objects into flexible ribbons. Inverted Crushing reforms crushed material instead of breaking it. Stretch and Crushing only act on solid matter, so they have little to work on in an air spell. The seal stacks six unrelated kinds of modifier, and Dispersion directly contradicts Holding. The large wind sigil dominates, and Dispersion and Holding compete to shape it. The solid-matter signs and Reflection add weak, erratic influences, so the result is likely unstable. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored. The slightly rough ring makes the spell somewhat weaker and shorter lived than a clean drawing would.
effect: Sends a strong rush of air outward from the seal in every direction, which keeps trying to gather into a held shape before breaking apart again, so the gusts pulse and waver instead of flowing steadily. Loose debris caught in the air sometimes twists into ribbon-like streamers or briefly clumps back together. The air may also shimmer as faint, distorted reflections appear and vanish. The effect fades sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00281.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric rings, both closed and a little rough. A downward-pointing Convergence triangle sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the inner ring and neatly drawn. Five Projection signs, flat brackets, sit about two thirds of the way out from the center at the north-northwest, northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast and south-southeast. Four have their open side facing the center. The east-southeast one is inverted, opening outward toward the ring. At the west-southwest is a Projection-like bracket with an extra short stroke rising from one end, which matches no known sign exactly. The signs crowd the eastern half, leaving the west and southwest mostly empty. The band between the two rings holds no signs, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so Convergence acts as the core. It draws the spell's magic and any loose material down to a single point and packs it tightly. Projection pushes an effect outward from the seal, and with most of these signs on the eastern side, the focused output is biased east instead of spreading evenly. The west-southwest glyph is read as a Projection variant, which is a guess, so it adds a weaker push toward that side. The inverted Projection at the east-southeast would reverse the push and hold the effect back on that side. This directly contradicts its outward-facing neighbors. The four outward Projections dominate, but the opposition makes the eastern output likely unstable. The second ring strengthens the seal, though it carries no extra signs. The rough linework of the rings and several signs makes the spell somewhat weaker and shorter lived. The moderate size of the central sign gives a moderate intensity.
effect: Gathers whatever magic or loose material is fed into it into a tight, compact point and casts it outward, mostly toward the east, with a faint secondary push to the west-southwest. Toward the east-southeast the output stutters, sometimes pulling back toward the seal before lurching outward again. The whole effect fades sooner than a cleanly drawn seal would.

name: s42_00282.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A Rain sign sits upright at the center in place of a sigil. Its square has inward-curving sides and short triple strokes at each edge, and its middle is empty, with no element sigil inside it. It is moderate in size relative to the ring. Six Binding signs, each a large arc paired with a smaller arc, form an inner circle about two-thirds of the way out. They sit at the north, east-northeast, southeast, south, west-southwest and northwest, each with its larger arc toward the center. Two more Binding signs sit just inside the ring at the north and west-southwest, directly beyond the inner ones at those points. These two face the opposite way, with their larger arcs toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind or light sigil is present, so the Rain sign at the center sets the core behavior: summoning a target material. Because no sigil sits inside it, the spell is not tied to one element. It is drawn upright rather than inside out, so it summons rather than repels. Binding halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit. With six evenly spaced inner Binding signs facing the center, the summoned material is drawn into one cohesive mass and held still within the seal's area. The two outer Binding signs face outward, the reverse of the inner ones. They add a second, outward binding at the north and west-southwest, so the mass is held somewhat more firmly toward those sides. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The neat drawing and closed ring mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Summons material from above in a moderate amount. Instead of scattering like rainfall, it gathers into a single cohesive mass that stops and hangs in place over the seal, where it can be moved as one piece. The mass holds slightly more firmly on its northern and west-southwestern sides than elsewhere.

name: s42_00283.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil sits upright at the center and is small relative to the ring. Five signs are spaced unevenly around it, most of them about three quarters of the way out. A Refuse sign, a diamond on crossed legs, sits at the east-northeast, tilted at an angle. A small Piercing sign, a short stroke through a diamond, sits at the northeast. An inverted Crushing sign sits at the north-northwest, with its zigzag set so it reads as inverted relative to the center. A Mimicry sign sits at the west, drawn small, sideways and roughly. A Selection-like grid of crossed lines sits near the ring at the southwest. The upper half holds more signs than the lower half, which is largely empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its small size gives a modest intensity. Piercing makes the water manifest as projectiles. Refuse gathers unwanted material toward where it points, so the shots pick up debris and steer it off at an angle. Inverted Crushing reforms broken material into its original shape. Here that pulls scattered spray back into drops, which works against the shattering impact of Piercing. Selection confines a spell to the object it is drawn on, which contradicts projectiles meant to leave the seal. Mimicry imitates movement, but with no decorative sigil it has no clear model to copy, and its rough drawing weakens it further. The seal stacks five unrelated kinds of modifier, several of them at odds. The water sigil and Piercing dominate, Refuse adds the steering, and the signs lean north-northwest. The other modifiers pull against each other, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Fires a few modest bolts of water that drag along nearby grime and debris and veer off toward the north-northwest. Some bolts burst into spray that pulls back into droplets mid-flight. Others stall near the seal or twitch in shaky, half-copied motions, so the volley lands unevenly and often fizzles before reaching anything.

name: s42_00284.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short strokes on either side, sits upright at the center and spans about half the ring's radius. Six Solidification signs, each two small circles joined by a short straight line, sit near the ring at the north-northwest, northeast, east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest, and west-northwest. They are drawn at slightly different angles and sizes. The north-northwest sign has its upper circle toward the ring, and the others have theirs toward the center. The west-northwest sign is a little rougher than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Solidification makes the magic drawn with it more solid, so the moved air is firmed into something that holds together instead of flowing freely. The six signs are spread evenly around the ring with no directional signs, so the effect is not pushed toward any side and stays centered on the seal. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing contradicts. The single slightly rough Solidification sign weakens that part a little without breaking the spell.
effect: Gathers the surrounding air and firms it into a dense, solid-feeling mass centered on the seal, strong enough to push against and hold back objects. The firmness is even all around, though it is slightly softer and less steady toward the west-northwest side.

name: s42_00285.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but drawn roughly: its outline is lumpy and uneven rather than round, bulging into flattened sides. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is fairly small relative to the ring. Six Piercing signs, each a short stroke through a small diamond, surround it. Four sit near the ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest. Two more sit somewhat closer to the center at the east-northeast and north-northwest. Each is tilted along a line toward the center. The two northern signs are drawn with heavier, darker strokes than the rest, and several of the signs are a little shaky. More signs cluster on the northern half than the southern. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Piercing makes the magic manifest as projectiles or offensive strikes, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many are produced, so six signs give six bolts of driven air. Piercing is non-directional, so its tilt and placement do not aim the bolts. No directional sign such as Columns or Regions is present, so nothing drives them along a set line. The heavier clustering on the northern side may loosely favor that side, but this is a guess. Only one kind of modifier is present, so there is no conflict between signs. However, the rough, shaky strokes weaken the spell and shorten its life, and the ring is far from round, which makes the effect fleeting and risks the seal failing to activate at all.
effect: Gathers the surrounding air into about six modest bolts that strike out from the seal without a fixed aim, perhaps drifting slightly toward the north. The bolts form unevenly, some weaker than others. They lose force quickly and break apart after a short distance, and the whole spell may sputter out almost at once or fail to start.

name: s42_00286.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and fairly round. There is no element sigil. A large, roughly drawn Glaives sign stands upright at the center, its long stem reaching about halfway to the ring. Seven signs are spread around it. A Projection bracket sits at the north, open side toward the center. A small Aeriforms Defined sign of three short strokes sits at the north-northeast, rotated at a slant. A small Envelopment sign sits at the east-northeast. A Dispersion sign sits at the southeast, its curve toward the ring. A Reflection sign, an hourglass of two triangles, sits at the south-southeast. A Sights Set sign sits at the southwest, its arrow pointing out toward the ring. A second, smaller Glaives sign sits at the west-northwest, prongs pointing inward. Most glyphs are a little rough, and both Glaives and the Reflection sign are drawn roughly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Glaives takes the core role, and the second Glaives reinforces it. Glaives set how deeply magic embeds itself in flesh, so this seal is built to sink its effect into a living body, and the large central glyph gives strong intensity. Sights Set lets the caster aim the spell at a chosen target. Projection and Dispersion both push the effect outward from the seal, while Envelopment wraps it around the target. Aeriforms Defined ties the magic loosely to air or gas. Reflection points it at a reflected image instead of the target itself. That stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier: aiming, outward projection, wrapping, an airy quality and reflection.
