Glaives and Sights Set dominate, with Projection and Dispersion carrying the effect out. Envelopment, Aeriforms Defined and Reflection pull in other directions, so the result is likely unstable. The rough drawing of the core glyph further weakens the spell and shortens how long it lasts.
effect: Casts an aimed, air-like wave of magic that wraps around a chosen target and drives deep into its flesh. The depth of the effect wavers from moment to moment, part of it leaks away as a thin outward haze, and it sometimes latches onto a target's reflection instead of the target. The hold fades well before it would with a carefully drawn core.

name: s42_00287.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large fire sigil sits upright at the center, filling about half the ring's radius. A Sights Set sign lies at the east, its diamond end toward the center and its arrow pointing at the ring. A Pulling sign sits near the ring at the northeast with its arrowhead facing outward, so it is inverted. A Diamond sign sits near the ring at the southeast. A Columns sign at the south has its stem toward the center and its crossbar toward the ring, drawn a little roughly. A Pointing sign, tilted and tangled-looking, sits at the west-southwest. An Expansion sign of nested corner brackets sits at the west-northwest with its corners pointing outward. The signs cluster more heavily toward the south and east.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong, intense flame. Pointing gives the fire a conical shape that directional signs can drive. The lone, unbalanced Columns sign at the south pushes that cone toward its own side, and its rough drawing weakens its hold slightly. Sights Set lets the caster aim the effect, but it points east, competing with the southward Columns push. Inverted Pulling pushes things away from the seal rather than drawing them in. Expansion with corners outward makes the flame grow. Diamond tends to confine a spell to the inside of the container it is drawn on, which directly contradicts the outward projection, pushing and aiming. The seal stacks six unrelated kinds of modifier: shaping, direction, aiming, repulsion, growth and containment. The fire sigil, Pointing and the aiming and direction signs dominate. Expansion and the push are secondary. Diamond is the weakest and least compatible part, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Produces a powerful, swelling cone of fire that shoves nearby objects away and can be aimed by the caster, though it keeps dragging toward the south-southeast. The flame grows unevenly as it burns and wavers between where it is aimed and where it drifts. It sometimes curls back to sputter inside whatever the seal is drawn on before collapsing earlier than its strength would suggest.

name: s42_00288.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The outer ring is closed but drawn roughly and is slightly egg-shaped rather than truly round. A small Link sign sits upright at the center. Five Diamond signs sit near the ring at the west, northeast, southeast, south-southeast and southwest, each tilted at a different angle, with the southeast and southwest ones drawn in heavier strokes. Two Collection signs sit near the ring, one at the east and one at the north-northwest, where it crosses the edge of a smaller circle. That small circle is a neatly drawn sub-seal near the north with a closed ring, holding a single Stillness sign at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: There is no element sigil, so Link serves as the core. It identifies pieces that were broken off from, or made from, the same source and links them, and its small size gives a modest intensity. The five Diamond signs limit the spell to objects inside a container the seal is drawn on, leaving the container itself untouched. The two Collection signs gather material from above and around the seal so the spell can use it. The Stillness sub-seal adds a self-contained effect that holds magic static in one place. These are three kinds of modifier that work together without contradiction, and the signs are spread evenly, so no direction is favored. The rough strokes and the not-quite-round outer ring make the main seal weaker and shorter lived, and its effect is fleeting. The neatly drawn sub-seal is steadier than the seal around it.
effect: Gathers loose fragments inside a container that came from the same source, links them together and holds them still in place, without affecting the container itself. The pull is gentle, and the hold is brief: linked pieces begin to slip and drift apart well before the spell would normally end. Only the stilling at one spot near the edge lingers somewhat longer than the rest.

name: s42_00289.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small Crosshair sign sits upright at the center in place of an element sigil, drawn a little roughly. Three Refuse signs, each a diamond above a crossed X, sit about halfway out at the northeast, southeast and southwest, each with its diamond end toward the center. At the northwest, in the matching position, is a small, heavily inked cone-shaped glyph like a triangle with a rounded corner, which matches no known sign. A closed sub-seal joined to the outer ring by a short line sits at the north-northeast and holds a moderately sized fire sigil. A second linked sub-seal sits at the south-southwest and holds an earth sigil that fills much of its small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no element sigil, so Crosshair at the center is its core. It aims the seal's effect at whatever its short ends point to, giving a focused target instead of a general spread. Refuse is directional and collects unwanted material toward where it points. With all three pointing inward, refuse is drawn in toward the center. The northwest glyph is closest to Convergence, which is a guess. Read that way, it draws magic to a single point and packs loose particles together, which agrees with the inward pull of the Refuse signs. The second ring adds strength to the main seal. The linked sub-seals supply the elements. The large earth sigil makes handling solid matter the stronger effect, while the moderate fire sigil adds heat at a lesser intensity. The modifiers all work toward the center and do not contradict one another. The slightly rough Crosshair and signs make the effect a little weaker and shorter lived than a clean drawing would.
effect: Draws loose debris and waste from around the seal into a tightly packed heap at a targeted point, then heats and burns it down. The pull is a little uneven, with material from the northwest side arriving more slowly. The burning fades somewhat sooner than the gathering, so larger piles may be left only partly consumed.

name: s42_00290.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center and is small relative to the ring. Six Selection signs, each a small square crossed by a grid of lines, are spread around it. Four sit near the ring at the north-northwest, northeast, southeast, and southwest. The southwest one is drawn with heavier, darker strokes and touches the ring. The other two sit about halfway out, at the west-northwest and south-southeast. A single Concealment sign, an eight-armed star with eye marks on four of its arms, sits about halfway out at the southwest. More signs crowd the southwestern side than the northeast, which is mostly empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Selection is non-directional and confines a spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on. Six of them strongly limit the water to that object, so nothing around it is affected. Concealment hides a target. Paired with water and held to the drawn object by Selection, it uses the water to hide that object. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other, so the seal holds together. Concealment sits alone off-center at the southwest, the side where the signs cluster, so the hiding is strongest there rather than even all around. The heavy southwest Selection adds to that bias.
effect: Draws a thin veil of water over the object the seal is drawn on and hides it from view, without touching anything around it. The veil is fullest on the southwest side and thins toward the northeast, where the object may still show faintly through the water.

name: s42_00291.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The outer ring is closed and neatly drawn, and its center is empty. Four Crosshair signs sit just inside the ring at the north-northeast, northeast, east-southeast, and southwest positions. Three Immobility signs sit just inside the ring at the north-northwest, west-northwest, and south-southeast positions, each with its base bar toward the center and its curved top toward the ring. A small closed sub-seal sits inside the main ring at the south-southeast, just inside the southern Immobility sign. It holds an upright fire sigil that fills more than half of its small ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no central sigil, so the fire sigil in the sub-seal supplies the element, and the spell creates and shapes flame or heat. The sigil is large for its ring, which makes the fire concentrated, but the sub-seal itself is small, so the overall output is modest and short-lived. Crosshair makes a seal's effect target whatever its short ends point at. The four Crosshairs are spread around the ring and face outward, so the fire is aimed at several separate points rather than one. Immobility makes its target immovable relative to the seal and holds its shape. Its outward-facing orientation has never been seen to change its effect, so it is read here as holding. The signs are balanced around the ring. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they work together without contradiction, so the seal is stable.
effect: Places small, concentrated flames at several separate points around the seal. Each flame is locked in place relative to the seal and keeps a fixed shape instead of spreading or drifting. The fire is modest in size and burns out sooner than a larger fire seal would.

name: s42_00292.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, sits upright at the center. Five Launch signs surround it. Two, at the north-northwest and south-southeast, have their peaks toward the ring. Three, at the north-northeast, east-southeast and southwest, have their peaks toward the center. The north-northeast one sits closer to the center than the others and is drawn a little rough. Two Detection signs, each made of three parallel strokes of different lengths, sit near the ring at the west-northwest and east-northeast. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Launch makes the target generate in the direction it points, in a powerful but short-lived burst. Here the Launch signs point in opposite directions, which is a direct contradiction. The three inward-pointing signs outnumber the two outward-pointing ones, so they dominate and drive the water toward the center of the seal, where it converges and spouts upward. The two outward signs pull against this and fling some water away from the seal. Because of this conflict, the result is likely unstable. The slightly rough north-northeast sign adds a weaker, less reliable burst on that side. Detection has an unclear function, but it is tied to sensing presence, and its two balanced signs would set the bursts off when something is sensed near the seal.
effect: Releases short, forceful bursts of water that rush together over the seal and spout upward, apparently set off when something is sensed nearby. The spouts are modest, and they spray unevenly, with stray jets flung outward to the sides. The burst on the upper-right side often comes out weaker or sputters, and the spout can break apart before reaching full height.

name: s42_00293.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, at a moderate size relative to the ring. Five Rain signs sit about three quarters of the way out from the center, at the northwest, north-northeast, east-northeast, east-southeast and southwest positions. Each is a small concave four-pointed shape with short tick marks on its outer edges, and none is flipped inside-out. The east-northeast sign is turned differently from the others. The signs cluster more on the eastern half, leaving the west and south sparser. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell works on existing solid matter such as sand, soil and grit. Earth does not create matter, so the spell can only use material already present. The sigil's moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Rain summons the spell's material and brings it down from above, like rainfall. Rain is semi-directional with radial symmetry, so rotating it does not change its effect. Only flipping it inside-out would invert it, so the differently turned east-northeast sign still reads as normal Rain. Five Rain signs reinforce the same behavior, so the fall is fuller and more rain-like than an abrupt drop. Rain's own direction does not steer a spell, but the signs are bunched toward the east-northeast, so more of the effect is concentrated on that side. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. With a closed, neatly drawn ring, the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Draws up loose earth such as sand, soil and grit from the surroundings and lets it fall back over the area around the seal as a steady, moderate shower. The fall is heaviest on the east-northeast side and thinner toward the west and south.

name: s42_00294.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring and drawn a little roughly. Six signs sit near the ring, evenly spread. Four are Rain signs, each a small square with inward-curving sides and short lines on its edges, at the east, south-southeast, west and north-northwest positions. The south-southeast one is drawn more roughly than the others, and the west one is slightly rough. Two are Aeriforms Defined signs, each made of three short slanted strokes of rising length, at the northeast and south-southwest, with their tops toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell works on existing solid matter such as sand, soil and grit rather than creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity, and its slight roughness weakens the spell a little and shortens how long it lasts. Rain is semi-directional and summons its target so that it comes down from above. All four are drawn in their normal orientation, not flipped inside-out, so they call material down rather than pushing it away. Aeriforms Defined is tied to air and gases, so with earth it would loosen the material into fine, airborne particles. Reading it this way is somewhat uncertain because its exact function is not well established. The two kinds of modifier work together without contradiction. The signs are balanced, so no direction is favored. The rough Rain sign at the south-southeast makes the effect weaker on that side.
effect: Draws loose earth such as sand and soil into the air above the seal and lets it fall back over the surrounding area like a fine, dusty rain. The fall is moderate in strength and thinner and patchier toward the south-southeast. The shower thins out sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00295.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. An upright earth sigil sits at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Three four-lobed Billow signs sit close to the ring at the north-northeast, south-southwest, and west-northwest positions. Two Aeriforms Defined signs, each a cluster of three short strokes, sit about halfway between the center and the ring, one at the north and one at the east-southeast. Both point their tops toward the center. The east-southeast one is drawn a little rougher than the rest. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell works on solid matter such as soil, sand, and stone. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Billow is non-directional, so its orientation does not matter, and it turns available material into a fluffy cloud. Here it acts as a modifier on the earth sigil rather than taking the center. Three Billow signs spread around the ring apply that effect evenly. Aeriforms Defined is an air-related modifier, likely semi-directional. Both signs face inward in the normal orientation, so neither is inverted, and they add an airy, gaseous quality to the material. The two kinds of modifier complement each other rather than conflict, and the signs are balanced, so no direction is favored. The slightly rough east-southeast sign weakens the airy quality a little on that side.
effect: Loosens nearby soil and sand into a light, airy, cloud-like mass that is soft to the touch, at moderate strength and spread evenly around the seal. On the east-southeast side the cloud comes out a little denser and less buoyant than elsewhere, and it settles back sooner there.

name: s42_00296.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, outer ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center at moderate size, about a third of the ring's radius. Three Link signs sit near the ring at the north-northeast, east-northeast and south-southwest, each with its top toward the center. Five Concealment signs, each an eight-armed star with eye marks, sit near the ring at the east-southeast, south-southeast, west-southwest, west-northwest and north-northwest, each with its top toward the ring. The north-northwest one is drawn slightly rougher. Two small sub-seals sit inside the main ring on either side of the fire sigil. At the west is a round, closed sub-ring holding a small wind sigil. At the east is a closed sub-ring drawn unevenly into a lumpy, somewhat angular shape, holding a light sigil. The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and works flames and heat. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Link identifies objects broken off from, or made from, the same source and joins them, so the fire reaches only pieces that share a source with its target. Concealment hides the target, and five of them evenly spaced make the hiding effect cover the spell on every side. The west sub-seal adds wind, which moves the surrounding air and can carry or feed the flame. The east sub-seal adds light, which falls within the fire domain and produces light that diminishes over time. Its ring is not round enough, so its contribution is fleeting and may barely register. The signs are balanced, so no direction is favored. Only two kinds of modifier are stacked, linking and concealment, alongside two element sub-seals. Concealment and the light sub-seal pull slightly against each other, but they do not directly contradict, so the seal holds together.
effect: Kindles a moderate fire that stays hidden from sight and passes only between objects that came from the same source, with stirred air carrying it from piece to piece. A faint glow sometimes flickers through the concealment where the flame travels, but it sputters and fades almost at once rather than lighting the area.

name: s42_00297.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. Two sigils share the center: an earth sigil left of center, moderate in size relative to the ring, and a smaller light sigil to its right, drawn a little roughly. Two Cooling signs, each a short slanted stroke between pairs of dots, sit near the ring at the north-northeast and south-southwest. Two Dispersion signs sit near the ring at the northwest and east-northeast, each with its stem toward the center and its curve facing outward toward the ring. Three of the four signs cluster on the upper and upper-right side, so the arrangement leans toward the north-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the main element, so the spell acts on existing solid matter such as stone and soil. Its moderate size gives it a moderate intensity. The smaller light sigil adds a weaker second element that creates light, and that light naturally diminishes over time. Its rough drawing makes the light part weaker and shorter lived than the earth part. The two Cooling signs cool down whatever the spell affects. The two Dispersion signs make the magic pour outward instead of holding it at the seal or shooting it as a beam. The signs are unbalanced and lean toward the north-northeast, so the outward flow is stronger on that side. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other, so the seal is stable.
effect: Chills the stone or soil around the seal, with the cold seeping outward through the ground and reaching farther toward the north-northeast than in other directions. A faint glow spreads along with it, but the light is uneven and flickers, and it fades well before the cooling does.

name: s42_00298.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed. The ring is lumpy and uneven, bulging in places and noticeably out of round. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, drawn fairly large, reaching about halfway to the ring. Its strokes are slightly uneven. Four small Expansion signs, each made of nested corner brackets with the corners pointing outward, sit near the ring at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest, and west-northwest positions. They are spaced evenly around the seal. A couple of them are drawn slightly less cleanly than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on existing solid matter such as stone, soil, sand, and wood rather than creating it. Its large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong intensity. Expansion is semi-directional, so its rotation does not steer the spell. With its corners pointing outward, it is in its normal orientation, which makes the target grow. The four Expansion signs are evenly spaced, so the growth is balanced on all sides and favors no direction. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. However, the ring is not round enough, which makes the effect fleeting and gives it a chance of failing to activate. The rough sigil and the slightly rough signs further weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Makes stone, soil, or other solid earth swell in size evenly in all directions, with a fairly strong push. The growth flickers in only briefly before the matter shrinks back to its original size, and some castings fizzle without taking hold at all.

name: s42_00299.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A small earth sigil sits upright at the center. A Projection sign, a flat bracket with its open side facing the center, sits at the northeast about two-thirds of the way to the ring. A Partition sign sits at the west, tilted slightly and drawn a little roughly. A Coil sign, two crossing curves, sits at the north-northwest, also slightly rough. A Diamond sign sits close to the ring at the south-southeast. The four signs are spread around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil makes this a spell acting on solid matter such as stone, soil and wood, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Coil softens physical matter, so paired with earth it is the main working effect. Projection pushes an effect outward from the seal. Partition outlines the borders of an area of effect. Diamond limits the spell to what lies inside the container it is drawn on, not the container itself. Partition and Diamond both hold the effect within bounds, while Projection pushes it outward, so they pull against each other. The seal also stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: softening, projection, boundary and containment. The earth sigil and Coil dominate, and Partition and Diamond keep the effect mostly contained, with Projection the weakest and least reliable part. The result is likely unstable. The slightly rough Coil and Partition signs make the softening and the boundary a little weaker and shorter lived.
effect: Softens stone, soil or wood within a bounded area, sparing the surface the seal is drawn on and acting only on what lies inside it. The softening is mild and patchy, some spots turning pliable while others stay hard. The edge of the affected area wavers, occasionally pushing the effect outward in brief surges, and the spell tends to fade sooner than expected.

name: s42_00300.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. A small Partition sign, a peaked roof shape over a flat bar, sits upright at the center. There is no element sigil. Six Repetition signs are evenly spaced inside the inner ring at roughly the east, south-southeast, southwest, west, north-northwest and northeast positions, all about the same distance from the center. Two of these, at the south-southeast and southwest, look slightly rougher than the rest. Two more Repetition signs sit in the band between the rings, one at the north and one at the south. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Partition sign acts as the core of the seal. Partition outlines the borders of an area of effect that extends outward and upward, and the other symbols within that area decide what happens inside it. Here every other symbol is Repetition, which continuously resets whatever it affects to the state it was in when the spell first took hold, including its shape and temperature. The six inner Repetition signs are evenly spaced, so the effect is balanced across the whole area. The second ring strengthens the core spell, and the two Repetition signs in the outer band at north and south reinforce the resetting. Only two kinds of glyph are present, and they work together without contradiction. The two slightly rough signs make the effect a little less steady on the south-southwest side.
effect: Marks out a bounded area around the seal and holds everything inside it in place in time. Anything within that area that is damaged, moved, spoiled, warmed or cooled is steadily restored to the state it was in when the spell began. Along the south-southwest edge of the area, the restoring lags slightly behind the rest of the space.

name: s42_00301.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. The signs sit in the band between the outer and inner rings. An Envelopment sign, a slanted stroke hooked at both ends, sits at the center and is moderate in size relative to the ring. Inside the inner ring are two small sub-seals, each with its own closed ring. The one at the west-northwest holds a fire sigil filling a little under half its ring. The one at the east-southeast holds a larger earth sigil filling more than half its ring. In the outer band, three Expansion signs sit at the west, east, and south-southeast. The western one is drawn with heavier, rougher strokes, and the eastern one is also slightly rough. A Levitation sign sits at the north-northwest with its arrow pointing outward toward the ring. At the northeast is an unidentified glyph, a right-angled triangle with a small circle at one corner, resembling a small cone. More signs crowd the northern half than the southern. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The two sub-seals supply the elements: fire creates flames and heat, and earth moves existing solid matter. Because both sub-seals are small relative to the main ring, both effects are modest, with earth somewhat stronger since its sigil is larger within its ring. Envelopment at the center is the core of the seal and makes the combined effect surround its target. Expansion has corners on all sides, so turning it does not invert it, and all three make the result grow. Levitation is directional, and its arrow points outward, the opposite of its usual inward orientation. It lifts the target, and pointing outward tilts the lift toward the north-northwest. The northeast glyph matches no known sign. Its closest match is Convergence, a triangle that focuses magic to a single point, but that reading is a guess. Read that way, it pulls the effect toward one point and works against Expansion's outward growth. The seal stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: envelopment, expansion, levitation, and convergence. Envelopment and the three Expansion signs dominate, Levitation is secondary, and the guessed Convergence clashes with the growth, so the result is likely unstable. The signs lean north-northeast, so the effect drifts that way. The rough Expansion signs at the west and east weaken growth on those sides.
effect: Wraps the target in a modest shell of warm, shifting earth that swells outward and floats upward, drifting toward the north-northeast. The shell grows unevenly, lagging on its west and east sides, and keeps trying to pinch inward toward one point, so it wobbles in size and shape. It tends to collapse before fully forming, leaving loose soil and a brief burst of heat.

name: s42_00302.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn neatly with two concentric rings, both closed, forming an outer band. A Selection sign, a square divided into four cells and crossed by a plus whose arms extend past it, sits at the center in place of a sigil and is moderately large relative to the ring. There is no element sigil. Inside the inner ring, a Sights Set sign sits at the south, with its diamond end toward the center and its arrow pointing down to touch the inner ring. An Immobility sign sits at the northeast near the inner ring, rotated so its base bar faces the ring. In the outer band, a very small Piercing sign sits at the east near the outer ring. A small Rain sign sits at the north in the band, close to the outer ring. Most signs cluster on the north-to-east side, while the west side is empty.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Selection sign acts as the core. It is non-directional and confines the spell to the object the seal is drawn on, and its size gives it the strongest pull in the seal. Sights Set lets the caster aim the effect at a chosen point. Immobility makes the target immovable relative to the seal, holding its shape as if frozen. Piercing turns the effect into projectiles or attacks, and Rain summons material down in a rainfall-like way. Piercing and Rain are both tiny and pushed out into the outer band, so they contribute only weakly. The seal stacks four unrelated kinds of modifier: aiming, immobility, projectiles and summoning. Immobility directly contradicts the outward motion of Piercing and Rain, and Selection's confinement to the drawn object works against effects cast away from it. Selection, Immobility and Sights Set dominate, so the seal mainly fixes and aims the object. The unbalanced layout leans the effect toward the east-northeast, and the result is likely unstable.
effect: Locks the object the seal is drawn on rigidly in place relative to the seal and lets the caster aim it toward a chosen target, with a pull toward the east-northeast. Faint jabs of force occasionally flicker off it to the east or patter down weakly from above, but they misfire and fade almost at once. Because these jabs fight the hold, the object jitters and the lock wavers instead of staying fully steady.

name: s42_00303.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the upper left between the west and north-northwest. There is no element sigil. A Binding sign, two stacked upward arcs with the larger one on top, sits upright at the center and is fairly large, reaching about half the ring's radius. Its strokes are slightly rough. Six signs surround it about three quarters of the way to the ring, evenly spread around the seal. Five are Partition signs, at the north-northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest and west, each turned with its peaked top toward the center. The sixth, at the northwest, is a Partition shape with a short extra stroke running off its top edge, which matches no known sign exactly. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Binding sign takes the center and sets the spell's core: halting the movement of the target material and binding it so it acts and moves as a single unit. Its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect, though its slightly rough drawing weakens it a little and shortens how long it lasts. Partition outlines the borders of an area of effect, and the signs are turned with their tops toward the center, so the border is drawn around the space over the seal. Even spacing gives that area a regular outline. The northwest glyph is closest to Partition. Reading it as Partition with an extra stroke is a guess, and the stroke would stretch that stretch of border slightly. Only two kinds of modifier are present and they work together. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: As drawn it does not activate. Once closed, it marks out a bordered area over the seal and holds any material inside it still, binding it together so it can be moved as one solid unit. The hold is strong but loosens somewhat sooner than a cleanly drawn version would, and the border bulges slightly outward on its northwest side.

name: s42_00304.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, outer ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits at the center, modest in size relative to the ring. Two small sub-seals sit inside the ring, each with its own closed ring. The one at the west-southwest holds a fire sigil that fills about half of its small ring. The one at the east-northeast holds a water sigil, and its ring line is slightly less even. Six Gathering signs sit near the outer ring. The one at the east-northeast points inward toward the water sub-seal, and the one at the west-southwest points inward toward the fire sub-seal; this west-southwest sign is drawn with heavier, rougher strokes. The other four, at north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and west-northwest, are turned sideways so they point roughly along the ring. At the south-southeast sits an octagon with an X inside, which matches no known sign. At the north-northwest sits a small triangle with a circle at one corner, loosely fire-like, which also matches no known sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The central fire sigil sets the main element, so the spell creates and shapes flame or heat. Its modest size gives moderate intensity. The two sub-seals add a second fire core and a water core of their own. Gathering lets a spell actively draw material from its surroundings. The two inward-pointing Gathering signs feed the two sub-seals directly, and the four sideways ones draw material around the ring so it circles before reaching the center. The octagon with an X is closest to Selection; this is a guess. Read that way, it confines the effect to the object the seal is drawn on. The triangle with a circle is closest to Strengthening; this is also a guess. Read that way, it reinforces the effect and makes it hotter and more durable. Fire and water oppose each other, so their effects partly cancel where they meet, but the modifiers do not contradict one another, and only three kinds are present. The rougher ring on the water sub-seal makes that part weaker and shorter lived. The rough Gathering sign feeding the fire sub-seal draws less steadily than the others.
effect: Draws heat and moisture in from the surroundings in a circling pull, feeding a steady, moderate flame held on the surface the seal is drawn on. A hotter knot of fire burns on one side, and a small pool of water gathers on the other, hissing into steam where the two meet. The water side fills unevenly and drains away well before the flame dies. The fire knot flickers a little as its supply of heat comes in fits.

name: s42_00305.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the outer ring closed and neatly drawn. An Immobility sign, upright and modest in size relative to the ring, sits at the center: a short vertical stroke over a horizontal base, bracketed by two curves. Three small sub-seals sit inside the main ring, each with its own ring closed. The one at the north-northeast holds a wind sigil, the one at the west holds a light sigil, and the one at the south-southeast holds an earth sigil. Each sigil fills roughly half of its small ring. Three hooked glyphs sit near the outer ring, roughly evenly spaced. At the west-southwest is a plain Envelopment sign. At the north-northeast is an Envelopment-like stroke with an extra stroke off one end. At the southeast is a glyph shaped like Envelopment with one half mirrored onto the other, so it looks somewhat like an arrow. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main seal has no element sigil, so the central Immobility sign acts as the core. It makes its target immovable relative to the seal, so the target holds its shape as if frozen while still able to be carried along with the seal. The three closed sub-seals each add an element. Wind moves air, light creates light that fades over time, and earth works on solid matter. Each sigil fills about half of its small ring, which gives a moderate intensity within its sub-seal, but the sub-seals are small, so their overall contribution is limited. The plain Envelopment sign makes the effect surround its target. The two altered glyphs most closely resemble Envelopment, though reading them that way is a guess. On that reading they add the same surrounding behavior, and the extra and mirrored strokes do not clearly change it. The three are spread evenly, so the wrapping is balanced on all sides. Only two kinds of modifier are present, holding in place and surrounding, and they work together. The neat drawing and closed rings mean the spell activates and holds steady.
effect: Wraps the target in a layered shell of held air, soft light and firmed earth, and locks it so it cannot move relative to the seal while keeping its shape. The air and earth stay fixed around the target. The light glows gently and slowly dims over time.

name: s42_00306.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both neatly drawn and both open. The outer ring has a gap on the east-northeast side. The inner ring has a gap on the southeast side. A light sigil, a diamond set inside a square with four short spokes, sits upright at the center and is modest in size relative to the ring. Six Stability and Level Planes signs, each a set of short wavy parallel strokes, sit in the band between the two rings at the northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest, west and north-northwest positions. Each sits near the outer ring with its top toward it. The south-southwest sign is drawn in a heavier stroke than the others. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its modest size gives a moderate intensity. Stability and Level Planes is non-directional and makes its target balance on a level plane in the air, like something floating on water that can turn and drift but stays on the surface. The six signs are spread evenly around the seal, so no side is favored, and the heavier stroke on one sign does not change its kind. There are no directional signs, so nothing pushes the light outward or upward in a beam. The second ring adds strength to the core spell. Only one kind of modifier is present, so nothing conflicts. Both rings are open, so the seal will not activate until they are closed.
effect: The seal does not activate as drawn. If closed, it would create a moderate light that hovers level in the air above the seal, drifting and turning gently while staying balanced on one plane, and slowly dimming over time.

name: s42_00307.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a wide gap at the top just left of north. A small light sigil sits at the center: a diamond inside a square with four short spokes. Six Strengthening signs are evenly spaced about three quarters of the way out from the center, at the south-southeast, southwest, west, north-northwest, northeast and east. Each has its apex pointing outward toward the ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Light from this sigil normally fades over time. Strengthening makes its target stronger, harder and more durable, so six of them reinforce the light and help it resist that fading. All six share the same outward orientation and are evenly balanced, so they add no direction and the light stays centered on the seal. There is only one kind of modifier and nothing contradicts it. The neat drawing does not weaken the spell, but the ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: It does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it would produce a modest, steady glow centered on the seal that holds its brightness far longer than ordinary magical light before slowly dimming.

name: s42_00308.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with two concentric closed rings and a wide band between them. A small earth sigil, upright, sits at the center of the inner ring. Four Partition signs sit in the band between the rings, at the west-northwest, north-northeast, east-southeast and south-southwest positions. Each has its peaked top toward the outer ring. They are spaced evenly around the seal. The west-northwest and south-southwest signs are cleanly drawn, while the north-northeast and east-southeast signs show slightly doubled, rough strokes. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell manipulates solid matter such as soil, stone and sand rather than creating it. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity. Partition is a directional sign that outlines the borders of an area of effect, extending outward and upward. The effect that fills that area is set by the symbols inside it, here the earth sigil. With all four Partition signs facing outward and spaced evenly, the boundary spreads evenly around the seal with no favored direction. The second ring holds the Partition signs apart from the core and adds strength to the outlined area. No signs contradict each other, and only one kind of modifier is present. The two roughly drawn Partition signs weaken the boundary slightly on their sides.
effect: Marks out a bounded area that spreads outward and upward from the seal, and moves nearby soil, stone or sand to fill and shape it along that outline. The effect is modest in strength. The boundary on the north-northeast and east-southeast sides holds less firmly and fades sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00309.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. It has two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. At the center sits a large glyph, about half the ring's radius: an octagon with an X drawn through it. It matches no known sign exactly and is closest to Selection. Six chevron signs sit evenly around the inner ring at the north-northwest, northeast, east, south-southeast, south-southwest and west. Five are Regions signs with their points toward the center. The one at the north-northwest is stretched wide and slanted like a check mark, but it also points inward and reads as a widened Regions sign. Two small sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line, and both rings are closed. The northwest sub-seal holds a small earth sigil drawn a little roughly. The southeast sub-seal holds a single Diamond sign, fairly large within its ring. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The only element comes from the linked earth sub-seal, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, soil and wood. It manipulates that matter rather than creating it. The earth sigil is small and a little rough, so its contribution is modest and somewhat short-lived. The central octagon-and-X is read as Selection, which is a guess. Under that reading, it confines the spell's effect to the object the seal is drawn on. All six Regions signs point inward and are balanced, so the magic manifests only inside the ring and never outside it. The doubled ring adds strength to the core spell. The Diamond sub-seal works against Selection: Diamond makes a spell affect only what is held within the object it is drawn on, not the object itself. These two directly contradict each other. The large central Selection reading dominates over the smaller linked Diamond, so the effect mostly stays on the marked surface, but the result is likely unstable.
effect: Works the stone, soil or wood within the bounds of the seal, and nothing outside it is touched. The effect wavers between the surface the seal is drawn on and any loose material resting inside that area. The surface shifts in patches while nearby contents twitch unevenly. The earth magic is modest and fades sooner than expected.

name: s42_00310.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is open, with a gap at the lower right near the south-southeast. There is no element sigil. Two signs share the center: a Binding sign, two stacked arcs opening downward, on the left, and an upright Rain sign, a square with concave sides and short spiked strokes at each corner, on the right. A Cooling sign, a slanted stroke with dots on either side, sits at the north-northwest, and a second Cooling sign sits at the south, turned the other way. A Piercing sign, a diamond on a long line, sits at an angle at the east-northeast. A Partition sign lies on its side at the west. A heavily stroked Launch sign, a broad V shape, sits at the east-southeast, rotated away from its upright position. Near the ring gap at the south-southeast is a small glyph lying sideways: a small circle at the end of a stem that ends in a crossbar. It matches no known sign. The signs are spread evenly around the ring.
justification: No element sigil is present, so Rain and Binding at the center form the core. Upright Rain summons the spell's material down from above, and Binding halts that material's movement and makes it act as a single unit. Rain is small relative to the ring, so the summoning is modest. The two Cooling signs make the material cold. Piercing turns it into projectiles. Partition outlines the borders of the area where the effect manifests. Launch adds a strong but short-lived burst in the direction it points. The glyph near the gap looks closest to a Columns sign with a Solidification circle at its foot. This reading is a guess, but it would drive the material in a column and firm it up. The seal stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier: summoning, binding, cooling, projectiles, area borders and bursting force. Binding, which halts movement, also directly contradicts Launch, which flings material outward. The central Rain and Binding dominate, with Cooling reinforcing them, so the result is likely unstable. The ring is open, so the seal does not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Does not activate while the ring is open. If closed, it would call a modest fall of cold material into a bounded area and press it into hardened clumps that are flung out as projectiles in short bursts. The clumps tend to split apart before they firm up, and the bursts fire unevenly, some lurching sideways while others drop limply where they formed.

name: s42_00311.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Nine Mimicry signs surround it, all pointing radially with their tops toward the ring. Six form an inner circle about halfway out, at the north-northeast, east, southeast, south-southwest, west-southwest and northwest. Three more sit closer to the ring, at the north-northeast, south-southwest and west-northwest. A few of the Mimicry signs are drawn with slightly rougher strokes than the rest. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates air. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Mimicry guides or imitates the movements of a target object. No decorative sigil gives it a creature to copy, so it copies the target the spell acts on. Nine Mimicry signs reinforce one another and strengthen how closely the air follows that motion. Because the signs are balanced around the ring, no direction is favored. The effect follows wherever the target moves. Only one kind of modifier is present, so there is no conflict. The few slightly rough signs only make the tracking a little less exact.
effect: Stirs up a strong current of air that follows and copies the movements of its target, moving with it in any direction. The current tracks the target closely, though now and then it lags or drifts slightly out of step before catching up.

name: s42_00312.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but badly misshapen, a lumpy, roughly five-lobed outline rather than a circle. There is no element sigil. Two small signs sit side by side near the center: an upright Regions sign, a caret pointing north, on the left, and a small upright Coil sign on the right. Three four-lobed Billow signs sit about halfway to two-thirds of the way out, at the north, southeast and west-southwest, each turned at a different angle and spaced evenly around the seal. The strokes throughout are shaky and rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the seal is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind and acts on whatever material reaches it. The three Billow signs set the main behavior, turning available material into a fluffy cloud. Billow is non-directional, so its different rotations change nothing, and its even spacing keeps the cloud balanced. Coil softens physical matter, which fits Billow by loosening solid material before it is fluffed, though it cannot act on liquids or gases. The single Regions sign points north, so the effect manifests toward that side of the seal rather than evenly around it. These three kinds of modifier work together without contradiction. The rough drawing and especially the ring, which is far from round, weaken the seal, so the effect is fleeting and may fail to activate at all.
effect: Softens solid material near the seal and puffs it into a soft cloud that billows out toward the north side. The cloud forms thin and patchy, often sputters out partway through, and collapses back into loose material after only a moment, if it forms at all.

name: s42_00313.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center and is fairly large relative to the ring. Six Strengthening signs are evenly spaced inside the inner ring, roughly at the south-southwest, west, north-northwest, northeast, east, and south-southeast positions. Each sign is turned with its top toward the center. Outside the outer ring at the north-northwest, a short line joins a small linked seal. That seal has its own closed ring and holds a small upright fire sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on existing solid matter such as stone, soil, sand, and wood rather than creating it. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect, and the second ring adds further strength to the core spell. Strengthening makes its target harder, stronger, and more durable. Six of them, evenly spaced, reinforce the effect without favoring any side, and no directional sign moves it away from the seal. The linked seal adds fire magic, meaning heat, to the main spell. That seal is small and its sigil is modest, so the heat is gentle rather than a flame. Heat working alongside reinforced earth points to baking or tempering the material. There is only one kind of modifier plus two complementary sigils, so the seal is coherent and stable.
effect: Hardens and reinforces the stone, soil, or sand it acts on, leaving the material much tougher and more durable. The effect is even all around the seal. A gentle, steady heat runs through the material as it hardens and bakes it solid, much like firing clay.

name: s42_00314.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A fire sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Four Gathering signs sit about two-thirds of the way out from the center, at the north-northeast, east-southeast, south-southwest and northwest positions. Each has its arrowhead pointing outward toward the ring. Two four-lobed Billow signs sit closer to the ring at the east and west points. The eastern one is drawn in a heavier, filled line and the western one in a lighter outline. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes flame and heat. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Gathering lets a spell draw material from its surroundings to build its effect. Four of them spread evenly around the seal pull that material in from every side. Billow turns available material into a soft, fluffy cloud. Here it acts as a modifier beside the fire sigil, not in place of one, so the gathered material is puffed into cloud and charged with the fire's heat. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they support each other: one supplies material and the other shapes it. The signs are balanced around the ring, so no direction is favored and the effect stays centered on the seal.
effect: Draws in loose material from all around the seal and puffs it into a soft, billowing cloud that carries a moderate warmth. The cloud gathers evenly over the seal rather than drifting in any one direction.

name: s42_00315.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. A small fire sigil sits upright at the center, roughly drawn. Four Collection signs, each a small triangle crossed by a line, are spaced evenly about two-thirds of the way out, at the north-northeast, east-southeast, southwest and northwest positions. Each has its barred end toward the center and its open side facing outward toward the ring. All four are drawn somewhat roughly, the southwest one most heavily. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell. Its small size relative to the ring gives a modest intensity, and its rough drawing weakens it further and shortens its life. Collection normally gathers material above and around a seal for the spell to use, with its open side facing inward. Here all four signs face the other way, a configuration that has never been seen. As a guess, reversing Collection reverses its action, so the seal would push material away from itself instead of drawing it in. The four signs are evenly balanced, so no direction is favored and the effect spreads equally on all sides. The signs do not contradict one another and only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal is not unstable. Because the signs and sigil are roughly drawn, the effect is weaker and shorter lived than a clean version would be.
effect: Produces a small flame that drives heat and loose material outward evenly in all directions, warming and clearing the area around the seal instead of feeding the fire. The flame flickers and sputters as it burns, pushing harder on some sides than others, and it dies out sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00316.png
description:
A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A large, boldly drawn Dancing Puppets sign sits upright at the center, filling about half the ring's radius. It has no element sigil inside it. Five single signs sit near the ring:
- A Windows sign, a small circle lined with slanted hatching, at the northwest.
- A Piercing sign, a diamond on a slanted stroke, at the northeast.
- An Immobility sign at the east, its top toward the ring.
- A Pulling sign at the south, its stem toward the ring and its arrowhead pointing inward toward the center.
- A Holding sign at the west-southwest, drawn as a pair of curls turned well off upright.

The signs are spread evenly around the ring, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification:
With no element sigil, the central Dancing Puppets sign acts as the core. It lets the target's movement be manipulated, including at long distance, and its large size makes that the strongest part of the seal.

The modifiers each pull in their own way:
- Pulling points inward in its normal orientation, so it draws the target toward the seal.
- Piercing makes the target manifest as a projectile, and a single sign means a single projectile.
- Holding is likely non-directional, so its rotation does not matter. It keeps the target in a set shape while still letting it move.
- Windows normally lines a seal as a full extra ring. Drawn as one small mark, it would only weakly connect the seal to a separate space; this reading is a guess.
- Immobility makes the target immovable relative to the seal, which directly contradicts Dancing Puppets.

The seal also stacks far more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: motion control, pulling, projectile, shape holding, portal and immobility. Dancing Puppets dominates, with Pulling and Piercing next. Immobility works against all of them, so the result is likely unstable.
effect: Draws a nearby object toward the seal, holds it in a single sharp projectile shape, and lets it be sent darting about under remote control. The flight is jerky: the object repeatedly locks in place mid-air before lurching on, and often stalls short of where it is steered. A faint link to another space may flicker open, letting the projectile slip briefly elsewhere, but it wavers and collapses almost at once.

name: s42_00317.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, main ring closed and neatly drawn. An earth sigil sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. A Stillness sign sits near the ring at the northwest, and a Dispersion sign sits about two-thirds of the way out at the northeast. In the southern half, a Rain sign sits midway out at the south-southwest, with a Pointing sign just beyond it near the ring, its top turned toward the center. At the southeast, an Envelopment sign sits midway out, with an Immobility sign beyond it near the ring, its top turned toward the center. Most signs cluster on the southern side. Two small sub-seals sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The northeast sub-seal has a closed ring with a wind sigil at its center. The southwest sub-seal has an open ring with a Partition sign at its center in place of a sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on existing solid matter such as soil, stone and sand rather than creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Rain summons the target material in a falling form. Envelopment wraps the effect around its target, and Pointing gives the material a conical shape. Pointing is likely non-directional, so its inward-facing top changes nothing. Stillness keeps the effect fixed in one place, and Immobility holds the material's shape as if frozen. Immobility has never been seen inverted, so its inward-facing top adds uncertainty. Dispersion makes magic pour outward, which directly contradicts the holding effect of Stillness and Immobility. The seal also stacks more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: summoning, enveloping, conical shaping, holding and dispersal. The earth sigil, the holding pair and Envelopment dominate, with Rain and Pointing shaping the material, while Dispersion works against them. The result is likely unstable. Because the signs lean south, the effect concentrates on that side. The closed wind sub-seal links air movement to the spell. The Partition sub-seal would outline the borders of the area of effect, but its ring is open, so that part does not activate.
effect: Draws loose earth down in a falling shower toward the south side of the seal and tries to wrap it around a target as a pointed, cone-like shell that holds still, while a linked current of air stirs around it. The shell sets firmly in some places while other parts keep leaking outward and crumbling away, so it forms unevenly and tends to break apart early. The bordered area meant to contain the effect does not form. Once its ring is closed, it would outline where the earth gathers.

name: s42_00318.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn neatly with two concentric rings, both closed. The inner ring sits well inside the outer one, leaving a wide band between them. An earth sigil sits upright at the center and is small to moderate relative to the ring. Eleven Cooling signs, each a short bar flanked by dots, surround it. Five sit in the band between the rings, at the north, east-northeast, east-southeast, south and west-northwest, all facing outward toward the ring. Six sit inside the inner ring, at the north, northeast, east-southeast, south, west-southwest and west-northwest, and most of these are turned to various angles. The outer north sign and the inner south sign are drawn a little roughly. The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on existing solid matter such as stone, soil and sand rather than creating it. Its small-to-moderate size relative to the ring gives a modest base intensity. A second ring adds strength to the core spell. Cooling is the only kind of modifier present. It is semi- or non-directional, so the varied rotations do not steer the spell. Instead, the large number of Cooling signs deepens the chilling effect. Because the signs are evenly placed in both bands, no side is favored and the cold spreads uniformly. The two slightly rough signs are minor and only slightly weaken their spots. With a single kind of modifier, nothing contradicts and the spell holds steady.
effect: Steadily chills the stone, soil or sand the seal acts on, drawing heat out evenly on all sides. The cold builds well beyond a mild coolness, though it runs a touch weaker at the northern and southern edges.

name: s42_00319.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The main ring is closed but drawn roughly and noticeably lumpy rather than round. Two glyphs sit side by side at the center: a Selection sign on the left and a water sigil on the right, both small to moderate relative to the ring and slightly rough. Four Billow signs sit near the ring at the north-northwest, north-northeast, east, and south-southwest. The north-northeast and south-southwest ones are drawn in heavy, rough strokes, and the other two are lighter. A single Columns sign sits at the southwest with its stem toward the center. Three smaller circles with closed rings sit outside the main ring, each joined to it by a short line. The northern one holds a small Expansion sign whose nested brackets appear to point outward. The southeastern one holds a Glaives sign, and the west-southwestern one holds an Envelopment sign. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its modest size gives a moderate intensity. Selection shares the center and confines the effect to the object the seal is drawn on. The four Billow signs are non-directional and evenly spread, so they turn the water into a soft, fluffy cloud on all sides. The lone Columns sign gives the effect a column shape, and because it is unbalanced it pushes that column toward the southwest. The joined circles add effects. Expansion with its corners outward makes the result grow. Envelopment makes the effect surround its target. Glaives sets how deeply the magic embeds into flesh. That stacks well over three unrelated kinds of modifier: confinement, billowing, direction, growth, envelopment and embedding. Selection's confinement also works against the outward push of Columns and the surrounding pull of Envelopment. The water sigil and Billow dominate, with Envelopment and Expansion next, so the result is likely unstable. The rough strokes weaken the spell and shorten its life. A ring this far from round gives only a fleeting effect and may fail to activate at all.
effect: Turns water into a soft, cloud-like billow that swells outward and tries to wrap around the object it marks, leaning off toward the southwest. The cloud grows unevenly and sometimes clings to the skin and seeps into it, while at other moments it drifts loose. The spell may sputter without starting, and when it does take hold it wavers and dissipates after only a short time.

name: s42_00320.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is open, with a wide gap across the bottom between the south-southwest and south-southeast. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes on either side, sits upright at the center and is fairly large, a little under half the ring's radius. Six Solidification signs surround it, each drawn as two small circles joined by a short line. Five sit near the ring, at the north-northeast, east, southeast, west-southwest and northwest, each with its top end toward the center. A sixth sits closer in at the south, about two-thirds of the way out, tilted slightly. The east sign is drawn with heavier strokes, and the northwest, north-northeast and east signs are a little rough. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its fairly large size relative to the ring gives a fairly strong intensity. Solidification makes the magic it is tied to more solid, so the moved air is firmed into something that can hold and resist like a solid body. All six signs are of one kind and are spread evenly around the ring, so no direction is favored and the effect stays centered on the seal. The south sign sitting closer in does not change the kind of effect. The slight roughness of three signs on the north and east side makes the firming a little weaker and less lasting there. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: As drawn, it does not activate. Once closed, it would gather the surrounding air and press it into a firm, nearly solid mass centered over the seal, able to push back against or support what touches it. The mass would be slightly softer and quicker to give way on its north and east side than elsewhere.

name: s42_00321.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but hand-drawn and a little lumpy, so it is not quite round. Two glyphs share the center, both a little rough. On the left is a Detection sign, three vertical strokes of increasing height. On the right is a tall, narrow glyph resembling a fire sigil stretched vertically, slightly smaller than the Detection sign. Five Immobility signs surround them. Those at the north, south, northeast and southeast have their tops toward the center. The one at the west is turned the other way, with its top toward the ring. The north and south signs sit closer in, about halfway to the ring, while the others sit near the ring. Two small, faint glyphs sit near the ring at the northwest and southwest. Each looks like a Gathering sign with a small circle on its stem, oriented with its top toward the center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The tall center glyph matches no known sigil exactly. Its closest match is the fire sigil, so reading it as fire is a guess. Under that reading the spell works with flame and heat, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. The Detection sign shares the center as a second core; it is likely a sensing component, so the spell responds to something it detects nearby. The two circled Gathering-like glyphs are read as Gathering, also a guess, and would draw heat or material in from the surroundings. The small circle may lend a slight firming quality like the circles of Solidification. The Immobility signs hold the effect fixed in shape and position relative to the seal. Four face the usual way, but the one at the west is reversed and pulls against that hold. The four normal signs dominate, but the conflict makes the result likely unstable on the west side. The slightly irregular ring and rough strokes further weaken the spell and shorten how long it lasts.
effect: Draws heat in from the surroundings and holds it as a fixed, upright flame anchored to the seal. The flame flares up when something comes near. The western side never quite settles, so the flame periodically leans or drifts that way before snapping back. The whole effect gutters and fades sooner than a cleanly drawn version would.

name: s42_00322.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes, sits upright at the center at a moderate size, a little under half the ring's radius. Seven Dispersion signs are scattered around it. Four sit roughly two-thirds of the way out with their tops toward the ring, at the north-northeast, southeast, southwest and west. Three more sit right against the ring with their tops toward the center, so they are inverted, at the east-northeast, west-southwest and north-northwest. The north-northeast sign is a little roughly drawn. At the northwest, about two-thirds out, is a short straight stroke that matches no known sign exactly. More signs cluster on the western and northwestern side than elsewhere. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves and manipulates existing air rather than creating it. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Dispersion makes a seal's magic pour or leak outward instead of beaming in one direction, so the moved air spreads out from the seal rather than forming a jet. Inverted Dispersion works much like normal Dispersion, and inverted Columns also behaves this way, so the three signs set against the ring add to the outward spill rather than opposing it. The northwest stroke is closest to Dispersion with its two halves mirrored onto each other, which is a guess. With no distinct front or back, it would leak air both ways along its line and add a little untargeted spill on that side. The signs are unevenly spread and weighted toward the west-northwest, so more of the outflow goes that way. The slightly rough north-northeast sign makes the flow on that side a bit weaker and shorter-lived. Only one kind of modifier is present, so the seal holds together.
effect: Stirs the surrounding air and lets it pour outward from the seal as a spreading, moderate breeze rather than a focused gust. The flow is noticeably stronger toward the west-northwest. It is a little weaker toward the north-northeast, and that side fades sooner than the rest.

name: s42_00323.png
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed but drawn roughly and noticeably lumpy rather than round. An earth sigil sits at the center, roughly drawn and moderate in size relative to the ring. Six signs sit near the ring. A Selection sign is at the north. A Pointing sign is at the northwest, tilted, with its top toward the ring. An Orb sign is at the east. An inverted Rain sign, drawn inside-out, is at the southeast. A Stillness sign is at the south, turned nearly upside down. An Expansion sign is at the west-southwest, inked thickly and heavily but still legible, with its top toward the center and not inverted. At the west, inside the main ring, sits a small neatly drawn sub-seal with a closed ring and a small water sigil at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The earth sigil sets the main element, so the spell acts on solid matter, at moderate intensity. The water sub-seal adds a small, separate water effect. It is neat and closed, so it is the most reliable part of the seal, but its tiny ring keeps it weak. Selection confines the effect to the object the seal is drawn on. Expansion, not inverted, makes that object grow. Stillness holds the effect in place. Inverted Rain creates a zone that pushes material away. Pointing tapers the matter into a cone, while Orb defines a spherical space. These two shapes directly contradict each other. The seal also stacks far more than three unrelated kinds of modifier: confinement, growth, holding, repulsion, and two competing shapes. The earth sigil with Selection and Expansion dominates. Stillness and the repelling Rain are secondary, and the Pointing and Orb clash is the least predictable part, so the result is likely unstable. The rough linework and uneven ring further weaken the spell and shorten its life.
effect: Swells the solid object the seal is drawn on and tries to hold it fixed in place while shoving loose material away from it, with a faint trickle of water gathering at one side. The swelling comes in uneven pulses, and the object's form keeps wavering between a rounded bulge and a tapering point. The whole effect flickers and collapses back after only a short time.

name: s42_00324.png
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, neatly drawn, with the ring open at a gap near the top, spanning north-northwest to north. There is no element sigil. A Crosshair sign sits upright at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. Five Stillness signs sit near the ring at the west-northwest, northeast, east, south-southeast, and southwest positions, each rotated so its top faces the ring. At the north-northwest, right beside the gap, is a smaller, thinner glyph that matches no known sign exactly: a forked shape like Gathering with a small circle on its stem. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the Crosshair sign takes the center and sets the core behavior: the seal's effect targets whatever its short ends point at. Because no element is named, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth, or wind and acts on whatever it targets. The five Stillness signs hold a magical effect static in a single location. Spread evenly around the ring, they fix the targeted point firmly in place without pulling it any direction. The unnamed glyph is closest to Gathering, though this is a guess. Read that way, it lets the spell draw in material from its surroundings, adding a slight pull of nearby material toward the held target. Its single, smaller placement makes this a minor part of the spell. Targeting, holding in place, and gathering do not contradict each other, so the seal is coherent. The ring is open, so the spell will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: It does not activate while the ring is open. Once closed, it locks whatever it is aimed at in place, keeping it from moving or drifting. It also draws a small amount of nearby material in around the held target.

name: s42_00325.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. The ring is closed but noticeably uneven, bulging and flattening in places rather than tracing a true circle. Two small sigils sit side by side at the center, each about a quarter of the ring's radius: a light sigil on the left, drawn somewhat roughly, and a water sigil on the right, slightly rough. Two Solidification signs, each two small circles joined by a short line, sit about halfway out at the north and south points. Six small Diamond signs sit close to the ring, spread evenly at roughly the south-southwest, west-southwest, northwest, north-northeast, east-northeast and southeast positions. Several signs are drawn a little shakily. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The seal has two sigils. Light creates light that fades over time, and water manipulates, collects or creates water. Both are small relative to the ring, so the intensity is modest. Solidification makes the magic drawn within it more solid. The pair sits on opposite sides, so the firming is balanced and gives the water a firmer, more cohesive body that carries the light. Diamond most likely confines a spell to the contents of the container it is drawn on without affecting the container itself. Six evenly spaced Diamond signs hold the effect to whatever the seal's vessel contains. Diamond and Solidification are compatible and only two kinds of modifier are present, so the seal is not unstable. However, the ring is not round enough, and the rough sigils and signs weaken the spell and shorten its life, so the effect is likely brief and may fail to catch at all.
effect: Firms the water held inside the container the seal is drawn on into a soft, jelly-like glowing mass, while leaving the container itself untouched. The glow is dim, flickers unevenly, and fades quickly. The water's firmness gives way soon after forming, so the effect lasts only a short time and sometimes fails to take hold.

name: s42_00326.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background. It has two concentric rings, both closed, but both are drawn roughly and are lumpy and somewhat polygonal rather than round. A large Stability and Level Planes sign, three wavy vertical lines drawn a little roughly, sits upright at the center and spans about half the ring's radius. There is no element sigil. Seven signs surround it. A neatly drawn Windows sign sits at the northwest. A slightly rough Stillness sign sits at the southwest, its top toward the center. A neat Regions chevron sits at the west with its point aimed inward at the center. A Pointing sign sits at the north, tilted at an angle. A Holding sign sits at the northeast, rotated diagonally. A slightly rough Aeriforms Defined sign sits at the southeast, its strokes splaying toward the ring. A Crushing sign sits at the south with its peaks toward the ring, so it is not inverted.
