The signs are spread evenly around the seal, and nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, the large central Stability and Level Planes sign takes the core position. It sets the spell's main behavior: keeping the target balanced on a level plane in the air. Its large size relative to the ring makes that effect strong. Holding keeps the target in the shape the seal defines, and Stillness keeps the effect fixed in one place. Both reinforce the central sign. The inward Regions sign confines the magic to the area inside the ring. Pointing gives the material a conical shape, and Aeriforms Defined ties the spell to air or gases. Windows links the seal's space to another location. Crushing, in its normal orientation, breaks the target into smaller and smaller pieces. This directly contradicts Holding and Stillness, which preserve shape. The seal also stacks far more than three unrelated kinds of modifier. The central balancing effect dominates, backed by Holding and Stillness, and Crushing is the main disruptive force. Windows, Pointing and Aeriforms Defined are secondary, so the result is likely unstable. Both rings are uneven and not round, and several glyphs are drawn roughly. That makes the spell weaker and short-lived, and it may fail to activate at all.
effect: Gathers air or loose material inside the seal into a cone that floats level and holds still above the seal, with part of it bleeding through into a distant linked space. The cone keeps grinding itself into finer and finer particles even as it tries to hold its shape, so it shudders, sheds fragments and tilts unevenly. It lasts only a fleeting moment before collapsing, and some attempts fizzle without manifesting at all.

name: s42_00327.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a white background, with the ring closed and neatly drawn. A Link sign sits at the center in place of a sigil. It is moderately sized, about a third of the ring's radius, upright, and its strokes are a little rough. There is no element sigil. Two Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke with hooked ends, sit near the ring at the east-northeast and west-southwest. A small six-spoked star, like a Concealment sign without its eye marks, sits at the north, about two thirds of the way out from the center. A Cooling sign, a short line flanked by dots, sits at the east-southeast at a similar distance. The signs are unevenly spread and weighted toward the east-northeast. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no element sigil, Link at the center sets the spell's core behavior. It identifies objects that were broken off from, or made from, the same source and links them. Because no element is present, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth, or wind. Its moderate size gives a moderate intensity, and its slightly rough strokes make it somewhat weaker and shorter lived than a clean drawing would be. The two Envelopment signs make the effect wrap around its targets instead of acting on a single point. The six-spoked star matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Concealment, which hides a target, so reading it as Concealment is a guess. Without the eye marks it may hide its targets less fully than the complete sign would. Cooling lowers the temperature of whatever the spell acts on. Envelopment and Concealment work together, Cooling adds one further quality, and none of the signs contradict each other, so the seal holds together. Because the signs are weighted toward the east-northeast, the effect is stronger on that side.
effect: Finds objects or fragments that share a common source, links them, and wraps each one in a cool, partly concealing shroud that hides it from casual view. The shroud is thicker and colder on the east-northeast side and thinner on the opposite side. It fades somewhat sooner than a cleaner drawing would allow.

name: s42_00328.png
description: A fully visible seal on a white background, ring closed and neatly drawn. The center of the main ring is empty. Three small Dancing Puppets signs sit about halfway out from the center, at the east-northeast, south and west-northwest. The southern one is drawn darker and blurrier than the other two. Three Purification signs sit near the ring at the north-northeast, southeast and west, each a small curl. The western curl is drawn more roughly than the others. A smaller seal sits outside the main ring at the north, joined to it by a short line. Its ring is closed, and it holds a small upright fire sigil at its center. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The main ring has no sigil, so the element comes from the linked sub-seal. Its fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and the sigil is small within a small sub-ring, so the intensity is modest. Dancing Puppets lets the movement of the target be manipulated. Paired with fire instead of wind, it would send the flames moving through the air rather than staying in one place. No directional signs are present, so that motion has no set course and is erratic. Purification normally separates waste from water. It is asymmetric, so its behavior is less predictable, and with fire it most likely acts as a cleansing burn that takes away impurities. Both kinds of sign are evenly balanced around the ring, so no side is favored. Only two kinds of modifier are present, and they do not contradict each other. The rough strokes on the southern and east-northeastern Dancing Puppets signs and the western Purification sign weaken those parts slightly.
effect: Creates small, modest flames that dart erratically through the air around the seal. They burn away impurities and waste from what they touch while leaving cleaner material behind. Some flames move more weakly and gutter out sooner than others, so the cleansing is patchy on some sides.

name: s42_00329.png
description: A fully visible seal drawn neatly in black on a white background, made of two concentric rings, both ring open. The outer ring has a gap on the west side, and the inner ring has a gap at the upper east, between the northeast and east. There is no element sigil, and the center is empty. Seven Reflection signs, each a small hourglass of two triangles meeting at a point, are the only signs present. Three sit out on the outer ring line: one at the north, one at the south, and one at the west-northwest inside the outer ring's gap. Four sit about halfway between the center and the inner ring, at the south, west-southwest, north-northwest, and east-northeast, the last three tilted to follow the curve of the ring. More signs sit on the western side than the eastern side. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: With no sigil, the seal names no element, so it works only through its signs. Reflection targets a reflected image found on the object the seal is drawn on. All seven signs are the same kind, so they reinforce one another and do not conflict. Reflection's hourglass looks the same from both ends, so the different ways the signs face make no clear difference. The signs are unbalanced and lean toward the west, which gives that side of the drawn surface a stronger hold on its reflection. No Projection or directional sign is present to send the captured image anywhere, so the effect stays on the surface itself. Both rings are open, so the seal will not activate until they are closed.
effect: The seal does not activate as drawn. If its rings were closed, it would take hold of the reflected image on the surface it is drawn on and keep that reflection fixed there. The hold would be strongest on the western side and weaker toward the east.
